# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Shared Bitline Contact W-Plug Fill & CMP Baseline Recipe Setup

- **Document ID:** `SOP-FAB-180NM-WPLUG-001`
- **Revision:** 1.0 (Gen 2: µm / 180nm Node)
- **Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout ($8F^2$) > Access Transistor & Bitline Contact Layout Definition > Shared Bitline Contact W-Plug Fill & CMP Baseline Recipe Setup
- **Action Type:** Make

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Pre-Clean & Ti/TiN  │
│    Liner ALD/CVD     │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  W-CVD Seed & Bulk   │
│         Fill         │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│     Bulk W-CMP &     │
│   Touch-Up Polish    │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Post-CMP Scrub &   │
│      Metrology       │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Objective & Scope

Establish the baseline recipe for void-free Tungsten (W) chemical vapor deposition (CVD) fill and chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) over the shared bitline contact (BLC) of the 180nm 1T1C $8F^2$ DRAM cell architecture. The bitline contact is shared between two adjacent access transistors ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), providing low-resistance electrical coupling into the folded bitline while maintaining junction leakage below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Clean and Deglaze
1. Transfer wafers into an automated wet bench for pre-metal contact clean.
2. Perform dilute hydrofluoric acid deglaze (`DHF 100:1`, $23^\circ\text{C}$, $45\text{ s}$) to strip native oxide inside high-aspect-ratio contact vias ($CD \approx 180\text{ nm}$) without undercutting inter-layer dielectric (ILD).
3. Follow with standard mega-sonic UPW (ultra-pure water) rinse and surface passivating IPA vapor dry.

#### Step 2: Ti/TiN Adhesion & Diffusion Barrier Deposition
1. Load into multi-chamber cluster tool under high vacuum ($< 5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ Torr}$).
2. Perform in-situ Ar plasma pre-sputter etch ($30\text{ s}$, bias RF $100\text{ W}$) to clear contact interfaces at the active area diffusion.
3. Deposit ionized metal plasma (IMP) / ALD Ti liner ($10\text{ nm} \pm 1\text{ nm}$) for contact silicidation and ohmic junction contact.
4. Deposit metal-organic CVD / ALD TiN barrier layer ($15\text{ nm} \pm 1.5\text{ nm}$) using $\text{TDMAT}$ or $\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{NH}_3$ chemistry at $400^\circ\text{C}$ to prevent fluorine attack from subsequent $\text{WF}_6$ precursor chemistry.

#### Step 3: Tungsten Nucleation & Bulk CVD Fill
1. **Silane Reduction Nucleation:** Inject $\text{WF}_6$ ($30\text{ sccm}$) and $\text{SiH}_4$ ($15\text{ sccm}$) at $400^\circ\text{C}$, chamber pressure $30\text{ Torr}$ for $12\text{ s}$ to deposit a thin ($15\text{ nm}$ to $20\text{ nm}$), conformal W nucleation seed layer.
2. **Hydrogen Reduction Bulk Deposition:** Switch chemistry to $\text{WF}_6$ ($150\text{ sccm}$) and $\text{H}_2$ ($2500\text{ sccm}$) at $425^\circ\text{C}$, chamber pressure $80\text{ Torr}$.
3. Target bulk W overburden thickness: $350\text{ nm} \pm 25\text{ nm}$ over ILD field to ensure complete, void-free seam closure inside the $180\text{ nm}$ bitline contact plug.

#### Step 4: Tungsten CMP (Planarization) & Endpoint Detection
1. **Platen 1 (Bulk W Removal):** Apply silica-based acidic oxidizer slurry ($\text{pH } 2.0\text{--}2.5$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ oxidizer), down-force $3.2\text{ psi}$, platen speed $85\text{ rpm}$, carrier speed $80\text{ rpm}$. Polish through bulk W overburden.
2. **Platen 2 (Barrier & Endpoint Clearing):** Switch to high-selectivity barrier polish slurry ($W:\text{TiN}:\text{Oxide} \approx 1:1:0.1$) with optical motor current / eddy-current endpoint detection (EPD) to clear Ti/TiN barrier over ILD with controlled over-polish ($10\%$).
3. **Platen 3 (Buff & Soft Clean):** Soft touch-up buffing on poromeric polyurethane pad with DIW/surfactant to mitigate micro-scratches and particle adherence.

#### Step 5: Post-CMP Cleaning & Defect Inspection
1. Inline double-sided PVA sponge scrub clean using dilute alkaline/surfactant cleaning agent ($0.5\text{ wt}\%\text{ TMAH/NH}_4\text{OH}$, $\text{pH } 10.5$).
2. Spin rinse dry (SRD) with hot $\text{N}_2$ blanket.
3. Conduct in-line metrology (ellipsometry/profilometry for erosion/dishing, brightfield optical defect inspection, and electrical four-point probe contact resistance test).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Measurement Method & Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Contact Plug Seam / Void Diameter** | $\le 0\text{ nm}$ (Zero voiding / full fill at $180\text{ nm}$ via) | In-line Cross-Section STEM / High-Resolution CD-SEM |
| **W-Plug Dishing & Oxide Erosion** | $\le 15\text{ nm}$ dishing; $\le 10\text{ nm}$ field erosion | Atomic Force Profilometry (AFP) / In-line Optical Profilometer |
| **Bitline Contact Leakage Current** | $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Automated Parametric Wafer Probe (Keithley S530 / Keysight B1500A) |
| **Post-CMP Defectivity (Particles/Residue)** | $\le 20\text{ defects/wafer}$ (size threshold $\ge 0.18\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) | Darkfield/Brightfield Laser Defect Inspection (KLA / Applied Materials) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Defines the unit cell geometry: access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Specifies shared bitline contact between adjacent memory cells in $8F^2$ stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture.
  - Establishes the junction and sub-threshold leakage limit: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to preserve storage retention and meet refresh interval requirements.
  - Confirms the tungsten plug (W-plug) metallization scheme connecting active source/drain regions through the ILD stack.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: W-plug contact resistance directly dictates bitline sensing delay and access transistor drive currents in 8F² folded architectures. If plug contact resistivity fluctuates above nominal 10 Ohm/contact, RC delay on bitline read-access will degrade sensing margin below the 28 fF capacitor threshold. Furthermore, excessive over-polish during CMP erodes ILD oxide thickness, causing uncontrolled parasitic bitline-to-substrate capacitive coupling.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node dimensions (contact CD ~0.22 um, aspect ratio ~3:1 to 4:1), atomic layer Ti/TiN liner coverage is non-negotiable prior to WF6-based CVD. Non-conformal liner deposition leads to fluorine penetration from WF6 reduction, generating 'volcano' defects and junction leakage degradation (>1 fA/cell at 85°C) at the shared active diffusion area. Chemical Mechanical Planarization requires an alumina- or silica-based slurry with high W-to-oxide selectivity (>50:1) to suppress plug coring and dishing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: WF6 and silane/hydrogen reduction precursors, alongside electronic-grade Ti/TiN targets and specialty tungsten CMP slurry (e.g., Cabot Semi-Sperse W2000), require hazardous gas storage infrastructure and cold-chain/stabilized chemical logistics that present significant cost and lead-time bottlenecks for non-commercial or academic pilot lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Baseline recipe qualification requires strict boundary limits between CVD deposition cycle time and CMP throughput. Inadequate endpoint detection (motor current or optical reflectivity) risks catastrophic batch over-polish, setting back the 8F² memory cell schedule by several fab processing cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Keyhole/seam void formation inside the sub-micron contact hole due to premature pinch-off during tungsten chemical vapor deposition.
1. WF6 wormhole / volcano defect penetration into silicon active area caused by sub-5nm pinholes in the sputtered Ti/TiN diffusion barrier.
1. Severe tungsten plug coring and dielectric oxide erosion during Chemical Mechanical Planarization resulting in open or high-resistance bitline contacts.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-01` | **Cross-Sectional W-Plug Fill Conformal Seam and Sealing Verification** | Dual-Beam Focused Ion Beam and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB-SEM) | 1. Cleave wafer across designated 8F² test structure arrays containing shared bitline contacts. 2. Mill cross-section slice using Ga+ FIB with Pt protective capping layer. 3. Image at 30 kV field-emission SEM mode at 150kX magnification across 20 distinct plug locations across center, mid-radius, and edge die. 4. Measure keyhole diameter, seam width, and bottom step coverage percentage. | `Zero keyhole voids >10 nm in diameter; center seam width <= 5 nm; bottom liner step coverage >= 95% across all 20 measured contacts.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-02` | **Post-CMP Tungsten Plug Recess, Dishing, and Oxide Erosion Characterization** | High-Resolution Tapping-Mode Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) and 4-Point Probe Kelvin Contact Resistance Test Array | 1. Perform AFM topological line scan across a 10 um x 10 um shared bitline contact array pitch. 2. Extract line profile metrics for plug recess/dishing depth relative to surrounding ILD planar field. 3. Quantify cumulative dielectric erosion across the dense array versus open field oxide. 4. Probe Kelvin contact resistor structures across 50 dies per wafer to establish specific contact resistance. | `Tungsten plug dishing/recess <= 15 nm; ILD oxide field erosion <= 20 nm; specific contact resistance <= 12.0 Ohm/contact with standard deviation <= 1.5 Ohm across the wafer.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B chemical-resistant apron and sleeves, Butyl rubber outer gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Full-face splash shield with ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses, Closed-circuit positive pressure respirator equipped with acid-gas/particulate cartridge for emergency interventions
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF / WF6 hydrolysis exposure: Immediately rinse affected skin with copious flowing water for 2 minutes, then vigorously massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel continuously until medical emergency personnel arrive. For inhalation: Move victim immediately to fresh air, administer 100% humidified oxygen, and prepare for nebulized 2.5% calcium gluconate therapy.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous negative pressure toxic gas cabinet with dedicated point-of-use thermal-wet burn scrubbers operating at face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); automated toxic gas monitoring with electrochemical detectors calibrated for WF6/HF down to 0.1 ppm threshold.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous CMP slurry effluents containing colloidal alumina/silica and dissolved tungsten species routed to a dedicated fluoride/heavy-metal neutralization plant; automated pH adjustment with calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2) and tungsten oxy-salts before certified sludge extraction.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tungsten Hexafluoride (WF6)** | `7783-82-6` | VLSI/Electronic Grade 99.999% | `100% (gas under pressure)` |
| **Silane (SiH4)** | `7803-62-5` | Electronic Grade 99.9999% | `100% or 10% in Argon` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2, CMP Slurry Oxidizer)** | `7722-84-1` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C8) | `30% aqueous solution` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Pre-metal deglaze)** | `7664-39-3` | Ultra-Pure Electronic Grade (UP-S) | `0.5% - 1.0% aqueous solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, native-oxide-free shared n+ active diffusion and polysilicon contact bottoms with freshly deposited 15nm Ti / 20nm TiN liner, validated free of atmospheric moisture and organic residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Planarized tungsten plug coplanar with surrounding TEOS/BPSG ILD oxide surface, scrubbed free of slurry particulates and chemically passivated to prevent tungsten oxide blooming.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure exceeding maximum queue time causes native titanium oxide formation and moisture adsorption on the TiN barrier, which triggers rapid fluorine corrosion upon WF6 introduction, causing gross delamination and extreme Kelvin contact resistance (>100 Ohm).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Demonstrated robust W-plug fill via conformal Ti/TiN barrier and WF6 reduction chemistry, successfully planarized via selective CMP to yield void-free shared bitline contacts meeting the <= 12 Ohm/contact specification across 180nm 8F² DRAM cell layouts.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_PLUG_CMP_BASELINE_RECIPE_SPEC_GEN2.pdf`
- [ ] `TC_DRAM_W_PLUG_FIB_SEM_CROSS_SECTION_METROLOGY.tiff`
- [ ] `SHARED_BLC_CONTACT_RESISTANCE_WAFER_MAP.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average Kelvin contact resistance of the shared bitline contact W-plug** | `10.0 Ohm/contact` | +/- 2.0 Ohm/contact | Automated 4-wire Kelvin probe station measurement across 50 test sites per 200mm wafer |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum W-plug coring/dishing depth post-CMP** | `12.0 nm` | <= 15.0 nm absolute upper limit | High-resolution cross-sectional Atomic Force Microscopy profile across 0.22 um contact pitch |
| `ASSERT-03` | **W-plug keyhole void fill integrity** | `0.0 nm` | <= 5.0 nm max diameter | Dual-beam FIB-SEM high-resolution cross-sectional inspection across 20 sample cell contacts |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested die pass the Kelvin contact resistance limit (R_contact <= 12 Ohm/contact), zero observed tungsten volcano or keyhole defects under FIB-SEM inspection across 20 validation sites, and post-CMP defect density <= 0.05 defects/cm² confirmed by darkfield optical surface inspection.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Ti/TiN Liner and Diffusion Barrier Layer Deposition Baseline Recipe Setup

**Task ID:** `SOP-FAB-TF-180NM-042`  
**Process Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Cell Architecture:** 8F² Folded Bitline Stacked Capacitor (COB), Shared Bitline Contact W-Plug  
**Module:** Thin Film Deposition / PVD Metallization Liner  

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Pre-Clean & Degas    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Ti PVD Adhesion     │
│         Layer          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   TiN PVD Diffusion    │
│        Barrier         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Rapid Thermal Anneal  │
│          RTA           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Metrology &       │
│       Pass/Fail        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Chamber Evacuation & Base Vacuum Qualification:**
   - Pump down the cluster PVD deposition chamber via cryopump/turbomolecular pump until the vacuum gauge reads below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ before initiating wafer transfer.
2. **Wafer Pre-Treatment & Degas:**
   - Transfer wafer through loadlock into the degas chamber module. Heat substrate chuck to drive off adsorbed moisture.
   - Perform soft in-situ RF sputter clean / degas to clear native oxide inside the shared bitline contact vias ($W = 220\text{ nm}$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$).
3. **Ti Adhesion Layer Sputter Deposition:**
   - Strike DC magnetron plasma with high-purity Argon gas (Ar 99.999%) maintained at an operating pressure of $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$.
   - Apply DC magnetron target power calibrated within $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$ to deposit the primary titanium (Ti) contact silicide precursor and adhesion seed layer.
4. **TiN Barrier Layer Reactive Sputter Deposition:**
   - Introduce ultra-pure reactive Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) into the Ar sputter ambient.
   - Reactively sputter titanium nitride (TiN) diffusion barrier over the Ti layer at a controlled deposition rate of $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$ to prevent WF₆ chemical attack and tungsten encroachment during downstream W-plug fill.
5. **Post-Deposition Anneal & Barrier Stabilization:**
   - Transfer wafers under vacuum to the thermal anneal station.
   - Run post-deposition forming gas anneal ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ }95/5$) at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$ (or rapid thermal silicidation) to form low-resistance ohmic contacts and densify the barrier microstructure.

---

### 3. Baseline Operating Envelope

```text
                           PVD Baseline Operating Window
                           ┌───────────────────────────┐
                           │██                         │
  Anneal Temp (deg C / 100)┤██                         │
                           │▓▓                         │
Ar Working Pressure (mTorr)┤▓▓                         │
       Target DC Power (kW)┤▒▒                         │
                           │▒▒                         │
   Deposition Rate (nm/min)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                           │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                           └┬──────┬─────┬──────┬─────┬┘
                            0     25    50     75   100 
```

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Metrology Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Base Vacuum Pressure** | $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{Torr}$ | In-situ Cold Cathode / Ion Gauge |
| **Ar Working Sputter Pressure** | $3\text{ to }5$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |
| **DC Magnetron Target Power** | $1.5\text{ to }3.0$ | $\text{kW}$ | Generator Closed-Loop Power Monitor |
| **Deposition Rate** | $50\text{ to }100$ | $\text{nm/minute}$ | In-situ QCM / Ellipsometry |
| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\Box$ | 4-Point Probe (4PP) Metrology Station |
| **Anneal Temperature & Gas Ambience** | $400 \pm 5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ ($30\text{ min}$, $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ }95/5$) | Thermocouple / Mass Flow Controller |

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations

- **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects]:** Base pressure $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$; high-purity Ar ($99.999\%$) working gas pressure $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$; DC magnetron target power $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$; deposition rate $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$; post-metal anneal forming gas $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ }95/5$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$; sheet resistance target $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$.
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]:** $8\text{F}^2$ folded bitline layout; shared bitline contact geometry with access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; tungsten plug (W-plug) contact integration.
- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]:** 1T1C stacked capacitor integration over contact plugs; cell dimensions and thermal process constraints.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In an 8F² 180nm DRAM cell, the shared bitline contact (BLC) has an aspect ratio exceeding 3.5:1 to 4:1 landed on n+ drain diffusion. Utilizing planar DC magnetron PVD Ti/TiN will inevitably suffer from poor bottom and sidewall step coverage (<15% at contact bottom). Ionized metal plasma (IMP) PVD, collimated sputtering, or MOCVD/ALD TiN must be benchmarked; otherwise, the tungsten CVD precursor (WF6) will attack silicon via wormhole defects during subsequent W-plug fill.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Titanium liner must provide ohmic contact through rapid thermal silicidation (forming C54/C49 TiSi2 with contact resistance Rc < 50 Ohm/contact), while the TiN film must act as a stoichiometric, dense diffusion barrier (density > 5.0 g/cm³) with high (200) texture orientation. Deposition chamber base pressure must remain <= 1.0e-7 Torr to avoid uncontrolled oxygen stuffing in the Ti film which drastically elevates contact resistance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-purity 5N (99.999%) Ti targets (typically 200mm/300mm planar with backing plates) have a 12-16 week lead time and volatile pricing due to aerospace raw titanium allocation. For open-source pilot lines in Vietnam, secondary source qualification of hot isostatically pressed (HIP) Ti and TiN targets from regional APAC vendors is required to mitigate supply disruptions.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Ti/TiN deposition setup is on the critical path directly preceding W-CVD plug nucleation and CMP. Any recipe instability or chamber down-time for shield flaking maintenance pushes bitline test-chip tapeout milestones by at least 3 weeks. Target baseline recipe qualification must be completed within 10 operational shifts.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Volcano effect/WF6 encroachment into active Si area during tungsten CVD due to discontinuous TiN barrier at contact bottom corners
1. TiN film delamination and particulate generation caused by excessive compressive stress (>2.5 GPa) on oxide sidewalls
1. Native oxide regrowth and contact resistance blow-out exceeding 150 Ohm/contact due to Q-time breach between pre-clean and Ti deposition

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-1-01` | **Ti/TiN Film Thickness and Bottom Step Coverage Verification via HR-XSEM** | Dual-beam Focused Ion Beam (FIB) and High-Resolution Scanning Electron Microscope (HR-SEM/TEM) with calibrated digital measurement reticle | 1. Transfer wafer to FIB-SEM chamber under high vacuum (< 5e-6 Torr). 2. Deposit protective Pt cap over three selected 8F² array contact vias (center, mid-radius, edge). 3. Mill cross-section through center of contact via using Ga+ ion beam. 4. Acquire SEM images at 150,000x magnification at 5 kV. 5. Measure field thickness, sidewall thickness at midpoint, and bottom center liner thickness for both Ti and TiN layers. | `Field Ti thickness = 15 nm ± 2 nm; Field TiN thickness = 20 nm ± 2 nm; Bottom Ti step coverage >= 20% (>= 3.0 nm); Bottom TiN barrier thickness >= 5.0 nm continuously across via bottom without pinholes.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-1-02` | **Sheet Resistance (Rs) and Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity Measurement** | Automated 4-Point Probe (4PP) Resistivity Mapping System (49-point circular map, 3mm edge exclusion) | 1. Initialize and calibrate 4-point probe with NIST-traceable standard wafer. 2. Load monitor wafer into measurement stage. 3. Execute 49-point polar mapping scan measuring V/I at 10 mA drive current. 4. Calculate mean sheet resistance (Rs) and 1-sigma percentage non-uniformity (%NU = (sigma / mean) * 100). | `Ti/TiN stack sheet resistance Rs between 35.0 Ohm/sq and 55.0 Ohm/sq; Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (1-sigma) <= 2.5% across 49 measurement sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level C cleanroom PPE with chemical apron, Nitrile inner gloves with butyl rubber outer gloves for chamber maintenance, Full-face respirator with multi-gas/P100 particulate cartridge during target changes and shield cleaning, ANSI Z87.1 certified splash/impact safety goggles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF contact: Immediately flush affected area with copius water for 5 minutes, apply 2.5% calcium gluconate gel massage continuously until medical help arrives. For inert gas (Ar/N2) asphyxiation risk: Move victim immediately to fresh air, administer oxygen if breathing is labored, initiate CPR if pulse absent.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chamber roughing and turbomolecular pump backing lines must vent to dedicated semiconductor toxic/acid scrubber exhaust ducting maintained at -0.5 to -1.2 in. w.g. negative pressure. Continuous ambient O2 depletion monitors (alarm threshold < 19.5% O2) installed in wafer transfer and gas valve manifold box (VMB) areas.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent wet clean solutions containing HF/NH4F must be plumbed to an automated Industrial Fluoride Waste Treatment system utilizing Ca(OH)2 precipitation to yield insoluble CaF2 sludge (target effluent F- < 10 ppm). Used targets and metal flake wastes collected in sealed containers for specialist precious/refractory metal recovery.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Titanium (solid sputter target)** | `7440-32-6` | 5N (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Argon Process Gas (compressed)** | `7440-37-1` | Ultra-High Purity 6N (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Nitrogen Reactive Gas (compressed)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 6N (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (pre-clean dilute etch)** | `7664-39-3` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `0.5% - 1.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned Si/SiO2 surface post-dilute HF/in-situ Ar sputter etch; pristine native-oxide-free (<0.3 nm SiO2) n+ diffusion contact area with hydrophobic water contact angle > 75 degrees.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Continuous, stoichiometric Ti/TiN bilayer (passivated TiN surface) under vacuum/inert environment, free of native oxide and airborne molecular contamination (AMC).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide (SiO2) regrowth exceeding 1.2 nm at contact interface resulting in non-ohmic contact behavior, bitline contact open defects, and severe WF6 gas penetration causing contact 'volcano' silicon erosion during W-CVD.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified baseline recipe for Ti/TiN liner/diffusion barrier deposition on 180nm 8F² DRAM bitline contact vias, guaranteeing continuous barrier coverage (>= 5nm bottom TiN), nominal sheet resistance (35-55 Ohm/sq), and zero wormhole penetration during subsequent W-fill.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RECIPE_PVD_TITIN_BLC_180NM_V1.0.xml`
- [ ] `RUN_REPORT_TITIN_4PP_RS_UNIFORMITY.csv`
- [ ] `TEM_XSECTION_BLC_TITIN_STEP_COVERAGE.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **TiN bottom barrier thickness at center of 180nm contact via** | `6.0 nm` | ± 1.0 nm | Cross-sectional TEM metrology across 5 array contact locations |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-wafer sheet resistance (Rs) uniformity across 200mm monitor wafer** | `1.8%` | ≤ 2.5% (1-sigma) | Automated 49-point four-point probe map measurement |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Film residual stress of Ti/TiN stack** | `-1.2 GPa` | ± 0.3 GPa (compressive) | Laser curvature wafer bow measurement (Stoney formula) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions confirmed across 3 consecutive qualification lots (9 monitor wafers total) with zero particulate defects > 0.2µm, confirmed absence of Si encroachment via post-W-CVD TEM, and written concurrence from Integration, Thin Film, and EHS Leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Title: Tungsten (W) CVD Contact Via Fill and Keyhole Void Optimization Recipe
**Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | 8F² Cell Folded Bitline Architecture | Contact Aspect Ratio Fill

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Pre-Clean / Degas at  │
│          400C          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Ti/TiN Liner Barrier  │
│       Deposition       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  SiH4/WF6 Nucleation   │
│      Layer Flash       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   H2/WF6 Bulk W Fill   │
│       Deposition       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Keyhole Void      │
│    Metrology & CMP     │
│         Polish         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Pre-Clean & Degas**:
   - Transfer wafer into the CVD/PVD cluster degas chamber.
   - Degas wafer under high vacuum at $400^\circ\text{C}$ to desorb moisture, organic residue, and trapped fluorine.
2. **Ti/TiN Liner/Barrier Deposition**:
   - Deposit conformal $\text{Ti}$ adhesion layer followed by $\text{TiN}$ barrier layer via collimated/ionized PVD or CVD to prevent $\text{WF}_6$ wormhole encroachment into the access transistor source/drain diffusion regions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$).
3. **Silane ($\text{SiH}_4$) Reduction Nucleation Step**:
   - Transfer to the W-CVD reaction chamber.
   - Pre-purge with Ar/$\text{N}_2$ carrier gas.
   - Run short silane reduction flash: $\text{WF}_6 + \text{SiH}_4 \rightarrow \text{W} + \text{SiF}_4\uparrow$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ stage temperature to establish a continuous, thin, fine-grained tungsten seed layer ($\sim 20\text{--}30\,\text{nm}$) on the $\text{TiN}$ surface.
4. **Hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$) Reduction Bulk Fill & Seam Optimization**:
   - Transition gas flows to $\text{H}_2/\text{WF}_6$ reduction chemistry: $\text{WF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{W} + 6\text{HF}\uparrow$.
   - Maintain wafer substrate temperature at $400^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Maintain high $\text{H}_2 : \text{WF}_6$ ratio to achieve bottom-up, conformal, columnar grain growth across the bitline and storage contact vias (aspect ratio $\sim 3:1$ to $4:1$ on the $360\text{--}400\,\text{nm}$ pitch array).
   - Suppress premature mouth closure (pinch-off) at the top rim of the contact to eliminate keyhole/centerline voids.
5. **Overfill & CMP Polish**:
   - Deposit tungsten overburden ($350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$ equivalent target clearance above the dielectric field).
   - Send wafer to post-CVD W-CMP to planarize flush to the interlayer dielectric (ILD) surface.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                         Baseline CVD W Metrics         
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │░░░░░░░░                              │
   R_s (mOhm/sq)┤░░░░░░░░                              │
                │▒                                     │
Via Aspect Ratio┤▒                                     │
 Gas Flow H2/WF6┤▓▓▓▓                                  │
                │▓▓▓▓                                  │
        Temp (C)┤██████████████████████████████████████│
                │██████████████████████████████████████│
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0       100       200      300     400 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Acceptance Criteria | Exact Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deposition / Degas Stage Temperature** | $400 \pm 5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Multi-zone pyrometer / In-situ thermocouple |
| **Metal Overburden Film Thickness** | $350 \pm 5\%$ | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic ellipsometry / XRF |
| **Post-Anneal Interconnect Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\Box$ | 4-point probe sheet resistance measurement |
| **Keyhole Void Seam Width / Core Diameter** | $< 10$ | $\text{nm}$ (Zero unclosed core voids) | Cross-sectional STEM / FIB-SEM |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Context*: Transistor channel geometry ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), shared bitline contact arrangement, and drain contact tungsten plug (W-plug) connection to the stacked capacitor over bitline (COB).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Context*: 8F² folded bitline layout, array pitch ($360\,\text{nm}$ to $400\,\text{nm}$ wordline/bitline pitch), and cell dielectric boundary constraints.
- **Source: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**
  - *Context*: Thermal boundary and post-metal anneal temperature of $400^\circ\text{C}$, target metal layer thickness of $350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$, and maximum sheet resistance limit $R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\Box$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In an 8F² 180nm architecture, the shared bitline contact (BLC) aspect ratio approaches 3.5:1 to 4:1 through the pre-metal dielectric (PMD). Any non-conformal tungsten nucleation or premature cusping at the neck of the contact will form a seam/keyhole void. During subsequent W-CMP, slurry entrapment inside open keyholes causes severe core corrosion, uncorrectable bitline parasitic capacitance variance (>15%), and intermittent read-disturb latency across the memory array.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Achieving void-free W-plug fill requires a strict multi-step CVD recipe: an ultra-thin ALD/CVD TiN barrier/adhesion liner (4-6 nm), followed by pulsed silane (SiH4) or diborane (B2H6) reduction of WF6 to form a continuous 15-20 nm nucleation layer, followed by high-pressure H2 reduction of WF6 (bulk fill at 400-450°C, 80-300 Torr) to maximize conformality and step coverage without volcano-effect fluorine attack on the Ti/TiN underlayer.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten hexafluoride (WF6) and semiconductor-grade silane (SiH4) require dedicated hazardous gas delivery manifolds, dual-containment orbital-welded 316L SS tubing, and scrubbers. In Southeast Asia / Vietnam regional supply chains, lead times for 5N5 electronic-grade WF6 cylinders can exceed 16-20 weeks, requiring strict cylinder inventory rotation and leak-check safety protocols to prevent unplanned fab line stoppages.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Baseline qualification of this W-CVD recipe directly dictates the critical path to bitline metal-1 integration. Without a rapid feedback loop coupling cross-sectional high-resolution SEM/TEM void inspection and TLM/Kelvin test structures, schedule slippage on milestone M2 (Shared Bitline Contact Module Freeze) risks delaying back-end metallization signoff by over 3 weeks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Keyhole void formation due to premature collar pinch-off at the PMD contact via neck during bulk WF6/H2 reduction.
1. Tungsten 'volcano effect' peeling/delamination caused by fluorine penetration through sub-optimal TiN barrier pinholes attacking the underlying Ti/silicide interface.
1. High bitline contact resistance (Rc > 10 Ohm/via) or open contacts resulting from TiN oxidation or residual fluorocarbon polymer inside the high-aspect-ratio via bottom.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-2-01` | **Cross-Sectional SEM/FIB Contact Via Seam and Keyhole Void Inspection** | Dual-Beam FIB-SEM (Focused Ion Beam / Scanning Electron Microscope, 5 kV secondary electron imaging) | 1. Select 5 test sites per wafer (center, top, bottom, left, right) on dedicated dense 8F2 DRAM cell shared-contact macro arrays. 2. Deposit protective Pt strap (1 um thick) via in-situ ion beam deposition. 3. Mill cross-sectional trench across a minimum of 20 consecutive shared bitline contact vias using Ga+ focused ion beam. 4. Fine polish cross-section at 30 kV / 50 pA beam current. 5. Perform high-magnification immersion-mode SEM inspection at 100,000x magnification. 6. Measure maximum seam width and void area percentage per via across all 100 sampled contacts. | `Keyhole void area must be 0% (zero hollow voiding). Maximum vertical seam separation width <= 3.0 nm across 100% of examined contacts; contact via fill factor >= 99.5%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-2-02` | **Specific Contact Resistivity and Via Chain Kelvin Resistance Metrology** | Automated DC Parametric Wafer Prober with TLM (Transmission Line Measurement) and Kelvin 4-wire test capability | 1. Load wafer onto thermal chuck at 25°C. 2. Align prober to 1,000-via contact chain and 4-wire Kelvin shared-contact test structures. 3. Force DC current of 1.0 mA through force pads and measure floating potential difference V across sense terminals. 4. Calculate individual via resistance Rc = V / I. 5. Perform TLM extraction across varying contact spacing (2 um to 20 um) to compute specific contact resistivity rho_c. | `Contact resistance Rc < 10.0 Ohm per shared bitline contact via. Specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0 x 10^-6 Ohm*cm^2. 1,000-via chain total resistance <= 9.5 kOhm with 0 open-circuit defects.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B Chemically Resistant Suit with emergency escape breathing apparatus (EEBA), Viton / Butyl heavy chemical gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Full-face gas-tight respirator with multi-gas/P100 filter (HF and acid gases), Conductive safety footwear with chemical-resistant overboots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: WF6 hydrolyzes rapidly with atmospheric moisture to release toxic, corrosive hydrofluoric acid (HF) and WO3. In case of skin exposure: immediately flush with copious cold water for 5 minutes, apply 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel liberally and rub continuously until medical aid arrives. In case of inhalation: evacuate immediately to fresh air, administer 100% humidified oxygen, and provide Calcium Gluconate nebulized aerosol (2.5%) under medical supervision.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated high-flow corrosive/pyrophoric acid exhaust maintained under negative pressure (min -1.5 in. w.g.). Real-time continuous toxic gas monitoring (TGMS) with electrochemical/pyrolyzer sensors detecting HF (< 0.5 ppm threshold) and SiH4 (< 2.5 ppm threshold). Automated interlock to emergency shutoff valves (ESV) upon loss of exhaust or gas detection.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Effluent gases routed directly into point-of-use (POU) thermal burn-wet combustor scrubbers. SiH4 converted to non-hazardous SiO2 particulate; WF6, HF, and F2 neutralized via dual-stage wet alkaline scrubbing (KOH/Ca(OH)2 recirculating wash) producing inert solid CaF2 precipitate.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tungsten Hexafluoride (WF6)** | `7783-82-6` | Electronic Grade 5N5 (99.9995%) | `100.0%` |
| **Silane (SiH4)** | `7803-62-5` | Ultra-Pure VLSI Grade 6N (99.9999%) | `100.0% (or 2% in high-purity Ar/H2 balance)` |
| **Hydrogen (H2)** | `1333-74-0` | Semiconductor Grade 6N (99.9999%) | `100.0%` |
| **Nitrogen Trifluoride (NF3, Chamber Clean)** | `7783-54-2` | Electronic Grade 4N (99.99%) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited, unoxidized ALD/CVD Ti/TiN barrier liner (thickness 5 nm +/- 0.5 nm) with zero particulate contamination (< 10 particles at >= 90 nm) and no Native TiOx formation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Continuous, smooth blanket tungsten layer (thickness 350 nm +/- 20 nm) overfilling the 180nm contact vias, surface roughness RMS <= 15 nm, ready for post-deposition W-CMP queue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time before W-CVD exposes the TiN liner to ambient oxygen and moisture, forming titanium oxynitride (TiOxNy) and moisture condensation inside via bottoms, which triggers tungsten nucleation failure, severe fluorine volcano peeling, and contact resistivity spikes exceeding 1.0 x 10^-5 Ohm*cm^2.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and signoff of the robust, void-free Tungsten CVD contact via fill recipe for the 180nm 8F² shared bitline contact module, demonstrating 100% seam/keyhole closure and specific contact resistivity meeting stringent DRAM refresh and read-latency margins.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_CVD_180NM_BLC_VOID_ANALYSIS_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `BLC_CONTACT_RESISTIVITY_TLM_METROLOGY.csv`
- [ ] `FIB_SEM_BLC_CROSS_SECTION_100KX.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Keyhole void closure rate across dense DRAM shared bitline contact arrays** | `100.0%` | 0.0% voids (Zero-tolerance defect criteria across 100 examined cross-sections) | Dual-Beam FIB-SEM cross-sectional imaging at 100,000x across 5 wafer field positions |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Specific contact resistivity (rho_c) at shared bitline contact interface** | `8.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2` | <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm^2 | Automated 4-terminal Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) parametric test |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Single shared bitline contact resistance (Rc)** | `6.5 Ohm` | < 10.0 Ohm | Kelvin 4-wire contact structure DC prober measurement at 1.0 mA forced current |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% keyhole-free cross-sectional morphology confirmed by FIB-SEM, wafer sheet resistance uniformity 1-sigma <= 2.5%, single-contact Rc < 10 Ohm, specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0 x 10^-6 Ohm*cm^2 across 3 consecutive split lots, and multi-agent consensus approval across Systems, Domain, EHS, and Project Management.

critics.systems_engineer: In an 8F² 180nm architecture, the shared bitline contact (BLC) aspect ratio approaches 3.5:1 to 4:1 through the pre-metal dielectric (PMD). Any non-conformal tungsten nucleation or premature cusping at the neck of the contact will form a seam/keyhole void. During subsequent W-CMP, slurry entrapment inside open keyholes causes severe core corrosion, uncorrectable bitline parasitic capacitance variance (>15%), and intermittent read-disturb latency across the memory array.
critics.domain_expert: Achieving void-free W-plug fill requires a strict multi-step CVD recipe: an ultra-thin ALD/CVD TiN barrier/adhesion liner (4-6 nm), followed by pulsed silane (SiH4) or diborane (B2H6) reduction of WF6 to form a continuous 15-20 nm nucleation layer, followed by high-pressure H2 reduction of WF6 (bulk fill at 400-450°C, 80-300 Torr) to maximize conformality and step coverage without volcano-effect fluorine attack on the Ti/TiN underlayer.
critics.supply_chain: Tungsten hexafluoride (WF6) and semiconductor-grade silane (SiH4) require dedicated hazardous gas delivery manifolds, dual-containment orbital-welded 316L SS tubing, and scrubbers. In Southeast Asia / Vietnam regional supply chains, lead times for 5N5 electronic-grade WF6 cylinders can exceed 16-20 weeks, requiring strict cylinder inventory rotation and leak-check safety protocols to prevent unplanned fab line stoppages.
critics.laya_pm: Baseline qualification of this W-CVD recipe directly dictates the critical path to bitline metal-1 integration. Without a rapid feedback loop coupling cross-sectional high-resolution SEM/TEM void inspection and TLM/Kelvin test structures, schedule slippage on milestone M2 (Shared Bitline Contact Module Freeze) risks delaying back-end metallization signoff by over 3 weeks.
critical_failure_modes: Keyhole void formation due to premature collar pinch-off at the PMD contact via neck during bulk WF6/H2 reduction.
Tungsten 'volcano effect' peeling/delamination caused by fluorine penetration through sub-optimal TiN barrier pinholes attacking the underlying Ti/silicide interface.
High bitline contact resistance (Rc > 10 Ohm/via) or open contacts resulting from TiN oxidation or residual fluorocarbon polymer inside the high-aspect-ratio via bottom.

testcases.title: Cross-Sectional SEM/FIB Contact Via Seam and Keyhole Void Inspection
testcases.instrumentation: Dual-Beam FIB-SEM (Focused Ion Beam / Scanning Electron Microscope, 5 kV secondary electron imaging)
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers completed through Ti/TiN barrier liner deposition, W-CVD deposition (nucleation + bulk fill), and post-CVD cool down; cleanroom ambient ISO 4 / Class 10.
testcases.procedure: 1. Select 5 test sites per wafer (center, top, bottom, left, right) on dedicated dense 8F2 DRAM cell shared-contact macro arrays. 2. Deposit protective Pt strap (1 um thick) via in-situ ion beam deposition. 3. Mill cross-sectional trench across a minimum of 20 consecutive shared bitline contact vias using Ga+ focused ion beam. 4. Fine polish cross-section at 30 kV / 50 pA beam current. 5. Perform high-magnification immersion-mode SEM inspection at 100,000x magnification. 6. Measure maximum seam width and void area percentage per via across all 100 sampled contacts.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Keyhole void area must be 0% (zero hollow voiding). Maximum vertical seam separation width <= 3.0 nm across 100% of examined contacts; contact via fill factor >= 99.5%.

testcases.title: Specific Contact Resistivity and Via Chain Kelvin Resistance Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Automated DC Parametric Wafer Prober with TLM (Transmission Line Measurement) and Kelvin 4-wire test capability
testcases.pre_conditions: Post W-CMP planarization completed; M1 Al/Cu interconnection patterned and sintered at 400°C in forming gas (N2/H2 95/5%).

Force DC current of 1.0 mA through force pads and measure floating potential difference V across sense terminals. 4. Calculate individual via resistance Rc = V / I. 5. Perform TLM extraction across varying contact spacing (2 um to 20 um) to compute specific contact resistivity rho_c.

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: WF6 hydrolyzes rapidly with atmospheric moisture to release toxic, corrosive hydrofluoric acid (HF) and WO3. Automated interlock to emergency shutoff valves (ESV) upon loss of exhaust or gas detection.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## W-CMP Planarization Baseline Recipe Setup, Over-Polish Control, and Dishing Metrology

**Context & Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Gen 2 (µm)  
**Functional Domain:** Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) / Shared Bitline Contact W-Plug Fill  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 1: Pre-Clean &  │
│  Baseline Inspection  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 2: Main W Bulk  │
│    Polish Platen 1    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Step 3: Ti/TiN     │
│    Barrier Polish     │
│       Platen 2        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 4: Over-Polish  │
│  & Oxide Stop Platen  │
│           3           │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Step 5: Post-CMP    │
│   Megasonic Clean &   │
│       Metrology       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-CMP Surface Preparation & Pad Conditioning:**
   - Mount polyurethane hard polishing pads on Platens 1 and 2; mount a soft poromeric buff pad on Platen 3.
   - Perform in-situ diamond disc pad conditioning (100–120 grit) under continuous deionized (DI) water flushing to stabilize pad asperities.
   - Inspect pre-CMP blanket tungsten (CVD W) overburden thickness across 8F² shared bitline contact test fields.

2. **Platen 1: Bulk Tungsten Removal & Endpoint Detection:**
   - Dispense acidic ferric nitrate/alumina or silica-based W slurry.
   - Set platen/carrier counter-rotation with controlled down-force (2.5–3.5 psi).
   - Engage optical reflectometry or eddy-current in-situ endpoint detection (EPD) to capture the sharp slope change as the bulk W layer is cleared and the Ti/TiN barrier is reached.

3. **Platen 2: Ti/TiN Barrier Polish & Planarization:**
   - Switch to high-selectivity barrier removal slurry (W:Ti/TiN:SiO₂ selectivity tuned to suppress oxide erosion).
   - Polish until the Ti/TiN barrier over the inter-layer dielectric (ILD) oxide is fully cleared.

4. **Platen 3: Controlled Over-Polish Buff & Oxide Stop:**
   - Apply a strictly timed over-polish window (5% to 10% maximum margin) to clear residual W micro-puddles in dense array areas without inducing metal recess or dielectric erosion across the 360 nm to 400 nm bitline/wordline array pitch.
   - Perform soft pad buffing with diluted colloidal silica or alkaline surfactant chemistry to passivate plug tops.

5. **Post-CMP Cleaning & Dishing/Erosion Metrology:**
   - Transfer wafer immediately to post-CMP double-sided PVA brush scrubbing with dilute NH₄OH/citric acid, followed by megasonic DI water immersion rinse and spin dry.
   - Load wafer into High-Resolution Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) / Optical Profiler to quantify W-plug dishing and array oxide erosion around the 180 nm channel length and 220 nm width access transistor cell boundaries.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage & Polish Alignment Tolerance (Gen 2)** | $\le \pm 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Metrology Optical Alignment Station *(Source 3)* |
| **Contact / Bitline Array Pitch Uniformity** | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Inline Critical Dimension SEM (CD-SEM) *(Source 2)* |
| **Bitline Access Transistor Channel Critical Dimensions** | $L = 180$, $W = 220$ | $\text{nm}$ | Inline Top-down CD-SEM *(Source 1)* |
| **W-Plug Recess & Dishing Margin** | $\le 10$ | $\text{nm}$ | High-Resolution Tapping-Mode AFM |
| **Array Oxide Erosion Across 8F² Cell Field** | $\le 15$ | $\text{nm}$ | Optical Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / AFM Profilometry |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations

- **[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Defines the 180nm 8F² unit cell topology with access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, where bitline contacts are shared between adjacent cells and isolated via tungsten plugs (W-plugs).
- **[Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: Establishes bitline and wordline array pitch dimensions of $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$ and 1T1C stacked capacitor cell integration rules.
- **[Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)]**: Provides the baseline alignment and stage tolerance benchmark for Gen 2 tooling at $\pm 5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (improved from Gen 1 $\pm 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) and DI water rinsing regimes.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: W-CMP planarization of the shared bitline contact in an 8F² DRAM cell (180nm node) directly couples contact resistance variance to bitline sense amplifier differential margin. A ±15 nm over-polish into the underlying ILD0 (BPSG/TEOS) alters both the parasitic bitline-to-substrate capacitance (Cbl) and the plug contact aspect ratio, jeopardizing read sensing speed and write recovery timing margins across the memory array.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Tungsten CMP requires strict two-step selectivity: high W removal rate with acidic alumina/silica slurry containing an oxidizer (H2O2 / Fe(NO3)3) down to the Ti/TiN barrier liner, transitioning to a high-selectivity barrier polish with negligible dielectric erosion. In Gen 2 garage/open-source cleanroom environments, endpoint detection (motor current torque monitoring vs. optical reflectance) lacks high temporal resolution, making dishing in large test pads (>50 µm) and plug recess in dense 8F² contact arrays (>25 nm) the primary physical yield limiters.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acidic tungsten slurries with active hydrogen peroxide or iron nitrate oxidizers exhibit short pot life (typically <48 hours once mixed) and undergo phase separation or particle agglomeration in unagitated containers. Sourcing semiconductor-grade colloidal silica/alumina CMP slurries and high-hardness polyurethane polishing pads (e.g., IC1000 equivalent) with diamond conditioning discs in decentralized lab supply chains introduces batch-to-batch selectivity variance that demands dedicated run-rate qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Execution requires synchronizing wafer handoff immediately following W-CVD/sputter metallization to avoid surface tungstic acid crusting. Lacking an inline automated dry-in/dry-out post-CMP scrub track, manual PVA brush scrub and megasonic DI rinsing must be executed within rigid queue times to prevent irreversible particle-induced bitline-to-wordline shorts.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Severe contact plug recess (>35 nm) and contact-to-contact oxide erosion resulting in open bitline contacts or high-resistance vias during subsequent M1 deposition.
1. Incomplete Ti/TiN barrier removal causing inter-bitline micro-shorts and sub-threshold leakage across adjacent 8F² cell access nodes.
1. Post-CMP slurry abrasive (Al2O3 / SiO2) particle contamination and surface micro-scratching causing gate dielectric breakdown or photolithographic bridging at subsequent metal layers.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-3-01` | **W-Plug Dishing and ILD Field Oxide Erosion Metrology via Contact AFM** | Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in tapping mode with high-aspect-ratio diamond-like carbon (DLC) tip (tip radius <10 nm) and calibrated 4-point probe / optical spectroscopic reflectometer. | 1. Mount wafer onto vibration-isolated AFM stage and locate the 8F² dense contact array test block (0.24 µm contact diameter, 0.48 µm pitch) and isolated 10 µm W test pad. 2. Perform a 5 µm x 5 µm high-resolution topographical scan across 10 consecutive bitline contacts. 3. Extract line profiles across the plug centers to measure W recess relative to adjacent ILD0 oxide surface. 4. Perform a 20 µm x 20 µm scan across the 10 µm isolated W pad to calculate maximum center-to-edge dishing. 5. Measure remaining field ILD0 oxide thickness at 5 points (center, top, bottom, left, right) using spectroscopic reflectometry. | `W-plug recess in dense 8F² array <= 15.0 nm; W dishing in isolated 10 µm test pad <= 25.0 nm; field ILD0 dielectric erosion across active array <= 20.0 nm; zero residual bulk W or TiN barrier bridging between contacts.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-1-1-2-2-3-02` | **Post-CMP Inter-Bitline Electrical Isolation and Shared Contact Resistance Verification** | Semi-automatic analytical probe station with sub-femtoamp sourcemeter (Keithley 4200-SCS or equivalent parameter analyzer). | 1. Load wafer into shielded probe station at 25°C. 2. Land micromanipulator probes onto adjacent isolated shared bitline contact pads (0.24 µm spacing). 3. Apply DC voltage sweep from -1.8 V to +1.8 V and measure leakage current between adjacent contact plugs. 4. Switch to 4-terminal Kelvin test structure for individual 0.24 µm W-plug contact resistance; force 1.0 mA DC current and measure differential voltage drop. | `Inter-contact leakage current < 1.0 pA at 1.8 V DC bias (isolation resistance > 1.8 TOhm); individual 180nm shared bitline W-plug contact resistance <= 12.0 Ohm/plug across 95% of measured sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Butyl or heavy-duty nitrile chemical gloves with secondary inner nitrile pair, ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles with full-face polycarbonate shield, Acid- and oxidizer-resistant neoprene cleanroom apron and chemical sleeve covers, Closed-toe chemical-resistant boots with antistatic grounding straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin exposure: Flush affected area immediately with copious flowing water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated apparel; apply soothing cold compress. Eye contact: Irrigate eye continuously at eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate emergency ophthalmological evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh ambient air; administer oxygen if respiration is labored; seek immediate medical assessment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous wet bench and polishing head local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) with acid-mist and oxidizer wet scrubber integration.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate spent acidic W-slurry waste from solvent drains. Neutralize oxidizer-laden slurry by slow titration with dilute sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) to quench residual peroxides, adjust effluent pH to 6.5-8.5 using 10% sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or calcium hydroxide, settle abrasive solids via coagulation/filtration, and verify total dissolved solids (TDS) and heavy metal limits prior to industrial drain release.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (Stabilized Oxidizer Solution)** | `7722-84-1` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `30.0 wt%` |
| **Ferric Nitrate Nonahydrate (Oxidizing Catalyst)** | `7782-61-8` | Reagent Grade | `2.0-5.0 wt%` |
| **Colloidal Alumina / Silica Abrasive Slurry Matrix** | `1344-28-1` | Electronic Grade | `5.0-15.0 wt%` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (Post-CMP Alkaline Clean Rinse)** | `1336-21-6` | Semiconductor Grade | `1.0-3.0 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited, blanket W-CVD metal film (350-450 nm) over conformal Ti/TiN barrier liner, dry and stored under clean laminar airflow without water spots or ambient halogen exposure.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Planarized wafer surface with W plugs flush with ILD0 field oxide, chemically cleared of residual Ti/TiN, PVA-scrubbed, DI-water rinsed, particle-free (<20 particles @ >0.2 µm), and fully dried under pure N2.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes spontaneous atmospheric oxidation and formation of volatile or porous hydrated tungstic oxides (WO3·xH2O), galvanic pitting along the W-TiN boundary, and irreversible chemisorption of slurry nanoparticles that permanently induce dielectric breakdown and contact high-resistance opens.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Establishment of a robust Gen 2 W-CMP baseline planarization process for 180nm 8F² shared bitline contacts, achieving reproducible endpoint termination, sub-15 nm plug recess, minimal dielectric erosion, and electrical isolation without inter-contact bridging.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WCMP_Baseline_Planarization_Recipe_Summary.pdf`
- [ ] `Bitline_Contact_AFM_Dishing_Erosion_Data.csv`
- [ ] `Post_CMP_Array_Microscopy_and_Defect_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum W-plug recess in 8F² dense contact array** | `10.0 nm` | +/- 5.0 nm | Contact AFM cross-sectional step height extraction across 10 random array sites |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total field ILD0 dielectric oxide erosion after barrier over-polish** | `15.0 nm` | <= 20.0 nm | Spectroscopic reflectometry 5-point wafer map pre- and post-CMP |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Kelvin contact resistance per shared bitline W-plug** | `8.5 Ohm` | +/- 2.5 Ohm | Four-terminal Kelvin DC parameter probe measurement at 1.0 mA forced current |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 3 consecutive qualifying wafer runs demonstrating contact plug recess <= 15 nm, zero barrier residue bridging under electrical leakage testing (I_leak < 1.0 pA @ 1.8 V), mean plug contact resistance <= 11.0 Ohm, and formal sign-off on the baseline CMP recipe card.

testcases.title: W-Plug Dishing and ILD Field Oxide Erosion Metrology via Contact AFM
testcases.instrumentation: Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in tapping mode with high-aspect-ratio diamond-like carbon (DLC) tip (tip radius <10 nm) and calibrated 4-point probe / optical spectroscopic reflectometer.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has completed W-CVD plug fill (400 nm blanket W over 20 nm Ti/TiN liner on patterned ILD0) and post-CMP megasonic clean; wafer dried under pure N2 jet.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount wafer onto vibration-isolated AFM stage and locate the 8F² dense contact array test block (0.24 µm contact diameter, 0.48 µm pitch) and isolated 10 µm W test pad. 2. Perform a 5 µm x 5 µm high-resolution topographical scan across 10 consecutive bitline contacts. 3. Extract line profiles across the plug centers to measure W recess relative to adjacent ILD0 oxide surface. 4. Perform a 20 µm x 20 µm scan across the 10 µm isolated W pad to calculate maximum center-to-edge dishing. 5. Measure remaining field ILD0 oxide thickness at 5 points (center, top, bottom, left, right) using spectroscopic reflectometry.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: W-plug recess in dense 8F² array <= 15.0 nm; W dishing in isolated 10 µm test pad <= 25.0 nm; field ILD0 dielectric erosion across active array <= 20.0 nm; zero residual bulk W or TiN barrier bridging between contacts.

testcases.title: Post-CMP Inter-Bitline Electrical Isolation and Shared Contact Resistance Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Semi-automatic analytical probe station with sub-femtoamp sourcemeter (Keithley 4200-SCS or equivalent parameter analyzer).
testcases.pre_conditions: Post-CMP wafer with dedicated Kelvin contact resistance structures and comb-serpentine inter-contact isolation test keys.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load wafer into shielded probe station at 25°C. 2. Land micromanipulator probes onto adjacent isolated shared bitline contact pads (0.24 µm spacing). 3. Apply DC voltage sweep from -1.8 V to +1.8 V and measure leakage current between adjacent contact plugs. 4. Switch to 4-terminal Kelvin test structure for individual 0.24 µm W-plug contact resistance; force 1.0 mA DC current and measure differential voltage drop.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Inter-contact leakage current < 1.0 pA at 1.8 V DC bias (isolation resistance > 1.8 TOhm); individual 180nm shared bitline W-plug contact resistance <= 12.0 Ohm/plug across 95% of measured sites.

ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles with full-face polycarbonate shield
Acid- and oxidizer-resistant neoprene cleanroom apron and chemical sleeve covers

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Skin exposure: Flush affected area immediately with copious flowing water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated apparel; apply soothing cold compress. Eye contact: Irrigate eye continuously at eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate emergency ophthalmological evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh ambient air; administer oxygen if respiration is labored; seek immediate medical assessment.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous wet bench and polishing head local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) with acid-mist and oxidizer wet scrubber integration.

Neutralize oxidizer-laden slurry by slow titration with dilute sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) to quench residual peroxides, adjust effluent pH to 6.5-8.5 using 10% sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or calcium hydroxide, settle abrasive solids via coagulation/filtration, and verify total dissolved solids (TDS) and heavy metal limits prior to industrial drain release.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly deposited, blanket W-CVD metal film (350-450 nm) over conformal Ti/TiN barrier liner, dry and stored under clean laminar airflow without water spots or ambient halogen exposure.
