# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Cross-Sectional TEM/SEM Metrology & Plug Contact Resistance Defect Extraction
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Technology Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (8F² COB Topology) | **Module:** Metrology & Defect Extraction

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Inspection Lifecycle

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Dual-Beam FIB Sample  │
│          Prep          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    High-Resolution     │
│      In-Lens SEM       │
│       Screening        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  STEM/TEM Seam & Void  │
│    Defect Metrology    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Kelvin Nanoprobe Rc   │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Statistical Process   │
│     Window Defect      │
│       Pass/Fail        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Dual-Beam Focused Ion Beam (FIB) Site-Specific Lamella Preparation**:
   - Align the DRAM die to the active 8F² memory array across the cell contact via pattern (access transistor length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Deposit a protective $1.5\ \mu\text{m}$ Pt cap layer via in-situ electron-beam/ion-beam deposition over the crown-over-bitline (COB) storage node contact and tungsten plug (W-plug).
   - Perform bulk rough milling using $\text{Ga}^+$ ions at $30\text{ kV}$, followed by progressive low-kV polishing ($5\text{ kV}\rightarrow 2\text{ kV}$) to produce a damage-free cross-sectional lamella thin-foil ($< 50\text{ nm}$ thick) perpendicular to the bitline and wordline pitch ($360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$).

2. **Cross-Sectional In-Lens SEM Morphological Inspection**:
   - Transfer wafer coupons or lamellae into a high-resolution Field Emission SEM (FE-SEM) chamber at working vacuum $< 1\times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$.
   - Inspect the post-CMP planarization contact profile and the interface between the landing metal-1 (M1) aluminum interconnect layer (nominal $350\text{ nm}$) and the W-plug.
   - Screen for keyhole seams, gross tungsten pull-out, oxide erosion, or interface delamination across $\ge 20$ adjacent cell contacts.

3. **High-Resolution Bright-Field / High-Angle Annular Dark-Field (HAADF) STEM/TEM Metrology**:
   - Insert the lamella into an analytical (S)TEM operating at $200\text{ kV}$.
   - Image the full vertical aspect ratio of the W-plug connecting the access transistor active drain/source silicon area through the pre-metal dielectric stack to the storage node contact.
   - Quantify core seam morphology, void volume fraction, and barrier liner integrity (Ti/TiN) at the bottom contact curvature and sidewalls.

4. **In-Chamber Electrical Nanoprobe & Kelvin Contact Resistance ($R_c$) Extraction**:
   - Perform four-terminal Kelvin test structure probing on dedicated in-die W-plug chain arrays before and after forming gas anneal ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ 95/5$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$).
   - Sweep current ($I_{\text{force}} = -100\ \mu\text{A}$ to $+100\ \mu\text{A}$) and measure voltage drop ($V_{\text{sense}}$) to extract specific contact resistance ($R_c$) per single contact plug.
   - Cross-correlate measured resistance outliers directly with TEM void diameters to generate defect-impedance sensitivity curves.

5. **Defect Disposition & Process Window Validation**:
   - Classify contact plugs into clean, high-resistance seam defect, or open-contact categories.
   - Trigger upstream CVD $\text{WF}_6\text{--SiH}_4/\text{H}_2$ process adjustment if void prevalence or contact resistance exceeds statistical process control (SPC) limits.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                     Metrology Target Window Index      
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 Anneal Temp  ┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒     │
M1 Al Thick   ┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒     │
              │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
Line Pitch Max┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
              │██                                      │
M1 Sheet Res  ┤██                                      │
              └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
               0       100       200      300       400 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target & Tolerance | Physical Unit | Verification Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Metal-1 Contact Landing Thickness** | $350 \pm 5\%$ ($332.5$ to $367.5$) | $\text{nm}$ | Cross-Sectional FE-SEM / Calibrated In-Lens TEM |
| **W-Plug Contact Array Pitch Window** | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Automated STEM Dimensional CD Metrology |
| **Post-Anneal Interconnect Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ (Post $400^\circ\text{C}$, $30\text{ min}$ forming gas anneal) | $\Omega/\text{sq}$ | 4-Point Probe / Kelvin Nanoprobe System |
| **Access Transistor Physical Gate Oxide Thickness** | $3.5 \pm 0.2$ | $\text{nm}$ | High-Resolution Phase-Contrast TEM (HR-TEM) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Cell footprint based on $8\text{F}^2$ and $6\text{F}^2$ folded bitline layout with access transistor dimensions $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node contact via tungsten plug (W-plug) connecting the active drain to the crown capacitor.
  - Retention budget targets minimum storage capacitance of $28\text{ fF/cell}$ with leakage below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Bitline and wordline pitch constrained between $360\text{ nm}$ and $400\text{ nm}$.
  - Thermally grown silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) gate dielectric physical thickness calibrated to $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage capacitor capacitance retention budget requirement of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$.

- **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**:
  - Landing interconnect metal-1 layer thickness calibrated at $350\text{ nm} \pm 5\%$.
  - Post-metal forming gas anneal carried out at $400^\circ\text{C}$ in $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\ (95/5)$ for $30\text{ minutes}$.
  - Sheet resistance specification verified at $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\text{sq}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Purchasing turnkey external cross-sectional TEM/SEM and electrical TLM extraction services introduces measurement latency and potential sample alteration. FIB lamella preparation (Ga+ ion damage, amorphization, and curtaining) can artificially enlarge seam voids or delaminate the Ti/TiN barrier from the contact bottom, confounding true CVD tungsten step-coverage and CMP recess artifacts with sample prep defects. Correlation between physical void volume in high-aspect-ratio (AR ~4:1) contacts and measured Rc must be mathematically established rather than inferred from isolated cross-sections.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: The 180nm 8F² DRAM storage node contact requires specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm² and contact resistance Rc < 10 Ohm per contact. In a Buy-model metrology package, transmission line measurement (TLM) pad pitch (d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um) must be coupled with high-resolution bright-field TEM to inspect the TiSi2 salicide interface and TiN glue layer integrity. Volcanic WF6 penetration through pinholes in the CVD/PVD TiN liner causes sub-surface wormholes and contact lifting, directly spiking the Y-intercept on TLM regression plots.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Outsourced analytical laboratory turnaround time (TAT) poses a major risk to lot progression; standard 5-to-10 day queue times for dual-beam FIB-TEM and precision probe-card TLM will stall CMP and W-plug CVD tool qualification. Commercial service level agreements (SLAs) must specify an emergency 24-hour expedited window for FIB-SEM lamella lift-out and high-vacuum electrical testing, ensuring standard pricing per lamella and standardized coupon return under hermetic dry-N2 shipping seals.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Clear boundaries must separate the metrology vendor's scope from foundry process ownership. Acceptance payment milestones cannot be tied merely to delivering TEM micrographs; they must be contingent upon delivery of raw, calibrated STEM HAADF/BF digital images (minimum 0.15 nm/pixel resolution) and raw I-V parametric TLM sweeps with confirmed R² >= 0.998 for linear regression fit, eliminating vendor interpretation bias.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Ga+ ion beam amorphization or re-deposition during dual-beam FIB milling masking the Ti/TiN barrier thickness or artificially inducing void closure in the tungsten plug core.
1. Native oxide regrowth and ambient moisture uptake at cleaved wafer scribe lines prior to probe landing, skewing TLM transfer length (L_T) and yielding false-positive high contact resistivity (> 1.0e-5 Ohm*cm²).
1. WF6 encroachment/volcano defects etching underlying Si/TiSi2 junction, inducing micro-voiding beneath the barrier and catastrophic leakage or contact opening under storage node bias.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-2-2-3-01` | **Cross-Sectional STEM-EDS Interface Inspection and W-Plug Seam Void Quantification** | Dual-beam focused ion beam (FIB) with in-situ Omniprobe lift-out; 200 kV Field Emission Transmission Electron Microscope (FE-TEM / STEM) equipped with High-Angle Annular Dark-Field (HAADF) and Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS). | 1. Extract cross-sectional lamella across a minimum of 5 contiguous 180nm storage node contacts using 30 kV Ga+ FIB, followed by low-voltage (2 kV to 500 V) Ar+ or Ga+ polish to reduce surface amorphization below 1.5 nm. 2. Transfer specimen to 200 kV STEM under high vacuum (< 5e-7 Torr). 3. Acquire atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM and BF-STEM images along the [110] zone axis capturing the plug top, sidewall, seam, and bottom contact interface. 4. Measure Ti/TiN barrier thickness at the bottom (target >= 10 nm) and sidewall (target >= 5 nm), and determine central seam void width and vertical extent. 5. Perform EDS line profiles across the TiSi2/Si substrate interface to check for fluorine (F) accumulation and TiSi2 phase continuity. | `Pass if: Ti/TiN barrier bottom coverage >= 10.0 nm with zero discontinuous pinholes; central seam void width <= 15.0 nm with void area <= 5.0% of total plug cross-sectional area; fluorine atomic concentration at TiSi2 interface < 1.0 at.%; and zero TiSi2 delamination detected across all 5 sample plugs.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-2-2-3-02` | **TLM Specific Contact Resistivity and Sheet Resistance Extraction** | Automated analytical probe station with semi-shielded low-noise chamber (< 10 fA noise floor) and Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer (4-point Kelvin probe configuration). | 1. Verify probe tip alignment and planar contact resistance on gold reference calibration substrate (Rc_probe < 0.2 Ohm). 2. Land 4-point Kelvin probes onto adjacent TLM pads for each gap d in sequence: 5 um, 10 um, 20 um, 40 um, 80 um. 3. Execute bipolar DC current sweeps from -10 mA to +10 mA while recording differential voltage V to confirm strict Ohmic linearity (R² >= 0.999). 4. Plot measured total resistance R_T versus pad gap distance d. 5. Extract slope (R_s / W) to calculate diffusion sheet resistance R_s, Y-intercept (2 * R_c) to calculate contact resistance R_c, and X-intercept (-2 * L_T) to obtain transfer length L_T. 6. Compute specific contact resistivity rho_c = R_c * W * L_T. | `Pass if: Contact resistance R_c < 10.0 Ohm per contact; Specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm²; and linear regression coefficient of determination R² >= 0.998 across all 5 gap measurements.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, EN 374 compliant), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles with side shields, Flame-resistant and static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat, ESD safe conductive safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF contact: Immediately flush skin with copious amounts of water for 5 minutes; apply 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel continuously to affected area and seek emergency medical treatment. For eye exposure, irrigate with sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye wash or isotonic saline for 15 minutes. For Gallium/metal puncture: Wash wound with mild soap and running water, debride under medical supervision.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: FIB-TEM sample preparation wet bench must maintain dedicated laminar exhaust hood face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 fpm) vented to an acid/corrosive scrubber. Microscope column backing pumps and prep-chamber venting ports must be plumbed to dry toxic gas exhaust lines.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent coupon-cleaving acid solutions containing trace HF must be neutralized with 10% calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) or sodium bicarbonate slurry to precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2) solid cake; liquid effluent must verify pH 6.5-8.5 prior to industrial hazardous waste collection. Gallium-contaminated FIB grids must be segregated into solid heavy-metal hazardous waste containers.

| **Hydrofluoric Acid (for pre-TEM coupon oxide etch)** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C12) | `0.5% v/v` |
| **Isopropanol (wafer coupon cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C1) | `99.9%` |
| **Forming Gas (Sintering: 95% N2, 5% H2)** | `1333-74-0` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 5.0) | `5.0% H2 in N2` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-CMP cleared and de-ionized water megasonic rinsed tungsten plug array; top surface coplanar with surrounding TEOS/BPSG dielectric without slurry residue or organic corrosion inhibitors.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Argon-sputtered or forming-gas annealed contact test structure sealed under continuous dry nitrogen (< 5 ppm H2O, < 2 ppm O2) or ultra-high vacuum (< 1e-6 Torr) specimen holder.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide (WOx / SiOx) re-growth and atmospheric fluoride/moisture hydration leading to dielectric-plug junction degradation, pseudo-capacitive TLM hysteresis, and false reporting of specific contact resistivity exceeding 1.0e-5 Ohm*cm².

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Delivery of comprehensive analytical cross-sectional TEM/SEM structural metrics and electrical TLM extraction data confirming 180nm DRAM storage node W-plug fill conformity, barrier integrity, and ohmic contact performance compliant with <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm² specific contact resistivity.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_PLUG_TEM_HAADF_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `STORAGE_NODE_TLM_ELECTRICAL_EXTRACTION.csv`
- [ ] `STEM_EDS_INTERFACE_MAPS_HIGHRES.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Specific Contact Resistivity (rho_c) extracted from linear regression of TLM pad array** | `1.0e-6 Ohm*cm^2` | <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm^2 (Upper Specification Limit) | Keysight B1500A 4-point Kelvin DC resistance sweep across 5 TLM pad spacings (5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um) with linear regression analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Storage Node Tungsten Contact Resistance (Rc) per plug** | `6.5 Ohm` | < 10.0 Ohm | Extracted Y-intercept from TLM regression and cross-checked against Kelvin single-contact resistor structures |
| `ASSERT-03` | **CVD W-Plug Seam Void Maximum Width in 180nm contact core** | `0.0 nm` | <= 15.0 nm maximum width, <= 5.0% total contact area | 200 kV Field Emission STEM HAADF high-resolution calibrated cross-sectional digital line measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires: 1) Delivered TEM images proving conformal Ti/TiN barrier thickness >= 10 nm at the contact bottom and seam void width <= 15 nm across all sampled plugs; 2) Parametric TLM test data validating specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm² and per-contact Rc < 10.0 Ohm with R² >= 0.998; 3) Full EHS and chain-of-custody compliance records confirming sample integrity within the specified 30-minute air queue-time window.

expected_result.summary: Delivery of comprehensive analytical cross-sectional TEM/SEM structural metrics and electrical TLM extraction data confirming 180nm DRAM storage node W-plug fill conformity, barrier integrity, and ohmic contact performance compliant with <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm² specific contact resistivity.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Specific Contact Resistivity (rho_c) extracted from linear regression of TLM pad array
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Keysight B1500A 4-point Kelvin DC resistance sweep across 5 TLM pad spacings (5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um) with linear regression analysis

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Storage Node Tungsten Contact Resistance (Rc) per plug
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Extracted Y-intercept from TLM regression and cross-checked against Kelvin single-contact resistor structures

quantitative_assertions.assertion: CVD W-Plug Seam Void Maximum Width in 180nm contact core
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: <= 15.0 nm maximum width, <= 5.0% total contact area
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: 200 kV Field Emission STEM HAADF high-resolution calibrated cross-sectional digital line measurement

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Formal signoff requires: 1) Delivered TEM images proving conformal Ti/TiN barrier thickness >= 10 nm at the contact bottom and seam void width <= 15 nm across all sampled plugs; 2) Parametric TLM test data validating specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm² and per-contact Rc < 10.0 Ohm with R² >= 0.998; 3) Full EHS and chain-of-custody compliance records confirming sample integrity within the specified 30-minute air queue-time window.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-W-CMP-180NM-001`
**Module:** Metrology & Planarization  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling > COB Storage Node Contact & W-Plug Contact Resistance TCAD Modeling > W-Plug WF6 Reduction & CMP Planarization Contact Module Simulation > Tungsten CMP Overburden Removal & Dishing Metrology Profile Simulation  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / µm node)  
**Action Type:** Make / Characterization & Numerical Simulation  

---

### 1. Objective & Scope
Establish an industrial, step-by-step TCAD process and physical metrology simulation for **Tungsten Chemical Mechanical Planarization (W-CMP)** overburden removal and contact dishing/erosion profiling across the 180nm node Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) storage node contact and bitline contact plug matrix.

---

### 2. Physical & Structural Parameters

* **Technology Node Feature Size ($F$):** $180\text{ nm}$ ($0.18\text{ }\mu\text{m}$).
* **Cell Array Layout & Topology:** $8F^2$ folded bitline layout ($A_{\text{cell}} \approx 8 \times 0.18^2 = 0.2592\text{ }\mu\text{m}^2$).
* **Bitline & Wordline Pitch:** $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
* **Access Transistor Channel Geometry:** Gate Length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, Channel Width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
* **Contact Plug Dimensions:**
  * Contact Hole Diameter: nominal $180\text{ nm}$ ($F$).
  * Aspect Ratio: ~3:1 to 4:1 into BPSG / ILD matrix.
  * Shared bitline contact layout between adjacent cells; dedicated crown storage node contact plug.
* **Underlayer Barrier / Liner Stack:** Ti/TiN adhesion barrier liner ($10\text{ nm} / 15\text{ nm}$) prior to chemical vapor deposition ($WF_6$ reduction) of blanket Tungsten ($W$).
* **Target Post-CMP Remaining Dielectric Thickness:** Complete removal of overburden $W$ and Ti/TiN barrier on ILD with zero residual metal stringers across the $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ pitch matrix.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

```text
       [1. TCAD Domain Initialization]
                     │
                     ▼
      [2. Blanket W-Film Deposition Profile]
                     │
                     ▼
   [3. Primary W Bulk Overburden CMP Stage]
                     │
                     ▼
    [4. Ti/TiN Liner Soft-Landing & Over-polish]
                     │
                     ▼
  [5. Metrology Simulation & Profile Extraction]
                     │
                     ▼
      [6. Contact Quality Validation (TLM)]
```

#### Step 1: TCAD Domain Setup & Geometry Initialization
1. In the TCAD process simulator, define a 2D/3D periodic periodic array cell domain based on the $8F^2$ layout ($360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ pitch along wordline/bitline axes).
2. Configure underlying gate stack ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) with thermal gate $\text{SiO}_2$ dielectric ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$) and inter-layer dielectric (ILD / BPSG).
3. Etch contact vias ($180\text{ nm}$ diameter) down to source/drain diffusions.

#### Step 2: W-Plug CVD Profile & Overburden Generation
1. Perform conformal Ti/TiN barrier liner deposition simulation across the ILD surface and sidewalls.
2. Simulate blanket Tungsten CVD overburden ($WF_6$ reduction chemistry) with a nominal top-surface overburden thickness of $350\text{ nm} - 450\text{ nm}$ ensuring complete, seam-free fill of the $180\text{ nm}$ contact via.

#### Step 3: Primary Bulk Tungsten CMP Stage
1. Apply the Prestonian polishing removal rate equation:
   $$\text{MRR} = K_p \cdot P \cdot V$$
   * Set downforce pressure $P = 3.0\text{ psi} - 4.5\text{ psi}$ and relative velocity $V = 1.0\text{ m/s} - 1.2\text{ m/s}$.
2. Utilize an acidic silica/alumina-based slurry with oxidizer ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) calibrated to yield a bulk Tungsten removal rate of $250\text{ nm/min} - 350\text{ nm/min}$.
3. Run Stage 1 until optical/eddy-current endpoint detection signals complete bulk $W$ overburden clearance down to the Ti/TiN barrier interface.

#### Step 4: Ti/TiN Barrier Clearance & Over-Polish Stage
1. Switch polish parameters to a selective barrier slurry (low selectivity to oxide, controlled selectivity between $W$ and Ti/TiN).
2. Reduce downforce to $P = 1.5\text{ psi} - 2.0\text{ psi}$ to suppress mechanical shear stress on dense array plugs.
3. Apply a $15\% - 20\%$ over-polish budget to ensure zero metallic Tungsten or TiN bridging between adjacent bitlines/storage node plugs across the $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ pitch grid.

#### Step 5: High-Density Metrology Profile Extraction
1. Extract virtual AFM (Atomic Force Microscopy) and CD-SEM line scans across a 10-plug array track.
2. Measure:
   * **Plug Dishing ($\Delta h_{\text{dish}}$):** Depth difference between the surrounding ILD top plane and the center of the $180\text{ nm}$ W-plug.
   * **Oxide Erosion ($\Delta h_{\text{ero}}$):** Dielectric thickness loss in high-density contact array fields relative to open field areas.

#### Step 6: Electrical Continuity & Resistance Extraction
1. Couple the simulated post-CMP surface profile to the device resistance solver.
2. Formulate Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) verification structures (using $W = 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\text{ }\mu\text{m}$, gap spacing $d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) to confirm specific contact resistivity ($\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2$) meets integration baselines without plug recess degradation.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Metric | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Residual W Overburden & Bridging** | $0.0$ (complete removal across $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ pitch) | $\text{nm}$ | Virtual CD-SEM / Top-down profile inspection |
| **W-Plug Dishing ($\Delta h_{\text{dish}}$)** | $\le 15.0$ (for $180\text{ nm}$ nominal via diameter) | $\text{nm}$ | Virtual cross-sectional AFM extraction |
| **Array Oxide Erosion ($\Delta h_{\text{ero}}$)** | $\le 20.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | Differential profilometry profile |
| **Post-CMP Storage Cell Leakage** | $< 1.0$ (at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh retention) | $\text{fA/cell}$ | TCAD device leakage simulation |

---

### 5. Context Citations
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Bitline contact sharing, unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), W-plug erect drain contact structure, cell leakage budget ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
* **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:** $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ architecture, bitline and wordline pitch ($360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$), gate oxide thickness ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$).
* **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity:** Contact pad dimensions ($W = 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\text{ }\mu\text{m}$), gap spacings ($d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\text{ }\mu\text{m}$), and calculation formulation for specific contact resistivity ($\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: W-plug CMP planarization directly bounds the cell parasitic resistance and subsequent Crown capacitor bottom-electrode landing margin in the 8F² architecture. Failure to maintain uniform removal across dense cell array versus isolated peripheral test structures introduces localized topography step heights, degrading lithographic depth of focus (DoF) for the subsequent capacitor contact (SNC) mask.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node dimensions, slurry selectivity between tungsten (W) and the dielectric barrier (Ti/TiN, TEOS/ILD) must exceed 50:1 to mitigate excessive tungsten dishing (>30nm) and oxide erosion (>25nm). Slurry chemistry using ferric nitrate or hydrogen peroxide with silica abrasives must be tightly controlled to prevent micro-scratching and galvanic corrosion of the W-plug core (seam coring).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specialty W-CMP slurries containing stabilized acidic colloidal silica and hydrogen peroxide oxidizers face severe cold-chain storage and shelf-life degradation constraints in localized pilot foundry ecosystems. Pad conditioning diamond disks (e.g., 3M / Entegris) and post-CMP PVA brushes require qualified domestic second-sourcing to prevent unmitigated line stoppage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Planarization process qualification must converge within 4 wafer engineering runs without exceeding consumable slurry and conditioning pad budget allowances. TCAD dishing simulation calibrated to atomic force metrology must provide signoff-ready run-to-run parameter adjustments prior to pilot lot processing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Keyhole seam coring and localized galvanic erosion during post-CMP acidic clean resulting in high storage node contact series resistance or open cell defect.
1. Excessive ILD dielectric erosion and edge-over-erosion (EOE) across dense 8F² array boundaries leading to bitline-to-plug short circuits.
1. Residual tungsten stringers/slivers left on dielectric field oxide due to under-polishing, bridging adjacent wordline or bitline contacts.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-2-3-01` | **Atomic Force Profilometry W-Plug Dishing and ILD Oxide Erosion Quantification** | Park Systems NX20 Automated Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) with high-aspect-ratio diamond-like carbon (DLC) probe tip (tip radius < 10nm) | 1. Load wafer into AFM vacuum chuck and align to 8F² array dense memory cell macro coordinates. 2. Execute non-contact tapping mode scan over a 10 um x 10 um field containing 50 active W-plug contacts. 3. Extract cross-sectional step-height line profiles perpendicular to the plug grid across cell array and adjacent isolation oxide. 4. Calculate average peak-to-valley dishing depth across 20 consecutive plugs and array-to-field dielectric erosion step height. | `W-plug center dishing must be <= 15.0 nm; ILD field oxide erosion across the array boundary must be <= 20.0 nm; zero detected micro-scratches exceeding 5.0 nm depth.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-2-3-02` | **Cross-Sectional High-Resolution SEM Plug Recess and Interface Profile Verification** | Thermo Fisher Helios 5 DualBeam FIB-SEM equipped with in-situ Pt/C protective deposition gas injection system | 1. Locate target 180nm W-plug array using navigation electron beam at 5 kV. 2. Deposit 1.5 um sacrificial Pt protection strap over target 5 consecutive plugs. 3. Perform Ga+ focused ion beam trench milling at 30 kV, followed by 5 kV and 2 kV low-damage polishing cuts. 4. Image plug-to-dielectric interface at 200,000x magnification at 2 kV immersion mode. 5. Measure recess depth from ILD surface plane and evaluate Ti/TiN barrier liner integrity. | `Mean vertical plug recess must be between 5.0 nm and 18.0 nm; barrier liner thickness retention >= 8.0 nm; zero evidence of void coring along center seam (> 10 nm).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level C Chemical Protective Nitrile Over-Gloves (EN 374 compliant, min 15 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face splash shield combined with chemical safety goggles, Chemical-resistant neoprene lab apron and sleeves, Cleanroom-grade static dissipative safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with tepid water for 20 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Skin contact: Drench with emergency safety shower, remove contaminated cleanroom attire, and flush skin with water for 15 minutes. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly; do NOT induce vomiting; immediately contact emergency poison medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: CMP platen enclosures and chemical delivery modules must maintain continuous dedicated acid-exhaust ventilation with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) and negative differential pressure >= 25 Pa relative to cleanroom ambient, ducting directly to an operational wet acid scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: W-CMP slurry effluent containing abrasive silica and oxidizers must drain to dedicated heavy-metal and chemical-mechanical-planarization waste collection pipes. Waste is chemically coagulated with calcium chloride / polyaluminum chloride, pH neutralized between 6.5 and 8.5 with 10% sodium hydroxide, filtered for metal/slurry sludge removal, and verified via ICP-OES before discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI-C12) | `30 wt% in aqueous oxidizer concentrate` |
| **Ferric Nitrate Nonahydrate** | `7782-61-8` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `2 to 5 wt% in slurry catalyst` |
| **Colloidal Silica (Silicon Dioxide)** | `7631-86-9` | Ultra-High Purity CMP Abrasive | `5 to 15 wt% suspension` |
| **Citric Acid (Post-CMP Chelating Agent)** | `77-92-9` | Reagent Grade ACS | `1 to 2 wt% aqueous clean solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-deposited CVD tungsten blanket overburden (~400 nm) over Ti/TiN barrier liner, surface passivated under vacuum without visible peeling, delamination, or particle clusters.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Planarized tungsten contact plugs embedded in TEOS ILD; free of slurry abrasives and metallic residues (< 1E10 atoms/cm² metal contamination); passivated hydrophilic oxide surface.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended exposure to ambient cleanroom air promotes rapid galvanic corrosion at the W-to-TiN boundary, spontaneous formation of non-stoichiometric WO3 native oxides (> 4 nm) leading to unrecoverable contact resistance increases, and atmospheric airborne organic/boron contamination.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified TCAD mechanical dishing and erosion profile simulation calibrated against empirical AFM and FIB-SEM metrology runs, demonstrating sub-20nm planarity and complete tungsten overburden clearing across the 180nm 8F² DRAM cell array.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `w_cmp_dishing_erosion_afm_profile.csv`
- [ ] `w_plug_planarization_metrology_report.pdf`
- [ ] `fib_sem_cross_section_plug_recess.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum center-to-edge dishing depth across dense 180nm W-plug contact array** | `12.0 nm` | +/- 3.0 nm | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) 10um line scan profile analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Array boundary ILD TEOS oxide erosion step height** | `15.0 nm` | +/- 5.0 nm | High-resolution cross-sectional FIB-SEM calibrated step height metrology |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-clean residual tungsten particle density on field oxide (> 0.2 um)** | `0.05 particles/cm²` | <= 0.08 particles/cm² | Automated darkfield laser surface particle scanner inspection |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full statistical convergence over 3 test wafer sites confirming mean W-plug dishing <= 15nm, zero detectable W-stringer bridging shorts under electrical four-point probe contact resistance testing, and signoff endorsement from Metrology and Process Integration leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-WCMP-002`
**Title:** W-CMP Slurry Formulation & Prestonian Polish Rate Calibration  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Crown-Type COB 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling > COB Storage Node Contact & W-Plug Contact Resistance TCAD Modeling > W-Plug $\text{WF}_6$ Reduction & CMP Planarization Contact Module Simulation > Tungsten CMP Overburden Removal & Dishing Metrology Profile Simulation > W-CMP Slurry Formulation & Prestonian Polish Rate Calibration  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / $\mu\text{m}$)  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objectives
This SOP outlines the formulation and empirical Prestonian polish rate calibration of colloidal silica/alumina acidic slurry with $\text{Fe(NO}_3\text{)}_3 / \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ oxidizer systems for tungsten (W) plug planarization. The procedure establishes the Prestonian removal rate constant ($K_p$) governing the Preston equation:
$$\text{MRR} = K_p \cdot P \cdot V$$
where $P$ is downforce pressure and $V$ is platen relative linear velocity, ensuring controlled tungsten overburden removal down to the underlying dielectric ILD with minimal plug recess and dishing for 180nm 1T1C $8F^2$ Crown-COB contact structures.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                            W-CMP CALIBRATION FLOW                                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Slurry Formulation: Acidic colloidal silica + Oxidizer (pH 2.0 - 2.5)          |
|                                       │                                           |
|                                       ▼                                           |
| 2. Point-of-Use (POU) Delivery & Pad Conditioning (Grid-abrade diamond disk)       |
|                                       │                                           |
|                                       ▼                                           |
| 3. Multi-Point Preston Matrix Polish (Sweeping Downforce P & Platen Speed V)      |
|                                       │                                           |
|                                       ▼                                           |
| 4. Post-CMP Megasonic Clean & Metrology (Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / 4PP Sheet R) |
|                                       │                                           |
|                                       ▼                                           |
| 5. Preston Constant (Kp) & Selectivity Extraction (W-to-Oxide Rate Ratio)         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 2.1: Slurry Formulation & Point-of-Use (POU) Preparation
1. **Slurry Base Blending**: Blend high-purity deionized (DI) water with high-purity colloidal abrasive particles (mean primary particle diameter $50\text{--}70\text{ nm}$, abrasive solids loading $3.0\text{--}5.0\text{ wt}\%$) in a fluoropolymer-lined batch tank.
2. **Oxidizer & Acid Addition**: Add periodic/ferric nitrate catalyst $\text{Fe(NO}_3\text{)}_3$ ($0.05\text{--}0.15\text{ wt}\%$) and stabilize with malonic acid / nitric acid to buffer the formulation to an acidic regime of $\text{pH } 2.2 \pm 0.2$.
3. **POU Activation**: Meter hydrogen peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, $30\%$ semiconductor grade) via an in-line chemical delivery loop immediately prior to pad dispense at a volumetric ratio yielding $1.5\text{--}2.5\text{ wt}\% \text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$ in active slurry. Ensure continuous agitation to prevent abrasive agglomeration.

#### Step 2.2: Pad Conditioning & In-Situ Conditioning Setup
1. Mount a stacked polyurethane polishing pad (e.g., IC1000/Suba-IV concentric grooved pad) onto Platen 1.
2. Execute a 20-minute ex-situ break-in using a diamond conditioner disk ($100\text{ grit}$) at $40\text{ N}$ downforce and $95\text{ RPM}$ disk rotation under $250\text{ mL/min}$ DI water flush.
3. Configure in-situ diamond conditioning during all polishing sweeps at $25\text{ N}$ downforce, sweeping continuously across pad radius at $10\text{ sweeps/min}$ to maintain steady-state surface pad roughness ($R_a \approx 3.5\text{--}5.0\ \mu\text{m}$).

#### Step 2.3: Preston Matrix Execution on Blanket Monitor Wafers
1. Prepare prime $200\text{ mm}$ test monitor wafers:
   - Group A: Blanket CVD Tungsten ($500\text{ nm}$ W over $20\text{ nm}$ Ti/TiN adhesion liner on thermal $\text{SiO}_2$).
   - Group B: Blanket TEOS / High-Density Plasma (HDP) $\text{SiO}_2$ ($500\text{ nm}$).
2. Set slurry flow rate to $180 \pm 10\text{ mL/min}$ targeted at the pad center-wafer interface.
3. Execute sequential 60-second polish runs across a calibrated $P \cdot V$ matrix:
   - Condition 1: Downforce $P_1 = 2.0\text{ psi}$ ($13.8\text{ kPa}$), Platen/Carrier speed $\omega = 40/38\text{ RPM}$ ($V_{\text{avg}} \approx 0.65\text{ m/s}$).
   - Condition 2: Downforce $P_2 = 3.5\text{ psi}$ ($24.1\text{ kPa}$), Platen/Carrier speed $\omega = 70/67\text{ RPM}$ ($V_{\text{avg}} \approx 1.15\text{ m/s}$).
   - Condition 3: Downforce $P_3 = 5.0\text{ psi}$ ($34.5\text{ kPa}$), Platen/Carrier speed $\omega = 100/96\text{ RPM}$ ($V_{\text{avg}} \approx 1.65\text{ m/s}$).
4. Record motor current / friction torque profile for platen and carrier to monitor shear load linearity.

#### Step 2.4: Post-CMP Wet Clean & Surface Quench
1. Transfer wafer immediately into double-sided PVA brush scrubber with $0.5\text{ wt}\% \text{ NH}_4\text{OH}$ / dilute organic acid solution to arrest micro-etching and lift colloidal abrasive residues.
2. Megasonic rinse at $1.0\text{ MHz}$ under ultra-pure DI water for $45\text{ s}$ followed by surface-tension-gradient (Marangoni) isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor dry.

#### Step 2.5: Metrology & Prestonian Rate Calibration Extraction
1. Measure pre- and post-CMP W film thickness across 49-point diameter scans using a 4-Point Probe (4PP) resistivity mapping tool:
   $$T_W = \frac{\rho_{\text{eff}}}{R_{\text{sheet}}}$$
2. Measure pre- and post-CMP $\text{SiO}_2$ thickness across identical coordinates via Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (SE).
3. Compute Material Removal Rate ($\text{MRR}_W$ and $\text{MRR}_{\text{Oxide}}$) in $\text{\AA/min}$ or $\text{nm/min}$.
4. Plot $\text{MRR}_W$ versus $P \cdot V$ product ($\text{kPa} \cdot \text{m/s}$). Extract slope $K_p$ by linear regression and verify Prestonian linearity ($R^2 \ge 0.99$).
5. Compute slurry selectivity ratio:
   $$S_{W/\text{Ox}} = \frac{\text{MRR}_W}{\text{MRR}_{\text{Oxide}}}$$

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Tolerance / Spec Limit | Measurement Method / Tooling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Active Slurry pH** | $2.20$ | $\pm 0.15$ (Range: $2.05\text{--}2.35$) | Calibrated inline/benchtop automated pH electrode |
| **Tungsten Polish Rate ($\text{MRR}_W$)** | $280\text{ nm/min}$ (at $P=3.5\text{ psi}$, $V=1.15\text{ m/s}$) | $\pm 20\text{ nm/min}$ ($\pm 7.1\%$) | 4-Point Probe (4PP) 49-point sheet resistance map |
| **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU)** | $3.5\%$ ($1\sigma$) | $\le 5.0\%$ | $[(\sigma_{\text{MRR}} / \text{MRR}_{\text{mean}}) \times 100\%]$ (3mm edge exclusion) |
| **Selectivity ($W : \text{SiO}_2$)** | $45 : 1$ | $\ge 35 : 1$ | 4PP (W loss) vs. Spectroscopic Ellipsometry ($\text{SiO}_2$ loss) |
| **Prestonian Linearity ($R^2$)** | $0.995$ | $\ge 0.990$ across $[P \cdot V]$ test space | Linear regression fit ($K_p$ calibration curve) |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations
1. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Defines the structural baseline of the $180\text{ nm}$ node incorporating $8F^2$ stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture, tungsten plug (W-plug) interconnects, and strict leakage constraints ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$), requiring sub-nanometer planarization to prevent bridging and parasitic contact resistance degradation.
2. **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: Establishes $180\text{ nm}$ cell geometry, critical bitline/wordline pitch ($360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$), and gate dielectric baseline, dictating strict oxide erosion and dishing budgets during contact module plug clearing.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: W-CMP slurry polish rate must couple Prestonian mechanical parameters (downforce pressure 2.5-4.5 psi, platen speed 60-90 RPM) with electrochemical oxide formation kinetics to guarantee uniform Tungsten overburden removal across high-density 180nm 8F² DRAM cell array vs. peripheral logic regions, avoiding downstream step-height offsets prior to crown capacitor dielectric deposition.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Formulation requires strict control of oxidizer concentration (H2O2 2.0-4.0 wt% or ferric nitrate Fe(NO3)3) stabilized by malonic or citric acid complexes at pH 2.0-2.5; silica or alumina abrasive loading must remain below 5.0 wt% with mean particle diameter <70 nm to eliminate severe micro-scratching, plug pull-out, and W recess exceeding 15 nm in high-aspect-ratio (AR > 4:1) storage node contacts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Colloidal silica slurries with chelating and corrosion-inhibiting additives (e.g., benzotriazole/BTA derivatives) must be sourced at semiconductor electronic grade with tight batch-to-batch shelf-life specs (<6 months before aggregation); peroxide oxidizers require local point-of-use (POU) chemical blending systems to circumvent transportation degradation and uncontrolled exotherms.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration DOE for Prestonian polish rate and selectivity (W:TiN:TEOS target > 50:1:1) must converge within 12 wafer-run cycles to preserve schedule baseline for Gen 2 (µm/sub-µm) pilot line validation, mitigating abrasive slurry waste disposal compliance bottlenecks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry agglomeration causing catastrophic micro-scratching and mechanical gouging across 180nm W-plug arrays
1. Galvanic corrosion between TiN barrier and bulk W under acidic oxidizer over-exposure leading to keyhole contact voids
1. Prestonian non-linearity at low downforce resulting in incomplete peripheral bulk tungsten clearing and inter-node bridging

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B/C Cleanroom Chemical Splash Suit (Tyvek/Saranex), Heavyweight Nitrile/Neoprene double gloves with extended gauntlets, Full-face shield with ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical safety goggles, Acid-gas/organic-vapor dual-cartridge air-purifying half-mask respirator
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact: Immediately drench affected area with deluge emergency shower for minimum 15 minutes, remove contaminated clothing; for eye contact: irrigate eyes with isotonic saline or copious UPW for 20 minutes holding eyelids open, seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation; for inhalation: relocate to fresh laminar airflow, administer 100% humidified oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated acid-exhaust ducting on CMP platen enclosures maintaining negative static pressure >= 0.75 in-WG and face velocity >= 100 FPM; point-of-use H2O2 degassing vent with continuous oxidizer vapor monitoring.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate spent acidic slurry waste from standard fluoride and heavy organic streams; route effluent to dedicated heavy metal precipitation/flocculation neutralization tank, adjust pH to 7.5-8.5 using 10% NaOH/Ca(OH)2 slurry to precipitate dissolved tungsten species, filter suspended SiO2/abrasive solids prior to final POTW biological discharge.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-deposited WF6-reduced bulk CVD Tungsten film (400-500 nm) over Ti/TiN adhesion liner, free of dendritic nodules, moisture, or organic fluorocarbon residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Planarized, fully cleared TEOS field with exposed W-plugs, passivated hydrophilic native oxide (<1.5 nm WO3), scrubbed free of colloidal silica abrasives (residual particle count < 20 at >0.15 um).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Galvanic corrosion pitting at W/TiN seam interfaces induced by atmospheric moisture and trace oxidizer residues, causing accelerated plug voiding and contact resistance spikes exceeding 100 Ohms/contact.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-180NM-W-CMP-002`
## Title: Two-Step Bulk W Removal & TiN Barrier Polish Recipe Simulation
**Parent Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Crown-Type COB 3D Stack > COB Storage Node Contact & W-Plug Contact Resistance TCAD Modeling > W-Plug $\text{WF}_6$ Reduction & CMP Planarization Contact Module Simulation > Tungsten CMP Overburden Removal & Dishing Metrology Profile Simulation  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Simulation Setup

In the 180nm 1T1C COB DRAM flow, the tungsten contact plug connects the active device drain/source nodes to the crown storage capacitor and bitlines across tight cell pitch geometries ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, pitch $\approx 360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$). To form isolated, coplanar W-plugs without keyhole voiding, shorting, or excessive recess/dishing, CMP planarization utilizes a calibrated two-step polish model:
- **Platen 1 (P1 - Bulk Tungsten Polish):** High-removal-rate acidic slurry with selective oxidizer targeting bulk overburden clearance down to the TiN adhesion/barrier layer.
- **Platen 2 (P2 - Barrier & Soft Touch Polish):** Selective slurry targeting the TiN barrier layer and initial ILD/oxide touch, engineered to stop uniformly on the interlayer dielectric with minimal plug recess.

```
       [Bulk W Overburden (~400 nm)]
─────────────────────────────────────────────
 ─── TiN Adhesion/Barrier Layer (~20 nm) ───
=============================================
   ILD Oxide      | W-Plug |      ILD Oxide
 (Pitch: 360-400nm)| L=180nm| (Pitch: 360-400nm)
                  | W=220nm|
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Simulation Procedure

1. **Geometry & Substrate Profile Initialization:**
   - Import post-CVD W-fill topography into the surface kinematics TCAD engine.
   - Define cell geometry parameters: transistor gate length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, active width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, and cell array contact pitch across $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Initialize the layered thin-film stack: ILD oxide, conforming Ti/TiN barrier liner, and bulk tungsten overburden.

2. **Step 1: Bulk W Overburden Polish (P1 Model):**
   - Apply Prestonian removal kinematics: $\text{MRR} = K_p \cdot P \cdot V$, where downforce pressure is parameterized at $4.0 - 5.0\text{ psi}$ and platen/carrier rotational speeds set at $80 - 110\text{ rpm}$.
   - Select acidic silica slurry with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 / \text{Fe}(\text{NO}_3)_3$ oxidizer system calibrated for high tungsten etch rate ($> 3000\text{ \AA/min}$) and high selectivity to TiN ($\text{Sel}_{\text{W:TiN}} > 20:1$).
   - Run simulation until optical/motor eddy-current endpoint detection registers breakthrough to the TiN barrier layer.

3. **Step 2: TiN Barrier Clearance & Dielectric Touchdown (P2 Model):**
   - Transition kinematics to lower mechanical downforce ($1.5 - 2.5\text{ psi}$) and platen speed ($60 - 75\text{ rpm}$) to mitigate contact plug micro-scratching.
   - Switch slurry model to high-selectivity barrier polish chemistry ($\text{Sel}_{\text{TiN:W}} \ge 1:1$, $\text{Sel}_{\text{TiN:SiO}_2} \approx 3:1 - 5:1$).
   - Execute fixed-time polish simulation with controlled $15\% - 20\%$ overpolish to completely clear residual TiN stringers across dense array fields without punching through the ILD dielectric.

4. **Step 3: Topography & Dishing/Erosion Metrology Extraction:**
   - Extract cross-sectional profiles across the dense 8F² contact array.
   - Measure center-to-edge plug recess, contact plug dishing, array field oxide erosion, and perimeter topography.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transistor Contact Target Dimension** | $L = 180 \pm 10$, $W = 220 \pm 15$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-line CD-SEM / TCAD Mesh Extraction |
| **Contact Array Pitch Boundary** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Automated Metrology Profile Analysis |
| **Array Oxide Loss / Field Erosion** | $\le 15.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | Ellipsometric / AFM Simulation Profiler |
| **W-Plug Center Recess / Dishing** | $\le 20.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | High-Resolution AFM Profile Simulation |

---

### 4. Verified Source Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - *Unit Cell Geometry:* Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - *Capacitor Architecture:* Stacked Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) crown-shaped structure erected above the drain contact via tungsten plug (W-plug).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - *Cell Array Constraints:* 1T1C architecture with an $8\text{F}^2$ or $6\text{F}^2$ cell layout; bitline and wordline pitch is approximately $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The two-step Tungsten (W) CMP module must reliably decouple bulk tungsten overburden removal (Platen 1) from barrier TiN/adhesion layer clearing (Platen 2) to maintain across-wafer thickness variation below 4 nm across the 8F² DRAM cell array without inducing micro-scratches or parasitic dielectric erosion into the underlying pre-metal dielectric (BPSG/TEOS). In simulation space, coupling the Prestonian mechanical removal rate model with electrochemical passivation kinetics must accurately predict dishing at the dense storage node contact (SNC) plug arrays versus isolated periphery plugs.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Bulk W polishing requires high removal rate acidic ferric nitrate or hydrogen peroxide-based slurries (pH 2.0-2.5) with high selectivity to TiN (>50:1) to stop reliably on the thin (10-20 nm) barrier. Step 2 requires transitioning to a colloidal silica slurry with low W removal rate and high TiN:Oxide selectivity (ideally >3:1) to suppress plug recession/dishing below 15 nm while clearing residual TiN stringers that otherwise short adjacent bitline and storage node nodes.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Alumina-based bulk slurries present aggressive consumable wear on polyurethane polishing pads (IC1000/Suba IV stack) and severe slurry loop filter clogging; sourcing stabilized acidic colloidal silica slurries with optimized oxidizer shelf-life (H2O2 blending stability <72h) from regional SEA distributors is mandatory to avoid supply disruptions in open-source pilot runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The simulated two-step CMP sequence directly sets the baseline tool cycle time and consumable replacement budget per 100 wafers. The simulation must conclusively prove that endpoint detection (motor current drop + optical reflectivity shift) yields a reliable process window >15 seconds on 180nm nodes, avoiding yield-killing punch-through into TEOS oxide.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Excessive storage node contact W-plug dishing (>25 nm) leading to severe contact open or high sheet resistance during subsequent Crown capacitor bottom-electrode landing.
1. Incomplete TiN barrier clearing (TiN stringers/bridging) over shallow oxide isolation topologies causing inter-cell leakage currents >10 pA per cell.
1. Corrosion/pitting (galvanic corrosion) of W plugs induced by aggressive acidic slurry entrapment and post-CMP clean queue time exceeding allowable limits.

An industrial leaf Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for **AFM Topography & Optical Profilometry Dishing Metrology Characterization** following Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) of Tungsten (W) plugs in a 180nm Crown-Type COB DRAM architecture.

---

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): AFM Topography & Optical Profilometry Dishing Metrology Characterization

## Module: Metrology / CMP Planarization Contact Module
**Target Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (8F² Unit Cell, Crown-Type COB Architecture)  
**Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)  
**Objective**: Quantify micro-scale tungsten plug dishing and dielectric erosion across storage node and bitline contact plug arrays using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and non-destructive Optical Profilometry.

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Characterization Procedure

#### Phase A: Automated Optical Profilometry (Macro/Die-Level Dielectric Erosion & Step Height)
1. **Wafer Loading & Pre-Alignment**:
   - Transfer the post-W-CMP cleaned wafer onto the optical profilometer vacuum chuck.
   - Execute automated notch alignment and global coordinate mapping.
2. **Die-Level Roughness & Step-Height Scan**:
   - Calibrate white-light interferometry / phase-shifting interferometry mode with reference mirror tilt alignment.
   - Measure 49-point wafer mapping across center, middle, and edge radial zones to profile macro-topography variations across dense memory arrays versus isolated test structures.
   - Extract dielectric erosion profiles between active cell arrays (pitch: 360 nm to 400 nm) and peripheral oxide fields.

#### Phase B: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) High-Resolution Plug Dishing Profile
3. **AFM Tip Selection & Cantilever Calibration**:
   - Mount a high-aspect-ratio silicon tip (nominal tip radius < 10 nm, spring constant ~40 N/m).
   - Calibrate laser deflection sum signal and photodiode centering; establish resonance frequency (~300 kHz) for Tapping/Non-Contact Mode to prevent tip wear on tungsten plugs.
4. **Pattern Recognition & Navigation**:
   - Align the AFM optical optics to the COB contact plug array in the 8F² memory cell array (unit cell layout: access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Set scan coordinates to target the shared bitline drain contact and storage node W-plugs.
5. **Topography Acquisition**:
   - Set scan window to $2\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 2\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (capturing $>16$ adjacent contact plugs across the 360–400 nm pitch grid).
   - Set scan rate to $0.5\text{ Hz}$ to $1.0\text{ Hz}$ at $512 \times 512$ pixel resolution.
6. **Data Processing & Dishing Extraction**:
   - Apply 1st-order line-by-line polynomial flattening to eliminate sample tilt.
   - Extract cross-sectional height profiles across the center of adjacent tungsten plugs.
   - Calculate tungsten dishing depth ($H_{\text{dishing}} = Z_{\text{oxide\_field}} - Z_{\text{plug\_center}}$) and perimeter dielectric erosion.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **W-Plug Dishing Depth** | $\le 15$ | $\text{nm}$ | Tapping-mode AFM (cross-sectional line trace) |
| **Array Dielectric (Oxide) Erosion** | $\le 20$ | $\text{nm}$ | Optical Profilometry / AFM step-height |
| **Array Pattern Pitch Verification** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | $\text{nm}$ | AFM line profile (plug-to-plug pitch) |
| **Wafer-Level Topography Map Sampling** | $49$ | $\text{points}$ | Automated Optical Profilometry mapping |

---

### 3. Context & Literature Citations

* **Cell Geometry & Array Pitch**: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$ *(Sources: "180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench" & "Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering")*.
* **Interconnect Stack**: Crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) erected above drain contact via tungsten plug (W-plug) *(Source: "180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench")*.
* **Wafer Map Metrology Strategy**: Standardized automated 49-point wafer mapping protocol for tracking radial non-uniformity across process runs *(Source: "Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology")*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) provides the sub-Angstrom vertical resolution required to measure W-plug recess and oxide erosion across dense 180nm 8F² arrays, but its limited lateral scan throughput (typically <15 µm/s tip velocity) creates a severe metrology bottleneck if utilized across full 150mm/200mm wafer maps. Optical profilometry (white-light interferometry/coherence scanning) must be co-integrated to rapidly map macro-scale die dishing across wide scribe-line test structures (>50 µm field) and flag suspect dies for high-resolution AFM tip inspection. Correlation between the optical phase shift on heterogeneous W/SiO2 boundaries and true AFM physical height profiles must be rigorously calibrated to prevent optical artifact misinterpretation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Following Tungsten chemical-mechanical planarization (W-CMP), galvanic corrosion between the tungsten plug and the surrounding titanium/titanium-nitride (Ti/TiN) barrier bilayer can cause localized micro-corrosion trenches deeper than 25 nm, which standard optical profilometry will completely miss due to optical diffraction limits (<0.5 µm lateral resolution). For AFM metrology, high-aspect-ratio silicon cantilevers (tip radius <10 nm, cone angle <15°) running in non-contact/tapping mode are mandatory to resolve plug dishing and ILD dielectric erosion without dulling the tip or causing tungsten tip smearing across 180nm contact contacts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring production-grade in-line automated AFM platforms (e.g., Bruker, Park Systems) exceeds early-stage DRAM Foundation Gen 2 Capex limits. The metrology strategy must execute a 'Buy' on certified refurbished or semi-automated benchtop AFM systems fitted with acoustic isolation enclosures and active vibration tables, while sourcing off-the-shelf calibrated AFM cantilever tips (silicon, 300 kHz resonance) and optical step-height calibration standards (VLSI/NIST traceable 18nm and 100nm SiO2/Si pitch gratings) with dual-source vendor qualification to hedge against 12-week lead times.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: W-CMP dishing and erosion metrology directly gates the subsequent Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) bottom electrode / storage node contact (SNC) deposition module. If dishing exceeds 35 nm or plug pull-out occurs, subsequent dielectric stack step coverage fails, creating open-circuit contacts and catastrophic DRAM yield fallout. The metrology characterization package must deliver automated data export into TCAD/layout verification pipelines within a strict 4-week window, backed by reproducible run-to-run gauge repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R < 10%).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. AFM cantilever tip degradation and tip convolution artifacts causing artificial flattening or underestimation of sub-micron tungsten plug recess/dishing depth.
1. Optical refractive index and phase jump discontinuities between metallic W and dielectric SiO2 inducing false height offsets (>15 nm error) during optical profilometry.
1. Post-CMP slurry residue or native oxide growth (WOx) obscuring micro-topography and distorting step-height measurements due to exceeded ambient queue times.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-2-3-3-01` | **AFM Sub-Micron Tungsten Plug Recess and Array Erosion Metrology** | Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in Tapping/Non-Contact Mode with ultra-sharp silicon cantilever tip (nominal tip radius <10 nm, spring constant ~40 N/m, resonant frequency ~300 kHz), passive/active vibration isolation chamber, and acoustic enclosure. | 1. Load wafer onto vacuum chuck and align to 180nm 8F² DRAM cell array test keys (dense array and isolated 180nm contact pads). 2. Calibrate vertical Z-piezo deflection using NIST-traceable 18.0 nm ± 0.5 nm step-height calibration standard. 3. Acquire 5 µm x 5 µm high-resolution scan (512 x 512 pixels) at 0.5 Hz scan rate over the dense W-plug contact array. 4. Acquire 2 µm x 2 µm scan across isolated W-plug contacts. 5. Perform first-order line-by-line tilt leveling and extract extracted 1D cross-sectional profiles across 20 distinct W-plugs to measure recess depth relative to surrounding TEOS/BPSG ILD oxide plane. 6. Calculate mean plug recess depth and peak-to-valley array erosion across dense vs isolated regions. | `Dense W-plug recess depth must be between 5.0 nm and 25.0 nm (target 15.0 nm ± 5.0 nm); isolated W-plug recess <= 30.0 nm; dielectric array erosion <= 15.0 nm across the 5 µm array field. Standard deviation across 20 site profiles must satisfy 1-sigma <= 2.5 nm with zero observed tip-breakage artifacts.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-2-3-3-02` | **Optical Profilometry Macro Dishing and Scribe-Line Feature Profiling** | White Light Interferometer / Optical Coherence Scanning Profilometer equipped with 50x Mirau interferometer objective (NA >= 0.55), green/white dual LED illumination, and sub-nanometer phase-shifting vertical encoder. | 1. Position optical profilometer over macro W-pad test structures (50 µm x 50 µm and 100 µm x 100 µm CMP characterization pads) in scribe-line test groups. 2. Adjust fringe contrast and set vertical scan range to 2.0 µm with 2 nm vertical sampling interval. 3. Execute phase-shifting interferometry (PSI) scan over a 150 µm x 150 µm field of view. 4. Apply material-dependent phase change correction table for W-SiO2 boundary reflectivity differential. 5. Extract lateral dishing curve across the center line of the 50 µm and 100 µm pads. 6. Quantify center-to-edge pad dishing depth and field oxide thinning. | `Pad dishing on 50 µm x 50 µm W-pad must be <= 35.0 nm; dishing on 100 µm x 100 µm W-pad must be <= 50.0 nm; optical surface profile RMS roughness (Rq) of planarized dielectric adjacent to pads must be <= 0.8 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (antistatic, powder-free, dual-layer), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering polycarbonate safety spectacles, Full static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and conductive ESD booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA solvent: Flush immediately with copious laminar DI water eyewash for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Remove contaminated apparel. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors: Move personnel immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if respiration becomes labored. Seek medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Metrology bench must operate under Class 100 laminar flow hood with local exhaust ventilation (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s or 100 FPM) to vent solvent wipe vapors and maintain particle-free laminar airflow over AFM/profilometer scan stages.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA lint-free cleanroom wipes and swabs must be segregated in dedicated closed-cover, grounded, flame-retardant solvent waste bins. Spent liquid solvents must be deposited into designated chlorinated/non-chlorinated organic chemical carboys for licensed hazardous waste incineration. No drain disposal allowed.

| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1) | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (Resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, megasonic/PVA-scrub-cleaned post-W-CMP planarized surface, free of colloidal silica/alumina slurry particulate, with native WOx surface oxide < 1.0 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized, dust-free surface with verified step topography and zero AFM tip-induced mechanical scratching, maintained under dry N2 purge ready for Storage Node Contact barrier Ti/TiN/W re-deposition or Crown Capacitor ILD deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air queue time causes rapid tungsten galvanic and atmospheric oxidation forming hygroscopic WOx (WO3) hillocks and crystallites (>3.0 nm thickness), invalidating sub-nanometer dishing metrology and causing poor ohmic contact resistance or micro-void peeling at the subsequent capacitor storage node bottom interface.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical verification and quantitative characterization of tungsten chemical-mechanical planarization (W-CMP) dishing, array erosion, and plug recess across 180nm 8F² DRAM cell structures using calibrated AFM and Optical Profilometry. Successful delivery validates CMP polishing selectivity, establishing that contact plug recesses and macro pad dishing are strictly constrained within crown capacitor integration tolerances.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_CMP_Dishing_Erosion_AFM_Topography_RawData_Map.csv`

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **180nm dense DRAM cell tungsten plug recess depth below adjacent ILD oxide plane** | `15.0 nm` | ±5.0 nm | AFM tapping-mode 1D height profiling across 20 cell contacts calibrated against NIST 18nm standard |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Macro-scale scribe-line W contact test pad (50 µm x 50 µm) center dishing depth** | `<= 35.0 nm` | +0.0 nm / -10.0 nm | White Light Coherence Scanning Optical Profilometry with phase-corrected reflectivity boundary model |

> Both AFM dense array recess profiles (<= 20 nm) and Optical Profilometry 50 µm macro dishing (<= 35 nm) satisfy TCAD contact resistance integration thresholds with Gage R&R <= 8.0%, zero tip-convolution flags on cross-sectional analysis, and sign-off agreement from both Systems Engineering and CMP Process Integration leads.

Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)
Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology (Tompkins & Irene - Handbook of Ellipsometry)

critics.systems_engineer: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) provides the sub-Angstrom vertical resolution required to measure W-plug recess and oxide erosion across dense 180nm 8F² arrays, but its limited lateral scan throughput (typically <15 µm/s tip velocity) creates a severe metrology bottleneck if utilized across full 150mm/200mm wafer maps. Optical profilometry (white-light interferometry/coherence scanning) must be co-integrated to rapidly map macro-scale die dishing across wide scribe-line test structures (>50 µm field) and flag suspect dies for high-resolution AFM tip inspection. Correlation between the optical phase shift on heterogeneous W/SiO2 boundaries and true AFM physical height profiles must be rigorously calibrated to prevent optical artifact misinterpretation.
critics.domain_expert: Following Tungsten chemical-mechanical planarization (W-CMP), galvanic corrosion between the tungsten plug and the surrounding titanium/titanium-nitride (Ti/TiN) barrier bilayer can cause localized micro-corrosion trenches deeper than 25 nm, which standard optical profilometry will completely miss due to optical diffraction limits (<0.5 µm lateral resolution). For AFM metrology, high-aspect-ratio silicon cantilevers (tip radius <10 nm, cone angle <15°) running in non-contact/tapping mode are mandatory to resolve plug dishing and ILD dielectric erosion without dulling the tip or causing tungsten tip smearing across 180nm contact contacts.
critics.supply_chain: Procuring production-grade in-line automated AFM platforms (e.g., Bruker, Park Systems) exceeds early-stage DRAM Foundation Gen 2 Capex limits. The metrology strategy must execute a 'Buy' on certified refurbished or semi-automated benchtop AFM systems fitted with acoustic isolation enclosures and active vibration tables, while sourcing off-the-shelf calibrated AFM cantilever tips (silicon, 300 kHz resonance) and optical step-height calibration standards (VLSI/NIST traceable 18nm and 100nm SiO2/Si pitch gratings) with dual-source vendor qualification to hedge against 12-week lead times.
critics.laya_pm: W-CMP dishing and erosion metrology directly gates the subsequent Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) bottom electrode / storage node contact (SNC) deposition module. If dishing exceeds 35 nm or plug pull-out occurs, subsequent dielectric stack step coverage fails, creating open-circuit contacts and catastrophic DRAM yield fallout. The metrology characterization package must deliver automated data export into TCAD/layout verification pipelines within a strict 4-week window, backed by reproducible run-to-run gauge repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R < 10%).
critical_failure_modes: AFM cantilever tip degradation and tip convolution artifacts causing artificial flattening or underestimation of sub-micron tungsten plug recess/dishing depth.
Optical refractive index and phase jump discontinuities between metallic W and dielectric SiO2 inducing false height offsets (>15 nm error) during optical profilometry.
Post-CMP slurry residue or native oxide growth (WOx) obscuring micro-topography and distorting step-height measurements due to exceeded ambient queue times.

testcases.title: AFM Sub-Micron Tungsten Plug Recess and Array Erosion Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in Tapping/Non-Contact Mode with ultra-sharp silicon cantilever tip (nominal tip radius <10 nm, spring constant ~40 N/m, resonant frequency ~300 kHz), passive/active vibration isolation chamber, and acoustic enclosure.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has completed W-CMP polish, post-CMP double-sided megasonic PVA brush scrub clean, and dry spin-dry cycle. Wafer inspected under darkfield microscope to ensure zero macroscopic slurry contamination; transferred within dry nitrogen carrier box within 30 minutes of clean.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load wafer onto vacuum chuck and align to 180nm 8F² DRAM cell array test keys (dense array and isolated 180nm contact pads). 2. Calibrate vertical Z-piezo deflection using NIST-traceable 18.0 nm ± 0.5 nm step-height calibration standard. 3. Acquire 5 µm x 5 µm high-resolution scan (512 x 512 pixels) at 0.5 Hz scan rate over the dense W-plug contact array. 4. Acquire 2 µm x 2 µm scan across isolated W-plug contacts. 5. Perform first-order line-by-line tilt leveling and extract extracted 1D cross-sectional profiles across 20 distinct W-plugs to measure recess depth relative to surrounding TEOS/BPSG ILD oxide plane. 6. Calculate mean plug recess depth and peak-to-valley array erosion across dense vs isolated regions.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Dense W-plug recess depth must be between 5.0 nm and 25.0 nm (target 15.0 nm ± 5.0 nm); isolated W-plug recess <= 30.0 nm; dielectric array erosion <= 15.0 nm across the 5 µm array field. Standard deviation across 20 site profiles must satisfy 1-sigma <= 2.5 nm with zero observed tip-breakage artifacts.

testcases.title: Optical Profilometry Macro Dishing and Scribe-Line Feature Profiling
testcases.instrumentation: White Light Interferometer / Optical Coherence Scanning Profilometer equipped with 50x Mirau interferometer objective (NA >= 0.55), green/white dual LED illumination, and sub-nanometer phase-shifting vertical encoder.
testcases.pre_conditions: Optical calibration target (100.0 nm certified step height) verified with vertical repeatability < 0.2 nm. Wafer surface ambient dust count verified <= Class 100 cleanroom bench level.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position optical profilometer over macro W-pad test structures (50 µm x 50 µm and 100 µm x 100 µm CMP characterization pads) in scribe-line test groups. 2. Adjust fringe contrast and set vertical scan range to 2.0 µm with 2 nm vertical sampling interval. 3. Execute phase-shifting interferometry (PSI) scan over a 150 µm x 150 µm field of view. 4. Apply material-dependent phase change correction table for W-SiO2 boundary reflectivity differential. 5. Extract lateral dishing curve across the center line of the 50 µm and 100 µm pads. 6. Quantify center-to-edge pad dishing depth and field oxide thinning.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pad dishing on 50 µm x 50 µm W-pad must be <= 35.0 nm; dishing on 100 µm x 100 µm W-pad must be <= 50.0 nm; optical surface profile RMS roughness (Rq) of planarized dielectric adjacent to pads must be <= 0.8 nm.

ppe_required: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (antistatic, powder-free, dual-layer)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering polycarbonate safety spectacles
Full static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and conductive ESD booties
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin/eye contact with IPA solvent: Flush immediately with copious laminar DI water eyewash for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Remove contaminated apparel. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors: Move personnel immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if respiration becomes labored. Seek medical evaluation.

q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding ambient air queue time causes rapid tungsten galvanic and atmospheric oxidation forming hygroscopic WOx (WO3) hillocks and crystallites (>3.0 nm thickness), invalidating sub-nanometer dishing metrology and causing poor ohmic contact resistance or micro-void peeling at the subsequent capacitor storage node bottom interface.

Successful delivery validates CMP polishing selectivity, establishing that contact plug recesses and macro pad dishing are strictly constrained within crown capacitor integration tolerances.

quantitative_assertions.verification_method: AFM tapping-mode 1D height profiling across 20 cell contacts calibrated against NIST 18nm standard

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Macro-scale scribe-line W contact test pad (50 µm x 50 µm) center dishing depth
