# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Interfacial Thermionic-Field Emission & Current Crowding TCAD Simulation
**Node & Topology:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 2 µm) | 8F² Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB)  
**Process / Metrology Module:** Storage Node Contact & W-Plug Ti/TiN Barrier Interfacial Transport  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure defines the TCAD setup, mesh refinement, and transport model calibration required to extract interfacial contact resistivity ($\rho_c$), thermionic-field emission (TFE) carrier tunneling profiles, and 2D/3D current crowding distributions across the Ti/TiN barrier layer between the n⁺-diffusion drain/storage node contact ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and the tungsten (W) plug contact.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: 3D TCAD Geometry & Meshing Setup
1. Define the 180nm 8F² unit cell geometry for the access transistor drain contact:
   - Channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, transistor active width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Pitch matching the wordline/bitline boundary constraints ($360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$).
2. Construct the storage node contact stack:
   - Heavily doped n⁺-silicon active area ($N_D \ge 1\times 10^{20}\text{ cm}^{-3}$).
   - PVD/CVD Ti contact layer ($10\text{ nm} - 15\text{ nm}$) + TiN barrier liner ($10\text{ nm} - 20\text{ nm}$).
   - CVD Tungsten (W) plug fill.
3. Apply adaptive mesh refinement:
   - Grid spacing $\Delta z \le 0.5\text{ nm}$ normal to the $\text{TiSi}_x/\text{Si}$ and $\text{TiN}/\text{Ti}$ interfaces to capture tunneling band bending.
   - Lateral grid $\Delta x, \Delta y \le 2.0\text{ nm}$ along the perimeter contact edges to resolve perimeter current crowding.

#### Step 2: Physical Model & Transport Calibration
1. Enable quantum mechanical carrier transport models at the contact boundary:
   - Thermionic-Field Emission (TFE) and Field Emission (FE) non-local tunneling across the Schottky barrier ($\Phi_{Bn} \approx 0.55\text{ eV} - 0.60\text{ eV}$ for $\text{TiSi}_2/\text{n-Si}$).
   - Fermi-Dirac statistics with bandgap narrowing (BGN) enabled for degenerately doped regions.
   - Temperature-dependent carrier mobility (Philips unified mobility model) including high field velocity saturation.
2. Calibrate boundary temperatures across the operational specification ($25^\circ\text{C}$ to $85^\circ\text{C}$).

#### Step 3: Bias Sweep & Current Density Extraction
1. Apply quasi-stationary DC sweep across the Kelvin contact test structure from $V = -0.2\text{ V}$ to $+0.5\text{ V}$.
2. Extract the current density vector field $\vec{J}(x, y, z)$ through the contact via.
3. Integrate current density to compute:
   - Specific contact resistivity $\rho_c$ ($\Omega\cdot\mu\text{m}^2$).
   - Current crowding factor $\eta = J_{\text{edge}} / J_{\text{center}}$.
   - Effective contact resistance $R_c$ contributing to the cell RC budget.

#### Step 4: Storage Node RC Verification
1. Export extracted $R_c$ to the cell write/read RC delay model.
2. Verify total storage node series resistance ensures cell charge transfer ($Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$) without bottlenecking sense amplifier differential signal development ($\Delta V = 100\text{ mV} - 150\text{ mV}$) within the targeted retention cycle.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement / Validation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Active Area Critical Dimensions** | $L = 180 \pm 5$, $W = 220 \pm 5$ | $\text{nm}$ | Automated TCAD mesh boundary parser |
| **Grid Discretization (Interface)** | $\Delta z \le 0.5$ | $\text{nm}$ | Local mesh density inspection at Ti/Si interface |
| **Operating Simulation Temperature** | $85.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | TCAD thermal boundary condition check |
| **Bitline & Wordline Grid Pitch** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Layout coordinate boundary metric |
| **Target Sensing Voltage Margin** | $100 \text{ to } 150$ | $\text{mV}$ | Post-transport transient circuit simulation |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Sources Cited
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - *Confirmed geometry parameters:* Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) via tungsten plug (W-plug); leakage current evaluation baseline at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - *Confirmed pitch parameters:* Bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$; $8\text{F}^2$ cell topology retention window specification at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout:**
  - *Confirmed electrical budget:* Charge dump relation $Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$; differential sensing voltage target $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: TCAD transport modeling must explicitly couple non-local Fowler-Nordheim and thermionic-field emission (TFE) boundary conditions across the TiSi2/n+ poly-Si or TiSi2/active silicon junction with 3D Navier-Stokes/drift-diffusion solvers; ignoring dynamic carrier heating and non-parabolic band structure will underestimate current crowding at plug perimeter edges by >35%, skewing cell RC write-time constants.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node node dimensions, W-plug storage node contact diameter (~220nm) exhibits severe current crowding where Ti/TiN liner thickness thins down along contact sidewalls and bottom corners. Modeling must integrate quantum mechanical transmission probabilities (WKB approximation) with explicit dopant deactivation profiles (As/P segregation at silicide boundary) to extract specific contact resistivity rho_c accurately.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Physical calibration data relies on ultra-pure WF6, SiH4, and TiCl4/TDMAT precursors for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of Ti/TiN barrier stacks. Discrepancies between simulated contact resistance and physical fab lot yields often trace back to precursor lot variations and carbon/chlorine interfacial contamination rather than purely physical modeling errors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain project velocity for the 180nm open-source tapeout milestone, this TCAD work package must deliver calibrated compact SPICE subcircuit parameters (sub-grid lumped resistance matrix) for OpenROAD integration within 3 simulation iterations, avoiding open-ended mesh refinement cycles that do not converge within runtime budgets.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial current crowding leading to localized Joule heating (>150°C localized delta), inducing catastrophic electromigration and void formation at the bottom TiSi2/W interface.
1. Barrier thinning and TiSi2 agglomeration at plug corner singularities causing Fermi-level pinning and transition from ohmic TFE behavior to rectifying Schottky barrier behavior with rho_c > 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm2.
1. Numerical mesh non-convergence at sharp 90-degree TiN liner corners due to steep electric field gradients (>1.5 MV/cm), leading to unphysical carrier velocity runaway in simulation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-2-2-01` | **Specific Contact Resistivity Extraction via Simulated Kelvin Cross Bridge & TLM** | Synopsys Sentaurus TCAD / Silvaco Atlas 3D Device Simulator with Non-Local Quantum Tunneling Mesh and High-Precision Parameter Extraction Script | 1. Apply bias sweep V_contact from -0.5V to +0.5V across Kelvin cross-bridge terminal while holding substrate contact at 0V. 2. Calculate differential resistance dV/dI at V=0V. 3. Simultaneously simulate 5-pad TLM array (spacing d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 um; pad width W = 100 um) under identical interfacial mesh parameters. 4. Extract transfer length L_T and specific contact resistivity rho_c = R_c * W * L_T. | `Specific contact resistivity rho_c must fall within 3.0e-8 to 8.0e-8 Ohm*cm^2, and I-V characteristics must show linear ohmic behavior with linearity correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.998 across [-0.2V, +0.2V].` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-2-2-02` | **Interfacial Current Crowding Factor & Current Density Distribution Profile** | 3D TCAD Current Vector Field Visualizer and Boundary Flux Integrator | 1. Solve coupled Poisson-Drift-Diffusion and Hydrodynamic Transport equations. 2. Map current density vector J(x, y, z) across the Ti/TiN/TiSi2 interface plane. 3. Extract peak current density J_peak at contact bottom corner perimeter and average current density J_avg across contact area. 4. Compute crowding factor CF = J_peak / J_avg. | `Current crowding factor CF must be <= 3.8, and peak current density J_peak must not exceed 2.5e6 A/cm^2 under 10 uA forced read/write bias.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (Double-layer, chemical-resistant), ANSI Z87.1 Approved Full Face Shield and Chemical Splash Goggles, Flame-Resistant Anti-Static Cleanroom Smock, Butyl Rubber Apron for chemical handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF dermal exposure, immediately flush area with water for 5 minutes and liberally apply 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel continuously until medical care arrives. In case of inhalation or gaseous precursor leak, remove patient to fresh air, administer 100% oxygen, and seek emergency toxicology support.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Class 100 cleanroom dedicated toxic gas scrubbed exhaust with negative pressure ducting (>0.2 in. w.g.) and minimum face velocity of 100 fpm at chemical wet bench hoods; continuous toxic gas detection systems (TGDS) for HF, TiCl4, and WF6.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous fluoride-bearing effluents routed directly to dedicated Fluoride Waste Neutralization (FWN) system utilizing calcium hydroxide Ca(OH)2 precipitation forming insoluble CaF2; gaseous exhaust passed through point-of-use thermal-wet burn box scrubbers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Pre-metal pre-clean)** | `7664-39-3` | Electronic Grade (SEMI Tier 3) | `0.5% - 1.0% aqueous solution` |
| **Titanium Tetrachloride (CVD Ti/TiN Precursor)** | `7550-45-0` | Ultra-Pure 99.999% trace metals basis | `100% liquid precursor` |
| **Tungsten Hexafluoride (W-plug CVD)** | `7783-82-6` | VLSI Grade 99.999% | `100% compressed liquefied gas` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly opened silicon contact vias following post-RIE clean, stripped of native oxide via dilute HF (DHF 100:1) etch; hydrophobic surface termination (Si-H bond fraction > 90%).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Conformal 10nm Ti/20nm TiN barrier layer deposited via ALD/CVD, vacuum-sealed or loaded into rapid thermal anneal (RTA) chamber for silicidation to prevent Ti oxidation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide (SiO2) regrowth exceeding 0.8 nm thickness at the contact interface, which disrupts thermionic-field emission and increases specific contact resistance rho_c by over an order of magnitude (shifting from ohmic to Schottky rectifying).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Calibrated 3D TCAD simulation dataset and compact macro-model extracting specific contact resistivity (rho_c) and interfacial current crowding dynamics for the 180nm DRAM storage node W-plug Ti/TiN barrier interface, validated against empirical TLM linear regression standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_180nm_wplug_tfe_transport_report.pdf`
- [ ] `contact_iv_tlm_crowding_extracted_dataset.csv`
- [ ] `ti_tin_interface_current_density_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Simulated specific contact resistivity rho_c for TiSi2/n+ active silicon contact at 300K** | `5.5e-8` | +/- 1.5e-8 Ohm*cm^2 | 5-pad Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) linear regression slope and intercept extraction script |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Storage node contact current crowding factor (CF = J_peak / J_avg) at perimeter corners** | `3.2` | <= 3.8 | 3D interfacial current vector flux integration along contact bottom boundary mesh |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Extraction script successfully executes over TCAD dataset yielding rho_c within nominal target band, linearity R^2 >= 0.998 on Kelvin I-V curves, zero unphysical negative differential resistance anomalies, and delivery of verified SPICE subcircuit parameters (.subckt) directly integrated into the DRAM 8F2 cell layout parasitics deck.

critics.supply_chain: Physical calibration data relies on ultra-pure WF6, SiH4, and TiCl4/TDMAT precursors for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of Ti/TiN barrier stacks. Discrepancies between simulated contact resistance and physical fab lot yields often trace back to precursor lot variations and carbon/chlorine interfacial contamination rather than purely physical modeling errors.
critics.laya_pm: To maintain project velocity for the 180nm open-source tapeout milestone, this TCAD work package must deliver calibrated compact SPICE subcircuit parameters (sub-grid lumped resistance matrix) for OpenROAD integration within 3 simulation iterations, avoiding open-ended mesh refinement cycles that do not converge within runtime budgets.
critical_failure_modes: Interfacial current crowding leading to localized Joule heating (>150°C localized delta), inducing catastrophic electromigration and void formation at the bottom TiSi2/W interface.

Barrier thinning and TiSi2 agglomeration at plug corner singularities causing Fermi-level pinning and transition from ohmic TFE behavior to rectifying Schottky barrier behavior with rho_c > 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm2.
Numerical mesh non-convergence at sharp 90-degree TiN liner corners due to steep electric field gradients (>1.5 MV/cm), leading to unphysical carrier velocity runaway in simulation.

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Kelvin Test Structure Layout Setup & Alignment**:
   - Align the 4-terminal Kelvin test structure configured for the COB storage node W-plug contact over the access transistor active diffusion area (channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, bitline/wordline pitch $360\text{--}400\text{ nm}$).
   - Ensure the Ti/TiN barrier bilayer and W-plug via contact window dimensions match the drawn lithographic CD specifications.

2. **Instrument Hookup & 4-Wire Collinear S-Parameter / DC Meter Setup**:
   - Connect the outer force terminals (Pads 1 and 4) to a precision DC current source.
   - Connect the inner sense terminals (Pads 2 and 3) to a high-input-impedance ($> 10\text{ G}\Omega$) digital electrometer/voltmeter to measure floating potential difference without parasitic lead/probe loading.

3. **DC Current Forcing Sweep**:
   - Apply a constant DC drive current $I_{\text{force}}$ stepped between $1.0\text{ mA}$ and $10.0\text{ mA}$ across the outer force loop through the W-plug/barrier/diffusion contact interface.
   - Sweep forward and reverse polarities to verify ohmic linearity and rule out asymmetric non-ohmic Schottky rectification.

4. **Floating Potential Differential Measurement ($V_{\text{sense}}$)**:
   - Record the potential drop across the contact interface:
     $$V_{\text{contact}} = V_{\text{sense}} = V_2 - V_3$$
   - Calculate raw Kelvin contact resistance:
     $$R_{\text{k}} = \frac{V_{\text{sense}}}{I_{\text{force}}}$$

5. **2D/3D Current Crowding & Geometric De-embedding**:
   - Account for 2D/3D current crowding and sheet resistance ($R_s$) contributions of the underlying active diffusion/poly region using the four-point collinear sheet resistance formulation:
     $$R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right) = 4.5324 \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right)\quad [\Omega/\square]$$
   - Apply geometric finite-boundary correction factor $F(d/s)$ to decouple parasitic diffusion sheet resistance from interfacial resistance.

6. **Specific Contact Resistivity ($\rho_c$) Extraction**:
   - Extract the specific contact resistivity $\rho_c$ via:
     $$\rho_c = R_{\text{interface}} \cdot A_{\text{contact}}$$
     where $A_{\text{contact}}$ is the calibrated active contact area of the COB W-plug.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Metric / Tolerance | Physical Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DC Force Current Range** | $1.0\text{ to }10.0$ | $\text{mA}$ | Outer Kelvin Force SMU Probes ($1\text{--}4$) |
| **Active Transistor Geometry** | $L = 180 \pm 5$, $W = 220 \pm 5$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-line CD-SEM Metrology |
| **Bitline & Wordline Pitch** | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\text{nm}$ | CD-SEM / Scatterometry Metrology |
| **Cell Retention & Leakage Baseline** | $\text{Leakage} < 1.0\text{ fA/cell at }85^\circ\text{C}$; $\text{Retention} > 64$ | $\text{fA}$, $\text{ms}$, $^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermally Controlled Probe Station ($85^\circ\text{C}$) |
| **Sheet Resistance Scaling Pre-factor** | $4.5324 \pm 0.0005$ | $\text{ratio } [\pi/\ln(2)]$ | Thin-film 4-point probe potential ratio |

---

### 3. Citations & Literature Context Sources

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Validates unit cell access transistor geometry: channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Confirms stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture via tungsten plug (W-plug).
  - Supplies leakage current target below $1\text{ fA/cell at }85^\circ\text{C}$ with minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Validates bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$.
  - Supplies data retention target $> 64\text{ ms at }85^\circ\text{C}$ and cell capacitance budget of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$.
- **Source: Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance**:
  - Validates the DC operating current range of $I = 1\text{ mA to }10\text{ mA}$ through outer probes.
  - Supplies thin semiconductor film sheet resistance formula $R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right) = 4.5324 \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right)\ [\Omega/\square]$ and edge proximity correction factor $F(d/s)$ for finite geometries.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Extracting specific contact resistivity (rho_c) using Kelvin bridge structures on 180nm W-plug contacts requires rigorous decoupling of parasitic 2D/3D current crowding and sheet resistance (R_s) in the diffusion tap. Without 3D finite-element TCAD mesh correction factors (e.g., Berger's crowding correction), raw four-terminal Kelvin measurements will overestimate contact resistance (R_c) by 15-35%, propagating false parasitics into 1T1C storage node write-time simulations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node, the Ti/TiN liner barrier interface at the bottom of the contact plug directly determines ohmic quality. If the interfacial native oxide reduction by physical vapor deposition (PVD) Ti or chemical vapor deposition (CVD) Ti silicidation (C54-TiSi2 formation) is incomplete, non-linear Schottky transport dominates over field emission tunneling, driving rho_c well above the <= 1.0e-6 Ohm*cm^2 budget required for low-voltage DRAM sensing margin.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-metallization contact-hole wet clean requires semiconductor-grade ultra-pure hydrofluoric acid (dHF 100:1 or 50:1, UP-SSS grade) and ultra-high purity forming gas (95% N2 / 5% H2, 99.999% purity) for the 400°C post-metallization sinter. Supply disruption or cylinder grade downgrade directly impacts barrier adhesion and silicide phase transformation reproducibility across local foundry partners.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput on four-point automated probe stations (e.g., Keysight B1500A with Cascade probe card) must balance die-level statistical mapping against thermal chuck stabilization delays. To maintain tape-out milestones, Kelvin test structures must be integrated into standard scribeline parametric test vehicles (PCM) with standardized pad pitch (100 µm pitch, 50 µm pad dimension) compatible with standard probe cards.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete native oxide stripping or interfacial fluorocarbon polymer residue prior to Ti deposition, creating an insulating interfacial dipole layer that spikes rho_c above 1.0e-5 Ohm*cm^2.
1. Misalignment between Kelvin contact plug and underlying n+/p+ diffusion active area exceeding the 35nm overlay budget, inducing severe current crowding and non-symmetric potential tap readouts.
1. Barrier layer punch-through or micro-voiding during post-metallization forming gas annealing (400°C), triggering fluorine or tungsten diffusion into silicon and junction leakage degradation.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Acid-resistant fluoropolymer apron and chemical-splash sleeves, Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene outer gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Full-face polycarbonate shield (ANSI Z87.1) over chemical splash goggles, Class 100 cleanroom particulate mask and cleanroom antistatic safety boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For Hydrofluoric Acid exposure: Immediately flush skin with emergency shower for exactly 2 minutes; continuously apply 2.5% calcium gluconate gel wearing clean gloves, massaging into affected skin until medical personnel arrive. In case of eye contact, flush with sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye solution or copious isotonic saline for 15 minutes. For forming gas/N2 asphyxiation risk: Move victim immediately to fresh air, administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid wet-bench local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 fpm) ducted to wet acid scrubber; continuous toxic gas monitoring (TGMS) for HF and ambient H2 sensor (< 1% LEL trigger) interlocked with automatic shutoff valves.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous HF effluent routed to dedicated industrial fluoride waste sump; neutralized by calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2] dosing to precipitate insoluble calcium fluoride [CaF2]; supernatant verified pH 6.5-8.5 and total fluoride concentration < 10 ppm before municipal discharge.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Open contact-vias etched down to silicon active diffusion with photoresist fully stripped, post-dHF oxide-free hydrophobic surface termination (Si-H passivated).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sputtered Ti/TiN barrier bilayer (10nm Ti / 20nm TiN) fully capping contact-hole floor and sidewalls, isolated under vacuum or inert atmosphere.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide (SiO2) re-growth exceeding 0.8 nm thickness inside contact vias under cleanroom ambient exposure, resulting in non-ohmic tunnel barrier, contact resistance spiking (> 50 Ohm), and gross DRAM cell retention degradation.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Four-Point Kelvin Cross-Bridge Resistance Parameter Extraction & SPICE Calibration

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180NM-042`  
**Classification:** DRAM Foundation VN — Metrology / Characterization  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm Node / $\mu\text{m}$)  
**Target Structure:** Kelvin Cross-Bridge Sheet Resistance & Storage Node Contact / W-Plug Resistance Test Vehicle  

---

### 1. Objective & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure establishes the physical test protocol, parameter extraction methodology, and SPICE calibration sequence for 180 nm open-source 1T1C DRAM (8F² cell topology, access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$). The procedure measures sheet resistance ($R_s$), Kelvin contact resistance ($R_c$), and specific contact resistivity ($\rho_c$) across the Tungsten plug (W-plug) to storage node / drain diffusion boundary, mitigating parasitic lead resistance and current-crowding errors.

```
       [ Force I+ ]
            |
            v  (Cross-Bridge Arm)
 [ Sense V- ]-----[ Junction / Contact ]-----[ Sense V+ ]
            |
            v
       [ Force I- ]
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

#### Step 1: Probe Station Setup & Contact Verification
1. Mount the characterization wafer onto the analytical probe station chuck held at $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ (ambient calibration baseline) or $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$ (DRAM junction qualification temperature).
2. Align probe needles (tungsten carbide probe tips, tip radius $50\text{--}100\ \mu\text{m}$) to the Kelvin cross-bridge pad array.
3. Verify Kelvin pad footprint and spacing (conforming to standard TLM / Kelvin pad width $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, pad length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$). Verify open-circuit probe integrity prior to energizing.

#### Step 2: Cross-Bridge Sheet Resistance ($R_s$) Parameter Extraction
1. Apply the four-terminal van der Pauw / cross-bridge configuration:
   - Force a constant DC current $I = 1\text{ mA to } 10\text{ mA}$ between the outer orthogonal cross arms (probes 1 and 4).
   - Measure the floating potential difference $V$ across the perpendicular sense arms (probes 2 and 3).
2. Calculate the baseline diffusion/metal thin-film sheet resistance ($t \ll s/2$):
   $$R_s = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right) \approx 4.5324 \cdot \left(\frac{V}{I}\right)\quad [\Omega/\square]$$
3. Apply geometric correction factor $F(d/s)$ if boundary proximity to wafer edge is $< 40$ times probe spacing ($s = 1.0\text{ mm}$).

#### Step 3: Four-Point Kelvin Contact Resistance ($R_c$) Measurement
1. Route test current directly across the W-plug / diffusion interface:
   - Inject force current $I_{\text{force}} = 1\text{ mA}$ through the top contact arm via the tungsten plug.
   - Ground the bottom diffusion tap ($I_{\text{return}}$).
2. Sense the voltage drop across the interface using isolated voltage sense taps:
   $$V_{\text{sense}} = V_{\text{contact}} - V_{\text{diffusion}}$$
3. Extract Kelvin contact resistance directly free of parasitic lead resistance:
   $$R_c = \frac{V_{\text{sense}}}{I_{\text{force}}}\quad [\Omega]$$

#### Step 4: Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) Correlation & Specific Contact Resistivity ($\rho_c$)
1. Measure total resistance $R_T$ across adjacent TLM pads of width $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$ at stepped spacings:
   $$d = 5\ \mu\text{m},\ 10\ \mu\text{m},\ 20\ \mu\text{m},\ 40\ \mu\text{m},\ 80\ \mu\text{m}$$
2. Execute linear regression on $R_T$ vs. gap spacing $d$ using the relationship:
   $$R_T = 2 R_c + \left(\frac{R_s}{W}\right) \cdot d$$
   - Extract slope: $m = R_s / W$ (validates cross-bridge sheet resistance $R_s$).
   - Extract Y-intercept: $Y_0 = 2 R_c$ (confirms Kelvin extracted contact resistance).
   - Extract X-intercept: $X_0 = -2 L_T$, where $L_T$ is the transfer length.
3. Calculate specific contact resistivity:
   $$\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2\quad [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$$

#### Step 5: SPICE Model Parameter Calibration & Back-Annotation
1. Incorporate extracted $R_c$ and $R_s$ into the 1T1C subcircuit model:
   - Assign lumped resistor `R_SN_CONTACT` between the access transistor drain ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and the crown-type capacitor bottom electrode.
   - Include cell target parameters: $C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\text{ fF}$ and total cell leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. Run transient bitline charge-sharing simulations to verify sensing margin and RC settling delay.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Tolerance / Constraint |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Thin-Film Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $4.5324 \cdot (V / I)$ | $\Omega/\square$ | Verified via 4-point probe with $I = 1\text{ to } 10\text{ mA}$ |
| **Pad Geometry (Kelvin / TLM Structure)** | Width $W = 100$, Length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Spacings: $d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\ \mu\text{m}$ |
| **Minimum Storage Node Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | $\ge 28$ | $\text{fF}$ | Crown-type stacked capacitor (ONO / high-$k$, $\kappa > 15$) |
| **Unit Cell Retention Leakage Limit** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Measured at junction temperature $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 4. Context References & Literature Citations
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Access transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), crown-shaped capacitor over bitline (COB) with W-plug drain contact, dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$, capacitance budget $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$, leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
* **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity:** Pad dimensions ($W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$), gap spacings ($d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\ \mu\text{m}$), resistance relation $R_T = 2 R_c + (R_s / W) \cdot d$, and resistivity extraction formula $\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2\ [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$.
* **Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance:** Collinear tungsten carbide tips ($r = 50\text{--}100\ \mu\text{m}$, $s = 1.0\text{ mm}$), DC excitation current ($I = 1\text{ to } 10\text{ mA}$), thin-film geometric conversion constant $R_s = (\pi / \ln(2)) \cdot (V / I) = 4.5324 \cdot (V / I)\ [\Omega/\square]$, and edge correction factor $F(d/s)$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Extracting Kelvin contact resistance and cross-bridge sheet resistance directly feeds the compact model sub-circuits for 1T1C bitline sensing. The extraction methodology must decouple 2D current crowding and geometrical misalignment from true interface specific contact resistivity rho_c to avoid optimistic RC delay estimations in the sense amplifier margin models.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Four-point Kelvin planar cross-bridge resistor structures (CBKR) at the 180nm node are vulnerable to 2D current spreading error delta_R when contact hole boundaries approach diffusion tap edges. The extracted Kelvin resistance R_K must be corrected via finite element TCAD or the Loh analytical formulation: R_K = (rho_c / A_c) + (R_s * delta / W_diff) to guarantee that non-interface lateral diffusion sheet resistance does not contaminate the tungsten-plug to n+ diffusion contact resistance.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Parametric test wafer real estate on scribe lines is limited. Utilizing standardized probe card pitch (100 µm pad pitch, 40 µm x 40 µm probe pad landing area) compatible with automated parametric testers (e.g., Keysight 4080/Keithley S530) ensures testing throughput across multi-project wafer (MPW) runs without custom probe card tooling surcharges.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Delivery of calibrated SPICE subcircuit models (including contact resistance statistical distributions across wafer radius) is on the critical path for the tapeout signoff of the 8F² crown-capacitor bitline sensing block. Parameter parameter extraction bottlenecks will hold back tapeout milestone validation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Contact hole photolithographic misalignment causing overlap onto isolation oxide, generating asymmetric 2D current crowding and erroneous Kelvin sheet resistance readings (>30% skew).
1. Native oxide regrowth or insufficient pre-metal silicide sputter clean creating non-ohmic Schottky barrier behavior at the W-plug/TiN/n+ silicon junction, invalidating linear ohmic parameter extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-3-01` | **Four-Point Kelvin Contact Resistance & Ohmic Linearity Extraction** | Semi-automated probe station with thermal chuck (25°C to 125°C) coupled to Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer (High-Resolution SMU modules). | 1. Land probe tips on Kelvin Cross-Bridge test structure pads (Force High, Force Low, Sense High, Sense Low). 2. Force current I_force from Pad 1 (Metal 1) to Pad 2 (Diffusion active area) swept from -1.0 mA to +1.0 mA in 50 µA steps. 3. Simultaneously measure voltage drop V_sense across Pad 3 (Diffusion) and Pad 4 (Metal 1) using high-impedance sense lines. 4. Calculate differential Kelvin resistance R_K = dV_sense / dI_force around I = 0 mA and evaluate linear regression correlation coefficient R². | `Kelvin contact resistance R_K <= 45.0 Ohm per single contact (180nm contact diameter nominal 0.22 um), I-V linearity coefficient R² >= 0.9995 between -1.0 mA and +1.0 mA, and contact resistance variation across 9 wafer sites < 8.0% (1-sigma).` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-3-02` | **Cross-Bridge Sheet Resistance & Current Crowding Error Correction** | Keithley S530 Parametric Test System equipped with 4-terminal low-current switching matrix and high-precision digital multimeter/SMU. | 1. Contact cross-bridge sheet resistance arm pads. 2. Inject current I_s = 5.0 mA through the orthogonal arm and measure transverse voltage V_s to extract sheet resistance R_s = (pi / ln(2)) * (V_s / I_s). 3. Extract contact dimensions W_c and active diffusion width W via CD-SEM metrology log correlation. 4. Compute geometrical correction factor delta_R using the numerical TCAD model and subtract from measured Kelvin resistance: R_c_true = R_K - (R_s / 3) * (W_c / W)^2. 5. Calculate specific contact resistivity rho_c = R_c_true * A_contact. | `Specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 2.5e-7 Ohm*cm²; active diffusion sheet resistance R_s = 65.0 ± 5.0 Ohm/sq; current crowding correction term delta_R verified within 5% of calibrated TCAD benchmark.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Static dissipative cleanroom frock and ESD conductive footwear, Thermal protective gloves for chuck operation >85°C
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA: Flush with copious volumes of deionized water for at least 15 minutes. For N2 displacement/asphyxiation risk: Immediately remove victim to fresh air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored. For thermal probe burn: Cool area with cold water for 15 minutes; do not apply ice.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober enclosure must maintain laminar cleanroom airflow (0.45 m/s ± 20%) with dedicated local exhaust ventilation (minimum 50 CFM) during solvent pad cleaning.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent-soaked cleanroom wipes must be collected in sealed, grounded, flame-retardant hazardous solvent waste containers for high-temperature off-site incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 6.0 | `99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed Metal-1 aluminum/tungsten pad metallization, post-passivation window etch, and alloy anneal with hydrophobic, unoxidized probe pad surfaces.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Scrubbed and probed bond pad surfaces with probe mark depth < 0.2 µm, sealed under dry N2 purge prior to automated wafer dicing and packaging.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure leads to moisture absorption and pad surface oxidation (Al2O3 / oxide skin formation), leading to elevated contact probe resistance (>5 Ohm), probe punch-through pad damage, and false fail classifications during parameter extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed extraction of specific contact resistivity rho_c, true contact resistance R_c, and diffusion sheet resistance R_s from four-point Kelvin cross-bridge structures, accompanied by validated compact SPICE subcircuit parameters incorporated into the 180nm open-source DRAM design kit.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `kelvin_contact_extraction_wafer_map.csv`
- [ ] `spice_contact_calibration_report.pdf`
- [ ] `kelvin_cross_bridge_probe_mark_audit.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Specific contact resistivity (rho_c) for W-plug to n+ diffusion contact** | `1.8e-7` | +/- 0.4e-7 Ohm*cm^2 | Four-point Kelvin cross-bridge extraction with 2D current crowding analytical correction verified across 45 dies |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Kelvin I-V sweep linearity across nominal operating range (-1.0 mA to +1.0 mA)** | `0.9998` | >= 0.9995 R^2 | Least-squares linear regression on Keysight B1500A parametric measurement data |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Extracted diffusion sheet resistance (R_s) on cross-bridge arm** | `65.0` | +/- 5.0 Ohm/sq | Van der Pauw / cross-bridge dual-polarization voltage-current extraction |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% of tested dies meet rho_c <= 2.5e-7 Ohm*cm² and R² >= 0.9995, calibrated SPICE subcircuit models show < 3% delay discrepancy against TCAD mixed-mode cell transient simulations, and technical review signoff is executed by the Metrology Domain Expert and Circuit Design Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-180-KELVIN-001`
**Title:** Kelvin Cross-Bridge Test Structure Automated DC Probing & I-V Sweeps  
**Module:** Metrology & Electrical Characterization (PCM / TCAD Calibration)  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm, 8F² COB 1T1C DRAM)  
**Target Structure:** Tungsten Plug (W-Plug) to Storage Node Contact / Active Area Kelvin Cross-Bridge  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Flow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Load Wafer & Chuck   │
│        Thermal        │
│  Stabilization 85°C   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Optical Pattern    │
│  Alignment & Contact  │
│       Touchdown       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   4-Wire Kelvin DC    │
│    Current Forcing    │
│   I_force: -1mA to    │
│         +1mA          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Differential Sense   │
│   V_sense & Kelvin    │
│    Extraction R_c     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Ohmic Linearity &   │
│   Current Crowding    │
│      Assessment       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Wafer Load & Thermal Chuck Pre-Conditioning:**
   - Load the 180nm process control monitor (PCM) wafer onto the automated prober vacuum chuck.
   - Set the thermal chuck temperature controller to **85.0°C ± 0.5°C** (calibrated to the DRAM standard junction retention qualification baseline).
   - Allow thermal soak stabilization for ≥ 3 minutes to eliminate drift in test probe positioning.

2. **Automated Optical Alignment & Prober Touchdown:**
   - Execute prober optical pattern recognition (PR) on the Kelvin cross-bridge pad group (4-pad Kelvin layout: $I^+$, $I^-$, $V^+$, $V^-$).
   - Set probe tip z-axis overdrive to nominal **35 µm to 45 µm** past the initial electrical contact touchdown point to break the native aluminum/copper pad oxide without punch-through into lower dielectric layers.

3. **SMU Cabling & Triaxial Guard Setup:**
   - Connect four source-measure unit (SMU) channels with guarded triaxial cables configured in true 4-wire Kelvin topology:
     - **SMU 1 ($I^+$):** Force current path into the upper metal runner (W-plug top contact).
     - **SMU 2 ($I^-$):** Current return path via the orthogonal lower diffusion/active area arm ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
     - **SMU 3 ($V^+$):** High-impedance sense ($R_{in} > 10^{13}\,\Omega$) at the top potential tap.
     - **SMU 4 ($V^-$):** High-impedance sense at the lower diffusion potential tap.

4. **Automated DC I-V Sweep Execution:**
   - Apply a symmetrical bipolar current sweep across SMU 1 and SMU 2:
     - Sweep Range: **$-1.0\text{ mA}$ to $+1.0\text{ mA}$** in step sizes of **$50\ \mu\text{A}$**.
     - Compliance Voltage Limit: Set to **$2.0\text{ V}$** to prevent barrier dielectric puncture or localized thermal runaway.
     - SMU Integration Time: Set to **1 NPLC (Number of Power Line Cycles)** for high signal-to-noise resolution.
   - Concurrently acquire high-precision differential voltage $V_{\text{sense}} = V^+ - V^-$ across SMU 3 and SMU 4 at every current step.

5. **Specific Contact Resistance Extraction & Current Crowding Assessment:**
   - Calculate Kelvin contact resistance:
     $$R_c = \frac{\mathrm{d}V_{\text{sense}}}{\mathrm{d}I_{\text{force}}}$$
   - Fit the linear slope over the range $[-500\ \mu\text{A}, +500\ \mu\text{A}]$ to verify Ohmic contact behavior.
   - Check the Pearson correlation coefficient ($r^2$) of the I-V slope; deviations from linearity indicate non-uniform current crowding across the 180 nm contact interface or barrier diode formation.
   - Automatically log data arrays into the metrology database for TCAD compact model SPICE calibration.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Tolerance / Bounds | Engineering Justification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Prober Chuck Temperature** | $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ | DRAM thermal qualification baseline condition for retention/leakage reliability. |
| **Probe Overdrive Travel** | $40\ \mu\text{m}$ | $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ (Bounds: $35\ \mu\text{m} \le z \le 45\ \mu\text{m}$) | Assures low contact probe resistance without damaging test pads. |
| **Kelvin I-V Linearity ($r^2$)** | $\ge 0.9990$ | Dimensionless ($0.9990 \le r^2 \le 1.0000$) | Confirms Ohmic behavior across the W-plug interface without Schottky rectification. |
| **Kelvin DC Extraction Current** | $\pm 1.0\text{ mA}$ | Sweep step: $50\ \mu\text{A} \pm 0.1\ \mu\text{A}$ | Sufficient dynamic range for extraction while avoiding electromigration. |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

* **Source 1: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench***
  - *Context applied:* Unit cell geometry of access transistor ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$); stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture erected above drain contact via tungsten plug (W-plug); thermal retention evaluation at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
* **Source 2: *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering***
  - *Context applied:* 180nm cell retention baseline standard evaluated at $85^\circ\text{C}$ for 1T1C storage node stack.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated DC probing of micro-scale Kelvin cross-bridge structures (active area ~0.18 um x 0.18 um to 1.0 um x 1.0 um) requires strict triaxial shielding and low-current triaxial matrix switching to mitigate cable leakage and guard parasitic capacitance. A primary vulnerability is series cable/probe contact resistance and thermal electromotive force (EMF) corrupting sub-ohm extraction of W-plug contact resistance (Rc). The automated SMU firmware must implement pulsed DC or current-reversal techniques to null thermoelectric offsets, while maintaining compliance voltage limits below 0.5 V to prevent electrical overstress (EOS) punch-through of ultra-thin barrier layers (Ti/TiN).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Kelvin resistor test structures decouple lead and pad resistance, but 2D current crowding at the metal-to-diffusion/polysilicon boundary causes extraction errors if contact area aspect ratio deviates from TCAD design. Probing contact pads must account for probe-tip scrub damage on top aluminum/copper metallization without punching through to underlying inter-layer dielectric (ILD). Automated I-V sweeps must maintain strict linearity across +/-1 mA to +/-10 mA to verify true Ohmic contact behavior versus Schottky barrier modulation or non-linear Joule heating effects.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Tungsten carbide and beryllium copper cantilever or vertical probe cards face mechanical wear and tip oxidation after ~50,000 touchdowns. Sourcing replacement ceramic-blade probe cards with pitch down to 50 um pads incurs high lead times (12-16 weeks) under current global foundry metrology supply constraints. Automated probe tip cleaning protocols using abrasive ceramic pads (e.g., Al2O3 lapping sheets) must be scheduled every 250 touchdowns to prevent tip buildup and contact variability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test cell throughput directly dictates inline lot cycle time: executing 9-point or 25-point wafer mapping with 100-point bidirectional DC sweeps per Kelvin structure risks exceeding the metrology queue allocation of 18 minutes per 200mm wafer. Parameter extraction algorithms must be executed locally on the prober controller rather than post-processed in cloud pipelines to deliver real-time go/no-go wafer lot disposition before back-end passivation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-scrub over-travel causing mechanical punch-through of bond pads into ILD3/metal-1 layers, creating substrate leakage shorts.
1. Joule heating-induced electromigration or contact sintering during continuous DC sweeps exceeding 15 mA, permanently altering native TiSi2/W-plug contact resistivity.
1. Moisture-assisted probe tip oxidation and aluminum native oxide (Al2O3) accumulation leading to high contact resistance and false non-linear I-V sweeps.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Step probe station to Kelvin test structure pad coordinates (Force+, Force-, Sense+, Sense-). 2. Lower probe platen with 30 um nominal overdrive/scrub. 3. Force DC current sweep from -5.0 mA to +5.0 mA in 0.1 mA increments across Force+ and Force- terminals. 4. Measure differential voltage V_sense across Sense+ and Sense- using high-impedance sense SMU (input impedance > 10^13 ohms). 5. Compute slope dV/dI via least-squares linear regression to extract Kelvin resistance R_k. 6. Multiply R_k by active contact area A_c (0.18 um x 0.18 um) to determine specific contact resistivity rho_c. | `Contact resistance R_k must be within 12.0 ohm to 28.0 ohm (target: 18.5 ohm). Specific contact resistivity rho_c must be <= 6.0 x 10^-8 ohm-cm^2. Linear regression goodness of fit R^2 >= 0.9995 between -2.0 mA and +2.0 mA (no non-Ohmic curvature).` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-3-1-02` | **Kelvin Probe Contact Repeatability & Delta-I Current Crowding Boundary Verification** | Keysight B1500A SMU module, semi-automatic probe station with programmable touchdown counter, integrated optical microscope with pattern recognition autofocus. | 1. Perform 10 consecutive probe touchdowns on fresh qualification Kelvin pads with 25 um overdrive. 2. At each touchdown, apply pulsed current (pulse width 500 us, period 10 ms) at +1 mA and -1 mA. 3. Verify probe scrub mark dimensions post-test via inline optical pattern inspection. | `Touchdown resistance repeatability standard deviation sigma(R_k) <= 0.45 ohm across 10 cycles. Current crowding resistance deviation Delta_Rc <= 4.0% between 1 mA and 10 mA. Scrub mark depth must not exceed 120 nm (less than 25% of top metal pad thickness).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (powder-free, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and conductive ESD footwear, Grounded wrist strap with 1 Mohm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Wash affected skin thoroughly with deionized water and soap for 15 minutes. Eye exposure to IPA: Flush eyes at dedicated cleanroom eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes with eyelids held open; seek medical evaluation if irritation persists. Inhalation of N2 / asphyxiation hazard: Immediately remove victim to fresh outdoor air, administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored, and summon emergency medical team.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station enclosed in laminar flow hood maintaining positive-pressure ISO Class 4 clean air. Local chemical exhaust ventilation (100 FPM face velocity) on IPA manual wipe station. Continuous ambient oxygen deficit monitoring (alarm threshold set at 19.5% O2) in prober bay due to high-volume N2 purge.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA cleanroom wipes and swabs must be segregated in dedicated hazardous solvent waste bins with self-closing foot-operated lids and flame arrestors. Collect and dispose via licensed hazardous waste incinerator facility; do not dump into fab acid/solvent drains.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry post-CMP and deoxidized contact pads; native oxide thickness on Al-Cu/TiN probing pads < 1.5 nm, verified via inline spectroscopic ellipsometry.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Scrubbed pad metal surface with intact barrier underlayer; free of particle debris (> 0.2 um count = 0), ready for passivation layer deposition or post-probing bake.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure beyond 120 minutes promotes native oxide re-growth (Al2O3/TiO2) and atmospheric hydrocarbon adsorption on open contact pads, driving probe contact resistance erratic (> 50 ohms) and yielding erroneous TCAD calibration parameters.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full automated DC I-V characterization and parameter extraction completed across 25 field locations on the 200mm test wafer. Verified Ohmic linearity, specific contact resistivity (rho_c) for W-to-TiN/diffusion plugs, and contact crowding factors, delivering calibrated SPICE contact resistance sub-circuits for 180nm DRAM cell storage node simulation.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Current Crowding & Geometric Correction Factor Analytical Sheet Resistance Extraction

- **Task**: Current Crowding & Geometric Correction Factor Analytical Sheet Resistance Extraction
- **Scope & Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout ($8F^2$) > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling > COB Storage Node Contact & W-Plug Contact Resistance TCAD Modeling > Kelvin Structure Parasitic Contact Resistance & Current Crowding TCAD Extraction > Four-Point Kelvin Cross-Bridge Resistance Parameter Extraction & SPICE Calibration > Current Crowding & Geometric Correction Factor Analytical Sheet Resistance Extraction
- **Technology Generation**: Gen 2 ($\mu$m) / 180nm Node
- **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Methodology

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Analytical Extraction Procedure

1. **Test Structure Setup & Boundary Parameter Verification**:
   - Establish Kelvin Cross-Bridge Sheet Resistor (CBKR) test layout dimensions based on cell critical dimensions: contact size $d = 180\text{ nm}$ (matching access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$), diffusion/bridge tap width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, and pitch $\approx 360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Ensure thermal environment is stabilized at baseline chuck temperatures ($25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ for ambient or $85.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ for high-temperature DRAM retention verification).

2. **Kelvin Four-Terminal Current Forcing & Voltage Sensing**:
   - Inject positive forward DC current $I_F = 10.0\ \mu\text{A}$ through Terminal 1 (diffusion tap) down to Terminal 2 (W-plug/metal bridge) while maintaining reverse polarity check ($-10.0\ \mu\text{A}$) to eliminate thermoelectric EMF offsets.
   - Measure the sensed potential drop $V_M$ between high-impedance sense terminals (Terminal 3 on diffusion and Terminal 4 on top metal) using an electrometer/SMU input impedance $> 10^{13}\ \Omega$.
   - Calculate measured Kelvin resistance:
     $$R_{\text{meas}} = \frac{V_M(+I_F) - V_M(-I_F)}{2 \cdot I_F}$$

3. **Current Crowding & Geometric Ratio Formulation**:
   - Extract the dimensional boundary ratio $\delta = d / W = 180\text{ nm} / 220\text{ nm} \approx 0.818$.
   - Compute the analytical 2D sheet resistance correction factor $F_G(\delta)$ representing the non-uniform current flow at the contact periphery:
     $$F_G = \left[ 1 + \left(\frac{4}{\pi}\right) \left(\frac{W}{d}\right) \ln\left(\frac{4}{\pi \delta}\right) \right]^{-1}$$
   - When extraction involves cross-bridge sheet resistance strips ($L_s \gg W$), extract nominal uncorrected sheet resistance $R_{sq,\text{raw}} = \frac{\pi}{\ln(2)} \cdot \frac{\Delta V}{I_F}$.

4. **Analytical Contact Resistance ($R_c$) De-embedding**:
   - Compute the true sheet resistance $R_{sq} = R_{sq,\text{raw}} \cdot C_{\text{geom}}$, where $C_{\text{geom}}$ corrects for finite bridge arm widths.
   - Extract parasitic current-crowded interface contribution:
     $$R_c = R_{\text{meas}} - R_{\text{parasitic}}(F_G, R_{sq})$$
   - Formulate specific contact resistivity $\rho_c$ via 1D transmission line transfer length $\ell_t = \sqrt{\rho_c / R_{sq}}$.

5. **SPICE Parameter Calibration & Record Export**:
   - Fit extracted $R_{sq}$ and $R_c$ to the 180nm COB storage node contact SPICE sub-circuit model.
   - Export calibrated parameters into the BSIM/PDK deck for cell RC timing simulation (verifying retention window $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ and sense amp $\Delta V \ge 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Acceptance Window | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Kelvin Sense Current ($I_F$) Compliance** | $10.0$ | $\pm 0.1$ | $\mu\text{A}$ | Parameter Analyzer SMU Ammeter |
| **Contact Dimension Ratio ($d/W$)** | $0.818$ ($180\text{ nm} / 220\text{ nm}$) | $\pm 0.025$ | Dimensionless | In-line CD-SEM Metrology |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature Stability** | $85.0$ | $\pm 0.5$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Integrated RTD Thermocouple Controller |
| **Analytical $F_G$ Geometric Correction Residual** | $\le 2.0$ | Max $\pm 0.5$ | $\%$ | Analytical Model vs. Numerical 2D TCAD |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Access transistor channel dimensions: length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node W-plug contact topology erected above the drain contact.
  - Temperature baseline specification of $85^\circ\text{C}$ for leakage and retention targets.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - $8F^2$ cell layout architecture with bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
  - Minimum retention time requirement $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ with cell capacitance budget of $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
  - Differential signal development requirement of $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ across bitline network under cell capacitance $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and bitline load $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In standard Cross-Bridge Kelvin Resistor (CBKR) and TLM layouts for 180nm node features, current crowding along the diffusion-to-contact boundary causes serious parasitic 2D potential distortion. An uncorrected analytical model overestimates true contact resistance Rc by treating current injection as purely 1D, propagating artificial IR drop delays into DRAM bitline and storage node RC delay compact models.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Geometric correction factor (delta_geo) extraction must rigorously decouple sheet resistance Rs of the diffused N+ silicon bridge from the specific contact resistivity rho_c. At 180nm dimensions where contact window d_c approaches active line width W, 2D conformal mapping or finite-difference numerical correction is mandatory to avoid parasitic sheet resistance cross-talk in extracted transfer length LT.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electrical parametric testing (E-test) throughput relies heavily on automated probe card card-pitch consistency and wafer prober chuck repeatability. If automated parameter extraction algorithms require excessive iterations or custom Kelvin configurations without standard 4-point pinouts, testing costs escalate and cycle time for inline metrology lots is severely compromised.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Delivery of calibrated SPICE compact models for cell access transistors and storage node contacts is gating tapeout milestone M2. The analytical correction factor engine must be verified and implemented in automated test extraction pipelines without delaying scheduled wafer prober inline measurement windows.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Current crowding-induced geometric overestimation of contact resistance Rc exceeding 25%, causing false failure in contact engineering signoff.
1. Misalignment between active diffusion and tungsten plug mask distorting effective Kelvin tap width W and skewing correction factor delta_geo beyond analytical limits.
1. Probe-contact pad degradation and localized joule heating during continuous current ramping causing non-ohmic I-V curves and erroneous Rs extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-3-2-01` | **Cross-Bridge Kelvin Resistor Geometric Correction Factor and Sheet Resistance Parameter Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with high-resolution SMU modules (HRSMU) and Cascade Microtech 200mm semi-automated probe station. | 1. Force current I_force from Pad 1 (active diffusion tap) to Pad 2 (metal interconnect) stepped from -1.0 mA to +1.0 mA in 50 uA increments. 2. Simultaneously sense differential voltage V_sense across Pad 3 (diffusion voltage tap) and Pad 4 (metal voltage tap) with input impedance > 10^13 Ohms. 3. Measure sheet resistance Rs_bridge independently on adjacent van der Pauw cross structure. 4. Calculate raw Kelvin resistance R_K = dV/dI. 5. Apply 2D analytical conformal correction: R_c_corrected = R_K - (Rs_bridge * delta_geo), where delta_geo accounts for contact edge-to-tap overlap geometry. | `Linear regression R^2 of I-V curve >= 0.9999; calculated geometric correction factor delta_geo matches TCAD conformal benchmark within +/- 3.0%; extracted corrected Rc <= 15.0 Ohms/contact.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-1-3-3-2-02` | **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) Transfer Length and Specific Contact Resistivity Verification** | Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer configured with 4-terminal preamplifiers and micro-manipulator probe tips (tungsten carbide, 5 um radius). | 1. Perform 4-point Kelvin I-V sweep (-500 uA to +500 uA) between consecutive TLM pads (width W = 100 um) across gap spacings d = [5, 10, 20, 40, 80] um. 2. Extract total resistance R_T for each gap spacing from the inverse slope of the linear I-V region. 3. Perform linear least-squares regression of R_T versus pad gap distance d: R_T = (Rs / W) * d + 2 * R_c. 4. Extract diffusion sheet resistance Rs from slope * W. 5. Determine transfer length LT from x-intercept (-2 * LT) and compute specific contact resistivity rho_c = R_c * W * LT. | `TLM linear regression coefficient R^2 >= 0.9995 across all 5 spacing increments; extracted diffusion sheet resistance Rs = 35.0 +/- 3.5 Ohms/sq; specific contact resistivity rho_c <= 1.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Cleanroom ESD conductive smock and conductive ESD heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with solvent (IPA), flush affected area immediately with clean deionized water or saline solution for at least 15 minutes at cleanroom eye-wash station. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, immediately move personnel to fresh ambient air and seek occupational medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station housing must be connected to local cleanroom exhaust ducting operating at minimum 50 CFM face velocity; automated N2 purge box must feature passive pressure-relief venting to prevent asphyxiation hazard in micro-environments.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-wetted wipes and micro-swabs in designated flame-retardant, grounded hazardous solvent solid-waste containers. Liquid IPA waste must be segregated into clearly labeled solvent-carboys for off-site hazardous waste incineration; no drain disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly patterned and etched aluminum/copper contact pads with native oxide thickness < 1.0 nm post-solvent clean.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-tested contact pads sealed with dry N2 blow-off, showing minimal probe scrub mark depth (< 15% metal thickness) and zero organic contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time promotes uncontrolled native aluminum/copper oxidation on probe landing pads, creating non-linear Schottky-like contact resistance, probe tip fouling, and irrecoverable measurement artifacts in Kelvin extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Delivery of an experimentally validated, mathematically rigorous analytical model and extraction pipeline for geometric correction factors (delta_geo) on 180nm CBKR and TLM structures, successfully isolating genuine contact resistivity from current crowding distortions and updating SPICE parameter decks.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `kelvin_current_crowding_correction_report.pdf`
- [ ] `cbkr_tlm_sheet_resistance_extraction_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `wafer_level_contact_resistivity_distribution_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Diffusion sheet resistance extracted via corrected CBKR matches independent 4-point probe TLM extraction** | `35.0 Ohm/sq` | +/- 5.0% | Automated regression cross-validation against independent van der Pauw and TLM structures across 9 wafer sites |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Specific contact resistivity (rho_c) for W-plug to N+ diffusion boundary** | `8.5e-8 Ohm*cm^2` | <= 1.0e-7 Ohm*cm^2 | Analytical transfer length calculation combined with 2D conformal current crowding de-embedding |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Geometric correction factor delta_geo correlation to finite-difference TCAD electrostatic simulation** | `0.185` | +/- 0.010 | Numerical 2D Laplace equation solver comparing analytical conformal mapping output against simulated potential fields |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Statistical confirmation of R^2 >= 0.9995 across all 9 measured wafer locations, validation of delta_geo against TCAD reference models within specified 5% tolerance, and formal signoff of calibrated contact resistance parameters into the 180nm DRAM Foundation VN PDK SPICE subcircuits.
