Measure parallel capacitance Cp and conductance Gp at 100 kHz with 0.0 V DC bias. 3. Move probe pair A to On-Wafer Short dummy structure and measure series resistance Rs and inductance Ls at 1 MHz. 4. Land on 100-cell parallel crown capacitor test structure (target >= 2.80 pF total, representing >= 28 fF/cell) and extract raw C-V from -1.5 V to +1.5 V. 5. Apply two-step de-embedding equation: C_cell = (Cp_raw - Cp_open) / 100.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: On-wafer Open stray capacitance Cp_open must be <= 12.0 fF at 100 kHz; de-embedded single-cell capacitance at 0.0 V bias must be >= 28.0 fF with dissipation factor D <= 0.015.

ppe_required: Cryogenic safety gloves (EN 511 rated)
Full-face polycarbonate impact/cryo shield
Cryogenic thermal apron
Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 under-gloves)
Closed-toe ESD static-dissipative safety shoes
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For cryogenic burns/frostbite: Flush immediately with tepid water (40-42 C), do not rub tissue; cover with sterile dressing and seek immediate medical evaluation. In case of inert gas asphyxiation/oxygen depletion: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration and supplemental oxygen if trained; call emergency response.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous dual ambient oxygen depletion monitors with dual-threshold acoustic alarms (amber at 19.5% O2, evacuation red at 18.0% O2); dedicated vacuum pump exhaust piped directly to house scrubber ductwork at >= 50 SCFM.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Exhausted cryogenic boil-off routed through vacuum relief manifold to ambient vaporization stack. Spent IPA solvent collected in dedicated flammables carboys for hazardous chemical waste reclamation.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Freshly post-metallization annealed and solvent-cleaned pad surface, free of organic residues and native oxide thickness < 1.0 nm on top probe pads.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Vacuum-baked and desorbed test pad surface with controlled probe micro-scrub indentations (< 15 um length, < 0.5 um depth), stored in sealed dry N2 carrier box.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Moisture absorption and ambient oxidation of landing pads elevate series contact resistance beyond 1.5 Ohms, causing phase error in high-frequency admittance measurements and false failure of EOT targets.

expected_result.summary: Completed verified thermal/cryo open-short calibration baseline and extraction of de-embedded crown capacitor test structures across 77 K to 398 K, ensuring intrinsic cell capacitance meets or exceeds the 28.0 fF/cell design threshold.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title**: Multi-Frequency High-Frequency (10 kHz – 1 MHz) & Quasi-Static C-V Sweep Recipe Execution
- **Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack
- **Action Type**: Make / Characterize
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)

---

## 1. Process Flowchart

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Wafer Load & Thermal  │
│     Stabilization      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Open/Short Cable &   │
│    Tip De-Embedding    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Quasi-Static C-V    │
│  Ramp: -1.8V to +1.8V  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Multi-Frequency C-V:  │
│   10 kHz, 100 kHz, 1   │
│          MHz           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Parameter        │
│  Extraction: C_cell &  │
│          EOT           │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Station Setup & Thermal Stabilization**:
   - Secure the 180nm test wafer onto the semi-automatic prober chuck under light-shielded, dark-box enclosure.
   - Set chuck temperature to **85°C** (thermal stress baseline for 64 ms retention certification) and allow temperature to stabilize for at least 15 minutes.
2. **De-Embedding & Calibration**:
   - Perform two-terminal Open/Short/Load calibration at the probe-card needle tips to de-embed coaxial cable parasitic capacitance, series resistance ($R_s$), and contact resistance on dedicated test structures.
3. **Quasi-Static (QS) C-V Sweep**:
   - Connect the High-Voltage electrometer/SMU channel to the capacitor top plate node and Low to the bottom contact plug (W-plug test pad).
   - Execute linear voltage staircase ramp from **$-1.8\text{ V}$ to $+1.8\text{ V}$** at a controlled ramp rate ($dV/dt = 0.05\text{ V/s}$) to measure the quasi-static equilibrium capacitance profile ($I_{QS} = C \cdot dV/dt$) and detect mobile charge / slow interface traps ($D_{it}$).
4. **Multi-Frequency High-Frequency (HF) C-V Sweeps**:
   - Configure the LCR / Impedance Analyzer meter using parallel equivalent model ($C_p - G_p$) with an AC oscillator amplitude of **$25\text{ mV}_{\text{rms}}$**.
   - Execute DC bias sweeps from **$-1.8\text{ V}$ to $+1.8\text{ V}$** sequentially across discrete probe frequencies:
     - **10 kHz**: Low-frequency dispersion check.
     - **100 kHz**: Mid-band reference curve.
     - **1 MHz**: High-frequency bulk accumulation capacitance extraction.
5. **Parameter Extraction & Validation**:
   - Extract maximum accumulation capacitance $C_{\text{cell}}$ from the accumulation regime at 1 MHz.
   - Calculate Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) using $EOT = \frac{\epsilon_{\text{SiO2}} \cdot \epsilon_0 \cdot A}{C_{\text{cell}}}$ considering the crown 3D cylinder surface area and dielectric permittivity ($\kappa > 15$).
   - Confirm cell retention budget feasibility against the 1 fA/cell leakage envelope at 85°C.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                    Metrology Target Thresholds         
           ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
           │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Temp (degC)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
   EOT (nm)┤▒▒▒                                        │
           │▒▒▒                                        │
C_cell (fF)┤███████████████                            │
           │███████████████                            │
           └┬──────────┬─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬┘
           0.0       21.2      42.5       63.8     85.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance / Window | Units | Verification Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $28.0\text{ to }30.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | 1 MHz HF C-V Meter ($C_p$) |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | $3.5$ | $3.0\text{ to }4.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | Extracted from accumulation $C_{\text{cell}}$ |
| **Metrology Chuck Temperature** | $85.0$ | $\pm 0.5$ | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ | Thermal Chuck Controller |
| **Dielectric Leakage Current** | $< 1.0$ | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-femtoamp Electrometer / SMU at 85°C |

---

## 4. Context References & Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *Crown-shaped capacitor with ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ high-k stack ($\kappa > 15$)*.
  - *Minimum $28\text{ fF}$ per cell capacitance budget for soft-error noise immunity*.
  - *Sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^{\circ}\text{C}$*.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *1T1C stacked capacitor target $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ per cell to ensure data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^{\circ}\text{C}$*.
  - *Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) window of $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ utilizing $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$*.
- **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
  - *Differential charge sharing relationship $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s} (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{DD}/2)$ confirming signal readout sensitivity requirements*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Extracting equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) and cell capacitance (>=28 fF) across high-frequency (10 kHz - 1 MHz) and quasi-static regimes on a 180nm 3D crown capacitor array requires de-embedding parasitic cable capacitance, chuck stray admittance, and series resistance (Rs). At 1 MHz, series resistance attenuation severely distorts measured capacitance in accumulation unless a rigorous two-frequency or five-element impedance correction model is mapped directly onto the SMU/LCR firmware.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Quasi-static capacitance measurement on high-k Ta2O5 / ONO dielectric stacks is prone to displacement current corruption by excessive DC leakage (I_leak > 1 nA/cm²). The integration ramp rate (dV/dt) must be constrained between 10 mV/s and 100 mV/s to ensure quasi-equilibrium without swamping the pA-level displacement signal, and interface trap density (Dit) extraction via the Castagné-Vapaille high-low frequency method must account for slow trap responses in Ta2O5.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Requires a calibrated precision LCR meter (Keysight E4980A or B1500A with MFCMU and HRSMU units), low-noise triaxial cables, and beryllium-copper or tungsten probe tips (tip radius <= 5 µm). Lead times for micro-chamber triaxial feedthroughs and replacement probe tips currently sit at 6-8 weeks; thermal drift in unchilled probe stations can exceed 1 µm/hour, necessitating localized vibration-isolation tables.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Recipe execution must not become a metrology bottleneck; automated step-and-repeat wafer mapping across 9 site locations (center, middle, edge) must finish within 45 minutes per wafer. De-embedding calibration routines (open/short/load) must be verified prior to each lot run to prevent downstream scrap of the entire 180nm metallization lot.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Series resistance (Rs) masking and phase angle drop below 80 degrees at 1 MHz, causing artificial roll-off of apparent accumulation capacitance and gross underestimation of dielectric constant.
1. Dielectric leakage current exceeding displacement charging current during quasi-static sweep, resulting in non-physical negative capacitance or asymptotic runaway in the extracted C-V curve.
1. Probe contact punch-through or micro-scrub damage fracturing the top TiN/polysilicon plate of the fragile high-aspect-ratio 3D crown cylinder.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-2-2-01` | **Multi-Frequency High-Frequency (10 kHz - 1 MHz) C-V Accumulation & Depletion Sweep** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A MFCMU, low-noise triaxial probe station in dark, Faraday-shielded enclosure, 5 µm W-probe tips. | 1. Land probes on top electrode (TiN) pad and bottom common plate pad using micro-manipulators with contact resistance < 5 Ohms. 2. Configure MFCMU in Cp-Rp mode with AC oscillation level of 30 mV RMS. 3. Perform DC bias sweep from -2.0 V to +2.0 V in 25 mV increments with hold time 2.0 s and delay time 100 ms. 4. Record high-frequency curves at 10 kHz, 100 kHz, and 1 MHz. 5. Apply two-frequency series resistance de-embedding to extract true oxide capacitance (Cox). | `Array total capacitance normalized per cell C_cell >= 28.0 fF at V_bias = 1.0 V (100 kHz), loss tangent tan(delta) < 0.05 across 10 kHz - 100 kHz, and phase angle theta > 82 degrees in strong accumulation.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-2-2-02` | **Quasi-Static C-V Ramp & Interface Trap Density (Dit) Extraction** | Keysight B1500A with B1517A High Resolution SMU (HRSMU) or 4156C Precision Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer, dark box ambient. | 1. Connect Force/Sense triaxial lines to top and bottom plates. 2. Configure linear staircase voltage ramp from -1.5 V to +1.5 V at a ramp rate dV/dt = 50 mV/s. 3. Measure quasi-static displacement current I_qs with fA-level resolution: C_qs = I_qs / (dV/dt). 4. Combine high-frequency 100 kHz C-V curve from TC-01 with C_qs curve using the high-low frequency method to extract Dit: Dit = (Cox / q) * [ (C_qs / (Cox - C_qs)) - (C_hf / (Cox - C_hf)) ]. | `Minimum mid-gap interface state density Dit <= 5.0e11 eV^-1 cm^-2, equivalent oxide thickness EOT <= 3.2 nm (for Ta2O5/ONO composite stack), and curve hysteresis between forward and reverse sweeps Delta_Vfb <= 40 mV.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible, double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat and grounded wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with cleaning solvents (IPA), flush affected area immediately with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes. For inhalation of nitrogen gas displacement hazard, move victim to fresh air immediately and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station enclosure must maintain local laminar HEPA downflow (ISO Class 5) with exhaust vent velocity >= 100 LFM to exhaust solvent vapors and prevent N2 asphyxiation accumulation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and swabs contaminated with IPA must be segregated into dedicated sealed, flame-resistant hazardous waste bins under a certified solvent exhaust hood for hazardous solvent incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade | `> 99.8%` |
| **Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 Grade | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly patterned and annealed top electrode TiN/polysilicon test pads, free from organic residue and native surface moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-C-V probed pads showing micro-scrub witness marks (< 1.5 µm depth), blow-cleaned with filtered dry N2 and sealed in desiccator cassette.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture adsorption and airborne hydrocarbon condensation on unpassivated test pads cause anomalous surface leakage and false Dit humps (> 1e12 eV^-1 cm^-2), rendering EOT extraction inaccurate.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful execution of multi-frequency (10 kHz - 1 MHz) and quasi-static C-V profiling on 180nm crown capacitor test arrays, providing de-embedded EOT <= 3.2 nm, per-cell capacitance >= 28.0 fF, and low interface state density confirming dielectric stack viability.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `cv_multifreq_deembedded_raw_data.csv`
- [ ] `eot_dit_extraction_summary_report.pdf`
- [ ] `probe_mark_inspection_micrograph.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Extracted single-cell equivalent capacitance at 100 kHz in accumulation** | `28.5 fF` | +/- 1.5 fF | Measurement on 10k-cell test array divided by 10,000 after Rs and open/short de-embedding |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Extracted Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) of Ta2O5/ONO crown dielectric stack** | `3.0 nm` | +/- 0.2 nm | Calculated from Cox in strong accumulation (V_bias = 1.5 V) using standard permittivity epsilon_SiO2 = 3.9 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Mid-gap interface trap density (Dit)** | `3.5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2` | <= 5.0e11 eV^-1 cm^-2 | Castagné-Vapaille high-low frequency method comparing 100 kHz HF-CV and 50 mV/s QS-CV curves |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full automated sign-off requires all 9 wafer sites to exhibit C_cell >= 28.0 fF with goodness-of-fit R² >= 0.995 on de-embedded multi-frequency model, Dit <= 5.0e11 eV^-1 cm^-2, and zero structural collapse observed during post-probe microscopic inspection.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-DRAM180-CV-QM01
**Title:** Quantum Mechanical C-V Inversion Extraction for EOT, Flatband Voltage & Cell Capacitance Modeling ($\ge 28\text{ fF}$)  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | 8F² Crown-Type COB | Metrology & Device Modeling  
**Target Node:** 180nm (Gen 2)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP defines the metrology characterization and extraction procedure for high-accuracy equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), flatband voltage ($V_{\text{fb}}$), quantum-mechanical band-bending corrections, and final 3D crown storage node capacitance ($C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$) on 180nm 1T1C DRAM test structures.

---

### 2. Process Flow & Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Test Structure Loading & Calibration                                           |
|    - Load 180nm wafer with Crown Capacitor Array / Test MOS Diode onto chuck      |
|    - Execute open/short/load impedance calibration on LCR meter (10 kHz - 1 MHz)  |
+-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. High-Frequency & Quasi-Static C-V Acquisition                                  |
|    - Perform split multi-frequency C-V sweeps (-2.0 V to +2.0 V) at 25°C & 85°C   |
|    - Extract accumulation, depletion, and strong inversion capacitance profiles  |
+-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Quantum-Mechanical (QM) Inversion Modeling & EOT Fit                           |
|    - Solve 1D Schrödinger-Poisson equations for poly/metal gate and substrate QM  |
|      carrier confinement and centroid displacement Delta z_centroid               |
|    - Correct C_total = (1/C_diel + 1/C_qm_poly + 1/C_qm_sub)^-1 to extract EOT   |
|    - Determine V_fb and normalize to single 3D Crown Cell Area                     |
+-----------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Cell Capacitance & Signal Budget Verification                                  |
|    - Scale extracted capacitance per unit area to 3D crown cylinder aspect ratio  |
|    - Validate single-cell storage capacitance C_s >= 28 fF and evaluate Delta V   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Tool Setup and Impedance De-embedding
1. Mount the processed 180nm wafer containing large-area test macro capacitors and dense crown array test pads onto the temperature-controlled probe station chuck.
2. Set chuck temperature to $85^\circ\text{C}$ (worst-case retention baseline) and $25^\circ\text{C}$ (calibration baseline).
3. Connect precision LCR meter / semiconductor parameter analyzer probes using shielded Kelvin triaxial connections. Run Open/Short compensation to de-embed cable and contact parasitic capacitances.

#### Step 2: Multi-Bias C-V Sweep Acquisition
1. Apply DC bias voltage sweep from $-2.0\text{ V}$ to $+2.0\text{ V}$ with step size $\le 20\text{ mV}$ and AC oscillator amplitude $v_{\text{ac}} = 15\text{ mV}$.
2. Measure capacitance-voltage ($C$-$V$) and conductance-voltage ($G$-$V$) responses across test frequencies ($10\text{ kHz}$, $100\text{ kHz}$, and $1\text{ MHz}$).
3. Verify that series resistance correction is applied using conductance:
   $$C_{\text{corr}} = \frac{(G^2 + \omega^2 C_m^2) C_m}{G^2 + \omega^2 C_m^2 (1 - R_s G) - \omega^2 R_s C_m^2}$$

#### Step 3: Quantum Mechanical (QM) Correction & EOT/V_fb Extraction
1. Import corrected inversion and accumulation C-V curves into the Poisson-Schrödinger solver.
2. Account for quantum-mechanical finite carrier centroid offset ($\Delta z_{\text{centroid}}$) in the silicon substrate and polysilicon/metal gate:
   $$C_{\text{meas}}^{-1} = C_{\text{diel}}^{-1} + C_{\text{qm,inv}}^{-1} + C_{\text{poly}}^{-1}$$
3. Extract Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT):
   $$\text{EOT} = \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{SiO2}} \cdot \kappa}{\varepsilon_{\text{diel}}} \cdot t_{\text{phys}} = \varepsilon_{\text{SiO2}} \cdot A \cdot \left(\frac{1}{C_{\text{diel}}}\right)$$
4. Extract flatband voltage ($V_{\text{fb}}$) from the flatband capacitance $C_{\text{fb}}$ derived from Debye length screening calculations.

#### Step 4: 3D Crown Cell Capacitance Projection
1. Map extracted EOT and dielectric constant ($\kappa$) onto the 3D crown cylinder geometry (height, perimeter, inner/outer cylinder surfaces, and tungsten plug contact interface).
2. Compute single-cell capacitance $C_s$. Verify compliance with the differential readout signal margin:
   $$\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s} \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right)$$
   ensuring noise immunity against soft errors and bitline coupling.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Method / Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | $3.0\text{ nm}$ to $4.0\text{ nm}$ | Max $\le 4.0\text{ nm}$ | QM Poisson-Schrödinger C-V fit ($\text{nm}$) |
| **Cell Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28.0\text{ fF}$ | Min $\ge 28.0\text{ fF/cell}$ | Scaled 3D Crown Array C-V ($\text{fF/cell}$) |
| **Access Transistor Channel Geometry** | $L = 180\text{ nm},\; W = 220\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 5\%$ process window | Inline CD-SEM / Electrical Inversion ($\text{nm}$) |
| **Measurement Chuck Temperature** | $85^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermocouple chuck sensor ($^\circ\text{C}$) |

---

### 4. Context References
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Access transistor channel dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node capacitance requirement: minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ for soft-error immunity and bitline coupling suppression.
  - Temperature verification requirement: $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - EOT target for stacked crown/cylinder capacitors using high-$\kappa$ dielectric stacks: $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$.
  - Minimum storage capacitance boundary: $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ for data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**
  - Charge sharing and signal development equation: $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right)$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Extracting quantum-mechanical (QM) corrected C-V parameters on 3D crown capacitors introduces significant non-planar electrostatic fringing and polysilicon/substrate gate depletion effects. Classical 1D Poisson-Boltzmann inversion severely overestimates physical oxide thickness (underestimating EOT by 0.3-0.5 nm) due to charge centroid displacement (~1 nm away from the physical dielectric interface in accumulation/inversion). The extraction framework must couple Schrödinger-Poisson 1D/2D electrostatic solvers with the compact BSIM-CMG/BSIM4 model cards to avoid distorting cell retention budget simulations at the system 1T1C integration level.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For Ta2O5/ONO high-k dielectric stacks targeting >=28 fF/cell in an 8F² 180nm footprint, quantum inversion correction is vital to de-embed quantum confinement of the 2D electron gas (2DEG) at the storage node interface. High interface trap density (D_it > 1.0 x 10^11 cm^-2 eV^-1) and dielectric dispersion across 10 kHz to 1 MHz will distort flatband voltage (V_fb) extraction if high-low frequency frequency-dependent series resistance (R_s) and loss tangent (tan delta) corrections are omitted prior to applying the Hauser or Berkeley Quantum C-V simulator.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Multi-frequency LCR meters (Keysight E4980A / B1500A with WGFMU) and cryogenic/high-temperature prober chuck thermal controllers require dedicated calibration kits (open/short/load de-embedding substrates). Sourcing specialized tungsten or beryllium-copper sub-micron probe tips (tip radius <= 0.5 µm) and high-purity forming gas (N2/H2 95%/5%) for interface passivations is subject to a 6-to-8 week lead-time barrier in domestic Vietnamese fab networks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must balance the slow sweep rates required for quasi-static C-V (QSCV, < 50 mV/s to avoid deep depletion artifacts) with production indexing. The characterization pipeline must automate full-wafer 49-point C-V profiling, open/short parasitic fixture de-embedding, and QM fitting parameter exports within a strict 4-hour queue-time envelope post-metallization to prevent ambient surface charge drift from skewing the statistical baseline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Series resistance (R_s) and parasitic cabling capacitance masking the true accumulation capacitance C_ox, driving numerical instability in the quantum mechanical Schrödinger-Poisson solver.
1. Excessive dielectric tunneling leakage (J_leak > 1.0 x 10^-7 A/cm² at 1.0 V) in sub-4nm EOT Ta2O5/ONO stacks degrading the out-of-phase impedance component, which causes spurious flatband voltage extraction and unphysical negative D_it values.
1. Deep depletion generation under high-frequency sweeps due to inadequate minority carrier generation, corrupting the quasi-static inversion capacitance profile.

Feed de-embedded C-V curve into quantum mechanical Poisson-Schrödinger solver (Hauser model) incorporating non-parabolic band structure and gate depletion. 5. Extract quantum-corrected EOT, flatband voltage V_fb, and fixed oxide charge Q_f. | `Quantum-corrected EOT must be <= 3.80 nm with 49-point wafer standard deviation sigma <= 0.08 nm; Flatband voltage shift |Delta V_fb| <= 65 mV against theoretical metal-semiconductor work function difference (corresponding to Q_f / q < 5.0 x 10^10 cm^-2); D_it at midgap <= 1.0 x 10^11 cm^-2 eV^-1.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-2-3-02` | **Full Crown-Capacitor Array Inversion Capacitance Verification at Operating Bias** | Keysight B1500A with High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU) and B1520A MFCMU, Keithley 4200A-SCS with CVU, shielded probe card with coax/triax interface. | 1. Land multi-contact wedge probe card on 10,000-cell Crown Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) test array. 2. Apply DC bias sweep from 0.0 V to 1.8 V with AC perturbation signal of 15 mV RMS at 100 kHz. 3. Measure total array small-signal parallel capacitance C_p and dissipation factor D. 4. ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom-compliant nitrile gloves (double-gloved, accelerator-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Anti-static dissipative cleanroom smock and hood, Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) wrist strap with 1 Mohm integrated resistor and heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes at eyewash station. In case of inhalation of inert N2/forming gas purge resulting in asphyxiation or dizziness: Immediately remove victim to fresh uncontaminated air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has stopped. In case of localized thermal/cryogenic contact: Immerse affected area in lukewarm water bath (38-42 °C); do not apply direct radiant heat.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom air recirculating laminar flow hood with Class 1 ULPA filtration (air velocity 0.45 m/s ± 20%); dedicated point-of-use scrubbed exhaust for prober chamber solvent vapors (face velocity >= 0.5 m/s); continuous ambient O2 deficiency sensors and lower explosive limit (LEL) H2 monitors with audible/visual interlocks set at 19.5% O2 and 25% LEL H2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be discarded into FM-approved self-closing hazardous flammables waste receptacles. Spent chemical solvents routed to segregated volatile organic solvent drains for drum disposal. Forming gas purge routed through catalytic burn-box / inert dilution line prior to atmospheric discharge.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched and annealed top electrode metallization (TiN / poly-Si) following forming gas anneal (400 °C, 30 min, 5% H2/N2); passivated interface free of organic residues, native oxide regrowth, or fluorinated etch polymers.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized, non-destructively probed top-plate contacts free of probe-scrub particle contamination and gate punch-through punch marks; surface dry-nitrogen purged and desiccated ready for passivation dielectric deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure beyond 30 minutes in cleanroom air drives moisture absorption into high-k Ta2O5/ONO thin films and native oxide growth on contact pads, inducing flatband voltage hysteresis Delta V_fb > 120 mV, interface trap generation (Delta D_it > 5.0 x 10^11 cm^-2 eV^-1), and uncorrectable quantum inversion modeling divergence.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): High-Temperature (85°C) C-t Transient & Dielectric Leakage Relaxation Characterization

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) [DRAM Architecture] > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling [Circuit Design] > Crown-Type 3D Cylinder Geometry & High-k Ta2O5/ONO Dielectric Stack Optimization [Circuit Design] > C-V & C-t Metrology Extraction for EOT, Target Cell Capacitance (>=28 fF) & Dielectric Leakage Characterization [Metrology] > High-Temperature (85°C) C-t Transient & Dielectric Leakage Relaxation Characterization [Metrology]
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Buy

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Cell Capacitance Cs >= 28 fF, Read Margin Delta V >= 150 mV.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer / SPICE Verification.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Characterizing C-t transient and dielectric leakage relaxation at 85°C directly addresses the physical boundary condition for the JEDEC standard 64 ms refresh window. However, parasitic resistance from the bottom electrode contact and peripheral routing in a high-density 180nm crown capacitor array (target >=28 fF/cell) will introduce RC time constants that convolute true Poole-Frenkel or trap-assisted dielectric relaxation with circuit-level settling times. An open-short de-embedding test structure protocol on the wafer layout must be strictly enforced.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C (358 K), Ta2O5 / ONO dielectric stacks exhibit strong thermal activation of oxygen vacancies and trap states, causing Curie-von Schweidler power-law relaxation (J ~ t^-n) and transient displacement currents that emulate persistent leakage. If pulsed C-t metrology does not clearly decouple reversible dipole/dielectric polarization currents from non-reversible Fowler-Nordheim or Poole-Frenkel conduction at V_plate = 1.0 V (half-Vdd / operational bias), retention time modeling will severely underestimate cell storage capability.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-temperature automated wafer probers equipped with triaxial thermal chucks, dry nitrogen local enclosures, and femtoamp-resolution SMUs (e.g., Keysight B1500A/B1505A with WGFMU modules) suffer from tight maintenance calibration schedules and chuck thermal drift at 85°C. Spare high-temperature triaxial probe needles (BeCu or tungsten-rhenium) and dry N2 purge supplies must be secured in the Vietnamese pilot lab to avoid downtime during long C-t transient runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: C-t relaxation tests spanning 100 ms to 1000 s across multiple dies at 85°C create a critical metrology throughput bottleneck for Gen 2 verification. The test matrix must strictly budget sample sizes across wafer center, middle, and edge locations to prevent thermal-soak waiting cycles from extending the overall silicon characterization milestone schedule beyond the 10-day packaging release window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal expansion mismatch during 85°C soak causing triaxial probe tip skating, micro-scratching top-plate aluminum pads, or micro-cracking the thin 3D crown cylinder rim.
1. Moisture condensation or frost during post-85°C chuck cooling down to ambient room conditions without continuous N2 purge, causing surface ionic leakage across pad test gaps.
1. Dielectric soft-breakdown during sustained 85°C voltage stress inducing irreversible trap generation and localized leakage paths, corrupting subsequent transient relaxation extractions.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Apply initial bias pulse V_pre = 0.0 V for 5.0 s to discharge all residual trap charges. 2. Step bias voltage instantaneously to operating cell plate potential V_bias = +1.0 V (100 kHz AC oscillation level = 25 mV RMS). 3. Record transient capacitance C(t) continuously from t = 1.0 ms to t = 100 s with 1.0 ms sampling resolution. 4. Extract total cell capacitance normalized per cell at t = 64 ms. | `Cell capacitance C_cell(t = 64 ms) >= 28.0 fF/cell across >= 95% of tested dies at 85°C. Total capacitive relaxation drift Delta_C / C_0 between t = 1 ms and t = 100 s must be <= 6.5%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-02` | **85°C Dielectric Current Relaxation and Quiescent Leakage Characterization** | Keysight B1500A with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU, 1 fA resolution) connected via low-noise triaxial cables to micro-chamber probe station maintained at 85.0°C. | 1. Pre-condition structure with zero bias for 10 s. 2. Step voltage on top-plate contact to V_stress = +1.0 V (E-field ~2.5 to 3.0 MV/cm across EOT). 3. Measure transient current I(t) logarithmically from t = 10 ms to t = 300 s. 4. Fit relaxation exponent n in I(t) = I_0 * t^-n and determine steady-state leakage current density J_leak at t = 64 ms. | `Steady-state dielectric leakage current density J_leak at t = 64 ms (V = 1.0 V, 85°C) must be <= 1.0 x 10^-8 A/cm^2 (equivalent to cell leakage <= 1.5 fA/cell). Relaxation exponent n must satisfy 0.75 <= n <= 1.15 without soft-breakdown jumps (> 3 sigma current spikes).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-resistant safety gloves (rated >= 150°C) for hot chuck inspection, Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact splash safety goggles, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and grounded ESD wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn contact from probe chuck: immediately flush affected skin with cold potable water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves without medical direction. In case of liquid IPA splash into eyes: flush copiously at eye-wash station for 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation immediately. Nitrogen asphyxiation hazard: move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober chamber must maintain positive N2 purge exhaust ducting connected to the sub-fab general cleanroom exhaust at a minimum linear velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to avoid inert gas suffocation hazards and solvent vapor accumulation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent wipes soaked with IPA used for probe tip cleaning must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-retardant stainless-steel hazardous waste bins and routed to dedicated solvent incineration stream. No aqueous acid or basic neutralization required.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Sintered top metal (Al-Cu/TiN) pads with unblemished passivation openings; surface clean, free of organic residues, moisture, or aluminum native oxidation blooming.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pads post-85°C prober touch-down showing scrub marks <= 15% of pad area; no thermal oxidation discoloration or moisture condensed residues.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits leads to ambient atmospheric moisture absorption into open dielectric micro-voids and hygroscopic oxidation of aluminum test pads, inducing erratic parasitic contact resistance and pseudo-relaxation leakage shifts during 85°C testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical extraction and signoff of high-temperature (85°C) C-t capacitive transient retention and dielectric leakage current relaxation on 180nm 8F² crown-type cell arrays, proving retention capacitance >=28 fF/cell and leakage <= 1.0e-8 A/cm² at 64 ms.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `DRAM180_GEN2_Dielectric_Relaxation_I-t_WaferMap.csv`

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> A minimum of 36 dies across 3 qualification wafers show cell capacitance >= 28.0 fF/cell and leakage <= 1.5 fA/cell at 85°C at t = 64 ms, with confirmed linear Curie-von Schweidler relaxation (0.80 <= n <= 1.10) and zero thermal breakdown signatures signed off by Lead Metrology Engineer.

critics.systems_engineer: Characterizing C-t transient and dielectric leakage relaxation at 85°C directly addresses the physical boundary condition for the JEDEC standard 64 ms refresh window. However, parasitic resistance from the bottom electrode contact and peripheral routing in a high-density 180nm crown capacitor array (target >=28 fF/cell) will introduce RC time constants that convolute true Poole-Frenkel or trap-assisted dielectric relaxation with circuit-level settling times. An open-short de-embedding test structure protocol on the wafer layout must be strictly enforced.
critics.domain_expert: At 85°C (358 K), Ta2O5 / ONO dielectric stacks exhibit strong thermal activation of oxygen vacancies and trap states, causing Curie-von Schweidler power-law relaxation (J ~ t^-n) and transient displacement currents that emulate persistent leakage. If pulsed C-t metrology does not clearly decouple reversible dipole/dielectric polarization currents from non-reversible Fowler-Nordheim or Poole-Frenkel conduction at V_plate = 1.0 V (half-Vdd / operational bias), retention time modeling will severely underestimate cell storage capability.
critics.supply_chain: High-temperature automated wafer probers equipped with triaxial thermal chucks, dry nitrogen local enclosures, and femtoamp-resolution SMUs (e.g., Keysight B1500A/B1505A with WGFMU modules) suffer from tight maintenance calibration schedules and chuck thermal drift at 85°C. Spare high-temperature triaxial probe needles (BeCu or tungsten-rhenium) and dry N2 purge supplies must be secured in the Vietnamese pilot lab to avoid downtime during long C-t transient runs.
critics.laya_pm: C-t relaxation tests spanning 100 ms to 1000 s across multiple dies at 85°C create a critical metrology throughput bottleneck for Gen 2 verification. The test matrix must strictly budget sample sizes across wafer center, middle, and edge locations to prevent thermal-soak waiting cycles from extending the overall silicon characterization milestone schedule beyond the 10-day packaging release window.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermal Chuck Setup & Kelvin Prober Calibration for 85°C C-t Metrology

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180NM-042`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip)  
**Target Structure:** Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) / 1T1C 8F² Cell Array  
**Process Action Type:** Make / Metrology Calibration  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Chuck Thermal      │
│   Stabilization 85°C   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Kelvin Triaxial     │
│    Open/Short/Load     │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Thermal Expansion    │
│   Contact Alignment    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    C-t Transient &     │
│  Relaxation Metrology  │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Environmental & Thermal Shielding Setup:**
   - Engage the dark Faraday EMI shield box over the manual/semi-automatic Kelvin prober station.
   - Initiate continuous dry purge ($N_2$ or CDA) at $2.0 \text{ to } 5.0 \text{ SLPM}$ into the test chamber to prevent moisture condensation and frost during thermal cycles.

2. **Thermal Chuck Ramp & PID Stabilization:**
   - Power on the closed-loop thermal chuck controller; program setpoint temperature to $85.0^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Maintain a controlled thermal ramp rate ($< 10^\circ\text{C}/\text{min}$) to prevent thermal shock and chuck mechanical distortion.
   - Allow a minimum isothermal dwell time of 20 minutes at $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ to achieve steady-state thermal expansion across the chuck plate ($\Delta T \le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$).

3. **Kelvin Triaxial Cable & Impedance Analyzer Calibration:**
   - Connect gold-plated tungsten probe tips via guarded triaxial low-noise Kelvin cabling (Force/Sense) to the LCR / C-V meter (e.g., Keysight E4980A / B1500A MFCMU).
   - Execute Open/Short/Load calibration at $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ directly at the probe-tip plane using an impedance calibration standard substrate:
     - **Open Correction:** Probe tips lifted $50\,\mu\text{m}$ above contact pads to calibrate out stray fixture capacitance and cabling parasitic conductance.
     - **Short Correction:** Probes dropped on shorting gold pad to eliminate lead and contact series resistance ($R_s$).
     - Verify background baseline capacitance floor is $\le 1.0\text{ fF}$ and leakage noise current is $\le 0.1\text{ fA}$.

4. **Wafer Loading & Thermal Drift Offset Compensation:**
   - Vacuum-mount the 180nm DRAM test wafer onto the $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ chuck.
   - Allow 5 minutes thermal soak for wafer chuck equilibrium.
   - Re-align probe needles to the 180nm Crown-type test structure pads (bitline contact / plate electrode pads, pitch $\sim 360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$).
   - Set contact overdrive to $15\,\mu\text{m}$ to ensure stable Kelvin contact without puncturing the top electrode metal/W-plug contact.

5. **C-t Transient & Leakage Relaxation Metrology Verification:**
   - Apply a baseline DC step bias to simulate cell retention charging and record capacitance transient $C(t)$ over a window exceeding $> 64\text{ ms}$.
   - Monitor dielectric relaxation and junction leakage current at $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ to verify low-leakage performance under thermal stress.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Unit | Verification Tool / Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chuck Temperature Setpoint & Uniformity** | $85.0$ | $\pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Surface RTD / Thermocouple (Three-Zone Thermal Dynamics) |
| **Total Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $28.0 \text{ to } 30.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Kelvin C-V / C-t Metrology ($180\text{nm}$ Cell Layout Topology) |
| **Total Dielectric & Junction Leakage Current ($85^\circ\text{C}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Triaxial Guarded SMU ($180\text{nm}$ Cell Layout Topology) |
| **Retention Interval Measurement Window** | $> 64$ | $\ge 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | C-t Sampling Sweep Interval (Legacy $180\text{nm}$ Architecture) |

---

### 4. Literature & Context Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - *Basis for Capacitance & Leakage Targets:* Dictates the crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture with minimum capacitance budget of $\ge 28\text{ fF}$ per cell to resist soft errors and coupling, and target leakage current $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - *Basis for Retention Timing & Cell Geometry:* Specifies 1T1C $8\text{F}^2/6\text{F}^2$ cell design requiring $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ storage capacitance maintaining retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, utilizing crown/cylinder $Ta_2O_5$ or ONO dielectric with EOT $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ and bitline/wordline pitch around $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$.
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:**
  - *Basis for Thermal Uniformity & Ramp Control:* Informs the closed-loop PID temperature stabilization criteria of $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ to counteract thermal fluctuation and avoid micro-stress or thermal shock dislocation during test cycles.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integrating an 85°C thermal chuck with high-precision femtofarad-level C-t capacitance metrology creates severe systemic electro-thermal coupling. The thermo-electric Seebeck effect across bi-metallic Kelvin probe needle junctions (e.g., tungsten-rhenium or BeCu to aluminum/copper bond pads) induces parasitic microvolt DC offsets that skew quasi-static capacitance and C-t transient integration currents. Furthermore, thermal expansion mismatch between the prober chuck, wafer substrate, and micro-positioner platen introduces mechanical drift exceeding 0.5 µm/min during thermal ramp, threatening contact integrity and pad scrub degradation on sub-micron test pads.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, crown-type capacitor dielectric characterization (Ta2O5/ONO stacks) exhibits accelerated Frenkel-Poole emission and trap-assisted tunneling relaxation currents, obscuring true dielectric relaxation if probe contact resistance and chuck thermal gradients are uncalibrated. A 4-wire Kelvin configuration directly at the tip level is required to isolate series resistance (Rs < 1.5 Ω) and eliminate chuck contact impedance. Calibration must execute Open/Short/Load correction directly at 85°C using an on-chuck alumina substrate to de-embed triaxial cable capacitance and thermal phase shifts across the 1 kHz to 1 MHz LCR test frequency range.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying triaxial high-temperature Kelvin probe needles (rated >= 200°C with low-leakage guard rings < 20 fA at 85°C) and a gold-plated low-noise thermal chuck system faces lead times exceeding 14 to 18 weeks due to specialized ceramic/PTFE isolation parts. Standard commercial probe arms experience dielectric breakdown and high leakage in cable jackets above 60°C. Sourcing dual-channel precision thermal controllers with calibrated PT100/Type-K chuck RTDs and Faraday-shielded enclosure interfaces requires pre-allocating qualified secondary suppliers (e.g., FormFactor/MPI compatible triaxial Kelvin arm assemblies).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The buy-and-commission timeline for the 85°C thermal chuck and Kelvin prober setup threatens the critical path for Gen 2 DRAM crown capacitor signoff. Vendor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and on-site site acceptance testing (SAT) must explicitly bundle thermal stability qualification (+/- 0.1°C at 85°C) and femtoampere baseline noise floor verification. If calibration protocols and calibration substrate kits (CS-5/ISS) are not procured concurrently with the primary chuck hardware, physical C-t parameter extraction milestones will slip by at least 6 weeks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal chuck thermocouple gradient error leading to actual wafer temperature deviation > ±2.0°C from setpoint (85°C), distorting temperature-dependent Arrhenius extraction of dielectric leakage and retention time.
1. Thermo-mechanical drift of probe tips resulting in loss of Kelvin contact, contact pad punch-through, or lateral scraping of top electrode thin films during isothermal soak.
1. Triaxial cable dielectric degradation and guard leakage at 85°C causing the C-t background noise floor to exceed 50 fF, invalidating the detection of 28 fF target cell capacitance.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-1-01` | **Thermal Chuck Temperature Uniformity & Stability Qualification at 85°C** | Calibrated 9-point surface thermocouple wafer (Type-K/RTD array, NIST-traceable), Precision Multi-channel DMM (Keysight 34970A/34972A), Prober Thermal Controller with integrated PID loop | 1. Mount the 9-point thermocouple instrumented wafer onto the gold-plated vacuum chuck and engage 700 mbar vacuum hold-down. 2. Ramp the chuck temperature from 25.0°C to 85.0°C at 5°C/min. 3. Allow a 30-minute thermal stabilization soak at 85.0°C. 4. Continuously log temperature across all 9 spatial sensors (center, inner ring, outer perimeter) for 60 minutes at 1 Hz sample rate. | `Spatial temperature uniformity across all 9 points must remain within <= +/- 0.5°C at steady-state 85°C; temporal stability over 60 minutes must maintain standard deviation sigma <= 0.05°C with zero thermal runaway.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-1-02` | **Kelvin Prober 85°C Open/Short Residual De-embedding & Femtoamp Noise Floor Baseline** | Precision LCR Meter / Impedance Analyzer (Keysight E4980A or B1505A MFCMU), Semi-automatic Prober with Triaxial Kelvin manipulators and guarded needle tips, Alumina Calibration Substrate (ISS) | 1. Position dual Kelvin probe tips 50 µm above open contact pads on the 85°C calibration substrate; execute Open Calibration compensation across 1 kHz to 1 MHz. 2. Land Kelvin tips onto short standard pad with 5 µm overdrive; execute Short Calibration compensation (target Rs < 0.5 Ω). 3. Measure open-circuit residual capacitance (C-open) and leakage current (I-leak) at 1.0 V DC bias for 300 seconds at 85°C. 4. Measure short-circuit loop resistance stability over 10 consecutive landings. | `De-embedded background open-circuit parasitic capacitance baseline must measure <= 1.5 fF at 100 kHz; residual leakage current at 85°C must remain <= 100 fA at 1.0 V DC bias; Kelvin contact resistance repeatability across 10 touchdowns must satisfy delta-Rs <= 0.05 Ω.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-resistant safety gloves rated to >= 150°C (Kevlar or Nomex outer shell), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety spectacles with side shields, Class 100 / ISO 5 compatible ESD-safe cleanroom coat and conductive wrist strap, Powder-free cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved under thermal PPE during hot wafer handling)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn exposure: Immediately flood affected skin with cool, clean potable water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek cleanroom medical triage. IPA exposure: For eye contact, flush with emergency eyewash for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; for inhalation, move individual immediately to fresh air; notify EHS safety officer.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober chamber requires local dry N2 purge exhaust ducting operating at 15-25 SCFM to prevent local oxygen depletion and extract trace thermal outgassing. Cleanroom ambient air change rate minimum 60 ACH with calibrated oxygen deficiency monitors (O2 alarm trigger < 19.5% v/v).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and cleaning swabs must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant hazardous solvent bins labeled for organic solvent disposal; purge and vent gas is directly ducted to facility scrubber/exhaust lines in accordance with SEMI S2 guidelines.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI-C12) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-metal or top-plate conductive layer patterned with bare contact pads (e.g., TiN/W or Al-Cu alloy) free of organic residue, native oxide scrubbed or passivated.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probed test pads with verified scrub marks (< 10% pad area consumed, no cratering into underlying dielectric stack), thermally equilibrated back to 25°C in clean N2 purge.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure beyond 45 minutes induces moisture adsorption and airborne molecular hydrocarbon contamination on exposed high-k capacitor dielectrics, resulting in false interface trap density (Dit) spikes, contact resistance inflation, and spurious C-t relaxation transients during 85°C bias soak.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical installation, thermal calibration, and RF/Kelvin electrical de-embedding of the 85°C prober thermal chuck work package, providing validated instrumentation ready for crown-type Ta2O5/ONO DRAM capacitor C-V/C-t metrology with femtoampere baseline resolution.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `kelvin_prober_open_short_deembedding_matrix_85C.pdf`
- [ ] `baseline_capacitance_leakage_noise_floor_log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Kelvin probe 4-wire open-circuit residual parasitic capacitance at 85°C across 10 kHz - 1 MHz** | `0.0 fF` | <= 1.5 fF | Precision LCR meter with calibrated Open/Short correction on alumina calibration substrate in dark enclosure |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Kelvin tip contact series resistance on aluminum/tungsten calibration test pads under 5 um overdrive** | `0.35 Ohm` | <= 0.50 Ohm | 4-point Kelvin DC resistance sweep at 10 mA forced current on short standard pads |

critics.systems_engineer: Integrating an 85°C thermal chuck with high-precision femtofarad-level C-t capacitance metrology creates severe systemic electro-thermal coupling. The thermo-electric Seebeck effect across bi-metallic Kelvin probe needle junctions (e.g., tungsten-rhenium or BeCu to aluminum/copper bond pads) induces parasitic microvolt DC offsets that skew quasi-static capacitance and C-t transient integration currents. Furthermore, thermal expansion mismatch between the prober chuck, wafer substrate, and micro-positioner platen introduces mechanical drift exceeding 0.5 µm/min during thermal ramp, threatening contact integrity and pad scrub degradation on sub-micron test pads.
critics.domain_expert: At 85°C, crown-type capacitor dielectric characterization (Ta2O5/ONO stacks) exhibits accelerated Frenkel-Poole emission and trap-assisted tunneling relaxation currents, obscuring true dielectric relaxation if probe contact resistance and chuck thermal gradients are uncalibrated. A 4-wire Kelvin configuration directly at the tip level is required to isolate series resistance (Rs < 1.5 Ω) and eliminate chuck contact impedance. Calibration must execute Open/Short/Load correction directly at 85°C using an on-chuck alumina substrate to de-embed triaxial cable capacitance and thermal phase shifts across the 1 kHz to 1 MHz LCR test frequency range.
critics.supply_chain: Specifying triaxial high-temperature Kelvin probe needles (rated >= 200°C with low-leakage guard rings < 20 fA at 85°C) and a gold-plated low-noise thermal chuck system faces lead times exceeding 14 to 18 weeks due to specialized ceramic/PTFE isolation parts. Standard commercial probe arms experience dielectric breakdown and high leakage in cable jackets above 60°C. Sourcing dual-channel precision thermal controllers with calibrated PT100/Type-K chuck RTDs and Faraday-shielded enclosure interfaces requires pre-allocating qualified secondary suppliers (e.g., FormFactor/MPI compatible triaxial Kelvin arm assemblies).
critics.laya_pm: The buy-and-commission timeline for the 85°C thermal chuck and Kelvin prober setup threatens the critical path for Gen 2 DRAM crown capacitor signoff. Vendor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and on-site site acceptance testing (SAT) must explicitly bundle thermal stability qualification (+/- 0.1°C at 85°C) and femtoampere baseline noise floor verification. If calibration protocols and calibration substrate kits (CS-5/ISS) are not procured concurrently with the primary chuck hardware, physical C-t parameter extraction milestones will slip by at least 6 weeks.
critical_failure_modes: Thermal chuck thermocouple gradient error leading to actual wafer temperature deviation > ±2.0°C from setpoint (85°C), distorting temperature-dependent Arrhenius extraction of dielectric leakage and retention time.
Thermo-mechanical drift of probe tips resulting in loss of Kelvin contact, contact pad punch-through, or lateral scraping of top electrode thin films during isothermal soak.
Triaxial cable dielectric degradation and guard leakage at 85°C causing the C-t background noise floor to exceed 50 fF, invalidating the detection of 28 fF target cell capacitance.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): 85°C Deep-Depletion C-t Transient Extraction & Minority Carrier Generation Lifetime Characterization

**Process ID:** `MET-SOP-180NM-CT-85C`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm Open-Source DRAM Cell, 8F²)  
**Action Type:** Buy / External Metrology & Wafer Characterization System  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Architecture Flow

The objective of this procedure is to execute pulsed capacitance-time ($C\text{-}t$) transient measurements on crown-type storage capacitor test arrays and MOS access structures at elevated operating temperature (85°C). This extracts the minority carrier generation lifetime ($\tau_g$), surface generation velocity ($s_0$), and cell retention leakage under deep-depletion conditions using Zerbst analysis.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Wafer Mount on Temptronic Thermal Chuck (25°C)"] --> B["Thermal Ramp to 85°C ± 0.5°C soaking for 15 min"]
    B --> C["Open/Short RF Cable & Switch Matrix De-embedding"]
    C --> D["Pre-bias to Accumulation / Flatband Condition"]
    D --> E["Fast Pulse to Deep Depletion (V_pulse, rise time < 100 ns)"]
    E --> F["Acquire C-t Transient Decay to Inversion (1 kHz - 1 MHz)"]
    F --> G["Zerbst Analysis: -d(C_ox/C)²/dt vs (C_inv/C - 1)"]
    G --> H["Extract tau_g & Leakage Validation (< 1 fA/cell)"]
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Thermal Chuck Conditioning & Substrate Contact**:
   - Load the 180nm test wafer onto the high-temperature shielded probe station chuck (e.g., Temptronic ThermoChuck).
   - Set chuck temperature to **85°C**; allow thermal stabilization for 15 minutes. Verify dry air or nitrogen purge to avoid surface oxidation and moisture-induced parasitic leakage.
2. **Instrument Setup & De-embedding**:
   - Connect the precision LCR meter / pulse generator (e.g., Keysight B1500A / B1505A with WGFMU or fast C-V module) to the device under test (DUT) using shielded Kelvin triaxial probes.
   - Perform open-circuit and short-circuit zero compensation at 85°C to eliminate probe and cable parasitic capacitances.
3. **Pulsing & Transient C-t Sampling**:
   - Apply a baseline pre-charge gate/plate bias driving the test capacitor/transistor array into accumulation/equilibrium inversion.
   - Step pulse voltage into deep depletion with a rise time $< 100\text{ ns}$ to prevent premature carrier recovery during the transition edge.
   - Record high-frequency (100 kHz – 1 MHz) capacitance versus time $C(t)$ until the transient reaches the thermal equilibrium inversion capacitance ($C_{\text{inv}}$) over an acquisition window $\ge 64\text{ ms}$.
4. **Zerbst Transient Extraction**:
   - Construct the Zerbst plot:
     $$\left[-\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{C_{\text{ox}}}{C(t)}\right)^2\right] \quad \text{vs.} \quad \left[\frac{C_{\text{inv}}}{C(t)} - 1\right]$$
   - Extract the minority carrier generation lifetime ($\tau_g$) from the slope of the linear regime and surface generation velocity ($s_0$) from the intercept.
   - Compute total generation leakage current density and convert to single-cell equivalent leakage ($I_{\text{leak}}$) based on the $8\text{F}^2$ cell area ($L=180\text{ nm}, W=220\text{ nm}$).

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░                                       │
 Leakage Limit┤░                                       │
              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Retention Temp┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
       Cap EOT┤▓▓▓                                     │
              │▓▓▓                                     │
 C_cell Target┤██████████████                          │
              │██████████████                          │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
              0.0      21.2      42.5     63.8     85.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Baseline Specification | Target / Acceptance Criteria | Physical Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Measurement Chuck Temperature** | Thermal equilibrium stability | **$85 \pm 0.5$** | °C |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / ONO crown stack | **$3.0 \text{ to } 4.0$** | nm |
| **Target Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | Crown-type 3D cylinder capacitor | **$\ge 28$** (tolerance: $25 - 30$) | fF/cell |
| **Total 85°C Junction & Dielectric Leakage** | Subthreshold + generation leakage | **$< 1.0$** | fA/cell |
| **Data Retention Time Target** | Refresh window retention at 85°C | **$> 64$** | ms |

---

### 4. Verified Literature References

1. **`180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench`**:
   - Access transistor geometry: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ in folded bitline $8\text{F}^2$ architecture.
   - Storage capacitor: Crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) using ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ high-k dielectric ($\kappa > 15$).
   - Capacitance budget: $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$.
   - Leakage target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage kept below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **`Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering`**:
   - Cell capacitor retention baseline: $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF/cell}$ guaranteeing retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT): $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$ for $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ crown stacks.
3. **`Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout`**:
   - Readout signal dynamics: Bitline capacitance $C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$, yielding differential signal $\Delta V \approx 100\text{ to } 150\text{ mV}$ for $C_s \approx 25\text{ fF}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck stability at 85°C must maintain ±0.1°C precision across the wafer platen to prevent artificial drift in carrier thermal generation rates (g_th ~ n_i ~ exp(-E_g/2kT)). Stray cable capacitance and triaxial chuck leakage current at 85°C must be calibrated out down to sub-10 fA background noise floor; otherwise, the Zerbst analysis slope d(C_ox/C)^2/dt will be dominated by instrument parasitics rather than substrate minority carrier generation lifetime (tau_g).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, intrinsic carrier concentration n_i increases by roughly an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, substantially accelerating deep-depletion recovery and narrowing the measurement time window. The test pulse must transition cleanly from accumulation to deep depletion (-5 V to +5 V depending on p/n-well doping) with slew rates exceeding 10 V/us to prevent premature quasi-equilibrium inversion layer buildup prior to initial t=0 capacitance acquisition. Interface trap emission (D_it) and surface generation velocity (s_0) must be deconvolved from bulk lifetime (tau_g) via Zerbst intercept analysis.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Requires ultra-low noise triaxial high-temperature thermal probe tips (beryllium copper or tungsten with gold coating) and high-purity dry nitrogen (>=99.999% N50 grade) purge shroud to eliminate ambient moisture condensation and local thermal oxidation/surface charge drift during extended hot-chuck dwell times. Replacement cycles for high-temperature triax probe cards and low-leakage co-axial triax cables must be secured against thermal degradation of fluoropolymer dielectrics.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterization throughput on 200mm pilot wafers at 85°C requires long thermal soak stabilization times (>=15 minutes per wafer), creating a severe bottleneck for metrology cycle times. A 9-point representative site sampling strategy must be strictly enforced instead of full wafer mapping to balance statistical process verification of substrate minority carrier lifetime (tau_g >= 10 us) against inline DRAM lot turn-around times.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal chuck temperature gradient exceeding ±0.5°C inducing exponential spatial skew in extracted generation lifetime across wafer sites.
1. Chuck/triaxial shield leakage currents exceeding 100 fA at 85°C, masking true minority carrier generation and distorting Zerbst linear regression.
1. Inadequate voltage pulse transition edge causing premature partial inversion charge accumulation prior to acquisition of initial deep-depletion capacitance C_0.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-2-01` | **85°C Deep-Depletion C-t Transient Extraction on MOS Capacitor Monitor** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency C-V Measurement Unit (MFCMU), Temptronic ThermoChuck (85°C ± 0.1°C), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Shielded Probe Station with N2 purge enclosure | 1. Bias gate to accumulation at -2.0 V for 5.0 s to establish uniform accumulation charge. 2. Step gate bias abruptly (slew rate >= 20 V/us) into deep depletion at +3.0 V at t = 0. 3. Sample small-signal high-frequency capacitance C(t) at 100 kHz (AC oscillation level 25 mV RMS) at 1.0 ms intervals until steady-state inversion capacitance C_inv is achieved (slope dC/dt < 1.0 fF/s). 4. Record full C-t transient trace from t=0 to recovery. | `Initial deep-depletion capacitance C_0 must measure <= 0.35 * C_ox. Transient recovery time to 99% C_inv must be >= 1.20 s at 85°C, with zero anomalous step discontinuities or RF oscillation artifacts.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-2-02` | **Zerbst Plot Extraction of Bulk Minority Carrier Generation Lifetime (tau_g)** | Automated Parameter Extraction Script executed on Keysight B1500A raw C-t data files, calibrated against theoretical EOT and substrate doping N_sub derived from high-frequency C-V. | 1. Calculate depletion layer width W(t) = eps_Si * A * (1/C(t) - 1/C_ox) and steady-state width W_inv = eps_Si * A * (1/C_inv - 1/C_ox). 2. Construct Zerbst differential curve plotting -d(C_ox/C(t))^2/dt on the y-axis against (C_inv/C(t) - 1) on the x-axis. 3. Perform linear least-squares regression over the linear generation regime (0.1 <= (C_inv/C - 1) <= 0.8). 4. Extract bulk minority carrier generation lifetime tau_g = (2 * n_i / N_sub) * (C_ox / C_inv) / slope. | `Extracted minority carrier generation lifetime tau_g must be >= 15.0 us at 85°C across all 9 measurement sites. Coefficient of determination R^2 of linear Zerbst fit must be >= 0.985.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating cleanroom gloves (heat resistant up to 150°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Class 100 antistatic lint-free cleanroom smock and ESD wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn exposure from 85°C chuck: Immediately cool affected epidermal area under clean running deionized water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly. Cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and report to cleanroom medical response. For N2 asphyxiation hazard: Evacuate personnel immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous nitrogen purge enclosure exhaust venting into facility general fab exhaust at >= 35 CFM. Ambient room oxygen monitoring sensors interlocked with audible alarms set to trigger if O2 concentration drops below 19.5%.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be deposited in dedicated grounded, airtight hazardous solvent waste bins with flame arrestors. Exhausted dry N2 is non-hazardous and vented through rooftop HVAC scrubbed air discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | VLSI / Semiconductor Grade (>=99.999% N50) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (Chuck wipe/solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C12) | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Sintered forming gas (H2/N2) annealed top metal contact pads on monitor capacitors; clean, hydrophobic/native-oxide passivated surface free of organic contaminants.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically probed monitor pad with minor probe scrub marks (<5 um lateral scrub displacement); clean, dry, zero thermal oxidation stain.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time leads to atmospheric moisture adsorption and parasitic surface state generation (D_it drift), artificially increasing surface generation velocity s_0 and invalidating Zerbst bulk lifetime deconvolution.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable extraction and signoff of deep-depletion high-temperature (85°C) C-t transient relaxation dynamics and minority carrier generation lifetime (tau_g) on 180nm DRAM test capacitors, verifying silicon substrate defect purity and refresh margin compatibility.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM_180NM_85C_CT_TRANSIENT_RAW_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `ZERBST_LIFETIME_EXTRACTION_REPORT_85C.pdf`
- [ ] `WAFER_9PT_MINORITY_LIFETIME_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Extracted bulk minority carrier generation lifetime tau_g at 85°C** | `>= 15.0 us` | +50.0 us / -0.0 us | Linear regression slope extraction of high-frequency Zerbst plot on 9 wafer map sites |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Zerbst plot regression coefficient of determination R² across linear generation region** | `0.990` | >= 0.985 | Statistical Pearson coefficient calculation on -d(C_ox/C)^2/dt vs (C_inv/C - 1) curve |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum 85°C deep-depletion steady-state recovery duration t_rec** | `>= 1.50 s` | ± 0.25 s | Transient sampling timestamp measurement at 99.0% capacitance recovery threshold |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 designated wafer monitoring sites exhibit tau_g >= 15.0 us at 85.0°C ± 0.1°C with Zerbst R² >= 0.985, proving the substrate generation leakage is low enough to support the target DRAM retention budget (>64 ms at 85°C), validated and co-signed by Metrology Lead and Device Integration Lead.

testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1520A Multifrequency C-V Measurement Unit (MFCMU), Temptronic ThermoChuck (85°C ± 0.1°C), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Shielded Probe Station with N2 purge enclosure
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer mounted on vacuum thermal chuck at 85.0°C under continuous dry N2 purge (<5% RH). MOS test capacitor (Area = 10,000 um², EOT = 3.5 nm on p-substrate) contacted via triaxial probes with open/short/load calibration and cable compensation executed at 85°C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Bias gate to accumulation at -2.0 V for 5.0 s to establish uniform accumulation charge. 2. Step gate bias abruptly (slew rate >= 20 V/us) into deep depletion at +3.0 V at t = 0. 3. Sample small-signal high-frequency capacitance C(t) at 100 kHz (AC oscillation level 25 mV RMS) at 1.0 ms intervals until steady-state inversion capacitance C_inv is achieved (slope dC/dt < 1.0 fF/s). 4. Record full C-t transient trace from t=0 to recovery.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Initial deep-depletion capacitance C_0 must measure <= 0.35 * C_ox. Transient recovery time to 99% C_inv must be >= 1.20 s at 85°C, with zero anomalous step discontinuities or RF oscillation artifacts.

testcases.title: Zerbst Plot Extraction of Bulk Minority Carrier Generation Lifetime (tau_g)
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Parameter Extraction Script executed on Keysight B1500A raw C-t data files, calibrated against theoretical EOT and substrate doping N_sub derived from high-frequency C-V.
testcases.pre_conditions: Completed 85°C C-t transient dataset from TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-2-01 with verified substrate active area (100 um x 100 um) and baseline oxide capacitance C_ox = 98.6 pF.
testcases.procedure: 1. Calculate depletion layer width W(t) = eps_Si * A * (1/C(t) - 1/C_ox) and steady-state width W_inv = eps_Si * A * (1/C_inv - 1/C_ox). 2. Construct Zerbst differential curve plotting -d(C_ox/C(t))^2/dt on the y-axis against (C_inv/C(t) - 1) on the x-axis. 3. Perform linear least-squares regression over the linear generation regime (0.1 <= (C_inv/C - 1) <= 0.8). 4. Extract bulk minority carrier generation lifetime tau_g = (2 * n_i / N_sub) * (C_ox / C_inv) / slope.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Extracted minority carrier generation lifetime tau_g must be >= 15.0 us at 85°C across all 9 measurement sites. Coefficient of determination R^2 of linear Zerbst fit must be >= 0.985.

ppe_required: Thermal-insulating cleanroom gloves (heat resistant up to 150°C)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Sintered forming gas (H2/N2) annealed top metal contact pads on monitor capacitors; clean, hydrophobic/native-oxide passivated surface free of organic contaminants.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Electrically probed monitor pad with minor probe scrub marks (<5 um lateral scrub displacement); clean, dry, zero thermal oxidation stain.

expected_result.summary: Verifiable extraction and signoff of deep-depletion high-temperature (85°C) C-t transient relaxation dynamics and minority carrier generation lifetime (tau_g) on 180nm DRAM test capacitors, verifying silicon substrate defect purity and refresh margin compatibility.
