# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-180NM-042
**Title:** Dielectric Relaxation & Sub-fA High-Temperature Leakage Current Decomposition Analysis  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling > Crown-Type 3D Cylinder Geometry & High-k $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/ONO Dielectric Stack Optimization > C-V & C-t Metrology Extraction for EOT, Target Cell Capacitance ($\ge 28\text{ fF}$) & Dielectric Leakage Characterization > High-Temperature (85°C) C-t Transient & Dielectric Leakage Relaxation Characterization > Dielectric Relaxation & Sub-fA High-Temperature Leakage Current Decomposition Analysis  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Characterization  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objectives
This SOP establishes the characterization and metrology protocol to measure dielectric relaxation and decompose sub-femtoampere (sub-fA) leakage currents at elevated operating temperatures ($85^\circ\text{C}$) on 180nm 1T1C Crown-type stacked storage capacitors over bitline (COB). The procedure separates transient polarization/depolarization currents (Curie-von Schweidler relaxation: $I(t) \propto t^{-\alpha}$) from steady-state conduction mechanisms (Poole-Frenkel emission, Schottky barrier emission, and Fowler-Nordheim tunneling) to ensure data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 2. Equipment, Tooling & Test Structures
- **SMU / Electrometer:** Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer equipped with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU) capable of 0.1 fA measurement resolution and triaxial guarded probing.
- **Thermal Chuck:** Automated triaxial-shielded hot chuck system with closed-loop PID control calibrated to $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ inside an inert $\text{N}_2$-purged dark box.
- **Test Structures:** 
  - Array test pattern: $10^4$ to $10^6$ parallel Crown-type 1T1C storage nodes with shared cell plate ($V_{\text{plate}} = V_{\text{DD}} / 2$) and access transistors held in hard turn-off ($V_{\text{WL}} = 0\text{ V}$).
  - Standalone crown MIM capacitor macro (bypass access transistor) with equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) of $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```text
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       | 1. Wafer Load, Triaxial Shielding & 85°C Thermal Soak |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       | 2. Residual Charge Bleed & Baseline Drift Calibration |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       | 3. High-Field Charging & Transient C-t / I-t Logging  |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       | 4. Discharge (Depolarization) & Relaxation Profiling  |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       | 5. Extraction: Decomposition into Steady-State vs fA  |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Tool Setup, Triaxial Shielding & Thermal Soak
1. Load the 180nm test wafer onto the triaxial chuck inside the sealed Faraday cage dark box.
2. Purge the probe enclosure with dry $\text{N}_2$ to maintain relative humidity $< 5\%$ and eliminate surface moisture condensation at high temperature.
3. Ramp chuck temperature to **$85^\circ\text{C}$** and soak for $\ge 20\text{ minutes}$ to achieve thermal equilibrium across the wafer.
4. Establish triaxial guard connections down to the probe tips to suppress cable and fixture parasitic leakage below $0.05\text{ fA}$.

#### Step 2: Baseline Calibration & Pre-stress Discharge
1. Ground both the top plate ($V_{\text{plate}}$) and bottom storage node ($V_{\text{SN}}$) for $120\text{ s}$ to bleed any trapped remnant charges from prior thermal/electric handling.
2. Perform open-circuit zero-bias background current measurement for $60\text{ s}$; verify background fixture drift does not exceed $0.1\text{ fA}$.

#### Step 3: Voltage Step Stress & Charging Transient Measurement ($I_{\text{charge}}(t)$)
1. Apply a step stress bias representing worst-case DRAM storage state: $V_{\text{stress}} = V_{\text{DD}} / 2$ across the dielectric stack ($V_{\text{plate}} = V_{\text{DD}} / 2$, $V_{\text{SN}} = 0\text{ V}$ or $V_{\text{cell}} = V_{\text{DD}}$).
2. Sample current $I_{\text{charge}}(t)$ logarithmically from $t = 1\text{ ms}$ to $t = 100\text{ s}$ using the high-resolution SMU in integration mode (Medium/Long NPLC).
3. Record total charging current:
   $$I_{\text{total}}(t) = I_{\text{displacement}}(t) + I_{\text{relax}}(t) + I_{\text{leak}}(\text{steady-state})$$

#### Step 4: Discharging (Depolarization) Transient Measurement ($I_{\text{discharge}}(t)$)
1. Step the applied voltage abruptly back to $0\text{ V}$ across the capacitor stack while maintaining continuous current logging.
2. Measure the depolarization current transient $I_{\text{discharge}}(t)$ from $t = 1\text{ ms}$ to $t = 100\text{ s}$.
3. In pure dielectric relaxation (Curie-von Schweidler behavior), the reversible polarization current satisfies:
   $$I_{\text{relax}}(t) = I_0 \cdot t^{-\alpha} \quad (0.8 \le \alpha \le 1.2)$$

#### Step 5: Current Decomposition & Parameter Extraction
1. Subtract the discharge transient from the charging transient to isolate the true steady-state high-temperature leakage current:
   $$I_{\text{leak}}(\text{steady-state}) = I_{\text{charge}}(t) - |I_{\text{discharge}}(t)| \quad \text{for } t \ge 10\text{ s}$$
2. Normalize the measured current to per-cell equivalent based on the test structure array multiplier $N_{\text{cells}}$.
3. Confirm that normalized cell capacitance meets or exceeds **$28\text{ fF/cell}$** (minimum design margin: $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$) at $85^\circ\text{C}$ using $100\text{ kHz}$ high-frequency C-V extraction.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Tolerance / Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Measurement Chuck Temperature** | **$85$** | $^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ steady-state thermal soak |
| **Total Cell Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | **$< 1.0$** | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Measured at $85^\circ\text{C}$ at steady state ($t \ge 10\text{ s}$) |
| **Target Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | **$\ge 28$** (Acceptable window: $25\text{ -- }30$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Measured via HF C-V / C-t at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | **$3.0\text{ to }4.0$** | $\text{nm}$ | Extracted from high-k ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{ONO}$) stack |
| **Target Data Retention Duration** | **$> 64$** | $\text{ms}$ | Derived retention interval at $85^\circ\text{C}$ operating condition |

---

### 5. Context Sources & Citations
- **Source 1:** *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*  
  - *Citations:* Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) crown topology; $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{ONO}$ dielectric stack ($\kappa > 15$); minimum capacitance budget of $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$; leakage current target kept below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source 2:** *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*  
  - *Citations:* 1T1C $8\text{F}^2$ cell layout; capacitor maintaining $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$; data retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) of $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$.
- **Source 3:** *Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout*  
  - *Citations:* Cell charge transfer and signal development $Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$; precharge voltage $V_{\text{plate}} = V_{\text{DD}} / 2$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Decomposing leakage mechanisms at sub-fA levels at 85°C across an 8F² crown capacitor array requires distinguishing true dielectric leakage (Poole-Frenkel conduction, Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, and trap-assisted tunneling) from access transistor junction band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL), and subthreshold channel conduction. The test structure layout must isolate the storage node capacitor array directly via dedicated Kelvin probe pads without active access transistor junctions in the measurement loop; otherwise, high-temperature silicon substrate generation-recombination currents will completely mask the intrinsic dielectric relaxation and sub-fA ONO/Ta2O5 conduction currents.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dielectric relaxation follows the Curie-von Schweidler power law (I_relax ~ t^-alpha, where alpha ≈ 0.8–1.2) caused by dipole reorientation and slow-trap charge capture/emission. Measuring dielectric leakage at t < 10 ms captures displacement and relaxation currents rather than true steady-state DC leakage. The parameter extraction sequence must enforce a soak/charging time of at least 100 seconds prior to steady-state current sampling at 85°C under V_plate = 1.0 V (half-Vdd = 0.9 V to 1.0 V for 180nm core logic), and separate transient polarization current from Poole-Frenkel bulk conduction governed by Ta2O5 trap depths (E_t ≈ 1.1–1.5 eV) or ONO nitride traps.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sub-femtometer/sub-fA probe stations requiring triaxial guarding, dry-air/nitrogen purge enclosures, and low-noise parametric analyzers (such as Keysight B1500A with HRSMU or Keithley 4200A-SCS with preamplifiers) have single-vendor dependencies and limited fab line capacity. Probe needle tip oxidation and triaxial cable microphonics at 85°C chuck temperatures induce triboelectric and piezoelectric noise exceeding 5 fA. Fixtures and shielded triaxial probe cards must be sourced with certified PTFE/Kel-F high-temperature insulation to prevent false yields during pilot wafer characterization.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal ramp and stabilization overhead at 85°C alongside multi-decade time-domain (t = 10^-3 s to 10^3 s) relaxation characterization imposes an 18 to 25-minute test time per site. Across a 5-point wafer map on 25-wafer pilot lots, this creates an unmanageable metrology throughput bottleneck. The team must compress the testing routine by running high-temperature soak sweeps in parallel using multi-channel high-resolution SMUs and establishing mathematical extrapolation models for relaxation decay to maintain the Gen 2 milestone schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal expansion mismatch between chuck, wafer, and tungsten probe tips causing contact scrub and micro-arcing that punctures the ultra-thin (<4.5 nm EOT) high-k dielectric stack.
1. Parasitic surface moisture condensation and ionic contamination across probe card ceramic interfaces at elevated chuck temperatures generating extrinsic leakage exceeding 10 fA.
1. Misidentifying reversible Curie-von Schweidler polarization/relaxation current as irreversible steady-state dielectric leakage, resulting in premature and erroneous rejection of high-k deposition recipes.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-3-01` | **Sub-fA Time-Domain Dielectric Relaxation and Leakage Decomposition Characterization at 85°C** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (0.1 fA measurement resolution), triaxial Kelvin guarding, and Temptronic ThermoChuck thermal probe station with dark-box Faraday cage and N2 purge | 1. Land triaxial Kelvin probes on the dedicated 10,000-cell Crown Capacitor Array test structure (top cell plate contact to Force/Sense, bottom storage node common plug contact to Guard/Common Ground). 2. Apply a voltage step from 0.0 V to V_stress = +1.0 V at t = 0 s with a rise time < 100 µs. 3. Sample transient current I(t) continuously with logarithmic time sampling from t = 1 ms to t = 300 s at T = 85.0°C +/- 0.5°C. 4. Decompose total current I(t) into polarization relaxation current I_relax(t) = A * t^-alpha and steady-state DC conduction leakage I_dc via non-linear least-squares fitting over t = 50 s to 300 s. 5. Normalize extracted I_dc by 10,000 to obtain single-cell equivalent leakage. | `Single-cell normalized steady-state DC leakage I_dc <= 0.80 fA/cell at V_plate = 1.0 V, T = 85°C. Relaxation power law exponent alpha must satisfy 0.85 <= alpha <= 1.15. Zero dielectric breakdown events during 300 s stress.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-2-3-3-3-02` | **High-Temperature (85°C) Field-Dependent Poole-Frenkel vs. Tunneling Leakage Decomposition Sweep** | Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer equipped with dual 4201-SMU / 4200-PA Remote PreAmp units, shielded triaxial probe manipulators, high-temperature Temptronic thermal chuck inside dry-box enclosure | 1. Position needles on 10,000-cell crown capacitor array pads. 2. Pre-soak dielectric stack at V_bias = +1.0 V for 120 seconds to completely extinguish transient dielectric relaxation currents. 3. Execute stepped DC bias sweep from 0.0 V to +1.8 V in increments of 25 mV, holding each step for 1.0 s before integrating current over 10 power line cycles (PLC = 10, integration time 200 ms). 4. Construct Poole-Frenkel plot: ln(J/E) versus sqrt(E), where E = V_bias / EOT. 5. Extract dielectric trap barrier height Phi_t from the slope and evaluate linearity (R²) between 0.6 MV/cm and 1.5 MV/cm. | `Linear correlation coefficient R² >= 0.98 in the Poole-Frenkel regime (confirming bulk-trap conduction physics). Extracted effective trap depth Phi_t >= 1.20 eV. Single-cell equivalent leakage current at nominal V_dd/2 (0.9 V) <= 0.50 fA/cell at 85°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating heat-resistant cleanroom gloves (rated to 150°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical/splash and impact safety goggles, Class 100 cleanroom ESD-safe anti-static lab coat, Nitrile outer gloves worn over heat barriers for solvent wipe maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected skin area with copious cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes. Do not apply ice or oil-based ointments. Cover with sterile dressing and report to cleanroom occupational health center. Nitrogen Asphyxiation: If oxygen depletion alarm triggers, immediately evacuate victim to fresh open air; administer CPR or supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored or arrested.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober chamber enclosure must be connected to cleanroom dedicated tool exhaust maintaining negative static pressure of -50 Pa to -100 Pa and face velocity >= 0.5 m/s. Continuous ambient oxygen deficiency monitoring sensors (O2 alarm setpoint < 19.5% by volume) installed adjacent to the dry-box N2 purge station.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent wipes soaked with Isopropyl Alcohol used for chuck and needle de-fluxing/cleaning must be disposed of in grounded, self-closing dedicated flammable solvent waste containers. Exhaust gases from the prober purged directly into VOC abatement scrubbers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI Tier 3) | `99.9%` |
| **Gaseous Nitrogen (Dry N2 Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 (UHP) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed post-metal anneal (PMA) / forming gas anneal (450°C 95% N2 / 5% H2) with pristine top Al/Cu or W probing pads, free from oxidation, moisture films, or organic fluorocarbon residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested wafer surface with verified mechanical probe mark scrubbing depth < 150 nm, zero probe tip particulate contamination, and nitrogen-purged hermetic front-opening shipping box (FOUP) state.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity (>40% RH) beyond 45 minutes causes airborne moisture and hydroxyl group chemisorption onto exposed probe pad interfaces and dielectric edges, leading to surface parasitic conduction paths that artificially inflate measured leakage by 10x to 100x (>10 fA/cell) and invalidate sub-fA relaxation parameter fitting.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified characterization and decomposition of crown-type 1T1C storage capacitor dielectric relaxation and intrinsic steady-state leakage under 85°C high-temperature operational conditions. Conclusive separation of Curie-von Schweidler polarization current from bulk Poole-Frenkel and tunneling conduction confirms that intrinsic single-cell leakage meets the <1.0 fA/cell retention threshold for 180nm 64ms DRAM refresh cycles.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DIELECTRIC_RELAXATION_CT_85C_ARRAY_DECOMPOSITION.csv`
- [ ] `POOLE_FRENKEL_EXTRACTION_AND_LEAKAGE_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `PROBE_SCRUB_IMPACT_AFM_TOPOGRAPHY.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Single-cell normalized intrinsic steady-state leakage current at 85°C and V_plate = 1.0 V** | `0.65 fA/cell` | +/- 0.15 fA/cell | Keysight B1517A HRSMU time-domain current sampling over 300 s window with DC asymptote extraction on 10,000-cell array |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Dielectric relaxation decay power-law exponent (Curie-von Schweidler alpha)** | `0.98` | +/- 0.08 | Non-linear regression fitting of log(I_relax) vs log(t) from t = 10 ms to t = 10 s |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Poole-Frenkel trap energy barrier depth (Phi_t) for high-k dielectric stack** | `1.32 eV` | +/- 0.10 eV | Arrhenius and Poole-Frenkel plot extraction across 0.6 to 1.5 MV/cm electric field at 85°C |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formally signed off when array-measured single-cell leakage is verified < 0.80 fA/cell at 85°C, Curie-von Schweidler relaxation parameters exhibit R² > 0.95 across five wafer test sites, and dielectric leakage model parameters are compiled into the SPICE macro-model library for circuit refresh simulation.

testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Single-cell normalized steady-state DC leakage I_dc <= 0.80 fA/cell at V_plate = 1.0 V, T = 85°C. Relaxation power law exponent alpha must satisfy 0.85 <= alpha <= 1.15. Zero dielectric breakdown events during 300 s stress.

testcases.title: High-Temperature (85°C) Field-Dependent Poole-Frenkel vs. Tunneling Leakage Decomposition Sweep
testcases.instrumentation: Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer equipped with dual 4201-SMU / 4200-PA Remote PreAmp units, shielded triaxial probe manipulators, high-temperature Temptronic thermal chuck inside dry-box enclosure
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer held at 85.0°C +/- 0.2°C for minimum 15 minutes thermal equilibrium. Environmental relative humidity inside Faraday cage < 2.0%. Instrument noise floor verified <= 0.15 fA RMS.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position needles on 10,000-cell crown capacitor array pads. 2. Pre-soak dielectric stack at V_bias = +1.0 V for 120 seconds to completely extinguish transient dielectric relaxation currents. 3. Execute stepped DC bias sweep from 0.0 V to +1.8 V in increments of 25 mV, holding each step for 1.0 s before integrating current over 10 power line cycles (PLC = 10, integration time 200 ms). 4. Construct Poole-Frenkel plot: ln(J/E) versus sqrt(E), where E = V_bias / EOT. 5. Extract dielectric trap barrier height Phi_t from the slope and evaluate linearity (R²) between 0.6 MV/cm and 1.5 MV/cm.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Linear correlation coefficient R² >= 0.98 in the Poole-Frenkel regime (confirming bulk-trap conduction physics). Extracted effective trap depth Phi_t >= 1.20 eV. Single-cell equivalent leakage current at nominal V_dd/2 (0.9 V) <= 0.50 fA/cell at 85°C.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Cell Retention & Soft-Error Immunity Metrology (28 fF / <1 fA Leakage Verification)

**Context / Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (`DRAM Foundation VN`) > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling > Cell Retention & Soft-Error Immunity Metrology  
**Generation**: Gen 2 (µm / 180 nm)  
**Action Type**: Make / Verification  

---

### 1. Metrology Process Flow

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Prep & Probe  │
│       Contact        │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│     Storage Node     │
│     Capacitance      │
│      Metrology       │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Retention & Sub-fA  │
│  Leakage Profiling   │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Alpha Particle SER  │
│  Acceleration Test   │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│      Acceptance      │
│    Verification &    │
│      Pass/Fail       │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

#### Step 1: Test Structure Alignment & Wafer Thermal Stabilization
1. Load the 180nm test wafer onto a precision thermal probe station configured with a triaxial shielded chuck.
2. Align probe needles to the 1T1C test structures:
   - Access transistor geometry: channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Array architecture: Folded bitline ($8F^2$ layout, cell area $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$, pitch $= 360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$).
3. Ramp the thermal chuck temperature to $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ and hold for 10 minutes to reach steady-state thermal equilibrium.

#### Step 2: Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$) & Ratio Verification
1. Connect an LCR meter (operating at $100\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$, $V_{ac} = 25\text{ mV}$) via low-leakage Kelvin probes to the Crown-type stacked storage node test macro (high-$\kappa$ dielectric stack: $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ or ONO triple dielectric, $\text{EOT} = 3\text{ nm}$ to $4\text{ nm}$).
2. Measure the unit cell storage node capacitance $C_s$.
3. Measure bitline parasitic capacitance ($C_b$) on array blocks with 256/512 cells per bitline ($C_b \approx 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$).
4. Calculate the capacitance ratio:
   $$\text{Ratio} = \frac{C_b}{C_s}$$
   Ensure the ratio remains well below the $10:1$ critical read margin degradation boundary.

#### Step 3: Retention Time & Sub-fA Leakage Profiling at 85°C
1. Set access transistor gate oxide ($t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}\ \text{SiO}_2$) biases: apply wordline turn-off bias to ensure subthreshold channel cutoff.
2. Charge the storage capacitor to logic high ($V_{DD} / \text{Array Data High}$) and initialize the retention clock.
3. Monitor the storage node voltage decay curve over time using a sub-femtoampere electrometric probe / SMU.
4. Calculate total leakage current ($I_{leak} = I_{subthreshold} + I_{junction} + I_{dielectric}$) at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$:
   $$I_{leak} = C_s \cdot \left(\frac{dV_s}{dt}\right)$$
5. Verify that cell data retention remains valid past the target refresh window of $t_{ret} > 64\text{ ms}$.

#### Step 4: Alpha-Particle Induced Soft-Error Rate (SER) Immunity Metrology
1. Position a calibrated planar alpha-particle radiation source ($^{241}\text{Am}$, emission energy $\sim 5\text{ MeV}$) above the unencapsulated array macro at a fixed geometry.
2. Initialize array cells with alternating test bit patterns (`0xAA` / `0x55`).
3. Run cyclic retention/read sweeps to detect critical charge collection ($Q_{crit} = C_s \cdot \Delta V_{BL}$).
4. Confirm that the nominal storage charge ($Q_{stored} \ge 28\text{ fF} \cdot V$) suppresses bitline coupling disturbance and soft-error bit flips under continuous irradiation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Lower / Upper Limit | Measurement Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | Nominal: $28\text{ fF}$ | $25\text{ fF} \le C_s \le 30\text{ fF}$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Multi-frequency C-V / LCR test macro |
| **Cell Leakage Current ($I_{leak}$ @ 85°C)** | Target: $< 1.0\text{ fA}$ | $I_{leak} < 1.0\text{ fA}$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Electrometric SMU / $C_s \cdot (dV/dt)$ decay |
| **Data Retention Time ($t_{ret}$ @ 85°C)** | Target: $> 64\text{ ms}$ | $t_{ret} \ge 64\text{ ms}$ | $\text{ms}$ | Array retention read/refresh sweep |
| **Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)** | Nominal: $5:1$ to $9:1$ | $\le 9:1$ (Strict max: $< 10:1$) | Dimensionless | Ratio of measured $C_b$ (256/512-cell BL) to $C_s$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Citations

1. **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
   - Access transistor dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) erected above drain via W-plug.
   - ONO triple dielectric or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$\kappa$ stack ($\kappa > 15$).
   - Capacitance budget: Minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ for noise and alpha-particle soft-error immunity.
   - Leakage target: Subthreshold and junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

2. **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
   - Storage capacitance requirement: $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF/cell}$.
   - Retention requirement: $> 64\text{ ms}$ retention time at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - High-$\kappa$ equivalent oxide thickness: $\text{EOT} = 3\text{ nm}$ to $4\text{ nm}$.
   - Bitline and wordline pitch: $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$; gate dielectric: $3.5\text{ nm}$ physical $\text{SiO}_2$.

3. **Source: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**
   - Folded bitline $8F^2$ footprint: Area $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$ for common-mode noise rejection.
   - Storage node nominal capacitance: $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$ (acceptable: $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$).
   - Bitline parasitic capacitance: $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ for 256 or 512 cells per bitline.
   - Bitline-to-cell ratio: $C_b / C_s$ maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (degrades severely if $> 10:1$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Direct DC measurement of <1 fA leakage on an isolated 28 fF capacitor node via conventional probe card micro-positioners is physically intractable due to the femtofarad-scale node capacitance discharging instantaneously into standard coaxial cable capacitance (~100 pF/m) and probe parasitic capacitance (~1-5 pF). For Gen 2 (µm/garage-scale metrology transition), testing must rely on an indirect charge-retention readout scheme: pulsing the access transistor gate to charge the crown node, waiting a calibrated retention period (t_hold), and sensing the remaining bitline voltage split (delta-V_BL) through an on-chip test amplifier or array bitline sense amplifier, rather than placing a direct mechanical probe contact onto the storage node plug.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node dimensions (L=180 nm, W=220 nm), junction band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL), and trap-assisted recombination at the n+/p-well drain junction dominate over pure dielectric bulk leakage through ONO or Ta2O5/Al2O3 stacks. Furthermore, soft-error immunity (SER) against 5.4 MeV alpha particles from trace packaging uranium/thorium decay requires Q_crit = C_cell * (V_DD/2) >= 28 fF * 0.9 V = 25.2 fC; any local thinning or micro-voiding in the crown cylinder that drops capacitance below 25 fF will cause catastrophic Single Event Upset (SEU) rates under ambient background radiation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sub-femtoampere parametric analyzers (e.g., Keysight B1500A with B1517A HRSMU or Keithley 4200A-SCS with 4201-SMU preamps) and triaxial low-noise probe stations with dry-box N2 purge enclosures have prohibitive lead times and capital expenditure for open-source garage-scale fabrication. Metrology fixtures must utilize modular, salvaged semiconductor parameter analyzers or custom discrete transimpedance amplifier boards featuring ultra-low input bias current operational amplifiers (e.g., ADA4530-1 with 20 fA max bias at 25°C) mounted inside Faraday-shielded enclosures with PTFE insulation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The metrology test vehicle requires dedicated 1T1C test structures and Kelvin arrays on the scribe line / test chip perimeter rather than testing functional memory cells blind. Metrology cycle times must not bottleneck downstream dielectric atomic layer deposition (ALD) or ONO re-oxidation qualification; automated Python-controlled wafer mapping scripts must extract retention histograms across 64-site arrays within 15 minutes per wafer to provide rapid feedback to the photolithography and etch stations.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Parasitic leakage shunting through unpassivated surface states or moisture condensation on the probe fixture, inducing an apparent leakage >100 fA and masking true sub-femtoamp cell performance.
1. Capacitor crown mechanical collapse or stiction during wet strip/rinse steps resulting in short circuits between adjacent crown outer shells or pinhole punch-through of the high-k dielectric.
1. Access transistor subthreshold leakage degradation caused by localized gate-dielectric micro-damage or channel dopant deactivation, leading to retention decay in under 1 millisecond at 85°C.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Ground capacitor top plate (V_plate = 0.9 V or V_DD/2) and bitline (V_BL = 1.8 V). 2. Apply a write pulse to the access wordline (V_WL = 3.0 V, pulse width 50 ns) to charge the cell storage nodes to 1.8 V (Data '1'). 3. Lower V_WL to access transistor off-state (V_WL = -0.5 V negative back-bias) and float or precharge bitline to V_DD/2 (0.9 V). 4. Connect high-force/low-force triaxial terminals to array top-plate pad and common storage-node bottom-plate test line. 2. Set AC excitation signal to 100 kHz frequency, 30 mV RMS oscillation amplitude. 3. Sweep DC bias voltage from -1.5 V to +1.5 V across the dielectric stack with 50 mV step increments. 4. Record parallel capacitance (Cp) and dissipation factor (D) at each bias step. 5. Divide measured total capacitance by 10,000 to determine single-cell crown capacitance C_cell. | `Single-cell equivalent capacitance C_cell >= 28.0 fF at 0.9 V operating bias (total array capacitance >= 280 pF); dielectric dissipation factor tan(delta) <= 0.015 at 100 kHz.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant nitrile/neoprene outer gloves over cleanroom vinyl inner gloves, ANSI Z87.1 approved chemical splash goggles and full-face poly-carbonate shield, Polypropylene cleanroom acid-resistant apron and sleeves, Closed-toe ESD-safe cleanroom boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF contact: Immediately flush affected skin with copious flowing water for 2 minutes, then massage Calcium Gluconate 2.5% topical gel generously into skin until medical assistance arrives. For eye exposure, flush with sterile eyewash solution or 1% calcium gluconate eye drop solution for minimum 15 minutes. For N2 asphyxiation risk: Evacuate personnel to fresh air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet bench acid exhaust velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) with dedicated wet scrubber tie-in. Probe station enclosure requires continuous local laminar extraction (minimum 50 CFM) with real-time ambient oxygen deficit sensor (<19.5% O2 alarm).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous fluoride wastes must be collected in dedicated fluoropolymer (PVDF/HDPE) carboys, neutralized with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2), settled, and filtered before municipal discharge (neutralized effluent pH 6.5 - 8.5, fluoride concentration < 10 ppm).

| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas (purge and blanketing)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 99.999%) | `100% vol` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pristine pre-metal dielectric passivated crown structure, post-anneal, bare tungsten/aluminum probing pads free of native oxide film and fluorocarbon etch polymers.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Scrubbed, electrically probed, N2-desiccated wafer surface without mechanical pad gouging exceeding 15 nm depth or particulate redeposition (>0.3 µm defects < 5 per wafer).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air Q-time causes ambient moisture and airborne molecular contamination (organic amine/siloxane) condensation on open probe pads and exposed crown dielectric sidewalls, creating surface shunt resistance paths that induce false high-leakage signatures (>10 fA) and pad contact resistance spikes.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full parametric metrology qualification of Gen 2 180nm 1T1C crown-over-bitline cell arrays verifying target capacitance of >=28 fF and single-cell leakage <=1 fA at 85°C to guarantee >64 ms retention and alpha-particle soft-error immunity.

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher sign-off requires 100% verification across all 64 wafer sampling sites showing median retention time exceeding 64 ms at 85°C, median per-cell leakage <= 1.0 fA, unit capacitance >= 28.0 fF, and zero hard dielectric breakdown failures below 2.5 V top-plate stress.

testcases.procedure: 1. Connect high-force/low-force triaxial terminals to array top-plate pad and common storage-node bottom-plate test line. 2. Set AC excitation signal to 100 kHz frequency, 30 mV RMS oscillation amplitude. 3. Sweep DC bias voltage from -1.5 V to +1.5 V across the dielectric stack with 50 mV step increments. 4. Record parallel capacitance (Cp) and dissipation factor (D) at each bias step. 5. Divide measured total capacitance by 10,000 to determine single-cell crown capacitance C_cell.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Single-cell equivalent capacitance C_cell >= 28.0 fF at 0.9 V operating bias (total array capacitance >= 280 pF); dielectric dissipation factor tan(delta) <= 0.015 at 100 kHz.

ppe_required: Chemical-resistant nitrile/neoprene outer gloves over cleanroom vinyl inner gloves
ANSI Z87.1 approved chemical splash goggles and full-face poly-carbonate shield
Polypropylene cleanroom acid-resistant apron and sleeves
Closed-toe ESD-safe cleanroom boots

cas_chemicals.name: Hydrofluoric Acid (aqueous, for pre-metallization oxide clean)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For HF contact: Immediately flush affected skin with copious flowing water for 2 minutes, then massage Calcium Gluconate 2.5% topical gel generously into skin until medical assistance arrives. For eye exposure, flush with sterile eyewash solution or 1% calcium gluconate eye drop solution for minimum 15 minutes. For N2 asphyxiation risk: Evacuate personnel to fresh air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Wet bench acid exhaust velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) with dedicated wet scrubber tie-in. Probe station enclosure requires continuous local laminar extraction (minimum 50 CFM) with real-time ambient oxygen deficit sensor (<19.5% O2 alarm).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Aqueous fluoride wastes must be collected in dedicated fluoropolymer (PVDF/HDPE) carboys, neutralized with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2), settled, and filtered before municipal discharge (neutralized effluent pH 6.5 - 8.5, fluoride concentration < 10 ppm).

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pristine pre-metal dielectric passivated crown structure, post-anneal, bare tungsten/aluminum probing pads free of native oxide film and fluorocarbon etch polymers.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Scrubbed, electrically probed, N2-desiccated wafer surface without mechanical pad gouging exceeding 15 nm depth or particulate redeposition (>0.3 µm defects < 5 per wafer).
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding cleanroom air Q-time causes ambient moisture and airborne molecular contamination (organic amine/siloxane) condensation on open probe pads and exposed crown dielectric sidewalls, creating surface shunt resistance paths that induce false high-leakage signatures (>10 fA) and pad contact resistance spikes.

expected_result.summary: Full parametric metrology qualification of Gen 2 180nm 1T1C crown-over-bitline cell arrays verifying target capacitance of >=28 fF and single-cell leakage <=1 fA at 85°C to guarantee >64 ms retention and alpha-particle soft-error immunity.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Equivalent single-cell crown capacitance at 0.9 V cell bias
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-frequency 100 kHz C-V extraction on 10k-cell array using Keysight E4980A LCR meter

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum cell off-state retention leakage current per cell at 85°C
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Pulsed retention charge-decay integration across 64 ms wait time using Keysight B1500A HRSMU

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Critical charge (Q_crit) for soft-error upset immunity against 5.4 MeV alpha particles
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calculated product of measured minimum cell capacitance and operating half-rail voltage split (C_min * 0.9 V)

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Researcher sign-off requires 100% verification across all 64 wafer sampling sites showing median retention time exceeding 64 ms at 85°C, median per-cell leakage <= 1.0 fA, unit capacitance >= 28.0 fF, and zero hard dielectric breakdown failures below 2.5 V top-plate stress.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Array Test Structure & Low-Noise Probe Card Procurement
**Track / Hierarchy:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout ($8F^2$) [DRAM Architecture] > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling [Circuit Design] > Cell Retention & Soft-Error Immunity Metrology (28 fF / <1 fA Leakage Verification) [Metrology] > Array Test Structure & Low-Noise Probe Card Procurement [Metrology]  
**Technology Node:** Gen 2 (180 nm / $\mu$m)  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Target Specification:** Characterization of $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ storage cell capacitance, sub-femtoampere ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$) leakage metrology, and bitline parasitic profiling ($C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$).

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Design Kelvin/Array   │
│    Test Structures     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Draft Probe Card    │
│   Procurement Specs    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Card Assembly &     │
│    Triaxial Wiring     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Docking, Alignment &  │
│    Noise Metrology     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Design Array Test Vehicle & Pad Structure (Scribing & Kerf Layout):**
   - Place array test structures on the test vehicle incorporating standalone 1T1C cells ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ access transistors with shared bitline contacts) alongside parallelized mini-arrays (e.g., $100 \times 100$ cells connected to a common node to resolve sub-femtoampere current scaling).
   - Layout 4-terminal Kelvin test pads and grounded guard rings surrounding high-impedance nodes to prevent surface leakage across adjacent metal tracks. Maintain bitline and wordline contact pitch according to design rules ($360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$).

2. **Formulate Probe Card Technical Requirements & RF/DC Procurement Specification:**
   - Define probe card architecture requiring ultra-low-leakage ceramic or multilayer ceramic (MLC) needle guides with low-dielectric-absorption insulation (PTFE/ceramic substrate).
   - Specify individual probe tips with force ratings ($1.5\text{ to }2.5\text{ g/mil}$) to eliminate pad scrubbing punch-through on aluminum/copper top metal pads while maintaining contact resistance stability.
   - Require full triaxial cabling (Force, Sense, and Guard shields) terminated via low-noise triax connectors directly routed to the probe needles.

3. **Vendor Procurement & Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT):**
   - Release RFQ/Purchase Specification to certified precision probe card manufacturers with ISO/IEC low-current verification standards.
   - Require vendor validation of open-circuit path leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ chuck temperature to ensure background noise stays orders of magnitude below device leakage levels.
   - Inspect mechanical planarity, needle alignment, and tip wear under automated optical metrology prior to shipment acceptance.

4. **Prober Docking, Thermal Chamber Calibration & In-Situ Noise Floor Metrology:**
   - Dock the delivered low-noise probe card to the wafer prober interface in an electromagnetically shielded, dark, dry-air purged enclosure.
   - Ramp thermal chuck to $85^\circ\text{C}$ and run an open-air (probes lifted $50\,\mu\text{m}$ above wafer surface) baseline current sweep ($V = 0\text{ V to } 1.8\text{ V}$).
   - Verify that test station background noise floor and card leakage do not obscure the targeted sub-threshold and junction leakage threshold ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$).
   - Execute C-V metrology calibration using an LCR meter / parameter analyzer across frequencies ($10\text{ kHz to } 1\text{ MHz}$) to zero out bitline and cabling parasitics prior to validating storage capacitance ($C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Probe Card Background Noise / Path Leakage** | $< 1.0 \times 10^{-16}$ ($< 0.1\text{ fA}$) | $\text{A (Amperes)}$ | At $85^\circ\text{C}$ chuck temp, $V_{bias} = 1.0\text{ V}$, probes lifted |
| **Thermal Chuck Operating Temperature** | $85 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Closed-loop thermocouple probe station monitor |
| **Cell Storage Capacitance Resolution** | $\ge 28.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Small-signal C-V metrology at $100\text{ kHz}$, $V_{bias} = V_{DD}/2$ |
| **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance Characterization Range** | $250 \pm 25$ | $\text{fF}$ | Kelvin 4-terminal C-V extraction on standard bitline run |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources Cited

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - *Context applied:* Unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ access transistor, shared bitline contact), crown-type capacitor over bitline (COB), minimum cell capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$, and junction/sub-threshold leakage requirement $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - *Context applied:* Folded bitline layout pitch ($360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$ wordline/bitline pitch), $85^\circ\text{C}$ thermal test constraint for data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$, and capacitance range constraints ($25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$).
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout:**
  - *Context applied:* Bitline capacitance parameter ($C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$ vs $C_s \approx 25\text{--}28\text{ fF}$) for differential voltage signal evaluation and parasitic calibration.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Measuring sub-femtoampere (<1 fA) leakage per cell in an 8F² folded-bitline DRAM array structure requires mitigating cable triaxial leakage, dielectric absorption, and stray chuck capacitance. Standard cantilever probe cards introduce 100 fA to 1 pA parasitic background currents, rendering single-cell retention extraction impossible unless dedicated guarded trace routing, ultra-low-leakage ceramic blade needles, and active driven triaxial guards are specified up to the probe tip interface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm, verifying an 8F² folded bitline with Cs = 28 fF and Cb = 150-250 fF requires test structures with grouped sub-array matrix pads (e.g., 64x64 or 256x1 arrays) rather than isolated single cells to bypass the 1 fA thermal-noise instrument floor. For true single-node retention testing, the probe card must maintain parasitic tip-to-tip capacitance below 50 fF and contact resistance stability within ±0.2 Ω across 200 touchdown cycles on aluminum/copper bond pads.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom low-noise vertical MEMS or ceramic-blade low-leakage probe cards with driven coax/triax leads feature 12 to 18 weeks lead time. Vendor selection must require pre-shipment isolation screening certificates verifying <0.5 fA/V isolation resistance at 25°C and 85°C. Securing compatible probe card interfaces for semi-automated probe stations (such as MPI or FormFactor) must be dual-sourced to protect wafer sort schedules.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The CAPEX/OPEX allocation for custom sub-fA probe cards must be decoupled from the full reticle tapeout milestone. Procuring an MPW-compatible parametric test card with multi-DUT Kelvin connections enables parallel validation of discrete MOSFETs (W/L = 2.0/0.18 µm) alongside array test blocks without incurring multiple custom probe card NRE fees.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric charging and triboelectric surface leakage on probe card PCB substrate swamping true cell leakage (<1 fA) with >50 fA parasitic drift.
1. Mechanical needle scrub overshoot puncturing thin pad metallization or cracking inter-metal dielectric (IMD) on scaled 180nm test structures.
1. Moisture condensation on probe tips during elevated temperature/humidity cell retention testing causing erratic electrochemical leakage pathways.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-1-01` | **Probe Card Inter-Pin Triaxial Isolation and Background Parasitic Leakage Verification** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer equipped with B1517A High Resolution SMU (0.1 fA resolution) and triaxial-guarded probe station chuck. | 1. Connect B1517A SMU Force/Guard lines to adjacent probe tip channels (Storage Node Pin vs Bitline Pin). 2. Apply a voltage step from 0.0 V to 1.8 V with 100 mV increments, 5.0 s hold time per step to settle dielectric relaxation. 3. Record steady-state leakage current over 60 s continuous acquisition at V_force = 1.8 V. | `Measured leakage current across all unlanded signal needle pairs must be <= 0.8 fA at 1.8 V DC bias.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-1-02` | **Storage Node Array Test Structure Capacitance and Contact Resistance Integrity** | Keysight E4980A Precision LCR Meter (20 Hz to 2 MHz) with 4-terminal pair kelvin probe configuration and semi-automated wafer prober. | 1. Perform open/short/load calibration at probe needle tips. 2. Land needles on test array top-plate and storage node contact pads. 3. Measure parasitic contact resistance using 4-wire Kelvin sensing. 4. Measure parallel capacitance (Cp-D) at 100 kHz with 50 mV AC oscillation amplitude under 0.9 V DC plate bias across 10 distinct test dies. | `Probe contact resistance <= 1.5 Ω per pin; extracted cell capacitance per node must scale to 28.0 fF ± 2.0 fF per 1T1C equivalent node with loss tangent (D) < 0.02.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom ESD-safe static-dissipative lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA skin contact, rinse affected area with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes. In case of vapor inhalation, relocate personnel immediately to fresh air. Eye contact requires immediate eyewash flushing for 15 minutes and clinical medical review.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chemical handling and probe needle tip cleaning operations must be conducted under a laminar flow exhaust hood with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA cleaning wipes and solvent run-off into dedicated, labeled flammables waste containers with grounded grounding straps; dispose of via certified hazardous chemical waste contractors.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly fabricated Al/Cu bond pads post-passivation etch and forming gas anneal, free from native oxide build-up and organic airborne contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Needle-scrubbed pads free of deep trenching/pitting; wafer surface purged and sealed under inert N2 carrier prior to parametric test completion.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive native oxide and ambient moisture adsorption on test pads causing needle contact resistance instability (>5 Ω), leading to false dielectric leakage readouts and premature probe needle tip fouling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful delivery, incoming acceptance verification, and automated prober signoff of the ultra-low-noise triaxial probe card and matched 180nm DRAM 8F² array test macro, ensuring parametric isolation <1 fA and measurement capability for 28 fF crown cell retention metrology.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PROBE_CARD_ACCEPTANCE_CALIBRATION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `ARRAY_TEST_STRUCTURE_PARAMETRIC_IV_CV_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `TOUCHDOWN_SCRUB_OPTICAL_INSPECTION_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Probe card open-circuit background parasitic leakage current across all signal needles at 1.8 V DC** | `0.5 fA` | <= 1.0 fA | Keysight B1500A B1517A HRSMU 60-second integration current sweep at 23°C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Storage node cell capacitance extraction on 1x64 array test structure** | `28.0 fF/cell` | +/- 2.0 fF/cell | Precision LCR meter Cp-D measurement at 100 kHz, 0.9 V DC plate bias across 10 wafer sites |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Probe card needle contact resistance across 50 consecutive touchdowns on aluminum test pads** | `0.8 Ohm` | <= 1.5 Ohm | 4-wire Kelvin DC resistance measurement on calibrated shorting substrate |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Probe card background leakage verified <= 1.0 fA across 100% of triaxial signal pins at 1.8 V, needle contact resistance <= 1.5 Ω verified over 50 test landings without bond pad rupture, and baseline 28 fF capacitance extracted across target 8F² test arrays with complete acceptance calibration documentation signed off by Metrology Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Sub-Femtoampere Triaxial Direct-Current Leakage Characterization

**Discipline / Category**: Metrology  
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using Optical Inspection / Profilometer.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Measuring DC leakage below 1 fA across an 8F² cell array at 85°C requires sub-femtoampere electrometry integrated into a dry-nitrogen purged, thermally stabilized triaxial probe station. Parasitic cable capacitance combined with high-impedance DUT nodes introduces settling time constants (RC > 10 s) that severely throttle automated parametric wafer testing unless active driven-guard circuitry is extended down to within 200 µm of the probe needle tips. Furthermore, thermal chuck vibrations and Peltier-induced thermo-electric EMF (Seebeck effect) can generate spurious offset currents exceeding 0.2 fA, which will obscure actual capacitor dielectric tunneling and access transistor subthreshold leakage.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node (L=180 nm, W=220 nm, 28 fF crown capacitor), total retention leakage at 85°C must not exceed 1.0 fA/cell at VDD/2 (0.9 V) bias to satisfy the 64 ms refresh window. Characterization must deconvolute three parallel leakage paths: (1) access transistor subthreshold/drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) current, (2) p-n junction trap-assisted band-to-band tunneling (TAT/BTBT) through the storage node contact, and (3) Frenkel-Poole or Fowler-Nordheim emission across the ONO/Ta2O5 dielectric crown stack. Direct single-cell DC testing is prone to triboelectric and dielectric absorption noise; therefore, tests must utilize parallel test structures (e.g., 1,000-cell comb arrays) normalized per cell, or ultra-low leakage triaxial guarded single-cell test pads with micro-stepping settling times (>30 s per bias step).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Source measurement units (SMUs) with 0.1 fA measurement resolution (such as Keysight B1500A/B1517A HRSMU or Keithley 4200A-SCS with 4201-SMU preamps) face stringent procurement lead times and high calibration maintenance overhead in developing semiconductor ecosystems like Vietnam. Precision triaxial probe cards utilizing tungsten-rhenium needles embedded in ceramic Macor or fused-silica bodies with active guarding are single-sourced and fragile. In addition, high-purity dry nitrogen (Grade 5.0, 99.999%) supply stability for continuous environmental dew-point depression (< -60°C) is mandatory to prevent microscopic surface condensation leakage pathways.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: From an operational schedule standpoint, characterizing sub-fA current requires excessively long integration times (PLC >= 10 to 50 power line cycles) and settle delays of 15-45 seconds per voltage step. Measuring full I-V curves across 5 wafer sites on 25-wafer lots would stall inline parametric test lines for days. Laya PM requires a dual-track protocol: an inline screen measuring 1,000-cell array leakage at fixed operational bias points (0.9 V and 1.8 V) with a tight 5-second per site budget, supplemented by an offline comprehensive R&D characterization on dedicated split wafers to deconvolve dielectric and junction leakage physics.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Moisture-induced surface ionic conduction across passivation oxide and unguarded probe pad periphery, inducing false parasitic leakage currents between 10 fA and 1 pA at elevated temperature/humidity.
1. Dielectric relaxation and absorption currents in the triaxial coaxial cabling or probe insulation material yielding pseudo-exponential decay tails that masquerade as true steady-state DC leakage.
1. Triboelectric charge accumulation and mechanical micro-vibration of probe needles during chuck thermal expansion causing displacement current spikes (i = C * dV/dt + V * dC/dt) exceeding 5 fA.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-01` | **Single-Cell Storage Node DC Leakage Characterization at 85°C** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer equipped with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (0.1 fA noise floor), triaxial probe station with heated vacuum chuck (Cascade Microtech Summit 12000), shielded dark box, dew-point controller maintaining chuck enclosure dew point < -60°C, and ceramic-body actively guarded triaxial probe tips. | 1. Land actively guarded triaxial probes onto the 1T1C single-cell test structure: Bitline (BL), Wordline (WL), Storage Node Plate (VPL), and P-well substrate. 2. Force WL to -0.5 V (hard turn-off access transistor), P-well to 0 V, and VPL to 0.9 V (VDD/2). 3. Apply a voltage sweep on BL from 0.0 V to 1.8 V in 50 mV steps with a hold time of 30 seconds and measurement integration time set to 20 PLC (Power Line Cycles). 4. Record steady-state terminal currents on Storage Node/BL and measure gate/well currents to isolate leakage paths. 5. Extract storage node net DC leakage current at operational retention bias point (V_cell = 1.8 V and 0.0 V relative to VPL). | `Total steady-state leakage current entering/leaving the storage node must be strictly <= 1.0 fA at V_cell = 0.9 V relative to VPL (0 V or 1.8 V absolute cell node bias) at 85°C. Open-circuit noise baseline must remain <= 0.08 fA throughout the sweep.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-02` | **Crown Capacitor Dielectric Tunneling vs Access Transistor Subthreshold Separation** | Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer with 4201-SMU Remote Preamplifiers, triaxial probe wedge assembly, Faraday dark cage with pneumatic vibration isolation table, thermal chuck operating at 25°C and 85°C. | 1. On the 1,000-cell crown capacitor array (access transistors bypassed): Apply bias across top plate and bottom storage nodes from 0 V to 2.5 V in 100 mV steps (hold time 10 s, integration 10 PLC). Measure array current and divide by 1,000 to determine per-cell dielectric leakage I_diel. 2. On the 1,000-cell access transistor array (capacitors absent): Set V_ds = 1.8 V, V_bs = 0 V; sweep V_gs from -0.8 V to +0.5 V at 85°C. Measure subthreshold slope (SS) and off-state subthreshold leakage I_sub at V_gs = -0.2 V and 0.0 V. Divide by 1,000. 3. Synthesize total retention leakage: I_tot = I_diel + I_sub + I_junction. | `Per-cell capacitor dielectric leakage I_diel at 85°C and V_cap = 0.9 V must be <= 0.35 fA/cell. Access transistor off-state leakage I_sub at V_gs = -0.2 V, V_ds = 1.8 V, 85°C must be <= 0.45 fA/cell. Combined total leakage must not exceed 0.90 fA/cell.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloved for probe handling), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/splash-resistant safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and grounded ESD wrist strap, Thermal safety handling gloves for hot chuck servicing above 60°C
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of thermal contact burn from hot chuck (85°C-150°C), immediately immerse affected skin under cool running deionized water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical evaluation; do not apply salves. For IPA eye splash, rinse thoroughly at the nearest certified eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. If high-flow N2 purge leak induces asphyxiation symptoms (dizziness, hypoxia), move casualty immediately to fresh ambient air and administer oxygen if trained.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station thermal chamber exhaust must be connected to the dedicated cleanroom solvent/heat exhaust duct with minimum airflow of 75 CFM (0.035 m³/s). Continuous oxygen deficiency monitoring sensors (set point alarm at 19.5% O2) must be operational within a 2-meter radius of the N2-purged probe enclosure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and lens papers must be disposed of in dedicated, grounded, self-closing hazardous flammable waste cans for incineration. No chemical liquid effluents generated during electrical probe testing.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / SEMI Grade 1 | `99.9%` |
| **Dry Compressed Nitrogen Gas** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (Electronic Grade) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed Metal-1 / Passivation open etch with post-ash solvent clean, pristine dry pad metallurgy (aluminum-copper or nickel-gold caps) free of organic residue or native oxide skin.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Unoxidized, mechanically scrubbed probe pad impressions within specification (< 15 µm scrub mark depth, no delamination), returned to sealed N2 purge desiccator (< 5% RH).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended cleanroom ambient air exposure (> 45 minutes) causes atmospheric moisture adsorption and airborne amine/siloxane contamination on passivation surfaces, resulting in parasitic surface tracking paths that elevate measured leakage by 10x-100x (simulating false dielectric breakdown).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful electrical verification and deconvolution of sub-femtoampere DC leakage currents for the 180nm 1T1C 28 fF crown-type DRAM cell at both room temperature (25°C) and maximum operating retention junction temperature (85°C). The test package proves retention leakage compliance (< 1.0 fA/cell) to validate the target 64 ms refresh cycle without parasitic surface or instrumentation leakage corruption.

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Parametric qualification signoff requires across-wafer median leakage <= 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C across all 5 test sites on 3 qualification wafers, instrumentation baseline verified <= 0.08 fA, zero dielectric breakdown occurrences below 2.5 V, and formal peer review endorsement by DRAM Foundation VN Metrology and Integration Councils.

critics.systems_engineer: Measuring DC leakage below 1 fA across an 8F² cell array at 85°C requires sub-femtoampere electrometry integrated into a dry-nitrogen purged, thermally stabilized triaxial probe station. Parasitic cable capacitance combined with high-impedance DUT nodes introduces settling time constants (RC > 10 s) that severely throttle automated parametric wafer testing unless active driven-guard circuitry is extended down to within 200 µm of the probe needle tips. Furthermore, thermal chuck vibrations and Peltier-induced thermo-electric EMF (Seebeck effect) can generate spurious offset currents exceeding 0.2 fA, which will obscure actual capacitor dielectric tunneling and access transistor subthreshold leakage.
critics.domain_expert: At 180nm node (L=180 nm, W=220 nm, 28 fF crown capacitor), total retention leakage at 85°C must not exceed 1.0 fA/cell at VDD/2 (0.9 V) bias to satisfy the 64 ms refresh window. Characterization must deconvolute three parallel leakage paths: (1) access transistor subthreshold/drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) current, (2) p-n junction trap-assisted band-to-band tunneling (TAT/BTBT) through the storage node contact, and (3) Frenkel-Poole or Fowler-Nordheim emission across the ONO/Ta2O5 dielectric crown stack. Direct single-cell DC testing is prone to triboelectric and dielectric absorption noise; therefore, tests must utilize parallel test structures (e.g., 1,000-cell comb arrays) normalized per cell, or ultra-low leakage triaxial guarded single-cell test pads with micro-stepping settling times (>30 s per bias step).
critics.supply_chain: Source measurement units (SMUs) with 0.1 fA measurement resolution (such as Keysight B1500A/B1517A HRSMU or Keithley 4200A-SCS with 4201-SMU preamps) face stringent procurement lead times and high calibration maintenance overhead in developing semiconductor ecosystems like Vietnam. Precision triaxial probe cards utilizing tungsten-rhenium needles embedded in ceramic Macor or fused-silica bodies with active guarding are single-sourced and fragile. In addition, high-purity dry nitrogen (Grade 5.0, 99.999%) supply stability for continuous environmental dew-point depression (< -60°C) is mandatory to prevent microscopic surface condensation leakage pathways.
critics.laya_pm: From an operational schedule standpoint, characterizing sub-fA current requires excessively long integration times (PLC >= 10 to 50 power line cycles) and settle delays of 15-45 seconds per voltage step. Measuring full I-V curves across 5 wafer sites on 25-wafer lots would stall inline parametric test lines for days. Laya PM requires a dual-track protocol: an inline screen measuring 1,000-cell array leakage at fixed operational bias points (0.9 V and 1.8 V) with a tight 5-second per site budget, supplemented by an offline comprehensive R&D characterization on dedicated split wafers to deconvolve dielectric and junction leakage physics.
critical_failure_modes: Moisture-induced surface ionic conduction across passivation oxide and unguarded probe pad periphery, inducing false parasitic leakage currents between 10 fA and 1 pA at elevated temperature/humidity.
Dielectric relaxation and absorption currents in the triaxial coaxial cabling or probe insulation material yielding pseudo-exponential decay tails that masquerade as true steady-state DC leakage.
Triboelectric charge accumulation and mechanical micro-vibration of probe needles during chuck thermal expansion causing displacement current spikes (i = C * dV/dt + V * dC/dt) exceeding 5 fA.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Guarded Triaxial Probe Station Fixture Setup and Noise-Floor Calibration

### Executive Summary & Objective
This procedure specifies the hardware setup, triaxial active-guard routing, environmental shielding, and system calibration required to qualify a wafer-level probe station for sub-femtoampere direct-current (DC) leakage metrology on 180nm 1T1C DRAM cells. The primary target is ensuring a clean instrumentation noise floor capable of verifying junction/dielectric leakage targets strictly **$< 1\text{ fA/cell}$** at operating thermal conditions ($85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Faraday Shield &    │
│  Triaxial Cable Check  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Thermal Chuck      │
│    Conditioning 85C    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Open-Circuit      │
│    Baseline & Triax    │
│   Guard Verification   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   System Noise Floor   │
│  Acceptance Test < 1   │
│           fA           │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Faraday Enclosure & Vibration Isolation Setup**:
   - Float the pneumatic optical isolation table to decouple microphonic and mechanical ambient vibration.
   - Inspect the dark Faraday enclosure around the wafer stage; seal all optical access ports and verify ground continuity to clean instrumentation ground ($R_{\text{ground}} < 1\ \Omega$).
2. **Triaxial Cable Routing & Active Guard Fixturing**:
   - Connect high-isolation, low-noise triaxial cables (Centre Conductor: Force/Sense; Inner Shield: Active Guard; Outer Shield: Chassis Ground) directly from the Source Measure Unit (SMU) preamplifier to the probe arm manipulators.
   - Enforce minimum bend radius specifications on triaxial runs to prevent triboelectric charge buildup and micro-fractures in PTFE/Teflon insulation.
   - Connect the active guard potential of the SMU directly to the probe tip's concentric guard ring to eliminate cable/chuck shunt leakage paths.
3. **Thermal Conditioning of the Wafer Chuck**:
   - Set the thermal wafer chuck controller to $85^\circ\text{C}$ to match the standard retention qualification temperature.
   - Allow thermal stabilization for $\ge 30\text{ minutes}$ with closed enclosure lid to eliminate thermal drift and thermoelectric EMF voltages.
4. **Open-Circuit Triax Offset & Settling Calibration**:
   - Lift tungsten probe tips completely off the wafer surface ($\ge 500\ \mu\text{m}$ clearance).
   - Apply an SMU auto-zero / open-lead correction with an integration aperture set to 10–20 Power Line Cycles (NPLC).
   - Perform a stepped bias sweep across operating potential (0 V to nominal cell operating voltage) and monitor displacement/dielectric relaxation settling time.
5. **System Residual Noise-Floor Measurement & Sign-Off**:
   - Record continuous open-circuit current under full guarding at $85^\circ\text{C}$ across a 60-second measurement window.
   - Ensure peak-to-peak and root-mean-square (RMS) baseline fluctuations are safely below the 1 fA detection threshold.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition / Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **System Noise Floor (Residual Leakage)** | **$< 1.0$** | **fA** | Open-circuit probe lift-off, SMU guarded at $85^\circ\text{C}$, 10 NPLC |
| **Chuck Thermal Stability** | **$85.0 \pm 0.5$** | **$^\circ\text{C}$** | 4-wire RTD sensor reading during retention leakage qualification |
| **Target Storage Capacitance Budget** | **$\ge 28.0$** (range: $25 - 30$) | **fF/cell** | Crown-type stacked capacitor high-frequency C-V / charge extraction |
| **Data Retention Qualification Time** | **$> 64.0$** | **ms** | Refresh interval verification baseline at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### Citations of Literature Context
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *Context reference*: "Capacitance Budget: Minimum 28 fF per cell ensures noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling capacitance. Leakage Current Target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval..."
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *Context reference*: "The storage capacitor must maintain a minimum capacitance of 25 to 30 fF (femtofarads) per cell to ensure data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C. In 180nm nodes, stacked capacitors (Crown or Cylinder type) utilize silicon nitride (Si3N4) or tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5)..."

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Guarded triaxial cabling and chuck isolation must maintain an impedance mismatch barrier exceeding 100 TΩ up to the Keithley 4200A-SCS / Keysight B1500A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU) preamplifier head. Driven-guard potentials must track force terminals within 100 µV across the full ±1.5 V DRAM operating range to null capacitive displacement currents (i = C * dV/dt) and leakage across cable dielectric layers during sub-femtoampere cell retention evaluations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct-current leakage characterization of the 28 fF crown capacitor dielectric stack (e.g., Al2O3/ZrO2 laminate) requires verifying sub-femtoampere (< 1 fA) sensitivity to guarantee target DRAM retention time (> 64 ms at 85°C). Uncompensated triboelectric charge on PTFE/Kel-F probe arm isolators, thermal EMF gradients (> 100 nV/°C), and humidity-induced surface ionic conduction will mask genuine Fowler-Nordheim or Poole-Frenkel leakage currents if the Faraday dark box is not purged to < 5% RH.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-low noise triaxial probe manipulators (e.g., FormFactor/Cascade Microtech DCM-200 series or MPI TITAN-T) and custom gold-plated beryllium copper or tungsten triaxial probe tips incurs a 16 to 22 week procurement lead time. Local vendor alternatives must be pre-screened for hermetic low-noise triax-to-BNC/SMA breakout boxes and high-purity dry nitrogen purge interlocks to prevent test bay commissioning bottlenecks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement and physical qualification of this buy-item probe station fixture represent a gating predecessor for Crown Capacitor 3D Stack soft-error and leakage sign-off. Milestone M2.3 requires noise-floor calibration sign-off within 5 business days of delivery; failure to achieve baseline certification halts physical wafer characterization and slips tape-out readiness for Gen 2 180nm cell architecture.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Driven-guard potential offset exceeding 1 mV, creating parasitic leakage currents (> 10 fA) between guard and force conductors through cable polyolefin/fluoropolymer insulation.
1. Triboelectric or piezoelectric microphonic charge accumulation induced by building acoustic vibration or turbulent nitrogen purge flow (> 5 L/min) directly impinging on unshielded probe needles.
1. Moisture condensation and ionic contamination forming a surface conductive path across chuck ceramic sapphire/alumina standoffs when operating under elevated temperature retention sweeps.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-1-01` | **Open-Circuit Steady-State Noise Floor & Triaxial Guard Offset Verification** | Keysight B1500A with B1517A High Resolution SMU (HRSMU) or Keithley 4200A-SCS with 4200-PA Remote Preamplifier, Semi-Automated Guarded Triaxial Probe Station inside an optical Faraday Dark Shielding Box, Agilent 3458A 8.5-Digit DMM. | 1. Connect HRSMU Force, Guard, and Shield via triaxial low-noise cables (Model 4200-TRX) to Probe Manipulators 1 and 2. 2. Verify voltage difference between Guard and Force terminals using 3458A DMM in high-Z mode across 0.0 V, +1.0 V, and -1.0 V setpoints. 3. Configure SMU in DC Voltage mode: hold 0.000 V for 300 seconds settlement to exhaust dielectric absorption. 4. Execute current sampling integration at 10 PLC over 100 consecutive points. 5. Step force voltage from -1.5 V to +1.5 V in 100 mV increments, recording current with 10-second hold per step. | `Guard-to-Force offset voltage must measure <= 150 µV. RMS noise floor at 0 V must be < 0.20 fA, and maximum instantaneous leakage across the full -1.5 V to +1.5 V DC sweep must not exceed ±0.80 fA.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-1-02` | **Dielectric Absorption Relaxation and Chuck Triaxial Isolation Resistance Characterization** | Keysight B1500A / Keithley 4200A-SCS, High-Isolation Triaxial Thermal Chuck with Guarded Chuck Top Plate, Temperature Controller, Optical Faraday Shield. | 1. Apply a stress voltage of +5.0 V between chuck top plate (Force) and system ground with Guard actively driven for 60 seconds. 2. Step voltage instantaneously to 0.0 V and record the discharging/relaxation current transient at 1-second intervals for 180 seconds to quantify dielectric absorption / charge relaxation. 3. Apply a sustained +2.0 V bias across chuck top plate to bottom base for 120 seconds and calculate effective isolation resistance (R_iso = V_applied / I_measured). | `Dielectric relaxation current must decay below 0.50 fA within 60 seconds of 0 V transition. Sustained chuck isolation resistance (R_iso) must be >= 50.0 TΩ at +2.0 V (corresponding to measured leakage current <= 40.0 fA).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static/ESD safe, powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/impact-resistant safety spectacles with side shields, Dissipative ESD Cleanroom Coat and Conductive Heel Straps, Thermal insulating gloves (rated for -40°C to +150°C during thermal chuck handling)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with copious clean water at emergency eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmic medical evaluation. Skin Contact: Wash exposed area with mild soap and water; remove solvent-wetted gloves. Inhalation: Nitrogen displacement can cause rapid asphyxiation without warning; evacuate victim immediately into fresh air, initiate CPR if breathing ceases, and provide supplemental oxygen via trained first responder.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom air recirculation with dedicated local exhaust extraction (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s) on solvent cleaning wipes. Triaxial purge cabinet must feature continuous ambient oxygen monitoring with acoustic alarm set at < 19.5% O2 to safeguard against N2 asphyxiation in the enclosed metrology bay.
