---

### **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)**

#### **Title:** Temperature-Dependent DC Leakage Measurement & 85°C I-V Sweep Execution  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Gen 2 (µm)  
**Target Structure:** 1T1C Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) Cell ($8F^2$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$)

---

### **1. Scope & Objective**
Characterize sub-femtoampere direct-current ($DC$) leakage paths—comprising pass-transistor subthreshold leakage, access junction band-to-band tunneling/Shockley-Read-Hall generation, and crown capacitor dielectric leakage—at elevated junction temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$) to guarantee the minimum $> 64\text{ ms}$ DRAM cell retention interval.

---

### **2. Equipment & Test Setup**
- **Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer / SMU:** Keysight B1500A (equipped with High-Resolution SMU B1517A or Keithley 4200A-SCS with pre-amplifier remote unit).
- **Prober Station:** Temperature-controlled triaxial analytical probe station with enclosed dark box, dry nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) environmental purge, and active driven-guard coaxial/triaxial cabling.
- **Thermal Chuck Controller:** Closed-loop thermo-chuck capable of steady-state temperature stability within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across $25^\circ\text{C} - 125^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### **3. Step-by-Step Procedure**

#### **Step 1: Environmental Purge & Thermal Chuck Stabilization**
1. Load the 180nm DRAM test structure wafer onto the vacuum chuck.
2. Seal the prober enclosure and initiate a dry $\text{N}_2$ purge ($> 15\text{ SCFH}$) until the internal relative humidity drops below $5\%$ to prevent condensation and moisture-induced surface current paths.
3. Set the thermal chuck controller to **$85.0^\circ\text{C}$** and allow thermal soaking for a minimum of 15 minutes until chuck temperature settles within **$\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.

#### **Step 2: Sub-Femtoampere Triaxial Guarding & Zero-Offset Calibration**
1. Route triaxial inner shields (driven guard) directly to the probe needles contacting the Bitline ($\text{BL}$), Wordline ($\text{WL}$), Storage Node ($\text{SN}$ pad), and Substrate/Well ($\text{V}_{\text{BB}}$).
2. Execute open-circuit zero-null calibration with probes lifted $50\ \mu\text{m}$ above the contact pads.
3. Verify that the open-circuit baseline noise floor of the SMU does not exceed $\pm 50\text{ aA}$ ($0.05\text{ fA}$) over a 60-second baseline recording window.

#### **Step 3: Pin Bias & Terminal Conditions**
Contact the device terminals with tungsten/beryllium-copper probe tips:
- **Substrate / P-Well ($\text{V}_{\text{BB}}$):** Apply back-bias $\text{V}_{\text{BB}} = -0.5\text{ V}$ to $-0.8\text{ V}$ (or $0.0\text{ V}$ per test specification).
- **Wordline ($\text{WL}$ / Gate):** Force $\text{V}_{\text{WL}} = 0.0\text{ V}$ (access transistor turned OFF; inactive state). *(Note: Active state overdrive uses on-chip $\text{V}_{\text{PP}} \ge 2.5\text{ V} - 2.8\text{ V}$ during write/read cycles).*
- **Storage Node ($\text{SN}$):** Force full-charge state $\text{V}_{\text{SN}} = \text{V}_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ to test worst-case data '1' retention condition.
- **Capacitor Plate ($\text{V}_{\text{PL}}$):** Set cell plate to mid-point reference $\text{V}_{\text{plate}} = \text{V}_{\text{DD}} / 2 = 0.9\text{ V}$.

#### **Step 4: 85°C I-V Sweep Execution**
1. Configure SMU on the Bitline ($\text{BL}$) terminal:
   - **Mode:** Staircase Voltage Sweep.
   - **Sweep Range:** $\text{V}_{\text{BL}} = 0.0\text{ V}$ to $1.8\text{ V}$ in steps of $\le 50\text{ mV}$.
   - **Current Limit (Compliance):** $100\text{ pA}$ (to protect ultra-thin $3.5\text{ nm}$ gate oxide and $3 - 4\text{ nm}$ EOT capacitor dielectric).
   - **Settling Delay:** Set pre-measurement settling delay $\ge 500\text{ ms}$ per step to allow displacement currents ($I = C \cdot \frac{dV}{dt}$) of the $28\text{ fF}$ cell capacitor and fixture parasitics to decay below the leakage threshold.
   - **Integration Aperture:** Set Analog-to-Digital Converter integration aperture to **10 NPLC** (Power Line Cycles) or Long Mode to filter $50/60\text{ Hz}$ line noise.
2. Execute the sweep and record $I_{\text{BL}}$ vs. $\text{V}_{\text{BL}}$, $I_{\text{SN}}$, and $I_{\text{BB}}$ simultaneously.

#### **Step 5: Leakage Extraction & Pass/Fail Analysis**
1. Extract the worst-case leakage current $I_{\text{leak, total}}$ at $\text{V}_{\text{SN}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ and $\text{V}_{\text{BL}} = 0.0\text{ V}$ ($|V_{\text{DS}}| = 1.8\text{ V}$).
2. Decompose $I_{\text{leak}}$ into junction/subthreshold leakage ($I_{\text{DS, off}}$ flowing into $\text{BL}$) and dielectric leakage ($I_{\text{diel}}$ flowing from $\text{SN}$ to plate).

---

### **4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics**

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Cell DC Leakage Current at 85°C** | **$< 1.0$** | $\text{fA/cell}$ | SMU current extraction at $V_{\text{SN}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{BL}} = 0.0\text{ V}$, $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Storage Node Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | **$\ge 28.0$** (range: $25.0 - 30.0$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Small-signal high-frequency $C$-$V$ meter ($1\text{ MHz}$) |
| **Calculated Cell Retention Time at 85°C** | **$> 64$** | $\text{ms}$ | Derived retention: $t_{\text{ret}} = \frac{C_s \cdot \Delta V_{\text{margin}}}{I_{\text{leak}}} > 64\text{ ms}$ |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature Stability** | **$85.0 \pm 0.5$** | $^\circ\text{C}$ | RTD sensor reading during active sweep execution |

---

### **5. Literature Sources & Citations**
- *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*:
  - Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$); unit cell layout ($8F^2$); minimum cell capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF}$; leakage current specification $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*:
  - Storage capacitor retention requirement ($25 - 30\text{ fF}$ per cell to ensure data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$); crown capacitor dielectric EOT ($3 - 4\text{ nm}$); gate oxide thickness ($3.5\text{ nm}$).
- *High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture*:
  - Core supply voltage $\text{V}_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$; pass transistor threshold voltage $V_{\text{th}} \approx 0.5\text{ V} - 0.7\text{ V}$; wordline overdrive voltage $\text{V}_{\text{PP}} \ge 2.5\text{ V} - 2.8\text{ V}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Measuring sub-femtoampere DC leakage at elevated 85°C chuck temperature demands strict thermal-dielectric decoupling. Thermal expansion mismatch between triaxial chuck platen, tungsten prober tips, and 180nm Cu/Al bondpads can cause probe skate exceeding ±1.2 µm over an extended I-V dwell time, damaging thin-film crown top electrodes and injecting mechanical strain-induced piezoelectric leakage currents into the 28 fF capacitor dielectric stack.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, thermal generation current across the cell pass transistor junction and Poole-Frenkel or trap-assisted tunneling within the crown dielectric scale exponentially (Arrhenius relationship with Ea ~ 0.6–1.1 eV). If settling times per voltage step are below 5τ (dielectric relaxation plus triaxial cable RC delay), dielectric absorption and displacement current artifacts will overwhelm the true intrinsic DC leakage target of < 1 fA per cell.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dry thermal chuck purge relies on continuous boil-off liquid nitrogen (LN2) or ultra-high-purity gaseous nitrogen (UHP N2 99.999%) dew-point suppression (< -65°C). Any localized supply bottleneck or line-pressure drop in cleanroom bulk N2 delivery will lead to condensation and micro-frost formation during cooldown or rapid humidity ingress at 85°C, causing catastrophic surface flashover across unguarded probe needle shanks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal chuck dwell times combined with femtoampere integration cycles (long integration time >= 16 power line cycles) severely bottleneck automated prober throughput across 200mm/300mm test wafers. Balancing 64-site statistical retention verification with a maximum 30-minute air queue time before surface organic re-contamination requires strict wafer-level test site sampling optimization.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal tip-skate puncture through the high-k crown capacitor top electrode or barrier layer, causing ohmic short-circuiting to the cell plate.
1. Moisture and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption on unguarded Kelvin prober tips during 85°C exposure, masking intrinsic cell leakage with parasitic surface shunt conduction.
1. Electromigration or thermal creep of prober tips leading to intermittent contact resistance (Rc > 50 Ohm), introducing measurement bounce and premature SMU compliance tripping.

Linearity correlation coefficient R² of the Arrhenius fit must be >= 0.990.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-resistant cryogenic/high-temp Kevlar handling gloves (rated up to 250°C), Cleanroom class 100 anti-static nitrile gloves under-glove layer, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety goggles, Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat / ESD bunny suit
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For thermal burns from 85°C chuck contact: Immediately irrigate the burn area with cool, sterile saline or potable water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing and seek cleanroom occupational health personnel. For asphyxiation hazard due to N2 line breach: Promptly move the victim to fresh air, administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored, and initiate CPR if pulse or breathing ceases.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous prober enclosure local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at >= 50 CFM. Dual redundant ambient oxygen depletion sensor monitors with visual strobe and 85 dB audible sirens calibrated to alarm if cleanroom atmospheric O2 drops below 19.5% by volume.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipe substrates must be sealed in airtight flammable waste bins, grounded against static discharge, and disposed of via hazardous solvent incineration protocols per RCRA cleanroom standards.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly post-deposition or post-anneal pristine aluminum/tungsten probe pads, free of organic hydrocarbons, fluorine residue, and moisture condensation (contact angle < 15°).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically characterized probe pads showing scrub marks < 10% of total pad area, with probe mark depth <= 0.25 µm and zero thermal oxide discoloration, stored under dry N2 purge (RH < 2%).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Air exposure exceeding 30 minutes induces native moisture and ambient hydrocarbon adsorption onto pads and exposed passivation fissures, generating ionic surface conduction paths that elevate measured parasitic leakage above 1 fA and produce false-positive dielectric breakdown indications.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful electrical and thermal verification of sub-femtoampere cell retention leakage across 180nm 8F² crown-type capacitors at 85°C, confirming that intrinsic leakage stays strictly beneath the 1.0 fA/cell retention threshold with robust activation energy.

critics.systems_engineer: Measuring sub-femtoampere DC leakage at elevated 85°C chuck temperature demands strict thermal-dielectric decoupling. Thermal expansion mismatch between triaxial chuck platen, tungsten prober tips, and 180nm Cu/Al bondpads can cause probe skate exceeding ±1.2 µm over an extended I-V dwell time, damaging thin-film crown top electrodes and injecting mechanical strain-induced piezoelectric leakage currents into the 28 fF capacitor dielectric stack.
critics.domain_expert: At 85°C, thermal generation current across the cell pass transistor junction and Poole-Frenkel or trap-assisted tunneling within the crown dielectric scale exponentially (Arrhenius relationship with Ea ~ 0.6–1.1 eV). If settling times per voltage step are below 5τ (dielectric relaxation plus triaxial cable RC delay), dielectric absorption and displacement current artifacts will overwhelm the true intrinsic DC leakage target of < 1 fA per cell.
critics.supply_chain: Dry thermal chuck purge relies on continuous boil-off liquid nitrogen (LN2) or ultra-high-purity gaseous nitrogen (UHP N2 99.999%) dew-point suppression (< -65°C). Any localized supply bottleneck or line-pressure drop in cleanroom bulk N2 delivery will lead to condensation and micro-frost formation during cooldown or rapid humidity ingress at 85°C, causing catastrophic surface flashover across unguarded probe needle shanks.
critics.laya_pm: Thermal chuck dwell times combined with femtoampere integration cycles (long integration time >= 16 power line cycles) severely bottleneck automated prober throughput across 200mm/300mm test wafers. Balancing 64-site statistical retention verification with a maximum 30-minute air queue time before surface organic re-contamination requires strict wafer-level test site sampling optimization.
critical_failure_modes: Thermal tip-skate puncture through the high-k crown capacitor top electrode or barrier layer, causing ohmic short-circuiting to the cell plate.
Moisture and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption on unguarded Kelvin prober tips during 85°C exposure, masking intrinsic cell leakage with parasitic surface shunt conduction.
Electromigration or thermal creep of prober tips leading to intermittent contact resistance (Rc > 50 Ohm), introducing measurement bounce and premature SMU compliance tripping.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Thermal Chuck & Triaxial Shielded SMU Calibration at 85°C
**Branch / Generation**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Gen 2 µm)  
**Process Step**: [Metrology] Temperature-Dependent DC Leakage Measurement & 85°C I-V Sweep Execution  

---

### 1. Calibration Workflow Overview

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Dark Box Enclosure &  │
│     EMI Shielding      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Thermal Chuck Ramp   │
│         to 85C         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Chuck Thermal Soak &  │
│    Stability Check     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Triax Guard Offset   │
│      Compensation      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Sub-Femtoamp      │
│      Open-Circuit      │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Chamber Isolation & Environmental Control**:
   - Secure the wafer prober enclosure and engage the light-tight Faraday dark box to eliminate photoelectric carrier excitation and external 50/60 Hz electromagnetic pickup.
   - Connect the Source Measure Unit (SMU) force, sense, and driven-guard paths using low-noise triaxial cables directly to the thermal chuck and micro-positioner probe heads. Ensure outer shields connect to chassis earth ground and inner shields connect strictly to the driven active guard.

2. **Thermal Chuck Ramp to 85°C**:
   - Power on the closed-loop thermal chuck controller. Program the setpoint temperature to $85.0^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Engage dry CDA (Clean Dry Air) or nitrogen purge across the chuck surface to suppress moisture condensation and dielectric surface leakage.
   - Allow a minimum 15-minute thermal soak once the thermocouple sensor reaches $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ to establish uniform thermal equilibrium and minimize mechanical chuck expansion drift.

3. **Triaxial SMU Offset & Open-Circuit Calibration**:
   - Lift all measurement probes to the open-circuit position (air clearance $\ge 200\,\mu\text{m}$ above the wafer surface).
   - Execute instrument zero-offset / open-circuit calibration on the triaxial SMU at the $85^\circ\text{C}$ operational baseline to null out residual thermal EMF, cable dielectric absorption, and guard offset voltages.
   - Set the SMU measurement integration time to Long / High-Resolution (NPLC $\ge 10$) with the lowest physical current range enabled (10 fA or 100 fA range).

4. **Residual Leakage & Noise Floor Verification**:
   - Perform a 60-second baseline static DC current measurement with 0 V applied to verify that open-circuit background leakage remains well below the DRAM sub-femtoampere verification boundary prior to probing test dies.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                       Calibration Target Parameters    
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░                       │
      Min Cap (fF)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░                       │
                  │▒                                   │
SMU Noise Flr (fA)┤▒                                   │
     Temp Stab (C)┤▓                                   │
                  │▓                                   │
    Chuck Temp (C)┤████████████████████████████████████│
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     21.2     42.5    63.8    85.0 
```

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Tolerance / Baseline |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chuck Temperature Setpoint** | `85.0` | $^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ steady-state |
| **Open-Circuit SMU Leakage Noise Floor** | `< 0.2` | $\text{fA}$ (femtoamperes) | Maximum baseline limit (must be strictly $< 1\,\text{fA}$) |
| **Cell Capacitance Validation Threshold** | `28.0` | $\text{fF}$ (femtofarads) | $\ge 25\text{ to }30\,\text{fF}$ per cell minimum budget |
| **Cell Retention Refresh Target Temperature** | `85.0` | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Standard operational junction test point ($> 64\,\text{ms}$ refresh qualification) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *“Leakage Current Target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval...”*
  - *“Capacitance Budget: Minimum 28 fF per cell ensures noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling capacitance.”*
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *“The storage capacitor must maintain a minimum capacitance of 25 to 30 fF (femtofarads) per cell to ensure data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C.”*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck heating induces significant thermo-mechanical drift across probe micromanipulators and alters the dielectric loss tangent of the low-noise triaxial cable insulation (typically PTFE/Teflon), degrading triaxial guard isolation and increasing settling time for sub-femtoampere currents. The triaxial shield drive amplifier must maintain sub-microvolt guard-to-center offset under dynamic thermal dissipation at 85°C to avoid common-mode leakage currents dominating the <1 fA cell target.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, thermal generation current scales exponentially following Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination-generation kinetics. If chuck surface temperature uniformity deviates beyond ±0.2°C, the crown capacitor dielectric leakage verification will show artificial variance exceeding 15%, falsifying the 28 fF / <1 fA DRAM cell retention modeling. Furthermore, pyroelectric and thermoelectric EMF voltages generated across dissimilar contact metallization (e.g., tungsten probe tips to aluminum pad metallization) must be nulled via dual-polarity open-circuit zeroing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of specialized high-temperature, low-dielectric-absorption triaxial cabling assemblies (e.g., Gore or Belden semi-rigid triaxial assemblies with virgin PTFE dielectric rated to 125°C) and gold-plated thermal chuck surface plates carries lead times up to 16–20 weeks. A dual-vendor strategy for precision thermal chuck controllers (e.g., Temptronic/MPI vs. Cascade/FormFactor) is required to prevent downstream 180nm retention characterization delays.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration cycles at 85°C introduce thermal soaking bottlenecks; thermal chuck stabilization requires a minimum of 45 minutes per wafer batch. Probe tip thermal expansion and subsequent scrub mark drift on 8F² DRAM capacitor contact pads must be monitored via automated split-field optics to ensure pad blowouts or boundary shorts do not consume probe card life budgets.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal expansion-induced probe tip walking off the sub-micron crown capacitor contact pad during 85°C thermal soak, leading to open-circuit or dielectric rupture.
1. Triaxial cable dielectric polarization and charge storage release during elevated temperature steps, masquerading as intrinsic crown dielectric leakage.
1. Local chuck thermal non-uniformity (>0.5°C) across the active die area, skewing Arrhenius extraction of DRAM storage node retention limits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-2-1-01` | **Open-Chuck Triaxial Guard-to-Core Residual Leakage and Noise Floor at 85°C** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU), Temptronic ThermoChuck System with PID controller, Triaxial Gold-Plated Probe Manipulator inside an EMI/Light-Tight Faraday Cage | 1. Verify dry N2 purge flow at 5 SLPM inside the shielded environmental enclosure. 2. Execute automated SMU cable open-circuit zero/offset compensation at 85°C. 3. Apply a DC voltage step from 0.0 V to +1.5 V in 50 mV increments between the triaxial force/sense pin and chuck common ground. 4. Record DC leakage current at each step after an electrical settling hold time of 10.0 seconds. | `Residual background leakage current across 0 V to 1.5 V must be <= 0.35 fA RMS (peak residual < 0.80 fA). Guard-to-core resistance must exceed 1.0 x 10^16 Ohms.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-2-1-02` | **Thermal Chuck Isothermal Uniformity and SMU Drift Characterization at 85°C** | Pt100 4-wire RTD Sensor Matrix (9-point surface distribution on 200mm thermal chuck), Fluke 1586A Super-DAQ Precision Temperature Scanner, Keysight B1500A HRSMU | 1. Continuous logging of 9-point Pt100 surface temperature across the 200mm diameter chuck surface at 1 Hz for 30 minutes. 2. Measure center-to-edge Delta-T across all 9 sensors. 3. Connect triaxial HRSMU to a calibrated 10 Gigaohm standard transfer resistor placed on the chuck surface and perform a continuous 1.0 V DC current measurement for 15 minutes to measure thermal EMF drift. | `Surface temperature across all 9 test points must remain within 85.0°C ± 0.15°C (total spatial deviation <= 0.30°C). Measured SMU current drift through standard load must be <= 0.05% over the 15-minute measurement window.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated for >= 150°C, Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1), Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (under-layer), Static-dissipative lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected skin under cool running potable water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek cleanroom occupational health personnel. IPA Contact: In case of eye contact, irrigate with eyewash station for 15 minutes. Nitrogen Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh air immediately if hypoxia or lightheadedness occurs; administer medical oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous nitrogen purge line exhaust ducted directly to cleanroom HVAC general scrubbed return. Faraday enclosure air exchange rate maintained at >= 20 air changes per hour. Thermal chuck cooling exhaust vented outside local operator breathing zone.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited into dedicated, grounded flammable solvent waste cans with self-closing foot pedals. No liquid waste discharge to municipal drain; dispose via authorized hazardous chemical solvent waste reclamation stream.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Compressed)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 6.0 | `99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, dehydrated wafer with unpassivated crown capacitor test pads free of organic residue and particulate contamination (contact angle < 10°).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermal-tested wafer with pristine test pads showing no severe probe scrub piercing (> 0.2 µm depth) and zero condensed moisture residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption and native oxide formation on open aluminum/tungsten test pads causing contact resistance escalation and parasitic surface moisture leakage channels that mask intrinsic sub-femtoampere cell dielectric leakage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and validation of the thermal chuck heating stage and triaxial shielded SMU subsystem at 85.0°C, verifying an electrical noise floor <= 0.35 fA RMS, guard isolation >= 10^16 Ohms, and thermal chuck surface uniformity within ±0.15°C to support valid 28 fF crown DRAM cell retention characterization.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CALIBRATION_85C_TRIAX_NOISE_FLOOR.csv`
- [ ] `THERMAL_CHUCK_9POINT_UNIFORMITY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `SMU_OFFSET_ZEROING_COEFFICIENTS.json`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Triaxial open-circuit residual leakage current at 85°C across 0 to 1.5 V bias** | `0.25 fA` | <= 0.35 fA RMS | Keysight B1500A HRSMU 16-PLC integration step measurement with open tips elevated above chuck |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Thermal chuck isothermal surface temperature across 9-point grid at 85°C setpoint** | `85.00 °C` | ±0.15 °C | Fluke 1586A Super-DAQ with calibrated 4-wire Pt100 RTD sensor array logging over 30 min |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Triaxial guard-to-core isolation resistance at 85°C with 10V stress** | `5.0 x 10^16 Ohms` | >= 1.0 x 10^16 Ohms | High-voltage guard isolation DC leakage stress test on B1517A SMU |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 3 quantitative assertions verified within nominal tolerances; background noise floor verified at <= 0.35 fA RMS for 3 consecutive 15-minute intervals at 85.0°C; metrology calibration signoff approved by Systems Metrology Lead and DRAM Retention Characterization Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-DRAM180-042
**Title:** Temperature-Step Sub-Threshold & Node Junction Leakage I-V Sweep  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Metrology & Characterization  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the triaxial DC characterization procedure to extract sub-threshold channel leakage and storage node p-n junction leakage currents across temperature setpoints up to 85°C on test structures representing the 180nm 1T1C (8F²) access transistor ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and crown capacitor storage node.

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Test Setup
- **Automated Thermal Wafer Prober:** Shielded dark box with triaxial thermal chuck ($\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ stability, range: $25^\circ\text{C}$ to $125^\circ\text{C}$).
- **Precision Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer:** Equipped with High-Resolution SMUs (HRSMUs) supporting sub-femtoampere ($<0.1\text{ fA}$) measurement resolution.
- **Cabling & Shielding:** Full triaxial connections with driven active guards routed to within $<10\text{ mm}$ of probe tips.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

```
[Step 1: Calibration] ──> [Step 2: Probing Setup] ──> [Step 3: 25°C Baseline Sweep]
                                                                  │
[Step 5: Analysis & Log] <── [Step 4: 85°C High-T Sweep] <───────┘
```

#### Step 1: Open-Circuit Calibration & Residual Floor Verification
1. Lift probe needles $\ge 500\,\mu\text{m}$ above the wafer surface inside the sealed, light-tight triaxial enclosure.
2. Run SMU zero-offset correction and integration noise auto-nulling using Long Integration Time (PLC $\ge 16$ to 32 cycles).
3. Measure the open-circuit triaxial noise floor; verify background residual leakage is $\le 0.1\text{ fA}$ across the $-0.5\text{ V}$ to $+1.8\text{ V}$ range.

#### Step 2: Test Structure Probing & Pinout Assignment
1. Lower tungsten probe tips onto the designated Kelvin/triaxial test pads for the cell access transistor:
   - **SMU 1 (Bitline Node / Shared Contact):** Biased at precharge baseline $V_{\text{pre}} = V_{\text{DD}} / 2 = 0.9\text{ V}$ (or ground for sub-threshold sweeps).
   - **SMU 2 (Wordline Gate):** Swept from $-0.5\text{ V}$ to $+1.8\text{ V}$.
   - **SMU 3 (Storage Node / Crown W-Plug Pad):** Biased at cell high $V_{\text{cell}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ and cell low $0.0\text{ V}$.
   - **SMU 4 (Substrate / Well Contact):** Connected to $V_{\text{BB}} = -0.5\text{ V}$ back-bias or substrate ground.

#### Step 3: Room Temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$) Baseline I-V Sweep
1. Stabilize chuck temperature at $25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Sub-threshold Sweep:** Step $V_{\text{WL}}$ from $-0.2\text{ V}$ to $+1.0\text{ V}$ in $10\text{ mV}$ steps with $V_{\text{drain}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ to extract sub-threshold swing ($S$) and off-state channel current $I_{\text{off}}$ at $V_{\text{WL}} = 0\text{ V}$.
3. **Junction Leakage Sweep:** Hold $V_{\text{WL}} = -0.5\text{ V}$ (fully off), sweep storage node junction voltage $V_{\text{node}}$ from $0\text{ V}$ to $1.8\text{ V}$, measuring current $I_{\text{node}}$ to record baseline reverse-bias diode leakage.

#### Step 4: Temperature-Step Soak & $85^\circ\text{C}$ I-V Sweep Execution
1. Ramp the thermal chuck to $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ at $5^\circ\text{C/min}$. Allow a 15-minute thermal soak to prevent mechanical probe drift and chuck thermal gradient errors.
2. Execute the identical sub-threshold sweep ($V_{\text{WL}} = -0.2\text{ V} \to +1.0\text{ V}$) and junction reverse leakage sweep ($V_{\text{node}} = 0\text{ V} \to 1.8\text{ V}$) under shielded dark-box conditions.
3. Record steady-state off-current at $V_{\text{WL}} = 0\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{node}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, and $V_{\text{BB}} = -0.5\text{ V}$.

#### Step 5: Data Extraction & Pass/Fail Qualification
1. Extract combined off-state leakage $I_{\text{leak, total}} = I_{\text{sub-threshold}} + I_{\text{junction}}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. Verify total leakage satisfies the retention budget for the target retention window ($> 64\text{ ms}$).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Measurement Condition | Target / Tolerance | Physical Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Max Cell DC Leakage Current** | At $T_{\text{chuck}} = 85^\circ\text{C}$, $V_{\text{cell}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{WL}} = 0.0\text{ V}$ | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ |
| **Minimum Cell Storage Capacitance** | $C\text{-}V$ verification at $85^\circ\text{C}$, storage node to plate | $\ge 28.0$ (spec: $25 - 30$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature Stability** | Steady-state soak prior to & during sweep | $85.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Access Transistor Channel Geometry** | In-line CD-SEM / physical gate length | $180 \pm 5$ | $\text{nm}$ |

---

### 5. Literature & Context Citations
- **Transistor Geometry & Leakage Target:** Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*).
- **Capacitance & Retention Lifetime:** Storage capacitor minimum target $28\text{ fF}$ (within the $25 - 30\text{ fF}$ design window) ensuring cell retention interval $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Sources: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*; *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
- **Array Voltage Levels:** Bitline precharge target $V_{\text{DD}}/2$ ($0.9\text{ V}$ at nominal $1.8\text{ V}$ rail) (*Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout*).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Measuring sub-femtoampere currents across thermal stepping (25°C to 85°C) requires strict thermal-mechanical decoupling. Chuck expansion at 85°C induces probe skate on 180nm node landing pads (contact size < 0.22 µm), altering contact resistance and introducing micro-triboelectric charges. Triaxial cabling and Faraday-cage isolation must eliminate parasitic noise floor shifts above 0.1 fA, while settling delays (tau > 5RC) must be enforced after each temperature ramp to prevent displacement current artifacts (I = C * dV/dt + V * dC/dT).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, junction leakage across the access transistor storage node n+/p-well junction shifts from Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination-generation dominance toward diffusion current, exacerbated by trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL) when V_wordline is biased to V_off (-0.2V to 0.0V). To isolate channel sub-threshold conduction from junction perimeter/area leakage, an array-based test vehicle (e.g., 10k-cell test matrix with shorted bitlines) must be measured under swept back-bias (V_sub = 0V to -1.0V) and step gate biases (V_gs from -0.5V to 1.2V).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Thermal chucks capable of low-noise triaxial tri-temp operation (-40°C to 150°C) with ultra-low thermal drift (< 1 µm/°C) rely on specialized peltier/resistive units (e.g., Temptronic or MPI) and beryllium-copper/tungsten-rhenium cat-whisker probe tips. Long lead times (>16 weeks) on sub-fA triaxial feedthroughs and ultra-high impedance SMUs (Keysight B1500A with HRSMU or Keithley 4200A-SCS) necessitate pre-allocated metrology bay reservation and calibrated triax cable assemblies.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal characterization cycles threaten throughput: each 10°C ramp and thermal equilibrium step requires at least 8 to 12 minutes to settle below the 0.05 fA/s drift threshold. Test plans must streamline thermal dwell times and prioritize key screening temperatures (25°C, 55°C, 85°C) to keep wafer-level metrology under 90 minutes per wafer while safeguarding the 64ms DRAM retention window milestone.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal probe walk/skate causing probe tip slip off the sub-micron tungsten contact plug, resulting in open circuits or dielectric punch-through during SMU voltage ramp.
1. Pyroelectric and triboelectric displacement current contamination caused by rapid thermal chuck expansion during temperature stepping exceeding the target 1 fA leakage threshold.
1. Humidity condensation or moisture absorption on unpassivated pad surfaces during cooling cycles, generating parasitic surface ionic conduction channels that mask true silicon junction leakage.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-2-2-01` | **Access Transistor Sub-Threshold Swing & Off-State Leakage vs Temperature (25°C to 85°C)** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer equipped with B1517A High Resolution SMU (0.1 fA resolution), Temptronic ThermoChuck Triaxial Shielded Probe Station, Triaxial Kelvin Low-Noise Cabling inside Dark Faraday Enclosure. | 1. Position triaxial probe tips on Access Transistor Wordline (Gate), Bitline Contact (Drain), Storage Node Plug (Source), and P-well tap (Bulk). 2. Set chuck temperature to 25°C and hold for 10 minutes until thermal drift is < 0.02 fA/min. 3. Bias V_ds = 1.0 V, V_bs = -0.5 V; sweep V_gs from -0.5 V to +1.2 V in 20 mV steps, measuring I_ds and I_leakage with medium integration time (16 PLC) and 500 ms settling delay per point. 4. Ramp chuck temperature in steps of 20°C (45°C, 65°C, 85°C) at 2°C/min; wait 8 minutes dwell time at each plateau for thermal equilibration. 5. Repeat V_gs sweep at each temperature plateau and extract sub-threshold swing (SS, mV/dec) and off-state current I_off at V_gs = 0.0 V. | `Off-state channel leakage I_off at V_gs = 0.0 V, V_ds = 1.0 V must be <= 0.20 fA/cell at 25°C and <= 0.85 fA/cell at 85°C. Sub-threshold swing at 85°C must not exceed 95 mV/decade.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-2-2-02` | **Storage Node n+/p-Well Junction & GIDL Leakage Characterization at 85°C** | Keithley 4200A-SCS Parameter Analyzer with 4201-SMU and 4200-PA Remote Preamplifiers, Shielded Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automatic Probe Station with dry CDA/N2 purge. | 1. Verify contact integrity by performing low-bias ohmic check (-50 mV to +50 mV). 2. Hold access gate at V_wl = -0.2 V (wordline unselected) and substrate at V_sub = -0.8 V. 3. Step storage node voltage V_node from 0.0 V to 1.8 V in 25 mV increments with 1.0 s soak time per step to bleed out transient charging currents. 4. Measure junction reverse leakage current I_node into p-well. 5. Sweep V_wl from -0.5 V to +0.2 V at fixed V_node = 1.5 V to decouple gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL) from bulk band-to-band tunneling (BTBT). 6. Normalize measured total array leakage by 10,000 to determine single-cell equivalent leakage. | `Normalized single-cell storage node junction leakage at V_node = 1.5 V, V_wl = -0.2 V, T = 85°C must be <= 0.95 fA/cell. Total normalized GIDL current at V_wl = -0.5 V, V_node = 1.5 V must be <= 1.20 fA/cell.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal heat-resistant gloves (rated to 150°C) for hot chuck handling, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double gloving required), Anti-static ESD lab coat with continuous conductive grounding wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn exposure: Immediately flood affected skin with cold running water for a minimum of 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; seek immediate medical attention. Inhalation of nitrogen purge displacement (asphyxiation risk): Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has stopped; notify emergency response. Chemical contact (IPA): Flush eyes or skin with sterile eyewash or water for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Probe station thermal chamber purge must vent into continuous house dedicated solvent/exhaust system with minimum airflow velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); room oxygen depletion sensors (ODS) interlocked to audible alarm set at 19.5% O2 threshold.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA cleanroom wipes must be sealed in airtight flammable waste bins and disposed of via certified hazardous solvent disposal contractors. Nitrogen is exhausted to atmospheric relief stack outside facility envelope.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>= 99.9%) | `100%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched contact pads/plugs post-solvent clean (IPA/DI water rinse) and dry bake (110°C, 10 min), free of organic residue and surface native oxide growth (< 1.2 nm).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested wafer surface thermally ramped down to 23°C in dry N2 ambient, pad metallization unoxidized, free of thermal probe pitting exceeding 10% pad area.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes native oxidation and airborne moisture condensation on unpassivated storage node pads, inducing spurious surface leakage paths (> 10 fA) and contact barrier Schottky degradation that invalidates sub-fA metrology accuracy.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full temperature-stepped DC I-V characterization (25°C to 85°C) completed for access transistor sub-threshold slope and storage node junction leakage across wafer sample sites, confirming cell leakage stays within the 1.0 fA/cell retention budget at 85°C for the 180nm open-source DRAM architecture.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WP_DRAM180_IV_TEMP_SWEEP_RAW_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `WP_DRAM180_LEAKAGE_EXTRACTION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `WP_DRAM180_PROBE_LANDING_POST_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum access transistor off-state channel leakage (I_off) at 85°C** | `0.85 fA/cell` | +0.10 fA/cell | Keysight B1500A HRSMU measurement at V_gs = 0.0 V, V_ds = 1.0 V averaged across 20 site dies. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Storage node n+/p-well reverse-bias junction leakage at 85°C (V_node = 1.5V)** | `0.95 fA/cell` | +0.05 fA/cell | Array de-embedding from 10k-cell test matrix under Keithley 4200A-SCS triaxial sweep. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Sub-threshold swing (SS) degradation slope from 25°C to 85°C** | `88 mV/dec` | +/- 7 mV/dec | Log-linear slope fitting of I_ds-V_gs curve over three decades of sub-threshold drain current. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 20 monitored site dies demonstrate normalized total cell leakage (channel I_off + junction leakage) <= 1.0 fA/cell at 85.0°C +/- 0.5°C; background system noise floor confirmed < 0.1 fA before and after test; post-test microscope inspection verifies probe imprint scrub marks remain within landing pad boundaries without dielectric cratering.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Sub-Femtoampere Arrhenius Activation Energy & Retention Lifetime Extraction

**Context Path:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)` > `1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²)` > `Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling` > `Cell Retention & Soft-Error Immunity Metrology (28 fF / <1 fA Leakage Verification)` > `Sub-Femtoampere Triaxial Direct-Current Leakage Characterization` > `Temperature-Dependent DC Leakage Measurement & 85°C I-V Sweep Execution` > **`Sub-Femtoampere Arrhenius Activation Energy & Retention Lifetime Extraction`**  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm) | **Action Type:** Make

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Thermal Chuck     │
│  Setting: 25C to 85C  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Triaxial DC Leakage  │
│      Extraction       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Arrhenius Plot: ln   │
│   I_leak vs 1000/T    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    E_a Slope Fit &    │
│  Retention Tau Calc   │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Environmental Chamber & Triaxial Probe Station Stabilization**:
   - Mount the 180nm 1T1C test array wafer on the thermal chuck. Connect triaxial guarded Kelvin probe lines directly to the cell test pads (storage node crown via tungsten plug / bitline contact).
   - Enclose the probe station in a dry nitrogen-purged, light-tight Faraday shield to suppress ambient photo-generation and humidity-induced leakage.

2. **Multi-Temperature DC Leakage Sweep Execution ($25^\circ\text{C}$ to $85^\circ\text{C}$)**:
   - Program the thermal chuck to sweep temperatures from $25^\circ\text{C}$ up to $85^\circ\text{C}$ (e.g., $25^\circ\text{C}$, $50^\circ\text{C}$, $70^\circ\text{C}$, $85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Allow thermal stabilization ($\pm 0.1^\circ\text{C}$) at each setpoint.
   - Execute sub-femtoampere DC parameter extraction at nominal cell storage voltage to measure total node leakage $I_{\text{leak}}(T)$ (combining access transistor sub-threshold/junction leakage and dielectric conduction through the ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ stack).

3. **Arrhenius Extraction & Activation Energy ($E_a$) Calculation**:
   - Convert Chuck temperatures $T$ to absolute temperature (Kelvin, $K$).
   - Construct the Arrhenius characteristic curve: $\ln(I_{\text{leak}})$ versus $1000/T$.
   - Extract the activation energy $E_a$ from linear regression slope:
     $$\text{Slope} = -\frac{E_a}{k_B} \implies E_a = -k_B \times \frac{d(\ln I_{\text{leak}})}{d(1/T)}$$
   - Identify dominant leakage mechanisms: near silicon bandgap ($E_a \approx 1.1\text{ eV}$) indicating access transistor diffusion/subthreshold leakage, or mid-gap ($E_a \approx 0.55\text{–}0.7\text{ eV}$) indicating SRH generation-recombination / trap-assisted tunneling in the dielectric.

4. **Retention Lifetime ($\tau_{\text{ret}}$) Extrapolation**:
   - Compute retention lifetime at maximum operating temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$):
     $$\tau_{\text{ret}} = \frac{Q_{\text{usable}}}{I_{\text{leak}}(85^\circ\text{C})} = \frac{C_s \cdot \Delta V_{\text{margin}}}{I_{\text{leak}}(85^\circ\text{C})}$$
   - Validate against minimum signal development budget ($\Delta V = 100\text{–}150\text{ mV}$) on bitlines ($C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$, $C_s \ge 25\text{–}28\text{ fF}$).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │███████████████████████████████████│
   Delta V_sig (mV)┤███████████████████████████████████│
                   │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓            │
Ret Time @ 85C (ms)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓            │
        C_cell (fF)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                        │
                   │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                        │
  I_leak @ 85C (fA)┤░                                  │
                   │░                                  │
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                    0       25      50       75     100 
```

1. **Storage Node Leakage Current at $85^\circ\text{C}$**:
   - **Target**: $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*).
2. **Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_s$)**:
   - **Target**: Minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ (allowable range $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$) (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology / Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture*).
3. **Retention Refresh Lifetime at $85^\circ\text{C}$**:
   - **Target**: $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
4. **Readout Differential Signal Voltage ($\Delta V$)**:
   - **Target**: $100\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV}$ developed onto bitline with $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$ (*Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout*).

---

### Context Citations
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Specifies unit cell dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), crown stacked capacitor with ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$, minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$, and junction/subthreshold leakage target of $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: Defines 1T1C storage capacitor target of $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF/cell}$ to guarantee retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, with high-k EOT of $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$.
- **[Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout]**: Establishes bitline sensing condition with $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$, $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$, delivering differential voltage $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Extracting Arrhenius activation energy (E_a) from sub-femtoampere cell retention leakage requires decoupling intrinsic Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) generation-recombination from parasitic tester leakage, triaxial cable dielectric absorption (DA), and moisture-induced surface shunt conductances. The thermal chuck ramp between 25°C and 85°C must implement sufficient thermal stabilization delay (>180 s) to eliminate thermoelectric Seebeck EMF and chuck mechanical drift from distorting pA-to-fA log-linear slope fits.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node with crown-type cell capacitors (C_s ≈ 28 fF) operating under 1 fA retention leakage limits, the apparent activation energy must clearly differentiate between trap-assisted tunneling / band-to-band tunneling (E_a ≈ 0.2–0.4 eV) and depletion region midgap SRH generation (E_a ≈ 0.55–0.60 eV ≈ E_g/2) or diffusion leakage (E_a ≈ 1.1 eV). If the fitted E_a falls below 0.50 eV at 85°C, unpassivated trivalent dangling bonds (P_b centers) at the storage node junction/dielectric interface dominate, directly violating the target 64 ms refresh retention window.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-low-noise triaxial probe needles (e.g., tungsten-rhenium with guarding down to probe tip) and femtoampere SMUs (Keithley 4200-SCS with 4200-PA or Keysight B1500A with HRSMU) have long lead times (>16 weeks) and require certified calibration artifacts. Sourcing ultra-dry CDA/N2 purge gas (dew point <-70°C) is mandatory to prevent ice crystal formation or dew condensation on the guarded triaxial probe head during thermal cycling.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterization throughput is severely gated by SMU integration time (PLC > 10) and settling delays required for settling displacement currents (I = C * dV/dt + V * dC/dt) below 0.1 fA. Testing multi-site arrays across 25°C, 55°C, 70°C, and 85°C risks stalling the Metrology milestone if automated wafer-level chuck stepping and automated triaxial offset zeroing are not scripted with strict time-boxing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Cable Dielectric Absorption & Triboelectric Current: Rapid temperature or position shifts generate transient currents >10 fA, corrupting the low-temperature Arrhenius slope baseline.
1. Moisture Condensation & Surface Leakage: Insufficient dry nitrogen shielding within the triaxial thermal enclosure leads to moisture adsorption across guard rings, artificially depressing the extracted activation energy below 0.3 eV.
1. Probe Needle Thermal Drift & Contact Resistance Instability: Expansion of the thermal chuck between 25°C and 85°C shifts probe needle placement off the 180nm storage node test pad, causing intermittent contact or micro-arcing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-2-3-01` | **Sub-Femtoampere Temperature-Dependent DC Leakage & Arrhenius Slope Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer equipped with B1517A High Resolution SMU (0.1 fA resolution) and ASAP Triaxial Guarded Probe Station with Temptronic ThermoChuck (-40°C to +150°C, dry N2 purge shield). | 1. Land triaxial probe needle onto isolated 1T1C storage node test macro (C_cell = 28 fF) and bitline contact pad. 2. Set chuck temperature sequentially to 25°C, 55°C, 70°C, and 85°C. 3. Allow 300 s soak time at each setpoint for mechanical and thermal equilibrium. 4. Apply storage node bias V_SN = 1.0 V with substrate grounded and access transistor gate turned OFF (V_WL = -0.5 V). 5. Measure DC leakage current I_leak integrating over 10 PLC with 60 s delay for displacement current decay. 6. Plot ln(I_leak) versus 1000/T (K^-1) and extract slope -E_a/k_B via linear regression. | `DC leakage current at 85°C must be <= 1.0 fA; extracted Arrhenius activation energy E_a must be >= 0.55 eV (indicating midgap SRH-dominated generation) with linear regression coefficient of determination R^2 >= 0.985.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-2-3-02` | **Projected Cell Retention Lifetime & 64ms Window Derivation** | Keithley 4200-SCS with 4200-PA Remote Preamplifiers, triaxial test fixture, Faraday dark cage, temperature controller. | 1. Measure instantaneous retention discharge rate by applying full cell charge V_0 = 1.2 V (Q_0 = C_s * V_0 = 33.6 fC). 2. Record voltage droop Delta_V over holding time t_hold at 85°C under dry N2 atmosphere. 3. Calculate retention lifetime t_retention = (C_s * Delta_V_margin) / I_leak(85°C), where Delta_V_margin = 0.4 V. 4. Extrapolate retention distribution across 100 sample cells across center, mid-radius, and edge die locations. | `Projected storage cell retention time t_ret at 85°C must be >= 64.0 ms across all evaluated cells; catastrophic early tail bit retention fail rate must be < 0.01%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal insulating heat-resistant gloves (rated to 150°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, Class 100), Static-dissipative lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately immerse affected area in cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves; cover with sterile dressing and seek medical attention. Asphyxiation (Nitrogen displacement): Remove victim to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom air exchange (>60 air changes/hour); probe station equipped with dedicated oxygen-deficiency monitor (ODS alarm threshold < 19.5% O2) and local exhaust vent for thermal chuck purge exhaust.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA-wetted swab materials must be disposed of in dedicated flammable-waste hermetic containers for regulated solvent incineration; no liquid chemical effluent produced during routine metrology.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen, compressed gas (Chamber Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (Probe Needle Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-passivation (POA 450°C forming gas annealed) with intact silicon nitride / oxide cap; pristine dry aluminum/tungsten pad metallization free of native oxide overgrowth.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pads probe-scrub inspected (scrub mark depth < 50 nm); wafer maintained in hermetic FOUP under dry N2 to prevent moisture adsorption before package wire-bonding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes atmospheric humidity condensation and hydrocarbon adsorption on test pads and passivation sidewalls, increasing parasitic surface shunt currents beyond 10 fA and corrupting Arrhenius activation energy extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable extraction of DRAM cell leakage activation energy (E_a >= 0.55 eV) and retention lifetime validation exceeding 64 ms at 85°C across 180nm crown capacitor test structures with leakage current verified under 1.0 fA.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Arrhenius_Activation_Energy_Extraction_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Sub_Femtoampere_Leakage_Temperature_Sweep_Raw_Data.csv`
- [ ] `Retention_Time_Distribution_85C_Histogram.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Storage node cell DC leakage current at 85°C chuck temperature under 1.0 V reverse bias** | `0.75 fA` | +0.25 fA, -0.50 fA (max 1.00 fA) | Keysight B1500A HRSMU integration measurement (10 PLC, triaxial guarded enclosure, baseline subtracted) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Extracted Arrhenius activation energy (E_a) from 25°C to 85°C temperature sweep** | `0.58 eV` | +/- 0.03 eV | Linear regression analysis of ln(I_leak) vs 1000/T across 4 distinct temperature setpoints |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Projected minimum 1T1C storage retention time at 85°C for C_s = 28 fF and Delta_V = 0.4 V** | `112 ms` | -48 ms (strictly >= 64 ms) | Analytical derivation t_ret = (C_s * Delta_V) / I_leak(85°C) verified by voltage retention droop sampling |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All tested storage nodes on minimum 3 sample dies demonstrate leakage <= 1.0 fA at 85°C, extracted activation energy E_a >= 0.55 eV with regression fit R^2 >= 0.985, confirming dominant SRH depletion kinetics and retention lifetime exceeding 64 ms without early breakdown tail bits.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Subthreshold vs Junction Leakage Extraction & Retention Time Budget Analysis

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) [DRAM Architecture] > Crown-Type Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) 3D Stack & Dielectric Modeling [Circuit Design] > Cell Retention & Soft-Error Immunity Metrology (28 fF / <1 fA Leakage Verification) [Metrology] > Sub-Femtoampere Triaxial Direct-Current Leakage Characterization [Metrology] > Subthreshold vs Junction Leakage Extraction & Retention Time Budget Analysis [Metrology]
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Cell Capacitance Cs >= 28 fF, Read Margin Delta V >= 150 mV.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer / SPICE Verification.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Allocating retention time budgets across 180nm 1T1C cells requires strict partitioning between access transistor subthreshold leakage (I_sub) and storage node n+/p-well junction leakage (I_junc, comprising Shockley-Read-Hall recombination, trap-assisted tunneling, and band-to-band tunneling). At 85°C, with a nominal storage node capacitance C_s = 28 fF and bitline precharge V_BL = V_DD/2 = 0.9 V, maintaining differential sense margin ΔV ≥ 120 mV requires cell storage node voltage V_cell(t) to retain at least 1.45 V over a 64 ms refresh window. Total permissible leakage current cannot exceed I_total_leak = C_s * (ΔV_margin) / t_refresh = 28 fF * (1.8 V - 1.45 V) / 64 ms ≈ 0.153 fA, which necessitates an absolute worst-case target of <1.0 fA across 3-sigma process-voltage-temperature corners. Neglecting negative wordline bias (V_NWL = -0.5 V) in system power budget modeling will lead to catastrophic retention failures due to exponential subthreshold tailing.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Deconvolving I_sub from I_junc at sub-femtoampere scales cannot be achieved by single-point DC measurements on single-cell test structures due to the noise floor of standard parametric analyzers (~0.5 fA to 1 fA). Metrology must employ Kelvin triaxial guard structures on both single-transistor scribe test elements and dense 10^4-cell parallel array test keys. Temperature-dependent Arrhenius activation energy extraction is mandatory: I_sub displays weak temperature sensitivity governed by threshold voltage shift (dV_th/dT ≈ -1.5 mV/°C) and subthreshold slope degradation (~90 mV/dec at 85°C), whereas SRH junction leakage exhibits an activation energy E_a ≈ 0.55 eV to 0.6 eV (half bandgap), and trap-assisted tunneling displays E_a < 0.2 eV under high drain-substrate fields (V_SN = 1.8 V, V_PW = -0.8 V). Variable wordline-off bias (V_GS = -0.2 V to -0.6 V) and back-bias (V_BS = 0 V to -1.2 V) sweeps must be executed to isolate the exact junction field-enhancement components.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-low-noise triaxial probe cards (Keysight/FormFactor parametric needles) with triaxial low-noise guarded cabling (<0.05 fA/V leakage, sapphire/Teflon isolation) have lead times exceeding 26 weeks and require dedicated calibration verification fixtures. Utilizing standard coaxial probe cards will induce dielectric absorption and cable triboelectric noise exceeding 5 fA, rendering 180nm retention time metrology invalid. Spare guarded probe cards and dry nitrogen environmental probe enclosure modules must be dual-sourced and pre-staged in cleanroom stores prior to lot arrival.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test execution duration per wafer on sub-femtoampere parametric characterization scales non-linearly due to long settle times (t_settle > 10 s per bias step to eliminate dielectric displacement currents Q = C_cable * dV/dt). Full 25-point temperature/bias matrices on multiple test keys across 9 wafer sites will exceed 14 hours per wafer, creating a critical bottleneck in the Gen 2 characterization schedule. The PM demands automated multi-site screening using fast settling integration algorithms (Keysight B1500A High-Resolution SMU with triaxial guarding) to compress site characterization down to ≤12 minutes per die.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Displacement current contamination and cable dielectric polarization artifact: Cable dielectric absorption and settling times below 15 s causing false leakage readings >10 fA masquerading as access transistor subthreshold leakage.
1. Trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) saturation at storage node junction: Excessive local electric fields (>0.6 MV/cm) caused by phosphorus/arsenic halo/pocket implant overlap at the storage node plug boundary inducing localized retention pause faults (tail bits).
1. Triaxial guard floating or potential offset: Guard-to-force voltage offset exceeding 200 µV causing parasitic leakage currents across probe needle ceramic shunts, obscuring sub-femtoampere discrimination between I_sub and I_junc.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-fog safety spectacles with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat / cleanroom bunny suit, Cryogenic insulated gloves for liquid/gaseous nitrogen line handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Asphyxiation Hazard: In case of excessive N2 release or oxygen sensor alarm (<19.5% O2), immediately evacuate personnel to fresh air. Provide artificial respiration or oxygen administration by trained personnel if breathing is difficult. Skin contact with cryogenic N2 cold lines: Flush affected tissue immediately with copious tepid water (do not rub frozen parts). IPA exposure: Flush eyes or skin with sterile eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom laminar air flow (>90 fpm) combined with dedicated probe station enclosure exhaust discharging at ≥50 SCFM to prevent local nitrogen gas accumulation; continuous ambient O2 deficiency monitors with dual optical/audible alarms set at 19.5% (warning) and 18.0% (evacuate).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Exhausted nitrogen gas is vented via cleanroom scrubbed roof stack. Spent IPA wipes and pad cleaning residues must be sealed in airtight polypropylene solvent waste containers and disposed of via certified hazardous flammable waste incineration protocol.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched and annealed Al-Cu / TiN bond pads with native oxide thickness < 1.2 nm, free of organic photoresist residues, particulate contamination (Class 1 cleanliness, 0 defects > 0.2 µm).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-scrubbed test pads exhibiting scrub mark area < 15% of total pad area, scrub depth < 180 nm, passivated with dry nitrogen purge, devoid of metal peel or inter-pad bridge debris.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes severe pad oxidation and atmospheric moisture adsorption, increasing contact resistance by >50 Ohms and introducing electrochemical surface ionic leakage (>5 fA) across adjacent triaxial probe points, entirely masking true semiconductor junction leakage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable characterization report and calibrated analytical compact model establishing the retention time budget for 180nm 1T1C DRAM cells. The deliverable defines the deconvolution of subthreshold conduction (I_sub) and junction leakage (I_junc, TAT, SRH) at 25°C, 50°C, and 85°C, proving an aggregate leakage floor < 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C and validating a nominal 64 ms refresh retention window with >100% engineering margin.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

- [ ] `TC_DRAM_CELL_LAYOUT_2_3_2_3_Parametric_IVT_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `10k_Array_Retention_Time_Cumulative_Distribution_WaferMaps.tiff`

critics.systems_engineer: Allocating retention time budgets across 180nm 1T1C cells requires strict partitioning between access transistor subthreshold leakage (I_sub) and storage node n+/p-well junction leakage (I_junc, comprising Shockley-Read-Hall recombination, trap-assisted tunneling, and band-to-band tunneling). At 85°C, with a nominal storage node capacitance C_s = 28 fF and bitline precharge V_BL = V_DD/2 = 0.9 V, maintaining differential sense margin ΔV ≥ 120 mV requires cell storage node voltage V_cell(t) to retain at least 1.45 V over a 64 ms refresh window. Total permissible leakage current cannot exceed I_total_leak = C_s * (ΔV_margin) / t_refresh = 28 fF * (1.8 V - 1.45 V) / 64 ms ≈ 0.153 fA, which necessitates an absolute worst-case target of <1.0 fA across 3-sigma process-voltage-temperature corners. Neglecting negative wordline bias (V_NWL = -0.5 V) in system power budget modeling will lead to catastrophic retention failures due to exponential subthreshold tailing.
critics.domain_expert: Deconvolving I_sub from I_junc at sub-femtoampere scales cannot be achieved by single-point DC measurements on single-cell test structures due to the noise floor of standard parametric analyzers (~0.5 fA to 1 fA). Metrology must employ Kelvin triaxial guard structures on both single-transistor scribe test elements and dense 10^4-cell parallel array test keys. Temperature-dependent Arrhenius activation energy extraction is mandatory: I_sub displays weak temperature sensitivity governed by threshold voltage shift (dV_th/dT ≈ -1.5 mV/°C) and subthreshold slope degradation (~90 mV/dec at 85°C), whereas SRH junction leakage exhibits an activation energy E_a ≈ 0.55 eV to 0.6 eV (half bandgap), and trap-assisted tunneling displays E_a < 0.2 eV under high drain-substrate fields (V_SN = 1.8 V, V_PW = -0.8 V). Variable wordline-off bias (V_GS = -0.2 V to -0.6 V) and back-bias (V_BS = 0 V to -1.2 V) sweeps must be executed to isolate the exact junction field-enhancement components.

nodes.sop_content:
### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Node Title:** Temperature-Dependent $I_d\text{--}V_g$ and Reverse Diode $I\text{--}V$ Test Structure Setup  
**Generation:** Gen 2 ($\mu\text{m}$)  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Classification:** Metrology / Characterization  

```text
┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Wafer Chuck Thermal     │
│ Control (25°C -> 85°C)  │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Triaxial Probe Landing  │
│ on Test Structures      │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             │
             ├──────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Temperature-Dependent   │    │ Reverse Diode I-V       │
│ Id-Vg Sweeps            │    │ Junction Leakage Sweeps │
└────────────┬────────────┘    └────────────┬────────────┘
             │                              │
             ▼                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Extract Subthreshold    │    │ Extract Junction        │
│ Swing & Ioff            │    │ Leakage @ 85°C (<1 fA)  │
└─────────────────────────┘    └─────────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Test Structure Selection & Thermal Chuck Stabilization**
   - Mount the 180nm processed test wafer onto the triaxial thermal probe station chuck.
   - Align probes with high-magnification optics to the dedicated test structures:
     - Access transistor test structures: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ with gate oxide $t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$.
     - Dedicated storage node $n^+/p$-well reverse diode test structures representing the access transistor drain junction connected to the crown storage node W-plug.
   - Set chuck temperature to baseline room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$), allow thermal equilibrium for 10 minutes, and subsequently step temperature to elevated conditions ($50^\circ\text{C}$, $75^\circ\text{C}$, and target maximum operating condition $85^\circ\text{C}$).

2. **Triaxial Direct-Current Leakage Measurement Setup**
   - Connect Source-Measure Units (SMUs) via low-noise, guard-driven triaxial cabling to eliminate parasitic cable charging and system leakage down to sub-femtoampere ($< 1\text{ fA}$) resolution.
   - Enclose the probe station inside a dark, dry-nitrogen-purged, Faraday shielded enclosure to avoid photo-generated carriers and moisture condensation at elevated temperatures.

3. **Temperature-Dependent $I_d\text{--}V_g$ Characterization (Subthreshold Extraction)**
   - Apply nominal drain bias: linear regime ($V_{ds} = 50\text{ mV}$) and saturated operating regime ($V_{ds} = V_{DD} \text{ or } 1.8\text{ V}$).
   - Sweep gate voltage $V_{gs}$ across the subthreshold range (e.g., from $-0.5\text{ V}$ to $1.8\text{ V}$) while monitoring source current $I_s$ and drain current $I_d$ with integration time optimized for sub-fA current levels.
   - Record log($I_d$) vs. $V_{gs}$ at each temperature step ($25^\circ\text{C}$ to $85^\circ\text{C}$) to extract Subthreshold Swing ($SS$) degradation and determine off-state leakage ($I_{off}$ at $V_{gs} = 0\text{ V}$).

4. **Reverse Diode $I\text{--}V$ Sweep (Junction Leakage Characterization)**
   - Connect the triaxial SMU terminal across the cell storage node $n^+/p$-well diode junction.
   - Sweep reverse bias voltage $V_R$ across the cell operating window ($0\text{ V}$ to $V_{DD}/2 \approx 0.9\text{ V}$ and up to full supply voltage $1.8\text{ V}$).
   - Measure reverse saturation leakage current across the temperature gradient ($25^\circ\text{C} \to 85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - De-embed junction area and perimeter leakage components to quantify storage node leakage entering the bitline and substrate.

5. **Retention Time Budget De-Embedding & Validation**
   - Sum subthreshold off-state leakage $I_{off}$ and reverse-biased junction leakage $I_{junc}$ at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Verify that the combined cell leakage conforms to the retention discharge budget $\Delta V = \frac{I_{leak} \cdot t_{refresh}}{C_s}$, ensuring retention interval $> 64\text{ ms}$ for a minimum cell capacitance budget of $25\text{ fF}$ to $28\text{ fF}$.

---

#### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Total Cell Leakage Current ($I_{leak}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | At $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$, $V_{cell} = V_{DD}$, $V_{gs} = 0\text{ V}$ |
| **Access Transistor Dimensions ($L \times W$)** | $180 \times 220$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-line CD-SEM / Electrical Length Verification |
| **Thermal Chuck Operating Temperature** | $85.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Closed-loop RTD sensor chuck stabilization |
| **Target Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $25.0 \text{ to } 28.0$ (min. $\ge 25$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Metrology verification for $> 64\text{ ms}$ retention |

---

#### 3. Citations & References
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Channel geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), minimum storage capacitance target ($28\text{ fF/cell}$), and high-temperature leakage constraint ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: $1\text{T}1\text{C}$ cell storage retention specification ($> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$), storage capacitance window ($25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$), and gate oxide physical thickness ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$).
- **[Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout]**: Sensing charge redistribution budget ($Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{cell} - V_{BL})$), typical cell capacitance reference ($C_s = 25\text{ fF}$), and bitline precharge reference ($V_{DD}/2$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck ramp rates (ambient 25°C to 125°C) induce mechanical expansion and thermal drift on micro-manipulator triaxial probe tips, risking pad scrubbing, contact resistance fluctuation, or insulator delamination on micro-sized test pads. Guard rings and Kelvin triaxial guarding must be maintained across the entire temperature span to prevent thermal chuck leakage from eclipsing sub-femtoampere device currents.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At elevated operating temperatures (85°C to 125°C), bulk Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination/generation shifts toward intrinsic carrier generation, drastically increasing reverse junction leakage. In 180nm DRAM access transistors, separating the subthreshold swing degradation (dVg/dlog(Id)) from peripheral junction perimeter-vs-area leakage components requires multi-geometry test structures (e.g., area-intensive vs. perimeter-intensive finger diodes) measured across strict V_DS and back-gate bias steps.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring calibrated high-temperature low-leakage thermal chucks (e.g., Temptronic/FormFactor) and triaxial probe cards capable of <10 fA background noise up to 125°C requires long-lead supplier commitments and specialized triaxial cabling with anti-triboelectric, moisture-sealed jacketing.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The buy-action for turnkey parametric probe stations and automated parameter analyzers (e.g., Keysight B1500A with HRSMU modules) must include on-site acceptance testing (SAT) validating thermal stability and continuous sub-fA settling times under 60 seconds per bias point to avoid project milestone bottlenecks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal chuck thermocouple calibration drift causing incorrect activation energy (E_a) extraction for trap-assisted tunneling vs. SRH leakage.
1. Triaxial cable dielectric absorption and humidity ingress resulting in >50 fA spurious background leakage at 25°C, masking intrinsic sub-fA junction currents.
1. Probe-needle thermal creep gouging through thin 180nm top metallization contacts during thermal ramping from 25°C to 125°C.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

Contact source, drain, gate, and substrate pads of the 180nm access transistor test structure (W/L = 0.22 um / 0.18 um). 2. Set chuck temperature sequentially to 25°C, 85°C, and 125°C, allowing 15 minutes of thermal soak at each step. 3. Apply V_DS = 1.8 V, V_BS = -0.5 V. 4. Sweep V_GS from -0.5 V to +1.8 V in 20 mV increments with 200 ms integration/delay time. 5. Measure drain current (I_D) and gate leakage (I_G). 6. Extract off-state leakage I_off at V_GS = 0 V and subthreshold swing SS (mV/dec). | `I_off at V_GS = 0V must be <= 1.0 fA/um at 25°C and <= 15.0 fA/um at 85°C. Subthreshold swing at 25°C must be <= 85 mV/dec, and gate oxide leakage I_G must remain < 0.2 fA across all temperatures.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-3-1-02` | **Reverse PN Junction Diode I-V Temperature Characterization and Breakdown** | Keysight B1500A HRSMU, triaxial low-noise probe arms with tungsten tips (1 um radius), temperature-controlled vacuum thermal chuck with IEEE-488 GPIB automation. | 1.
