Extend sweep on designated sacrificial structure up to -50.0 V in 0.5 V steps to record avalanche breakdown voltage V_BR (defined at I_R = 1 uA). | `Reverse leakage current density J_R at -5.0 V must be < 10 nA/cm^2 at 25°C and < 200 nA/cm^2 at 85°C. Reverse breakdown voltage V_BR must be > 40.0 V with sharp avalanche onset.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal insulated Kevlar gloves for handling heated chuck surfaces up to 150°C, ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom nitrile ESD-safe gloves (100% synthetic), Static-dissipative cleanroom coat and ESD ground wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of cryogenic or high-temperature contact burns from thermal chuck, immediately flush affected area with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; seek immediate medical attention. In case of inert gas (N2) asphyxiation alarm, immediately evacuate personnel to open air and administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on probe station enclosure maintaining >= 50 FPM face velocity; room oxygen depletion sensor/alarm calibrated to sound at <19.5% O2 due to dry N2 purge volume.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of IPA-saturated cleanroom swabs in designated flameproof, grounded hazardous solvent bins; no wet chemical neutralization required for closed-loop electrical probe testing.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Semiconductor Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, for pad cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly post-metal etch and cleanroom anneal with native oxide on aluminum/copper pads removed via dilute organic clean; dry surface free of organic contaminants.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized test pads with minor probe needle scrub scrub marks (<15% pad area), immediately returned to sealed dry N2 wafer carrier.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time leads to atmospheric moisture adsorption and surface oxide growth on test pads, driving probe contact resistance >50 Ohms and inducing parasitic surface leakage channels >10 fA.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Turnkey thermal triaxial IV metrology setup fully qualified for 180nm DRAM cell transistor and junction leakage. Station achieves <0.8 fA open-circuit baseline and provides accurate activation energy (E_a) extraction from 25°C to 125°C with verified low-noise guard integrity.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC_DRAM_180NM_IDVG_TEMP_MATRIX.csv`
- [ ] `TC_DRAM_180NM_DIODE_IV_ARRHENIUS.pdf`
- [ ] `METROLOGY_SYSTEM_SAT_CALIBRATION_CERTIFICATE.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Background triaxial system open-circuit leakage floor across -5V to +5V at 25°C** | `0.5 fA` | +0.3 fA max | Keysight B1500A HRSMU open-circuit voltage sweep with probes lifted inside dry-N2 purged Faraday cage |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Access transistor off-state drain leakage I_off at V_GS = 0V, V_DS = 1.8V, T = 25°C** | `0.8 fA/um` | +0.2 fA/um | Automated parametric Id-Vg sweep with Kelvin triaxial sense lines |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Bulk PN junction reverse diode leakage current density J_R at V_R = -5.0V, T = 25°C** | `8.5 nA/cm^2` | +1.5 nA/cm^2 | Reverse bias I-V sweep normalized by calibrated test diode active area (10,000 um^2) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Parametric testbench successfully runs automated multi-temperature sweeps (25°C, 85°C, 125°C) across 5 consecutive wafer die locations with repeat measurement variance <5%, open-circuit system noise verified <0.8 fA, and Arrhenius plot extraction of junction activation energy yielding E_a within 0.95 eV to 1.15 eV.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** Subthreshold Swing and p-n Junction Leakage De-embedding Parameter Extraction  
**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180NM-DRAM-007`  
**Technology Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Cell Layout & Dimensions:** $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ Folded Bitline Crown-Type COB ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, $t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$)  

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Stage Stabilization:  │
│     Chuck at 85 C      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Direct-Current     │
│    Sub-Femtoamp I-V    │
│         Sweep          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ├─────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │    │                        │
│   Subthreshold Swing   │    │      Reverse-Bias      │
│      SS Parameter      │    │    Junction Leakage    │
│       Extraction       │    │      De-embedding      │
│                        │    │                        │
└───────────┬────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
            │                              │
            │ ╭────────────────────────────╯
            ▼ ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Cell Leakage Budget:  │
│   I_leak < 1 fA per    │
│          cell          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│ Retention Window Check:│
│   t_ret > 64 ms for    │
│      C_s >= 28 fF      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Environmental & Triaxial Metrology Bench Setup**
   - Mount the test wafer on a low-noise triaxial guarded thermal chuck inside an EMI-shielded dark box.
   - Set thermal chuck temperature to **$85^\circ\text{C}$** with thermal drift stabilized to within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Connect triaxial Kelvin probes to the Source Measurement Units (SMU) with guard shields driven to trace voltages to suppress cable leakage below $0.1\text{ fA}$.

2. **Access Transistor Subthreshold Sweep ($I_{D}\text{--}V_{GS}$)**
   - Land probes on the dedicated $8F^2$ access transistor test key ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Fix substrate body bias $V_B = 0\text{ V}$ and bitline terminal $V_S = 0\text{ V}$.
   - Apply cell storage node drain potential $V_{DS} = V_{DD}/2$ and $V_{DD}$ (representing full charge state).
   - Sweep wordline gate voltage $V_{GS}$ in the subthreshold regime from $-0.5\text{ V}$ to $+0.8\text{ V}$ with fine step increments ($\le 10\text{ mV}$) and settling integration time $\ge 100\text{ ms}$ per step.

3. **Subthreshold Swing ($SS$) Parameter Extraction**
   - Plot $\log_{10}(I_D)$ versus $V_{GS}$.
   - Extract the subthreshold swing parameter from the inverse maximum linear slope:
     $$SS = \left(\frac{\partial \log_{10} I_D}{\partial V_{GS}}\right)^{-1}$$
   - Verify gate dielectric integrity corresponding to the thermally grown $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ $\text{SiO}_2$ gate oxide layer.

4. **Storage Node p-n Junction Leakage De-embedding**
   - Probe the array de-embedding dummy key (storage node diffusion contact matrix with gate turned off, $V_{GS} < V_{T}$).
   - Sweep reverse bias voltage across the p-n junction $V_{\text{junction}}$ up to operating voltage conditions.
   - De-embed pad/cable parasitic currents and isolate the perimeter/area junction leakage components from channel subthreshold conduction.

5. **Retention Time Budget & Target Compliance Audit**
   - Sum subthreshold off-state leakage ($I_{\text{sub}}$) and reverse-bias p-n junction leakage ($I_{\text{junc}}$) at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to obtain total cell off-state leakage $I_{\text{leak}}$.
   - Compute nominal retention window with cell capacitance $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ (targeting minimum cell retention time budget $> 64\text{ ms}$).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage Thermal Chuck Temperature** | $85.0 \pm 0.5$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Embedded PT100/Thermocouple feedback |
| **Combined Cell Off-State Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-femtoampere triaxial DC probe measurement at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Unit Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28.0$ (min. range $25.0 \text{--} 30.0$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | $C\text{--}V$ multi-frequency impedance metrology |
| **Target Data Retention Refresh Interval ($t_{\text{ret}}$)** | $> 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Calculated retention budget ($\Delta Q / I_{\text{leak}}$) at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Transistor Physical Critical Dimensions** | $L = 180 \pm 5$, $W = 220 \pm 5$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-line CD-SEM verification |

---

### 4. Context References & Literature Citations

- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
  - Access transistor channel dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node capacitance specification: Minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ for alpha-particle soft-error immunity.
  - Leakage requirement: Combined subthreshold and junction leakage kept below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**:
  - $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ 1T1C stacked capacitor architecture.
  - Storage capacitor capacitance range: $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ ensuring data retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Gate dielectric: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness.
- **[Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout]**:
  - Cell charge transfer relationship $Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$.
  - Precharge equalization to $V_{DD}/2$ and differential readout sensing budget constraints.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: De-embedding subthreshold swing (SS) from p-n junction leakage in an 8F² 180nm 1T1C access transistor is critical to closing the cell retention error budget; uncompensated parasitic pad or triaxial cable leakage will corrupt the sub-femtoampere (<1 fA) measurement floor and result in false sense amplifier margin failures.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm, separating gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL), trap-assisted recombination at the n+/p-well storage junction, and weak inversion channel current requires temperature-dependent (25°C to 85°C) triaxial I_ds-V_gs and I_sub-V_ds sweeps; failure to account for substrate current will distort the extracted ideal ideality factor and subthreshold slope target.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Triaxial probe tips, ultra-low-noise triaxial switch matrices (Keysight B2200A or equivalent), and low-leakage probe cards have lead times exceeding 16 weeks; failure to maintain spare triaxial tips and kelvin-guarded cabling will halt wafer characterization and tape-out verification schedules.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterization throughput on 49-point wafer maps with ultra-low current settling times (minimum 1.5 s integration delay per step) risks a 48-hour per-wafer bottleneck; clear de-embedding calibration routines and automated signoff scripts must be locked before silicon fab delivery.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Parasitic leakage through probe card dielectric absorption or surface moisture exceeding the 0.5 fA noise floor, masking intrinsic storage junction leakage.
1. Misattribution of gate-dielectric tunneling or GIDL to bulk p-n junction diffusion current due to inadequate triaxial guard potential matching (V_guard != V_force).
1. Thermal chuck drift exceeding ±0.5°C during activation energy (E_a) parameter extraction, skewing Arrhenius de-embedding between band-to-band tunneling and Shockley-Read-Hall recombination.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-3-2-01` | **Subthreshold Swing (SS) Extraction via Triaxial I_ds-V_gs Sweeps** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1517A High Resolution SMU (HRSMU) and triaxial probe station enclosed in a dark, dry-N2 purged Faraday cage. | 1. Ground source (V_s = 0 V) and substrate (V_sub = 0 V). 2. Force drain bias V_ds = 50 mV (linear regime) and V_ds = 1.8 V (saturation regime). 3. Sweep gate voltage V_gs from -0.5 V to +1.2 V in 10 mV steps with a minimum integration time of 1.5 s per point. 4. Record I_ds, I_sub, and I_gate simultaneously. 5. Extract SS = d(V_gs) / d(log10(I_ds)) over two decades of drain current (10 pA to 1 nA). | `Extracted Subthreshold Swing (SS) must be between 75 mV/dec and 95 mV/dec at 25°C with linear/saturation DIBL shift <= 30 mV; open-circuit instrument background noise <= 0.2 fA.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-2-3-2-02` | **p-n Junction Reverse Leakage and GIDL De-embedding vs Temperature** | Keysight B1500A with HRSMU modules, Temptronic ThermoChuck system (-40°C to 125°C), Keithley 707B switching matrix with low-current triaxial cards. | 1. Float gate or hold at accumulation bias V_gs = -0.5 V to decouple channel conduction. 2. Set substrate p-well V_sub = 0 V. 3. Sweep storage node n+ drain junction bias V_drain from 0.0 V to 2.5 V in 25 mV increments. 4. Measure junction leakage I_leak at 25°C and repeat at 85°C. 5. De-embed area and peripheral junction components using multi-geometry test diodes. 6. Calculate activation energy E_a from Arrhenius slope ln(I_leak) vs 1/kT. | `Total reverse junction leakage at V_drain = 1.2 V, T = 25°C must be <= 0.8 fA/cell; at 85°C must be <= 12 fA/cell; extracted trap activation energy E_a >= 0.55 eV (indicating diffusion/recombination dominance rather than metallic trap pinning).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and conductive footwear, Thermal insulating gloves for hot chuck handling (>85°C)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA, flush immediately with copious potable water for at least 15 minutes. # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Retention Time Budget & 64ms Refresh Interval Statistical Sensitivity Modeling

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Statistical Modeling Lifecycle

```text
│      Step 1: Cell      │
│     Baseline Param     │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │

┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 2: Thermal     │
│   Leakage Scaling to   │
│          85C           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │

             │
             ▼

│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘

│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

```text
                                                        
            ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│

            │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                                   │
Dielec. Leak┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                                   │
Sub-Vth Leak┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                          │
            │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                          │

            │████████████████████                      │

           0.00      0.24       0.47      0.71     0.95 
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Cell Baseline Parameter Extraction**:
   - Extract access transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), gate oxide thickness ($t_{\text{ox}} = 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$), and crown capacitor equivalent oxide thickness ($EOT = 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$) to establish a nominal cell capacitance $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ (within the target specification of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$).
2. **Thermal & Leakage Component Modeling at $85^\circ\text{C}$**:
   - Model the subthreshold leakage across the access gate, drain-substrate junction leakage at the storage node, and dielectric tunneling leakage across the high-$\kappa$ capacitor ($EOT = 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$) under elevated thermal conditions of $85^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Statistical Monte Carlo Sensitivity Execution**:
   - Execute a $\ge 10,000$-run Monte Carlo statistical sensitivity sweep introducing process variations ($\pm 3\sigma$ variation in gate length $L$, oxide thickness $t_{\text{ox}}$, and crown capacitor area) to generate the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of cell retention times.
4. **Sense Margin Evaluation**:
   - Calculate the available differential sensing voltage on a folded bitline:
     $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \times \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right)$$
     using bitline capacitance $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$, verifying that $\Delta V \ge 100\text{ mV}$ remains sufficient for sense amplifier latching after leakage discharge.
5. **Retention Time Budget & Refresh Timing Closure**:
   - Compute the usable cell charge $Q_{\text{usable}} = C_s \times (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{min\_sense}})$ and verify that the worst-case statistical retention limit satisfies:
     $$t_{\text{ret}} = \frac{Q_{\text{usable}}}{I_{\text{leak}}} \ge 64\text{ ms}\quad \text{at } 85^\circ\text{C}$$

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28$ (range: $25\text{ -- }30$) | $\text{fF}$ | Small-signal CV extraction, 180nm crown capacitor |
| **Total Cell Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Total leakage (subthreshold + junction) at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Differential Sensing Voltage ($\Delta V$)** | $100\text{ to }150$ | $\text{mV}$ | Folded bitline readout with $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$ |
| **DRAM Refresh Interval ($t_{\text{ref}}$)** | $\ge 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Full array retention verification at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **`180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench`**:
  - Confirms unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$, and total leakage current target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **`Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering`**:
  - Confirms storage capacitance range of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$, retention time requirement $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, gate oxide thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$, and capacitor $EOT = 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$.
- **`Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout`**:
  - Confirms folded bitline architecture sensing equation $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \times \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right)$, typical parameters $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$, $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$, and signal development window of $100\text{ mV to }150\text{ mV}$.

---

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge extracted and persisted to [`retention_time_budget_modeling.md`](docs/knowledge/retention_time_budget_modeling.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In an 8F² folded bitline topology with 256/512 cells per bitline, bitline capacitance C_b ranges between 150 fF and 250 fF against a 28 fF nominal storage node (C_s). The statistical retention budget over a 64 ms refresh window at T_j = 85 °C requires total leakage per cell to stay strictly below 0.35 fA (assuming a ΔV sensing margin requirement of >= 100 mV across precharge VDD/2 = 0.9 V at VDD = 1.8 V). The statistical model must account for the tail of the log-normal leakage distribution driven by variable-range hopping and trap-assisted tunneling, ensuring that the 5-sigma tail population does not suffer bit flip failures before 64 ms.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node dimensions, subthreshold leakage of the access NMOS transistor and junction leakage at the storage node p-n junction dominate over dielectric leakage of the crown capacitor (assuming Al2O3/HfO2 or high-k MIM stack). Given negative wordline biasing during standby (V_NWL ≈ -0.3 V to -0.5 V) to suppress subthreshold drain current, gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL) and junction field-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination become the primary tail contributors. Statistical Monte Carlo sensitivity modeling must decouple junction trap density N_t from gate overlap GIDL coefficients to avoid over-optimistic retention predictions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Characterizing sub-femtoampere leakage tails down to 64 ms refresh intervals across multi-wafer runs requires automated parametric probe stations with low-leakage triaxial matrix switches and temperature-controlled thermal chucks (Keysight B1500A/B1542A or Keithley 4200A-SCS with sub-fA remote preamps). Sourcing and calibrating specialized probe cards with <100 aA residual offset leakage inside cleanroom thermal environments imposes strict supply lead times and maintenance overhead.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Statistical modeling and SPICE corner validation of the 64 ms refresh window must be completed and correlated with electrical test (E-test) micro-benchmarks prior to frozen tapeout signoff. Clear verification gates must be established between 125 °C stress tests, 85 °C standard operational margins, and the required redundancy/ECC repair budget to ensure overall array yield meets commercial readiness targets.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. GIDL-induced tail retention collapse: High electric fields at the access transistor gate-to-drain overlap during negative wordline hold drive band-to-band tunneling, dropping retention well below 64 ms for tail cells.
1. Trap-assisted junction leakage excursion: Heavy metal contamination or silicon micro-defects at the storage node n+/p-well junction create localized deep-level traps, causing anomalous multi-decade leakage spikes in 1 out of 10,000 cells.
1. Dielectric soft breakdown / stress-induced leakage current (SILC): Mechanical or localized thermal stress in the crown capacitor dielectric creates micro-conduction paths exceeding 1 fA, resulting in catastrophic retention loss during burn-in.

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Repeat across 500 site locations across wafer center, mid-radius, and edge. 6. Extract median and 5-sigma leakage currents (I_leak = C_s * dV/dt). | `Median leakage current at 85 °C must be <= 0.15 fA/cell; 5-sigma worst-case statistical tail leakage must not exceed 0.35 fA/cell, guaranteeing retention time t_ret = (C_s * ΔV_avail) / I_leak >= 64.0 ms with ΔV_avail >= 200 mV.` |

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible), UV-absorbing safety glasses (ANSI Z87.1 certified), ESD-dissipative cleanroom coat and conductive footwear

critics.supply_chain: Characterizing sub-femtoampere leakage tails down to 64 ms refresh intervals across multi-wafer runs requires automated parametric probe stations with low-leakage triaxial matrix switches and temperature-controlled thermal chucks (Keysight B1500A/B1542A or Keithley 4200A-SCS with sub-fA remote preamps). Sourcing and calibrating specialized probe cards with <100 aA residual offset leakage inside cleanroom thermal environments imposes strict supply lead times and maintenance overhead.
critics.laya_pm: Statistical modeling and SPICE corner validation of the 64 ms refresh window must be completed and correlated with electrical test (E-test) micro-benchmarks prior to frozen tapeout signoff. Clear verification gates must be established between 125 °C stress tests, 85 °C standard operational margins, and the required redundancy/ECC repair budget to ensure overall array yield meets commercial readiness targets.
critical_failure_modes: GIDL-induced tail retention collapse: High electric fields at the access transistor gate-to-drain overlap during negative wordline hold drive band-to-band tunneling, dropping retention well below 64 ms for tail cells.

Trap-assisted junction leakage excursion: Heavy metal contamination or silicon micro-defects at the storage node n+/p-well junction create localized deep-level traps, causing anomalous multi-decade leakage spikes in 1 out of 10,000 cells.

Dielectric soft breakdown / stress-induced leakage current (SILC): Mechanical or localized thermal stress in the crown capacitor dielectric creates micro-conduction paths exceeding 1 fA, resulting in catastrophic retention loss during burn-in.

testcases.title: Sub-Femtoampere Temperature-Dependent Retention Leakage Monte Carlo Parameter Extraction
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1517A High Resolution SMU (0.1 fA resolution) and Triaxial Shielded Probe Station with Temptronic ThermoChuck (-40 °C to +125 °C)
testcases.pre_conditions: 180nm DRAM test vehicle array with dedicated Kelvin/triaxial test pads connected to isolated storage nodes (C_s = 28 fF nominal); chuck pre-heated and stabilized at 85.0 ± 0.5 °C; chamber purged with dry N2 (<5% RH) to eliminate surface condensation and moisture-induced parasitic leakage.
testcases.procedure: 1. Ground bitline and substrate p-well (0.0 V). 2. Apply standby negative hold voltage V_WL = -0.40 V to the access wordline. 3. Precharge storage node to nominal cell '1' voltage (V_cell = 1.80 V) using SMU1 in voltage pulse mode. 4. Disconnect SMU1 voltage source and execute continuous sub-femtoampere direct-current integration across 1000 sampling cycles or measure voltage decay dV/dt over a 200 ms observation window. 5. Repeat across 500 site locations across wafer center, mid-radius, and edge. 6. Extract median and 5-sigma leakage currents (I_leak = C_s * dV/dt).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Median leakage current at 85 °C must be <= 0.15 fA/cell; 5-sigma worst-case statistical tail leakage must not exceed 0.35 fA/cell, guaranteeing retention time t_ret = (C_s * ΔV_avail) / I_leak >= 64.0 ms with ΔV_avail >= 200 mV.

testcases.title: 64ms Array Refresh Interval Retention Bit Error Rate (RBER) Statistical Sensitivity Test
testcases.instrumentation: Advantest T5588 or Teradyne Magnum DRAM Automated Test Equipment (ATE) with active thermal chamber enclosure set to 85 °C
testcases.pre_conditions: Full 180nm DRAM memory sub-array (minimum 1 Mb active array block) powered with VDD = 1.80 V, VDD/2 precharge = 0.90 V, substrate V_BB = -0.50 V, negative wordline off-level V_NWL = -0.40 V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Write solid physical data pattern '1' (all high potential) to all 1 Mb cells. 2. Suspend automatic refresh commands for a programmed delay interval t_pause = 64.0 ms. 3. Perform burst read across the array and record all failing bit addresses (bit flips where sense amplifier latches '0'). 4. Repeat measurement for step increments of t_pause: 32 ms, 64 ms, 128 ms, 256 ms, and 512 ms. 5. Plot cumulative distribution function (CDF) of cell retention times and extract Weibull slope parameters (beta and eta).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: At t_pause = 64.0 ms and T_case = 85 °C, raw bit failure count before ECC/redundancy repair must be <= 32 bits per 1 Mb array (raw BER <= 3.2e-5), fully within the single-error correction double-error detection (SEC-DED) and row redundancy allocation limit.

ppe_required: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (class 100 compatible)
UV-absorbing safety glasses (ANSI Z87.1 certified)
ESD-dissipative cleanroom coat and conductive footwear
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: In case of skin or eye contact with IPA rinse agent: flush copiously with clean deionized water or saline solution for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent fumes or N2 asphyxiation risk: immediately move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is difficult and seek medical attention.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Standard cleanroom laminar flow exhaust (ISO Class 5) maintaining >= 100 FPM laminar downflow; dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on chemical wipe stations for IPA pad cleaning.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Collect spent IPA cleaning wipes and solvent residues in grounded, closed flammables-rated hazardous solvent collection drums for specialized off-site solvent incineration.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-cleaned aluminum/copper test pads free of organic residue, post-passivation etch and clean, water contact angle < 20 degrees.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Characterized wafer with probe mark depth < 0.2 um, dry N2 desiccated storage container, moisture content < 1 ppm H2O.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive atmospheric exposure induces native oxide regrowth and moisture/ionic contamination on exposed micro-probing pads, creating shunt leakage paths across probe needles that obscure true sub-femtoampere device retention characteristics.

expected_result.summary: Verified statistical retention modeling and experimental extraction report establishing that the 180nm 8F² DRAM cell (28 fF crown C_s) maintains >= 64 ms refresh retention at 85 °C with a 5-sigma tail leakage <= 0.35 fA, validated through sub-fA SMU metrology and 1 Mb ATE bit failure analysis.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Storage node cell capacitance C_s nominal value
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-frequency (1 MHz) C-V extraction on crown capacitor test array at 25 °C

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Statistical 5-sigma worst-case total cell leakage current at 85 °C
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Sub-femtoampere SMU integration and dV/dt retention slope extraction on 500 test dies

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Array retention pause time bit pass yield at 85 °C for 64 ms refresh window
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: >= 99.9950% (<= 50 raw failing bits per 1 Mb sub-array)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Advantest/Teradyne automated test equipment 1 Mb pause-refresh retention test suite

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Formal approval from Systems Engineering, Circuit Design, and Quality Assurance upon demonstrating that empirical 85 °C leakage tail distributions validate the 64 ms refresh timing budget with positive read sensing margin (ΔV >= 100 mV into 250 fF bitline) across all process corners (FF, TT, SS).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Elevated Temperature Retention & Alpha-Source Soft-Error Rate Profiling

**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180nm Open-Source DRAM, 8F² / 6F² Cell Topology, Crown-Type COB)  
**Process Step / Domain:** Metrology & Reliability Engineering  
**Action Type:** Make / Characterization  

---

### 1. Metrology Process Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Wafer Mount &      │
│   Thermal Chuck Soak   │
│        at 85°C         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Pause-Refresh      │
│  Retention Sweep 64ms  │
│        - 500ms         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Alpha-Source      │
│  Irradiation 241Am /   │
│         232Th          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Differential Sensing  │
│   Readout & Bit-Flip   │
│        Logging         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Thermal Chuck Stabilization & Die Conditioning:**
   - Mount the 180nm DRAM wafer/die onto the automated probe station thermal chuck.
   - Ramp chuck temperature to **85°C ± 0.5°C** and allow a 15-minute thermal soak to equilibrate junction and sub-threshold temperatures across the array.
2. **Cell Array Bias Pre-conditioning & Background Pattern Write:**
   - Set supply rail $V_{DD}$ to nominal operation. Assert bitline equalization to balance complementary bitline pairs ($BL$ and $\overline{BL}$) to $V_{DD} / 2$.
   - Write solid '1' ($V_{cell} = V_{DD}$) and checkerboard patterns across the 8F² Crown-type COB array via row and column address decoders.
3. **Elevated Temperature Pause-Refresh Profiling:**
   - Disable automatic refresh cycles and apply calibrated pause intervals ($t_{pause}$) starting at $64\text{ ms}$ up to $500\text{ ms}$ at 85°C.
   - Assert wordlines ($WL$) to activate the 180nm access transistors ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Read out stored charge onto bitlines ($C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$); monitor differential signal development $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s} \cdot \left(V_{cell} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right)$ across CMOS cross-coupled sense amplifiers.
   - Record fail-bit maps and calculate total retention degradation caused by junction and sub-threshold leakage.
4. **Accelerated Alpha-Particle Soft-Error Rate (SER) Irradiation:**
   - Position an unsealed alpha-particle calibration source ($^{241}\text{Am}$ or $^{232}\text{Th}$ foil) at a fixed working distance directly above the unpassivated DRAM die surface.
   - Continuously cycle static retention tests under constant alpha flux at 85°C with nominal pause duration ($t_{pause} = 64\text{ ms}$).
   - Log soft-error upset events (single-bit flips $1 \to 0$ from electron collection at the cell storage node plug contact).
5. **Post-Exposure Recovery & Metrology Reporting:**
   - Retract the radiation source to the shielded enclosure.
   - Cool thermal chuck down to 25°C.
   - Compute fail-bit count versus pause time and calculate Soft Error Rate in FIT/Mb (Failures in Time per Megabit).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                         Metrology Target Thresholds    
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
        Sense dV (mV)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                │
Retention Target (ms)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                │
        Cell Cap (fF)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                         │
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                         │
   Leakage Limit (fA)┤█                                │
                     │█                                │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0.0    31.2    62.5    93.8  125.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Tolerance / Boundary Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28.0$ | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Minimum bound ($25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ range) |
| **Cell Retention Time ($t_{ret}$)** | $> 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Measured at $T_{chuck} = 85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Total Cell Leakage Current ($I_{leak}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-threshold + junction leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Sense Amplifier Differential Signal ($\Delta V$)** | $100\text{ to }150$ | $\text{mV}$ | Signal developed onto $C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$ |

---

### 4. Literature & Context Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node capacitance budget: Minimum $28\text{ fF}$ per cell to ensure noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling.
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage target: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - 1T1C stacked capacitor storage capacitance requirement: $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ to guarantee retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - High-k dielectric: $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$, $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$, or ONO stack with EOT of $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout:**
  - Precharge equalization level: $V_{DD} / 2$.
  - Bitline parasitic capacitance: $C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$.
  - Differential signal development: $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{cell} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right) \approx 100\text{ mV to }150\text{ mV}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal retention profiling at elevated chuck temperatures (85°C to 125°C) will induce severe subthreshold and junction leakage increases in the 180nm access pass-transistor that easily overshadow intrinsic 28 fF crown dielectric leakage. The test bench must decouple junction band-to-band tunneling (BBTT) and trap-assisted recombination from alpha-particle generated electron-hole pair collection by using synchronous pulse-gated bitline sense amplifiers and temperature-compensated VBB back-bias regulation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node with a target cell capacitance of 28 fF, the critical charge Qcrit is approximately Q = C * (V_DD / 2) = 28 fF * 0.9 V = 25.2 fC (~1.57e5 electrons). An unshielded Americium-241 (Am-241) foil source emits ~5.48 MeV alpha particles, depositing ~1.5e6 electron-hole pairs along a ~25 µm silicon track. Unless calibrated Mylar/aluminum degrader foils or micro-collimators are used to dial incident alpha energy to Bragg peak conditions (~1-2 MeV at the crown storage node funneling depth), soft-error rates will saturate the array bit-flip bitmap and obscure sensitive cell-to-cell retention tail distribution modeling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring licensed Am-241 alpha radiation calibration check sources (0.1 to 1.0 µCi activity) requires specific statutory radiation safety permits and lead-lined shielded storage containers. Furthermore, high-purity forming gas (H2/N2 5%/95%) for passivating dangling Si/SiO2 interface traps prior to temperature stress testing faces local regulatory gas-cylinder transport bottlenecks in domestic Vietnamese lab setups.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal chuck ramp cycles up to 125°C with active radiation testing risk contamination and accelerated pin wear on the multi-DUT ceramic burn-in test sockets. We must freeze test execution times per die to under 45 minutes and automate thermal-dwell logging to prevent thermal drift from shifting the baseline test matrix timeline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway of access transistor drain-to-substrate reverse bias leakage at 125°C (>5 fA/cell), causing false-positive retention pause fails that mask crown capacitor ALD dielectric reliability.
1. Direct alpha strike ionization within bitline sense amplifier differential latch nodes during sensing windows (SEU hit on sensing node vs storage node), misrepresenting array SER as cell retention failure.
1. Mechanical contact resistance drift and thermal expansion mismatch between probe needles and 180nm test pads during 25°C-to-125°C thermal cycling, inducing erratic bitline precharge voltage drops.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-01` | **Elevated Temperature Refresh Pause Retention Profiling (25°C to 125°C)** | Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automated Thermal Probe Station, Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1530A WGFMU, and Temptronic ThermoChuck System (-40°C to +200°C, ±0.1°C) | 1. Stabilize chuck temperature sequentially at 25°C, 85°C, 105°C, and 125°C with 10-minute isothermal dwell. 2. Write physical '1' checkerboard pattern across 64-kbit DRAM test vehicle block. 3. Halt refresh clock (pause state) for logarithmically stepped retention durations: 1 ms, 10 ms, 64 ms, 200 ms, 1000 ms, and 5000 ms. 4. Execute single-cycle read-back sweep via Keysight WGFMU pulse pattern; log fail bit count (FBC) and physical cell addresses. | `At 85°C, cell retention time tRET for >99.9% of array bits (pause time before first 64 bad bits) must exceed 64 ms with total cell leakage <= 0.44 fA/cell; at 125°C, retention pause must exceed 10 ms.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-02` | **Accelerated Alpha-Source Soft-Error Rate (ASER) Cross-Section Characterization** | Calibrated Americium-241 planar alpha check source (0.5 µCi / 18.5 kBq) with 12 µm Mylar degrader foil, vacuum-compatible alpha positioning jig, and FPGA-based high-speed DRAM error bit-mapping engine | 1. Expose the open DRAM cell storage array to Am-241 alpha beam with collimated flux of ~1.0e6 alpha/(cm²*hr). 2. Continuous read-write-verify loop operation at tREFI=64 ms for 10 hours continuous exposure. 3. Log single-bit upset (SBU) coordinates, multi-cell upset (MCU) clustering, and fail count timestamps. 4. Repeat exposure with DRAM array held in static retention pause mode (tPAUSE=32 ms) between refresh sweeps to isolate storage-node vs sense-amplifier hits. | `Array soft-error cross-section must be <= 1.2e-8 cm²/bit; projected soft-error rate (SER) under nominal terrestrial packaging materials (<0.001 alpha/cm²*hr) must not exceed 800 FIT/Mb (1 FIT = 1 failure in 10^9 device-hours).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Nitrile safety gloves (double-gloving protocol), ANSI Z87.1 certified radiation/laser impact safety goggles, Static-dissipative lab coat with thermal barrier sleeves, Personal thermoluminescent dosimeter (TLD) radiation badge for alpha/gamma tracking
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For radioactive alpha source breach or skin contact: Immediately remove contaminated clothing, wash skin thoroughly under tepid running water with non-abrasive detergent for 15 minutes without breaking skin barrier; notify Radiation Safety Officer (RSO). For thermal burns from 125°C chuck: Flush with cold sterile water for 20 minutes; apply sterile non-adherent dressing. For forming gas/H2 leak: Evacuate area immediately to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous HEPA and charcoal-filtered localized snorkel exhaust (minimum face velocity 100 FPM) over thermal chuck area; Class 1000 laminar flow hood; dedicated hydrogen sniffer alarm calibrated at 10% LEL in gas manifold enclosure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Am-241 sealed source must never be disposed of in standard chemical waste; return to manufacturer or store in lead pig container (minimum 6 mm Pb equivalent) in registered Class II radiological vault. Solvent-soaked wipes to be collected in flammables airtight hazardous waste drums.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Americium-241 (Alpha emitter sealed source)** | `14596-10-2` | Radioactive Sealed Calibration Source Standard | `0.5 µCi (18.5 kBq activity)` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SEMI Tier C) | `99.9%` |
| **Forming Gas (5% H2 in 95% N2 balance)** | `1333-74-0` | UHP (Ultra-High Purity 99.999%) | `5.0% H2` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly cleaved or etched passivated test die post-forming gas anneal with clean unoxidized aluminum-copper bond pads and zero particulate debris.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermal-tested die with intact passivation, verified de-energized, surface-cleaned with electronic IPA wipe, free of alpha-emitter wipe contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture adsorption and native pad oxidation increase contact resistance by >50 Ohms, causing timing skew and erroneous false-leakage detection during thermal pause testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed elevated temperature retention Weibull profile and accelerated alpha soft-error cross-section characterization for 180nm 28 fF crown COB DRAM cell test array, validating retention > 64 ms at 85°C and terrestrial SER < 800 FIT/Mb.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_retention_weibull_temp_profile_85c_125c.csv`
- [ ] `alpha_source_soft_error_rate_cross_section_report.pdf`
- [ ] `cell_fail_bit_map_clustering_topography.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Array 99.9% Bit Retention Time at 85°C Chuck Temperature** | `64` | +inf/-0.0 ms | Keysight B1500A WGFMU pause-refresh sweep bit-error threshold analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum Single Cell Equivalent Total Off-State Leakage Current at 85°C** | `0.44` | +0.10 fA | Extracted from delta-V sense threshold decay across calibrated 28 fF storage node |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Accelerated Alpha Particle Soft-Error Cross Section (Am-241 5.48 MeV)** | `1.2e-8` | +0.3e-8 cm^2/bit | Bit-flip count divided by integrated incident alpha particle fluence over 10-hour exposure |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal approval from Lead Metrology Engineer and Radiation Safety Officer confirming zero alpha wipe contamination, full retention Weibull curve convergence over 64 kbit array with tRET >= 64 ms at 85°C, and SER extrapolated model <= 800 FIT/Mb under 0.001 alpha/(cm²*hr) nominal package flux.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-TRET85`  
**Title:** Thermal Chuck Calibration & Elevated Temperature Retention Time ($t_{RET}$) Characterization at 85°C  
**Generation / Node:** Gen 2 (180 nm Open-Source DRAM Chip, 8F² / 6F² COB Stack)  
**Classification:** Metrology / Reliability Testing  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Thermal Chuck Setup  │
│  and Cal at 85 deg C  │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Wafer Soaking and   │
│     Surface Probe     │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Pattern Write: Data  │
│     1 and Data 0      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Variable Pause     │
│  Pause-Refresh Test:  │
│     10ms to 128ms     │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Burst Readout and   │
│   Bit-Fail Mapping    │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Retention Time     │
│    Extraction and     │
│   Acceptance Check    │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Thermal Chuck Closed-Loop Calibration
1. Power on the wafer prober thermal chuck controller and configure the setpoint to **85.0°C**.
2. Mount a calibrated surface thermocouple/RTD sensor wafer onto the chuck under full vacuum.
3. Allow the PID controller to settle; verify temperature uniformity across center, middle, and edge chuck zones within **$\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$** of the 85.0°C target.

#### Step 2: Wafer Loading & Thermal Stabilization
1. Load the 180nm DRAM test wafer (containing 1T1C cells with $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, and crown-type COB capacitors) onto the chuck.
2. Engage chuck vacuum (> 60 kPa) and soak the wafer for a minimum of **15 minutes** to ensure complete die and silicon substrate thermal equilibrium at 85°C.

#### Step 3: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) Interface & Pin Alignment
1. Align the probe card pins to the test pads on the DUT (or designated retention metrology test arrays).
2. Establish clean probe contact and verify contact resistance across power ($V_{DD}$), wordline ($V_{PP}/V_{WL}$), bitline precharge ($V_{BLP}$), and cell plate ($V_{CP}$) supply rails.

#### Step 4: Pattern Initialization (Write Cycle)
1. Write deterministic test data patterns into the cell array:
   - **Phase A:** Solid Data '1' (high state stored on the crown capacitor).
   - **Phase B:** Solid Data '0' / Checkerboard pattern to evaluate neighboring cell disturbance.
2. Ensure write cycle timing matches nominal array access specifications before starting the retention hold.

#### Step 5: Pause-Refresh Retention Hold & Burst Readout
1. Inhibit all internal and external refresh cycles ($Auto\text{-}Refresh / Self\text{-}Refresh$).
2. Apply a variable pause (hold) interval ranging from **10 ms to 128 ms** (stepping through 16 ms, 32 ms, 64 ms, and 128 ms) while holding the chuck strictly at 85°C.
3. At the end of each pause interval, execute a high-speed burst read command sequence across all addresses and capture the read data buffer.

#### Step 6: Bit-Fail Mapping & Leakage Extraction
1. Compare output data against the initialized pattern to record bit failures (single-bit flips).
2. Generate Bit-Fail Maps (BFM) and extract the cumulative failure distribution $t_{RET}$ curve.
3. From the retention degradation curve, calculate the cell access-transistor sub-threshold and storage node junction leakage current:
   $$I_{leak} = C_{cell} \cdot \frac{\Delta V_{SN}}{t_{RET}}$$

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Tolerance / Limit | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Data Retention Time ($t_{RET}$)** | **$> 64$** | Minimum threshold at 85°C across array | $\text{ms}$ |
| **Cell Storage Node Capacitance ($C_{cell}$)** | **$\ge 28$** (nominal 25 – 30) | Minimum allowable crown capacitance | $\text{fF/cell}$ |
| **Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage Current ($I_{leak}$)** | **$< 1.0$** | Maximum allowable leakage at 85°C | $\text{fA/cell}$ |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature Accuracy** | **$85.0 \pm 0.5$** | Sustained soak & test uniformity | $^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 3. Context & Literature Citations

1. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
   - Minimum cell storage capacitance specification of **$25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$** per cell.
   - Requirement for elevated temperature data retention time **$> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$**.
2. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
   - 1T1C unit cell dimensions: channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Minimum capacitance budget of **$28\text{ fF/cell}$** to guarantee noise immunity.
   - Access transistor sub-threshold and junction leakage target of **$< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$** to maintain target refresh intervals.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck expansion and mechanical Z-drift during the 25°C to 85°C ramp alter probe needle scrub depth and contact resistance on 180nm pads. Closed-loop PID chuck control must integrate chuck RTD surface feedback with active optical autofocus or dynamic Z-travel compensation to prevent micro-cracking of top passivations or capacitor crown metal during multi-hour soak times.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, subthreshold and junction leakage current escalate exponentially (governed by Arrhenius activation energy Ea ≈ 1.1 eV for intrinsic silicon and band-to-band trap-assisted tunneling), collapsing nominal retention from seconds down to milliseconds. Thermal calibration must guarantee spatial gradient across the 150mm/200mm platen is ≤0.5°C, otherwise tail-distribution bits (variable retention time - VRT) cannot be distinguished from thermal Chuck non-uniformity.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-accuracy thin-film surface RTDs (Class 1/10 DIN Pt100) and vacuum-compatible thermal interface sheets have lead times exceeding 8 weeks. Procuring replacement Kelvin probe cards rated for continuous 125°C operation with low leakage coaxial/triaxial cabling must be secured immediately to avoid metrology tool downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Elevated temperature profiling is on the critical path for Gen 2 tape-out freeze. Thermal stabilization cycles (soak times of 20 min per wafer) risk creating a massive testing bottleneck unless batch test script routines and automated 9-point thermal wafer mapping are validated during stage qualification.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal Chuck gradient exceeding ±1.0°C across wafer diameter causing artificial skew in Weibull retention failure slope.
1. Probe card needle thermal drift inducing probe scrub slip off the 180nm bond pads and shorting adjacent bitlines.
1. Moisture condensation during rapid cool-down cycle post-test compromising moisture barrier and triggering corrosion of exposed test pads.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-01` | **Thermal Chuck 9-Point Surface Isothermal Mapping & PID Stability at 85°C** | Semi-automated probe station with integrated thermal chuck, calibrated 9-point thin-film Pt100 RTD wafer instrument, Keithley 2700 multichannel DMM, high-precision thermal camera with emissivity calibration. | 1. Mount 9-point RTD wafer onto the chuck and engage vacuum. 2. Set chuck PID setpoint to 85.0°C with ramp rate 5.0°C/min. 3. Allow 20 minutes soak after setpoint reached. 4. Log continuous temperature readings across all 9 sensors for 30 minutes at 1 Hz sampling. 5. Calculate spatial delta (T_max - T_min) and temporal jitter (3-sigma). | `Spatial temperature uniformity across all 9 points must be within 85.0°C ± 0.5°C; temporal temperature oscillation must remain < ±0.15°C over 30 minutes.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-02` | **Elevated Temperature (85°C) 64Kb DRAM Array tRET Retention Profiling** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer / custom FPGA automated memory test fixture, Triaxial probe card, dry N2 purged thermal chamber. | 1. Contact array test pads with triaxial probe needles. 2. Write checkerboard pattern (AAh/55h) to array at VDD = 1.8V. 3. Inhibit refresh cycles and hold in pause state for variable delay t_pause (logarithmic sweep: 1 ms to 1000 ms). 4. Read back array contents and record fail bit count (FBC) per delay step. 5. Plot cumulative failure distribution (Weibull) and extract tRET at 99.9% cell retention. | `Median cell retention time (tRET_50%) must exceed 120 ms at 85°C; worst-case retention (99.9% pass yield, tRET_0.1%) must exceed 32 ms at VDD = 1.8V.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulated heat-resistant gloves (rated to 150°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and nitrile gloves (Class 100 compatible), Closed-toe conductive cleanroom footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn: Immediately rinse burned area with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and report to cleanroom medical officer. Inhalation of nitrogen purge gas (asphyxiation risk): Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide CPR/oxygen if breathing ceases.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Enclosed probe station must maintain active exhaust ventilation at 50 CFM to clear any solvent vapors from IPA cleaning and prevent N2 accumulation in operator breathing zone; ambient O2 monitor calibrated with audible alarm threshold at 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be disposed of in designated flammables-rated, self-closing metal waste receptacles; no liquid chemical drainage allowed directly into standard cleanroom drains.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Compressed)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP Grade 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-passivation etch and Al/Cu bond pad clean; dry, pristine pad metallization free of native oxide film build-up and organic residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermal cycle completed; cooled to 25°C in dry N2 ambient; pad surfaces inspected for probe needle scrub burnish; vacuum bagged with desiccant.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes pad oxidation and ambient organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption, causing erratic contact resistance (>200 Ohms) and false probe-tip scrub damage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical calibration of the thermal probe chuck to 85.0°C ± 0.5°C across 150mm platen and comprehensive retention time (tRET) characterization of the Gen 2 180nm 8F² DRAM cell array, demonstrating compliance with refresh interval targets under high thermal stress.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `thermal_chuck_9pt_calibration_report_85C.csv`
- [ ] `dram_180nm_gen2_tret_retention_weibull_85C.pdf`
- [ ] `probe_mark_depth_thermal_drift_inspection.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Thermal chuck 9-point surface temperature uniformity at 85°C steady-state** | `85.0` | ±0.5°C | Calibrated 9-point RTD wafer logging over 30 minutes continuous soak |
| `ASSERT-02` | **DRAM cell array worst-case retention time (99.9% pass yield) at 85°C** | `32.0` | >= 32.0 ms | Automated array pause-refresh test sweep across 64Kb test block via Keysight B1500A |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Z-axis probe needle scrub displacement under 25°C to 85°C thermal transition** | `2.5` | <= 5.0 µm | High-magnification optical profilometry on post-test aluminum bond pad scrub witness marks |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit approval requires verification that chuck spatial delta is <= 0.5°C across all 9 zones, array worst-case retention time at 85°C exceeds 32 ms across 3 separate die locations, and zero probe walkout/shorting is detected.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermal Chuck Multi-Point Temperature Uniformity Calibration & PID Stabilization at 85°C

---

### 1. Process Overview & Context
This procedure establishes multi-point temperature uniformity calibration and closed-loop PID thermal stabilization for wafer probe thermal chucks operating at **85°C**. Precise thermal stabilization is essential for validating the **180nm 1T1C Open-Source DRAM cell** (<1 fA/cell leakage target and retention time $t_{\text{RET}} > 64\text{ ms}$ at 85°C).

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Calibration       │
│      Preparation       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  PID Tuning & Ramp to  │
│          85C           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Multi-Point       │
│   Uniformity Mapping   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Verification &     │
│   Baseline Sign-Off    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Tool Preparation & Sensor Setup**:
   - Inspect the thermal chuck surface for particulate contamination, residual vacuum grease, or mechanical scoring. Clean with electronic-grade isopropanol (IPA) and lint-free wipes.
   - Load an instrumented 200 mm/300 mm silicon calibration wafer equipped with a multi-point surface thermocouple array (center, load, source/periphery zones).
   - Engage chuck vacuum (>600 mmHg) to ensure intimate thermal contact across all wafer zones.
   - Verify that laminar dry $N_2$ purge gas flow is regulated through the mass flow controller (MFC) at 1 to 5 SLPM to suppress ambient thermal drafts and moisture condensation.

2. **PID Thermal Loop Initialization & Ramp**:
   - Initialize the digital multi-zone PID controller with feedforward decoupling parameters.
   - Configure setpoint temperature to **85.0°C**.
   - Initiate closed-loop heating ramp from ambient to 85°C at a controlled rate ($\le 5^\circ\text{C/min}$) to eliminate localized thermal gradient shock.
   - Monitor proportional, integral, and derivative loops to suppress transient temperature overshoot.

3. **Multi-Point Thermal Soak & Stabilization**:
   - Allow the thermal chuck and wafer system to soak for 15 minutes once the control sensor reaches 85.0°C.
   - Record multi-point thermocouple readings across center, inner ring, and edge zones at 1 Hz sampling frequency.
   - Apply zone-offset calibration trims in the multi-loop digital PID controller to counter radial and edge-loss gradients until all sensors converge within $\pm0.5^\circ\text{C}$ of 85.0°C.

4. **Steady-State Stability & Metrology Hand-off**:
   - Log steady-state temperature data continuously for 30 minutes.
   - Confirm that temperature oscillation around the 85.0°C setpoint does not exceed $\pm0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Disengage the calibration wafer, log calibration parameters into the metrology station database, and clear the thermal chuck for $t_{\text{RET}}$ (>64 ms) and junction leakage (<1 fA/cell) wafer-level retention profiling.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                       Target Calibration & Stabilization Specs
                       ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                       │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
PID Settling Time (min)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 Peak Overshoot (deg C)┤▒▒                             │
                       │▒▒                             │
Temp Uniformity (deg C)┤██                             │
                       │██                             │
                       └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                       0.0     3.8    7.5    11.2  15.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Operating Setpoint Temperature** | `85.0` | Exact Nominal Target | `°C` | Calibrated Surface Thermocouple Grid |
| **Multi-Point Thermal Uniformity** | `±0.5` | Max deviation across all wafer zones | `°C` | Center vs. Edge Multi-Point Array Mapping |
| **Peak Transient Overshoot** | `≤ 0.5` | Max deviation during setpoint ramp | `°C` | Digital PID Process Variable Logger |
| **Thermal Settling Time** | `≤ 15.0` | Max duration to reach $\pm0.5^\circ\text{C}$ envelope | `min` | Closed-Loop Temperature Datalogger |
| **Purge Gas Flow Rate** | `1 to 5` | Steady-state laminar flow | `SLPM` | In-line Mass Flow Controller (MFC) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Referenced For*: Target 85°C retention validation requirement; cell leakage target $<1\text{ fA/cell}$ at 85°C for 180nm 1T1C stacked capacitor cells ($C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\text{ fF}$).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Referenced For*: Retention specification $t_{\text{RET}} > 64\text{ ms}$ at 85°C across 180nm node 1T1C crown/stacked capacitor arrays.
- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
  - *Referenced For*: Digital PID multi-zone control architecture with feedforward decoupling, steady-state multi-point temperature uniformity tolerance of $\pm0.5^\circ\text{C}$, and gas flow regulation at 1 to 5 SLPM via mass flow controllers (MFC).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck multi-zone resistive heating and peltier/liquid chiller closed-loop control must interface seamlessly with probe card touchdown mechanics. At 85°C, thermal expansion (CTE mismatch between chuck gold/nickel-plated surface and the 150mm/200mm Si wafer) introduces Z-drift up to 12 µm and lateral probe scrub displacement. PID loop tuning must prevent temperature overshoot above 85.5°C to avoid accelerated thermal runaway or premature dielectric leakage during 1T1C retention testing, with decoupled feedforward compensation for air purge convective cooling.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: 1T1C DRAM retention time (tRET) at 85°C exhibits an exponential Arrhenius decay governed by sub-threshold leakage, junction band-to-band tunneling, and capacitor dielectric trap-assisted leakage (leakage doubling roughly every 8°C). A spatial non-uniformity of ±1.0°C across the chuck results in an unacceptable ~10% artifactual retention variance across wafer dies. PID stabilization must achieve within ±0.1°C steady-state stability and across-wafer spatial uniformity within ±0.3°C across 17 measuring points on an instrumented wafer.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) precision thermal chuck system (e.g., ERS electronic or Temptronic/inTEST Thermal Solutions) requires lead-time mitigation (typically 16-24 weeks) and vendor-calibrated multi-sensor wafer kits. Purchasing must ensure compatibility with our manual/semi-auto wafer prober platen (Triaxial BNC/SMU high-isolation feedthroughs capable of sub-fA leakage measurements) and availability of NIST-traceable calibration artifacts.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement and buy-off milestones for the 85°C thermal chuck calibration directly gate the retention metrology and alpha-source soft-error profiling campaigns. We must lock vendor acceptance testing (FAT/SAT) criteria to 17-point temperature grid mapping and 60-minute drift tests prior to release for 180nm DRAM crown capacitor retention characterization, keeping capital budget inside Gen 2 allocation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal chuck surface gradient exceeding ±0.5°C due to edge convective losses and non-uniform vacuum chuck groove suction, creating false weak-retention cell clusters at the wafer periphery.
1. PID integral windup during 25°C to 85°C ramp-up causing >1.5°C overshoot, triggering thermal stress, probe tip slippage, and permanent micro-crack damage to 1T1C capacitor stacks.
1. Ground loop interference or thermoelectric Seebeck EMF noise coupled into ultra-low current (<1 fA) probe lines via unshielded thermal chuck resistive heating elements.

PID overshoot during minor disturbances must be <= 0.2°C with recovery time <= 45 seconds. Chuck surface isolation resistance to ground must remain > 100 TΩ at 85°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating heat-resistant cleanroom gloves (rated to 150°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, ESD-safe cleanroom coat and anti-static ESD heel grounders, Nitrile under-gloves for wafer handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn contact: Immediately flush affected skin area with cold, clean deionized water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply salves or oils without medical evaluation. IPA contact: Flush eyes or skin immediately with sterile eyewash or water for 15 minutes. Inhalation of nitrogen purge displacement: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer CPR or supplemental oxygen if breathing is impaired.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Prober thermal enclosure local exhaust ventilation operating at min. 50 CFM to safely vent heated air and outgassing solvents; ambient cleanroom air circulation maintained at Class 100 (ISO 5) with positive pressure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-retardant hazardous chemical solvent waste cans and disposed of per volatile organic compound (VOC) protocol.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed metallization/passivation wafer with clean back-side (free of particle contamination, organic residues, or slurry spots that impair thermal chuck contact).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermally stabilized, moisture-free wafer post-85°C retention metrology, cooled to < 30°C in dry N2 ambient to prevent moisture condensation and native oxidation.
