# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## SOP-MET-180-042: Variable Pause Refresh Test Sequence & 85°C $t_{\text{RET}}$ Automated Shmoo Profiling

### 1. Purpose & Overview
This SOP defines the automated test procedure to characterize cell retention time ($t_{\text{RET}}$), evaluate sub-threshold/junction leakage at elevated temperature, and generate pass/fail Shmoo operating envelopes for 180nm 1T1C crown-type stacked capacitor-over-bitline (COB) DRAM arrays.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
                      VARIABLE PAUSE REFRESH TEST FLOW
                      
 [Step 1: Thermal Chuck]       [Step 2: Array Preconditioning]
    Set Chuck to 85°C     -->     Write Solid '1' & '0' / Checkerboard
   (Verify ±0.5°C stab.)          Precharge BL//BL to V_DD / 2
            |
            v
 [Step 3: Pause Refresh]       [Step 4: Readout & Sensing]
    Halt Refresh Clocks   -->     Assert WL; Charge Share (Cs onto CBL)
    Sweep t_PAUSE (0-256ms)       Activate Cross-Coupled SA Latch (SAN/SAP)
            |
            v
 [Step 5: Automated Shmoo]
    Sweep V_DD vs. t_PAUSE
    Log Bit Fail Count & Cumulative Retention Distribution
```

1. **Thermal Stabilization**:
   - Mount the 180nm DRAM wafer/package on the calibrated thermal chuck.
   - Ramp and stabilize chuck temperature to **$85^\circ\text{C}$**. Maintain thermal equilibrium for a minimum of 5 minutes prior to test vector initiation.

2. **Array Preconditioning & Pattern Write**:
   - Assert equalization circuits to precharge complementary bitlines ($\text{BL}$ and $\overline{\text{BL}}$) to $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$.
   - Execute full-array write sequences using both Solid ('1's and '0's) and physical Checkerboard patterns to account for bitline-to-bitline coupling capacitance. Ensure storage capacitors ($C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$) are fully charged.

3. **Variable Pause Refresh Execution**:
   - Inhibit the automated auto-refresh/self-refresh commands to float the cell charge.
   - Apply a variable pause interval ($t_{\text{PAUSE}}$) stepped logarithmically/linearly from **$1\text{ ms}$ to $256\text{ ms}$** (including standard checkpoints at $32\text{ ms}$, $64\text{ ms}$, and $128\text{ ms}$).

4. **Array Readout & Sensing**:
   - Post-pause, assert wordline ($\text{WL}$) on the access transistor ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Allow cell charge transfer onto the bitline ($C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$) to develop differential signal $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s} \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{DD}}/2)$.
   - Strobe the CMOS cross-coupled sense amplifier latch signals ($\text{SAN}$ pulling to ground, $\text{SAP}$ pulling to $V_{\text{DD}}$) to resolve and evaluate bit states against expected data.

5. **Automated Shmoo Plot Generation**:
   - Execute a 2D Shmoo automated matrix stepping core supply voltage ($V_{\text{DD}}$) on the Y-axis versus pause interval ($t_{\text{PAUSE}}$) on the X-axis.
   - Record fail counts per array, extract $t_{\text{RET}}$ per bit, and construct the cumulative retention time distribution profile.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Tolerance / Limit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature** | $85$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 0.5\ ^\circ\text{C}$ steady-state |
| **Minimum Retention Time ($t_{\text{RET}}$)** | $> 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Minimum across array at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Storage Cell Leakage Current** | $< 1$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Maximum total junction/subthreshold leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Bitline Readout Signal ($\Delta V$)** | $100 \text{ to } 150$ | $\text{mV}$ | Minimum differential signal at sense amplifier input ($C_s \ge 25\text{--}28\text{ fF}$, $C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$) |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **Temperature & Retention Criteria**: Target retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
- **Leakage & Capacitance Bounds**: Total sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ with cell storage capacitance budget $\ge 28\text{ fF}$ (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*).
- **Cell Geometry & Signal Sensing Dynamics**: Access transistor dimensions $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; differential signal development $\Delta V = 100\text{ to } 150\text{ mV}$ onto bitline with $C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$ using folded-bitline cross-coupled sense amplifiers (*Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout*).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated Shmoo profiling across variable pause refresh intervals at 85°C must strictly decouple ATE driver clock jitter, channel skew (<50 ps), and chuck thermal drift from intrinsic 1T1C storage node leakage. A 0.5°C gradient across a 200 mm thermal chuck can shift subthreshold junction leakage by >4%, skewing the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) of cell retention time (tRET).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, access transistor subthreshold leakage (I_off at V_GS=0V) and cell junction trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) dominate over dielectric leakage for 28 fF crown capacitors. Shmoo plots mapping V_DD (1.6V–2.0V) vs. pause duration (10 ms to 1000 ms) must explicitly identify the bimodal tail distribution caused by variable retention time (VRT) metastable silicon defects.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Automated thermal chuck test fixtures rated for 85°C continuous testing with pogo-pin/probe card stability (beryllium copper or tungsten rhenium tips) face extended lead times (14–18 weeks). Low-leakage triaxial cable harnesses (<10 fA noise floor) and specialized high-density ATE load boards must be second-sourced to avoid critical path delays in Gen 2 validation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The full 64Mb test matrix with fine-pitch voltage/pause-time Shmoo steps can consume over 36 hours of ATE time per wafer. We must implement an adaptive binary-search pause step algorithm to converge on the 99.999% retention boundary within 4 hours per wafer to align with milestone delivery schedules.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal chuck boundary gradient (>±1.0°C) inducing false bimodal retention failure tails not attributable to VRT or intrinsic cell leakage.
1. Probe-needle contact resistance degradation or tip oxidation at 85°C causing false sense amplifier read margin collapse during pause refresh testing.
1. Variable Retention Time (VRT) traps in the access transistor junction creating erratic bit-flip transitions between consecutive pause refresh passes.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-2-01` | **Automated Variable Pause Refresh Shmoo Characterization at 85°C** | Advantest T5588 ATE or NI PXIe-6570 Digital Pattern Generator coupled with Temptronic ThermoChuck TP03000 (±0.1°C stability), Agilent B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer, and probe station with low-noise triaxial probe card. | 1. Write Solid Data '1' across the target 64Mb array sector. 2. Suspend auto-refresh command and hold array quiescent for pause interval t_pause starting at 10 ms. 3. Read back sector data at 200 MHz and record bit fail count (BFC). 4. Increment t_pause logarithmically up to 1000 ms in 20 logarithmic steps. 5. Repeat steps 1–4 across V_DD stepped from 1.60 V to 2.00 V in 50 mV increments. 6. Generate 2D Shmoo bitmap matrix (V_DD vs. t_pause). | `Cell retention time tRET for 99.9% of cells must exceed 64 ms at 85.0°C across nominal operating voltage (V_DD = 1.80 V ± 10%); worst-case tail cell retention (tRET_min) must exceed 32 ms.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-2-02` | **Variable Retention Time (VRT) Defect Screener via Extended Multi-Pass Pause Cycling** | Memory ATE with deep vector memory, temperature-monitored high-temp ceramic probe card, Keysight 3458A DMM monitoring chuck thermocouple feedback. | 1. Execute write cycle with Checkerboard pattern. 2. Apply fixed pause time equal to nominal tRET threshold (64 ms) without refresh. 3. Read back array and log failing bit addresses into fail bitmap (FBM). 4. Loop steps 1–3 for 1,000 continuous iterations without modifying bias voltages. 5. Cross-correlate fail bit addresses across iterations to detect blinking/metastable bits that alternate between passing and failing. | `Total variable retention time (VRT) blinking bits must not exceed 0.005% (50 ppm) of total tested storage nodes at 85°C over 1,000 iterations.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal protective Kevlar gloves rated to 150°C, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact splash safety goggles, Anti-static ESD-dissipative cleanroom coat, Nitrile gloves (cleanroom Class 100 compatible)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn: Immerse contact area in cool running water for at least 15 minutes; apply sterile non-adherent dressing; seek medical evaluation. Nitrogen asphyxiation risk: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local exhaust ventilation on probe station enclosure maintaining >=50 FPM face velocity; room oxygen depletion monitoring sensor with audible alarm at <19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA cleaning wipes must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant solvent waste cans and disposed of via certified hazardous chemical waste incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Chamber Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 99.999% | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Chuck Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry post-passivation pad open with clean, unoxidized Al/Cu or Ni-Au test pads; free of organic residues and moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-scrubbed bond pads with scrub depth <0.8 µm; zero chuck-induced thermal contamination or back-surface particulate build-up.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure causes native oxidation and ambient moisture adsorption on test pads, leading to elevated probe contact resistance (Rc > 2 ohms), false contact opens, and localized thermal chuck corrosion.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Delivery of comprehensive 85°C automated Shmoo profile datasets and cumulative retention distribution curves demonstrating compliant 1T1C cell retention (>=64 ms at 85°C for 99.9% of bits) on 180nm Open-Source DRAM silicon.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_85c_tret_shmoo_matrix_summary.csv`
- [ ] `dram180_vrt_blinking_bit_distribution_report.pdf`
- [ ] `dram180_wafer_retention_fail_bitmap.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |

critics.systems_engineer: Automated Shmoo profiling across variable pause refresh intervals at 85°C must strictly decouple ATE driver clock jitter, channel skew (<50 ps), and chuck thermal drift from intrinsic 1T1C storage node leakage. A 0.5°C gradient across a 200 mm thermal chuck can shift subthreshold junction leakage by >4%, skewing the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) of cell retention time (tRET).
critics.domain_expert: At 85°C, access transistor subthreshold leakage (I_off at V_GS=0V) and cell junction trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) dominate over dielectric leakage for 28 fF crown capacitors. Shmoo plots mapping V_DD (1.6V–2.0V) vs. pause duration (10 ms to 1000 ms) must explicitly identify the bimodal tail distribution caused by variable retention time (VRT) metastable silicon defects.
critics.supply_chain: Automated thermal chuck test fixtures rated for 85°C continuous testing with pogo-pin/probe card stability (beryllium copper or tungsten rhenium tips) face extended lead times (14–18 weeks). Low-leakage triaxial cable harnesses (<10 fA noise floor) and specialized high-density ATE load boards must be second-sourced to avoid critical path delays in Gen 2 validation.
critics.laya_pm: The full 64Mb test matrix with fine-pitch voltage/pause-time Shmoo steps can consume over 36 hours of ATE time per wafer. We must implement an adaptive binary-search pause step algorithm to converge on the 99.999% retention boundary within 4 hours per wafer to align with milestone delivery schedules.
critical_failure_modes: Thermal chuck boundary gradient (>±1.0°C) inducing false bimodal retention failure tails not attributable to VRT or intrinsic cell leakage.
Probe-needle contact resistance degradation or tip oxidation at 85°C causing false sense amplifier read margin collapse during pause refresh testing.
Variable Retention Time (VRT) traps in the access transistor junction creating erratic bit-flip transitions between consecutive pause refresh passes.

testcases.title: Automated Variable Pause Refresh Shmoo Characterization at 85°C
testcases.instrumentation: Advantest T5588 ATE or NI PXIe-6570 Digital Pattern Generator coupled with Temptronic ThermoChuck TP03000 (±0.1°C stability), Agilent B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer, and probe station with low-noise triaxial probe card.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer mounted on thermal chuck stabilized at 85.0°C ± 0.2°C for at least 15 minutes; array programmed with Solid Data '1' pattern; V_DD set to nominal 1.80 V, V_PP = 3.30 V, V_BB = -0.60 V.
testcases.procedure: 1. Write Solid Data '1' across the target 64Mb array sector. 2. Suspend auto-refresh command and hold array quiescent for pause interval t_pause starting at 10 ms. 3. Repeat steps 1–4 across V_DD stepped from 1.60 V to 2.00 V in 50 mV increments. 6. Generate 2D Shmoo bitmap matrix (V_DD vs. t_pause).

testcases.title: Variable Retention Time (VRT) Defect Screener via Extended Multi-Pass Pause Cycling
testcases.instrumentation: Memory ATE with deep vector memory, temperature-monitored high-temp ceramic probe card, Keysight 3458A DMM monitoring chuck thermocouple feedback.
testcases.pre_conditions: Thermal chuck locked at 85.0°C; ambient dry N2 purge chamber active (<5% RH); array written with alternating Checkerboard/Inverse Checkerboard patterns.
testcases.procedure: 1. Execute write cycle with Checkerboard pattern. 2. Apply fixed pause time equal to nominal tRET threshold (64 ms) without refresh. 3. testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total variable retention time (VRT) blinking bits must not exceed 0.005% (50 ppm) of total tested storage nodes at 85°C over 1,000 iterations.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Cumulative Retention Failure Extraction & Sub-1-fA Storage Cell Leakage Analysis

**Hierarchy:** DRAM Foundation VN > 180nm Open-Source DRAM > Metrology & Reliability  
**Target:** 180nm Node, 8F² Crown-Type Capacitor-Over-Bitline (COB) Cell  
**Objective:** Perform variable pause-time retention characterization and extract cumulative bit-failure distributions ($t_{\text{RET}}$) to quantify sub-1-fA storage-node leakage at 85°C.

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Load & Thermal  │
│  Stabilization at 85°C │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Pause-Refresh      │
│    Retention Stress    │
│      Array Write       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Parametric Pause    │
│   Sweep (1ms-500ms)    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Bitline Delta V     │
│  Readout & Bit Error   │
│       Extraction       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Sub-1-fA Storage    │
│      Cell Leakage      │
│       Extraction       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Thermal Chuck Stabilization & Array Preparation:**
   - Mount the 180nm DRAM wafer onto the prober thermal chuck and set temperature to **85°C ± 0.5°C**.
   - Soak for a minimum of 15 minutes to eliminate thermal gradients across the array.
   - Initialize array biases: establish bitline equalization at $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$, substrate back-bias ($V_{\text{BB}}$), and wordline de-asserted off-state ($V_{\text{WL\_OFF}}$).

2. **Pattern Initialization & Background Charge Injection:**
   - Write solid logical data (`Data 1` / full $V_{\text{DD}}$ storage level) across the target memory block to charge all crown-type storage nodes ($C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$).
   - Disengage active refresh cycles to place the array in a paused, unrefreshed static retention state.

3. **Parametric Pause Time ($t_{\text{pause}}$) Sweep:**
   - Execute a logarithmic pause-time sweep stepping $t_{\text{pause}}$ from **1 ms to 500 ms** (covering the baseline target retention time of $> 64\text{ ms}$).
   - Maintain wordline pitch (360 nm to 400 nm) unselected during each dwell period to subject storage cells exclusively to access transistor subthreshold leakage, gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL), and dielectric leakage.

4. **Strobe Readout & Differential Sensing ($\Delta V$):**
   - At the expiration of each pause step, strobe the wordlines sequentially to dump residual cell charge $Q_s = C_s (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$ onto complementary bitlines.
   - Verify sense amplifier signal development ($\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s} (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{DD}}/2)$); flag bit failures where $\Delta V$ falls below the sense amplifier latching threshold (nominal developed window: 100 mV to 150 mV).

5. **Cumulative Retention Distribution & Sub-1-fA Leakage Extraction:**
   - Map failed bit coordinates against pause duration to plot cumulative failure percentage curves ($F(t_{\text{pause}})$).
   - Extract the per-cell effective leakage current at 85°C across the distribution using:
     $$I_{\text{leak}} = \frac{C_s \cdot \Delta V_{\text{margin}}}{t_{\text{fail}}}$$
     where $\Delta V_{\text{margin}} = V_{\text{DD}} - V_{\text{min\_sense}}$.
   - Separate intrinsic population retention from tail bits induced by localized trap states.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Tolerance / Limit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chuck Temperature** | `85` | `°C` | `± 0.5 °C` |
| **Cell Retention Time ($t_{\text{RET}}$)** | `> 64` | `ms` | Minimum specification at 85°C |
| **Cell Storage Leakage ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | `< 1.0` | `fA/cell` | Maximum allowable limit at 85°C |
| **Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | `28` | `fF/cell` | Minimum target (25 to 30 fF range) |
| **Readout Signal Margin ($\Delta V$)** | `100 to 150` | `mV` | Developed differential sensing window |

---

### Verified Context Citations

- **Thermal & Retention Targets:** Retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at 85°C chuck temperature, storage cell capacitance range 25 to 30 fF (minimum target 28 fF per cell) to guarantee soft-error and noise immunity (*Source: "180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench"*, *"Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering"*).
- **Leakage Boundary:** Storage-node leakage (subthreshold and junction leakage) held strictly below 1 fA/cell at 85°C (*Source: "180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench"*).
- **Differential Readout Dynamics:** Differential signal $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}(V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{DD}}/2) \approx 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ for $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$ (*Source: "Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout"*).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Direct current-voltage measurement of sub-1-fA storage node leakage at individual 1T1C cell terminals is physically inaccessible via standard mechanical microprobes due to parasitic probe card shunt leakage (~10-100 fA) and cable capacitance. The system must decouple parasitic tester leakage from intrinsic cell storage node leakage by using a calibrated array-based charge-decay pause-refresh test mode or on-chip differential charge-integrator test structures on wafer scribe-lines. Thermal chuck gradients (>±0.5°C across 200mm diameter) will distort the Arrhenius activation energy (Ea) extraction for trap-assisted tunneling and junction leakage across the cumulative retention time distribution.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, achieving tRET > 64 ms for a 28 fF crown capacitor requires total storage node off-state leakage I_leak < 0.22 fA per cell for a sensing window delta_V = 0.5 V (I_leak = C * delta_V / tRET). The dominant leakage paths are p-n storage node junction leakage (band-to-band tunneling and SRH recombination at W-plug contact interfaces), access transistor subthreshold leakage at VGS = 0V, gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL) during negative wordline hold bias (-0.5V), and dielectric leakage through the Ta2O5/ONO high-k stack. Variable Retention Time (VRT) phenomena induced by metastable silicon crystal lattice micro-defects will create anomalous bimodal tails in the cumulative failure distribution that must not be masked by average log-normal fits.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-low-current femtoampere parameter analyzers (e.g., Keysight B1500A with High-Resolution SMU / ASU units or Keithley 4200A-SCS with preamplifiers) and triaxial low-noise thermal chucks (+85°C stable) face high cleanroom capex and lead times exceeding 26 weeks. Sourcing ultra-low alpha packaging materials and triaxial low-leakage probe wedges rated for <0.1 fA baseline noise at elevated temperature represents a single-source dependency that can bottleneck parametric qualification runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Parametric testing of retention distributions across 64k-cell test arrays at 85°C requires multi-point retention pause intervals ranging from 1 ms to 10 s per die, leading to excessive wafer test dwell times (>4 hours per wafer). The team must implement an accelerated retention screen at 105°C correlated with 85°C Arrhenius scaling, using test array block parallelism to satisfy the Gen 2 tapeout milestone schedule without exceeding cleanroom metrology budget constraints.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Trapped metallic contaminants (Fe, Cu, Ni) at the tungsten contact plug/silicon active area interface causing deep-level SRH generation-recombination centers and anomalous tail-bit leakage exceeding 5 fA at 85°C.
1. Crown capacitor dielectric degradation due to pinholes or non-stoichiometric oxygen vacancies in the Ta2O5/Al2O3 stack leading to Poole-Frenkel conduction exceeding the 1.0 fA cell budget.
1. Subthreshold conduction leakage caused by threshold voltage (Vth) roll-off or drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) in the 180nm channel length access transistor at 85°C.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-3-01` | **Sub-1-fA Storage Node Junction & Dielectric Leakage Parametric Extraction** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer equipped with B1517A High-Resolution SMUs and AttoSense Pre-Amplifier Units (ASUs), triaxial shielding probe station with Temptronic ThermoChuck calibrated at 85.0°C ± 0.1°C, dry N2 purge chamber (<5% RH). | 1. Ground bitlines and p-well substrate (V_BL = 0V, V_well = 0V). 2. Force access transistor wordline into off-state bias (V_WL = -0.5V). 3. Apply voltage sweep on the capacitor plate terminal (V_CP) from 0.0V to 1.6V (Vdd) in 50 mV steps. 4. Measure quiescent leakage current at the storage array terminal using ASU with integration time set to 64 PLC (Power Line Cycles). 5. Normalize measured total quiescent current by 1024 cells to extract per-cell leakage. | `Per-cell total quiescent leakage current I_leak at V_CP = 1.6V and T = 85.0°C must be <= 0.85 fA/cell (Target: < 1.0 fA/cell maximum, pass threshold <= 0.85 fA).` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-3-02` | **Cumulative Retention Failure Time (tRET) Distribution & Tail-Bit Profiling at 85°C** | Advantest T5588 / Teradyne Magnum automated memory test system with high-speed digital pattern generator, elevated thermal chuck at 85.0°C ± 0.2°C, active nitrogen-purged test head enclosure. | 1. Write solid physical data pattern '1' (storage node = 1.8V) to all 64k addresses. 2. Inhibit memory refresh cycles for an incremental pause retention time t_pause starting at 10 ms up to 2000 ms in logarithmic intervals (10, 20, 40, 64, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000 ms). 3. Read back array data and log bit-failure bitmap per pause step. 4. Repeat procedure with inverted data pattern '0'. 5. Plot cumulative fail bit count versus pause time on a Weibull/log-normal retention distribution. | `At pause time t_pause = 64 ms and 85°C, total cumulative bit failure count must be <= 1 bit per 64-kbit array (cumulative failure rate <= 0.0015%); median retention time (t50) must exceed 450 ms.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating cleanroom gloves rated for 150°C contact, Standard ESD-safe cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Lint-free Nomex/polyester cleanroom smock
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burns from heated chuck: Immerse affected skin immediately in cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile dry dressing and seek cleanroom medical response. N2 asphyxiation risk: Immediately move victim to fresh air, administer CPR/supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored. IPA splash: Rinse eyes or skin with sterile eyewash/water for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom air recirculation with dedicated local exhaust on prober enclosure (minimum 50 CFM face velocity); continuous ambient O2 deficiency monitor calibrated with alarm trigger at <19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be deposited in dedicated grounded, self-closing stainless steel solvent waste bins with flame arrestors; exhausted N2 gas vented directly to facility cleanroom roof stack.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen (Gas, purge for thermal chamber)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% Semiconductor Grade) | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, for chuck face cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C4) | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Completed metallization and top passivation (Si3N4/SiO2) with open bond/probe pads free from oxidation, organic residues, or probe scrub marks.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested wafer surface with microprobe scrub scrub-depth < 0.2 µm on aluminum pads, zero surface condensation or organic contamination, dry N2 purged.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom humidity (>45% RH) induces moisture absorption in polyimide/passivation layers, causing surface leakage paths between probe pads and shifting measured sub-femtoampere currents by >2 orders of magnitude.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed physical verification and parametric extraction of 180nm 1T1C crown capacitor storage cell leakage (<1.0 fA/cell) and cumulative retention time distribution at 85°C across 64-kbit test arrays, confirming compliance with the >=64 ms refresh budget.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RETENTION_85C_CUMULATIVE_DISTRIBUTION_64K.csv`
- [ ] `SUB_FEMTOAMP_LEAKAGE_EXTRACTION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `WAFER_FAIL_BITMAP_TAIL_BITS_85C.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-3-01` | **Average storage node leakage current per cell at 85°C and Vdd = 1.6V** | `0.75 fA/cell` | +0.10 fA/cell, -0.30 fA/cell | High-resolution SMU/ASU integration on 1024-cell array test vehicle with parasitic tester floor subtraction |
| `ASSERT-TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-1-3-02` | **Cumulative bit retention failure rate at pause time t_pause = 64 ms at 85°C** | `0.0005%` | +0.0010%, -0.0005% | Automated DRAM test system 64k array pause-refresh functional test bitmap extraction |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires: (1) Median cell retention time t50 > 450 ms at 85.0°C ± 0.1°C across 5 wafer sites, (2) Extracted storage cell leakage <= 0.85 fA/cell at 85°C, and (3) Tail-bit failure rate at 64 ms <= 0.0015% with zero anomalous VRT clustering, approved by Lead Metrology Engineer and Systems Architect.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Procurement & Activity Calibration of Americium-241 ($\text{}^{241}\text{Am}$) Alpha Particle Emission Source

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the specifications, procurement criteria, and precision radiometric activity calibration for an encapsulated Americium-241 ($\text{}^{241}\text{Am}$) alpha particle source. The calibrated source is utilized to evaluate Soft-Error Rate (SER) susceptibility and critical charge ($Q_{\text{crit}}$) margin on 180nm Open-Source DRAM 1T1C storage cells ($8F^2$ topology, $\ge 28\text{ fF}$ crown stacked capacitors).

---

### 2. Verified Context & Technical Citations
- **Capacitance Budget & Soft-Error Threshold:** The storage node requires a minimum capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF}$ per cell (baseline range $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$) to ensure noise and soft-error immunity against alpha-particle strikes and bitline coupling capacitance (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*; *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
- **Leakage & Thermal Limits:** Target refresh retention demands sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain data retention times $> 64\text{ ms}$ (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology*; *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
- **Dielectric & Cell Structure:** Crown-type polysilicon/MIM stacked capacitor built with high-$\kappa$ dielectrics (effective $\kappa > 15$, equivalent oxide thickness $\text{EOT} = 3\text{--}4\text{ nm}$, gate dielectric physical thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$) over bitline (COB) contact (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology*; *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Source Specification & Regulatory Procurement Requisition|
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Receipt Inspection, Wipe/Leak Testing, & Mechanical Mount|
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Vacuum Chamber Radiometric Activity & Energy Calibration |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. DRAM Test Fixture Dose Alignment & Acceptance Sign-off   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Source Specification & Procurement Requisition
1. Prepare procurement documentation for a sealed-source planar disk ($\text{}^{241}\text{Am}$) deposited onto a platinum/gold/stainless substrate with an ultra-thin protective window (mylar or titanium foil, areal density $\le 0.1\text{ mg/cm}^2$) to minimize alpha energy straggling.
2. Specify nominal nominal alpha energy of $\sim 5.486\text{ MeV}$ and nominal activity level between $37\text{ kBq}$ to $370\text{ kBq}$ ($1\ \mu\text{Ci} - 10\ \mu\text{Ci}$), sized specifically for wafer-level or packaged-die open-cavity irradiation.
3. Validate regulatory licensing, safe handling protocols, and chain-of-custody documentation under national nuclear regulatory standards.

#### Step 2: Receipt Inspection & Mechanical Wipe Testing
1. Unpack source container within a certified radiological fume hood / containment bench.
2. Conduct standard dry/wet wipe leak testing across housing contours using a calibrated liquid scintillation counter or alpha contamination probe; verify removable surface contamination is below the non-exempt limit ($< 185\text{ mBq}$ or $< 0.005\ \mu\text{Ci}$).
3. Mount the sealed source inside an anodized aluminum collimator frame compatible with the micro-positioner stage of the vacuum probe station.

#### Step 3: Radiometric Activity & Energy Spectrum Calibration
1. Load the mounted source into a calibration vacuum chamber evacuated to low pressure ($< 100\text{ mTorr}$) to eliminate atmospheric air-straggling.
2. Position a Passivated Implanted Planar Silicon (PIPS) detector coaxially at a fixed calibration distance ($Z_{\text{cal}} = 50.0\text{ mm} \pm 0.1\text{ mm}$) with a precision circular aperture ($A_{\text{det}} = 100\text{ mm}^2$).
3. Acquire pulse-height alpha energy spectra for $t \ge 3600\text{ s}$ via a multi-channel analyzer (MCA).
4. Calculate absolute activity $A_0$ from the geometric factor $G = \frac{\Omega}{4\pi} = \frac{A_{\text{det}}}{4\pi Z_{\text{cal}}^2}$ and live-time count rate $R$:
   $$A_0 = \frac{R}{G \cdot \epsilon_{\text{intrinsic}}}$$
5. Confirm full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) spectral resolution to quantify window absorption attenuation.

#### Step 4: Flux Characterization & Handoff for DRAM SER Profiling
1. Map emission rate per unit area (flux $\Phi_\alpha$ in $\alpha\text{/}(\text{cm}^2\cdot\text{h})$) across the active target plane corresponding to the DRAM open-cavity test fixture.
2. Package source in a lockable lead-lined transfer container with the calibration certificate documenting $A_0$, date of assay, half-life decay schedule ($T_{1/2} = 432.2\text{ yr}$), and energy peak centroid.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Source Active Surface Contamination (Leak Test)** | $< 185\text{ mBq}$ ($< 5\text{ pCi}$) | Maximum permissible wipe activity | Liquid Scintillation Counter / Alpha Wipe Counter |
| **Alpha Energy Peak FWHM Resolution** | $\le 25\text{ keV}$ | Spectral broadening upper bound | PIPS Detector + MCA at $< 100\text{ mTorr}$ vacuum |
| **Absolute Radiometric Activity ($A_0$)** | $37.0\text{ kBq}$ to $370.0\text{ kBq}$ | $\pm 3.0\%$ absolute uncertainty ($k=2$) | Low-geometry defined-aperture silicon alpha spectrometer |
| **Collimator Z-Axis Displacement Accuracy** | $50.0\text{ mm}$ | $\pm 0.1\text{ mm}$ travel tolerance | Laser interferometric / micrometer gauge stage |

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Am-241 decay produces primary 5.486 MeV alpha particles alongside a secondary 59.54 keV gamma ray emission. When calibrating SER (Soft-Error Rate) on a 180nm 1T1C DRAM array with 28 fF crown cell capacitance (critical charge Qcrit ≈ 15-20 fC at 1.8V VDD/2 precharge), direct alpha flux can induce localized multi-cell upsets (MCU) through funneling collection in adjacent deep N-well/P-well diffusion regions. The positioning fixture must enforce a sub-micron collimated aperture (e.g., 500 µm gold/tungsten pinhole collimator) with an absolute standoff distance of 2.0 mm to avoid Bragg peak dispersion in air and inconsistent ionization density profiles at the silicon surface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating open-source DRAM alpha SER requires distinguishing between true alpha-induced charge deposition and parasitic self-absorption or surface oxidation on the foil source. A standard commercial smoke-detector disc (typically ~0.9 µCi or 33.3 kBq embedded in gold/palladium matrix) exhibits energy straggling from ~3.5 MeV to 5.5 MeV due to foil cladding. Without vacuum-chamber surface-barrier detector (SBD) pulse-height spectroscopy to determine the exact emission spectrum and effective active area flux (particles/cm²·s), calculating FIT (Failures in Time per Mbit) will suffer from up to 40% systematic error.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring radioactive isotopes (Am-241) even below general NRC/IAEA exempt quantities (<1 µCi / 37 kBq) is subject to strict local regulatory scrutiny by Vietnam's VARANS (Vietnam Agency for Radiation and Nuclear Safety). Sourcing certified alpha standard reference sources (e.g., Eckert & Ziegler sealed planar alpha sources with NIST-traceable calibration) incurs lengthy import licensing and customs quarantine. A domestic contingency plan leveraging hermetically harvested ionization chamber foils requires pre-screened batch qualification and wipe-testing documentation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Radioactive source deployment introduces immediate cleanroom and lab access bottlenecks. Uncalibrated or leaky sources pose hazardous alpha contamination risks to probe card chucks and test fixtures. Milestone signoff requires dual-gate delivery: physical delivery of a wipe-tested, leak-free sealed disc along with a calibrated energy-activity calibration certificate before mounting to the DRAM retention test stage.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Foil cladding micro-fracture or alpha-recoil sputtering leading to airborne or swipeable actinide contamination on probe station chucks and wafer dies.
1. Severe alpha energy straggling due to atmospheric air gap variability and gold-palladium foil corrosion, shifting the Bragg peak outside the active 180nm trench/crown depleted junction depth.
1. Uncontrolled broad-beam radiation damaging peripheral sense-amplifier CMOS circuitry (total ionizing dose threshold shifts) rather than isolating single-event upsets (SEU) in the memory storage capacitor nodes.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-2-01` | **NIST-Traceable Alpha Activity and Surface Energy Spectrum Verification** | Passivated Implanted Planar Silicon (PIPS) detector or Silicon Surface Barrier (SBD) detector, Multi-Channel Analyzer (MCA), roughing vacuum chamber (<0.1 Torr), NIST SRM 4904G reference standard. | 1. Acquire background spectrum in vacuum for 1800 s and subtract baseline noise. 2. Mount Am-241 test source on calibrated micrometer jig inside chamber and evacuate to <0.05 Torr. 3. Acquire alpha pulse-height spectrum for 3600 s. 4. Determine total count rate within the main 5.486 MeV peak and calculate absolute activity against the reference standard. 5. Perform FWHM (Full Width at Half Maximum) calculation to evaluate energy straggling. | `Total absolute alpha activity must be within 33.0 kBq to 37.0 kBq (0.9 to 1.0 µCi); FWHM of the 5.486 MeV alpha peak must be <= 65 keV in vacuum; alpha flux repeatability over 3 successive 10-minute acquisitions must exhibit CV <= 2.0%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-2-02` | **Collimated Beam Standoff and Removable Surface Contamination Wipe Test** | Liquid Scintillation Counter (LSC) or Zinc Sulfide (ZnS:Ag) alpha scintillation probe, Whatman 41 ashless filter smear papers, precision XYZ micrometer positioning stage, beam collimator fixture. | 1. Perform dry wipe over the outer source capsule housing, active face edge, and mounting holder using Whatman 41 filter paper applying moderate pressure (approx. 100-200 g). 2. Measure filter paper in scintillation counter for 600 s. 3. Install 500 µm tungsten collimator over active face. 4. Measure spatial beam footprint at 2.0 mm standoff in air using rastered SBD probe across a 5 mm x 5 mm grid with 200 µm step size. | `Removable radioactive contamination on wipe smear must be < 0.185 Bq (5 pCi / < 11 dpm); collimated flux at center must provide (1.2 +/- 0.15) x 10^3 alphas/cm²·s with beam boundary cutoff edge sharpness < 150 µm (10% to 90% flux transition).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Double powder-free nitrile gloves (inner 5 mil, outer 8 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified splash/impact safety goggles, Lead-lined or acrylic beta/gamma torso apron for secondary 59.5 keV photon shielding, NIOSH N100 or HEPA half-mask respirator during wipe testing or source mounting, Calibrated personal electronic dosimeter (gamma/X-ray) and extremity thermoluminescent dosimeter (TLD) ring, Low-lint antistatic cleanroom gown with wrist seals
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation or ingestion of Am-241 is an extreme internal radiation hazard. In case of suspected intake or puncture wound: immediately flush affected wound under copious running water for >= 15 minutes; do not scrub or abrade intact skin. Alert Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) immediately. The specific chelating antidote for internal actinide contamination is Diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (DTPA, calcium trisodium pentetate Ca-DTPA or zinc trisodium pentetate Zn-DTPA) administered strictly by licensed emergency medical personnel via IV or nebulizer within 1-2 hours.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All calibration, unboxing, and wipe-testing operations must be performed inside a dedicated Type I Class A ducted radioisotope fume hood or glovebox equipped with dedicated HEPA exhaust filtration (99.97% retention at 0.3 um) maintaining a minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Fume exhaust must bypass recirculating cleanroom HVAC lines.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Radioactive materials cannot be chemically neutralized. Contaminated smear swabs, gloves, and wipes must be segregated into clearly labeled, lead-lined radioactive waste bins marked with ISO radiation trefoil, isotope (Am-241), activity date, and initial activity. Disposal must follow statutory radioactive solid waste protocols via authorized national nuclear waste disposal repositories (VARANS approved vendor).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Americium-241 (encapsulated alpha source / AmO2 in Au-Pd matrix)** | `14596-10-2` | Radioisotope Standard Grade / Sealed Source | `33 to 37 kBq (0.9 to 1.0 uCi)` |
| **Ethanol (Decontamination Wipe Solvent)** | `64-17-5` | ACS Reagent / Semiconductor Grade | `>= 99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Sealed hermetic source capsule in dry protective shipping container with intact tamper seal and zero particulate debris on gold window.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Collimated, leak-tested source module securely seated in grounded Faraday-shielded test fixture ready for DRAM retention probe station interface.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes atmospheric moisture condensation, dust deposition, and progressive micro-corrosion of the ultra-thin gold/palladium source face, severely attenuating alpha kinetic energy below 5.0 MeV and inducing erratic, non-reproducible DRAM soft-error rates.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Procured, leak-tested, and metrologically characterized sealed Am-241 alpha radiation source calibrated to 35 kBq (+/- 5%) activity, equipped with a 500 um tungsten pinhole collimator for single-die DRAM retention and soft-error rate (SER) profiling without chamber contamination.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AM241_ACTIVITY_MCA_SPECTRUM_CALIBRATION.pdf`
- [ ] `ALPHA_FLUX_COLLIMATOR_SPATIAL_PROFILE.csv`
- [ ] `RADIATION_SAFETY_WIPE_LEAK_TEST_CERTIFICATE.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Calibrated absolute radioactive source activity across active gold foil face** | `35.0 kBq` | +/- 2.0 kBq | Multi-Channel Analyzer (MCA) with calibrated Passivated Implanted Planar Silicon (PIPS) detector in vacuum at 10.0 mm calibrated distance. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum alpha spectral peak Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) indicating minimal energy straggling** | `55.0 keV` | <= 65.0 keV | MCA Gaussian peak fitting of the 5.486 MeV alpha transition line under <= 0.05 Torr vacuum. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Non-fixed removable alpha surface contamination from housing and encapsulation perimeter** | `0.00 Bq` | < 0.185 Bq (< 5 pCi) | Whatman 41 smear wipe counted on liquid scintillation counter or calibrated ZnS:Ag alpha scintillation counter for 600 seconds. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff by Lead Metrologist and Radiation Safety Officer confirming valid wipe leak test (<0.185 Bq), MCA activity within 35.0 +/- 2.0 kBq, documented beam profile matching 500 um collimator geometry, and verified mechanical clearance on the 180nm DRAM wafer probe chuck.

```text
| STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP)                                                              |
| DRAM Foundation VN — Metrology & Reliability Engineering Council                                |
| SOP-MET-180-SER-001: Alpha-Particle Irradiation Exposure & Critical Charge (Qcrit) Profiling     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure defines the physical test protocol for measuring alpha-particle-induced Single-Event Upset (SEU) Soft-Error Rates (SER) and profiling critical charge ($Q_{crit}$) on 180nm 1T1C Crown-type Capacitor-Over-Bitline (COB) 8F² folded bitline memory test arrays (cell area $0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$). The objective is to verify that nominal $C_s \ge 28\ \text{fF}$ storage node capacitance provides sufficient charge margin to suppress alpha ionization upsets.

---

### 2. Physical Architecture & System Test Diagram

```text
       [ Vacuum Chamber / Irradiation Test Bench ]
                           │
       +───────────────────▼───────────────────+
       |   Americium-241 (Am-241) Alpha Source |
       |     (5.48 MeV collimated emission)    |
       +───────────────────┬───────────────────+
                           │ Fluence: 1.0E6 - 1.0E7 α/cm²
                           ▼
       +───────────────────────────────────────+
       |   Decapped 180nm DRAM DUT (Package)   |
       |  - 8F² Folded Bitline (0.259 µm² Area)|
       |  - Crown-Type COB MIM/High-k Stack    |
       |  - Array: 256/512 Cells per Bitline   |
       +───────────────────┬───────────────────+
                           │
       +───────────────────▼───────────────────+
       | Automated Memory Tester (ATE) / Param |
       |  - V_DD Sweep (1.5 V -> 2.0 V)        |
       |  - Data Pattern: Physical Solid '1'/'0'|
       |  - Retention Time: 64 ms at 85 °C     |
       +───────────────────────────────────────+
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Device Preparation & Baseline Characterization
1. Mount a decapped 180nm 8F² folded bitline DRAM test vehicle (open cavity package, die area exposed) onto the thermal-controlled test chuck inside the shielded radiation enclosure.
2. Establish environmental and operational baseline:
   - Chuck temperature: $85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Array core operating voltage ($V_{DD}$): Nominal $1.80\ \text{V}$ (swept across $1.50\ \text{V}$ to $2.00\ \text{V}$ during $Q_{crit}$ profiling).
   - Bitline precharge voltage: $V_{BLP} = V_{DD} / 2 = 0.90\ \text{V}$.
3. Verify baseline retention at $85^\circ\text{C}$ without radiation:
   - Ensure cell leakage current is $< 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Confirm pause-time/retention time exceeds $64\ \text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ with zero soft-fail bit count.

#### Step 2: Test Pattern Injection & ATE Timing Initialization
1. Using the automated test system, write deterministic test patterns into the target array blocks:
   - **Pattern A (Physical Solid '1')**: Storage node at $V_{DD}$ ($1.8\ \text{V}$), bitline precharged to $V_{DD}/2$. Sensitive to electron collection flipping data from '1' $\to$ '0'.
   - **Pattern B (Physical Solid '0')**: Storage node at $0\ \text{V}$.
2. Configure refresh timing parameters:
   - Set refresh interval: $t_{REF} = 64\ \text{ms}$.
   - Array bitline architecture: blocks configured with 256 or 512 cells per bitline ($C_b = 150\ \text{fF}$ to $250\ \text{fF}$; $C_b/C_s$ maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$).

#### Step 3: Collimated Alpha Irradiation Exposure
1. Position a calibrated planar $^{241}\text{Am}$ foil source (unsealed active area $10\ \text{mm} \times 10\ \text{mm}$, alpha kinetic energy $E_\alpha \approx 5.48\ \text{MeV}$) directly parallel to the exposed die surface at a fixed working distance of $d = 3.0\ \text{mm} \pm 0.1\ \text{mm}$ under nitrogen purge.
2. Set exposure flux to provide a calibrated surface alpha fluence between $1.0 \times 10^6\ \alpha/(\text{cm}^2\cdot\text{s})$ and $1.0 \times 10^7\ \alpha/(\text{cm}^2\cdot\text{s})$.
3. Initiate continuous dynamic read-pause-write cycling across the irradiated block while logging bit fail counts ($N_{fails}$) over an accumulation interval of $1000\ \text{s}$.

#### Step 4: Voltage Scaling & Critical Charge ($Q_{crit}$) Extraction
1. Step the storage cell high-level supply voltage $V_{DD}$ downward from $2.0\ \text{V}$ to $1.5\ \text{V}$ in discrete increments of $50\ \text{mV}$.
2. At each voltage point $V_k$, recalculate stored charge:
   $$Q_s = C_s \times (V_{DD} - V_{BLP}) = C_s \times \frac{V_k}{2}$$
3. Record Single-Event Upset Cross Section ($\sigma_{SEU}$) versus stored charge $Q_s$:
   $$\sigma_{SEU}(V_k) = \frac{N_{fails}(V_k)}{\Phi_\alpha \cdot N_{cells}}$$
4. Identify critical charge $Q_{crit}$ as the threshold charge where $\sigma_{SEU}$ exhibits an exponential roll-off toward zero (extrapolated 1% onset cross-section).

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 28.0$ (nominally $25.0 - 30.0$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | ATE CV-metrology / Charge transfer profiling |
| **Cell Junction & Sub-threshold Leakage** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Static pause-time retention decay metrology |
| **Critical Charge ($Q_{crit}$)** | $\ge 25.2$ | $\text{fC}$ ($Q_{crit} \approx C_s \cdot \Delta V_{BL}$, $\Delta V_{BL} \ge 0.9\ \text{V}$) | Alpha-induced bit-flip threshold voltage point |
| **Bitline-to-Cell Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)** | $5:1\text{ to }9:1$ (never $> 10:1$) | Dimensionless ratio | Bitline parasitic CV sweep ($C_b = 150 - 250\ \text{fF}$) |

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Unit cell geometry $L = 180\ \text{nm}$, $W = 220\ \text{nm}$, crown-shaped COB with ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-k stack ($\kappa > 15$). Minimum capacitance budget of $28\ \text{fF/cell}$ for alpha-particle soft error immunity; leakage current target $< 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
* **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: 1T1C $8\text{F}^2$ and $6\text{F}^2$ layouts with target storage capacitance $25 - 30\ \text{fF/cell}$ to achieve retention $> 64\ \text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
* **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: Folded bitline $8\text{F}^2$ cell area $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$; storage node capacitance $C_s \ge 25 - 30\ \text{fF}$ ($28\ \text{fF}$ nominal); bitline capacitance $C_b = 150 - 250\ \text{fF}$ across 256/512 cells per bitline; operating ratio $C_b / C_s$ strictly between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (must not exceed $10:1$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Alpha irradiation characterization for 180nm 1T1C DRAM requires decoupling storage node collection efficiency from bitline sensing flip dynamics. For an 8F² crown capacitor topology (28 fF target node capacitance operating at VDD/2 sensing), critical charge Qcrit is nominally Q = Ccell * (VDD/2 - Vmargin) ≈ 28 fF * 0.7V ≈ 19.6 fC. If the test fixture lacks sub-picosecond transient capture or real-time write/read cycling under controlled 5.48 MeV Americium-241 exposure, transient single-event upsets (SEU) will be conflated with accumulated total ionizing dose (TID) parametric leakage shifts in the pass transistor junction.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm feature sizes, the primary alpha strike collection mechanism is funneled drift across the storage node n+/p-well junction rather than pure diffusion. For 28 fF crown COB geometries, a 5 MeV alpha particle traversing silicon deposits ~1.2 MeV over 5 µm (~50 fC of electron-hole pairs). The metrology fixture must profile bit upset cross-section versus cell operating voltage (V_plate, V_BL, V_DD) across multiple incident angles (0° to 60°) to separate direct hits on the crown plug contact from carrier collection along the shared bitline diffusions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sealed Americium-241 foil or disk alpha calibration sources (nominal activity 0.1 µCi to 5 µCi) require strict atomic energy regulatory licensing, wipe-test certificates, and shielded storage enclosures. Substituting with uncalibrated sources or commercial ionization smoke detector foils risks source disintegration, particulate contamination of the probe station, and non-reproducible flux rates across wafer test campaigns.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Radiation profiling sits directly on the tapeout reliability critical path. The open-source characterization flow must establish a repeatable, low-cost tabletop exposure bench using a standard probe station or packaged test vehicle without requiring a beamline accelerator run. Standardizing test fixture socketing and automated FPGA-based pattern loop testing prevents schedule blowouts during multi-die statistical runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Alpha source particulate detachment or surface flaking causing uncontained radioactive contamination on the wafer probe chuck and optical microscope.
1. Funneling charge deposition triggering latch-up in the peripheral sense amplifier CMOS circuitry rather than isolated 1T1C cell SEU, resulting in catastrophic current runaway.
1. Total Ionizing Dose (TID) degradation of the gate oxide in pass transistors during extended static exposure, causing permanent threshold voltage (Vth) shift and false soft-error rate classification.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-3-01` | **Empirical Critical Charge (Qcrit) and Alpha-Induced SEU Cross-Section Profiling** | Calibrated 1.0 µCi Am-241 collimated planar alpha source (5.48 MeV), Keithley 4200A-SCS parameter analyzer, Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA automated high-speed DRAM tester board (operating at 50 MHz pattern cycle), Cascade Summit 12000 semi-automated shielded probe station. | 1. Position collimated Am-241 alpha source at a fixed 3.0 mm standoff distance normal to the active 8F² DRAM cell array window. 2. Write known test pattern (solid '1's, then solid '0's) into 64 kbit test block with storage plate voltage V_plate = 0.9V. 3. Cycle wordline refresh hold-time sweeps from 10 ms to 1000 ms under a calibrated flux of 1.2e4 alphas/cm²-sec. 4. Incrementally reduce internal cell operating voltage VDD from 1.8V down to 1.0V in 50 mV steps to modulate stored charge Q_cell. 5. Log soft-error bit flips per unit fluence at each voltage tier; extract critical charge Qcrit via Weibull fit curve inflection. | `Measured critical charge Qcrit must be >= 18.0 fC at nominal VDD = 1.8V (corresponding to Ccell >= 26.5 fF with 0.68V sense margin). Cell soft-error cross-section at 5.48 MeV must not exceed 2.5e-8 cm²/bit.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-3-02` | **Bitline Sensing Margin vs Retention Dynamic Upset Metrology Under Collimated Flux** | Agilent/Keysight 81110A Pulse Pattern Generator, Tektronix MSO64B 4 GHz Oscilloscope with high-Z active microprobes, Agilent B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer, calibrated aperture-collimated 0.5 µCi Am-241 fixture. | 1. Mount alpha source fixture with 500 µm aperture aligned strictly over the storage node crown array region (masking peripheral sense amplifiers). 2. Execute continuous pseudo-random DRAM read/write cycles (PRBS-7) for 3600 seconds under continuous irradiation. 3. Monitor sense amplifier differential bitline split (V_BL - V_BLB) transient waveform on oscilloscope triggered by read mismatch errors. 4. Shift aperture over bitline contact diffusions and repeat 3600-second read/write loop to quantify secondary upset mechanism. 5. Record ratio of single-bit storage node upsets versus multi-bit column burst errors. | `Single-bit storage node flips must account for > 95% of total recorded upsets (confirming adequate sense amp and bitline shielding isolation). Single-Event Upset Rate (SER) must be <= 500 FIT/Mb under terrestrial flux equivalent extrapolation.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Dosimetry ring badge (TLD) and chest radiation badge, Double nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness per pair), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Radiation-shielded containment box/glovebox for source handling, HEPA-filtered lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Alpha particles do not penetrate the dead outer stratum corneum layer of intact skin but present an extreme internal hazard via ingestion, inhalation, or open wounds. In case of accidental skin contact or handling puncture: Immediately flush area with copious tepid water and mild detergent for at least 15 minutes. Do not abrade skin. If internal contamination or inhalation is suspected, immediately notify Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) and initiate medical evaluation for chelation therapy (e.g., intravenous Zinc-DTPA / Calcium-DTPA under emergency physician direction).
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation must be conducted in a certified Class 1000/ISO 6 cleanroom bench or radiological fume hood equipped with continuous particulate monitoring and dedicated HEPA/charcoal exhaust ducting maintaining negative pressure (> 0.05 inches water gauge) and face velocity >= 100 FPM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wipe/swab testing of the source housing and wafer chuck must be performed before and after exposure using an alpha scintillation detector. Contaminated wipes, gloves, or substrate scrap must be sealed in 4-mil polyethylene bags, marked with radioactive isotope warning labels, and segregated into a designated Class A Low-Level Radioactive Waste (LLRW) disposal drum for licensed disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Americium-241 (Sealed Source)** | `14596-10-2` | Sealed Radioisotope Standard | `1.0 µCi activity electroplated foil` |
| **Isopropanol (Electronics Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly uncapped or chemically etched wafer passivation layer (Si3N4 / SiO2 stack intact over cell array, pad openings free from fluoride corrosion or native oxide buildup).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-irradiation surface verified radiation-decontaminated (< 0.2 Bq/cm² alpha wipe swab), moisture-free, purged with filtered dry N2.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient humidity causes moisture absorption into passivation micro-cracks and pad metallization, inducing galvanic oxidation and parasitic surface leakage across unshielded bitline contacts that masks true radiation-induced charge loss.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed empirical characterization of alpha-particle single-event upset cross-section and extraction of critical charge Qcrit for the 180nm open-source 8F² crown-capacitor 1T1C DRAM array under 5.48 MeV Am-241 exposure, validating retention robustness and confirming compliance with terrestrial SER targets (< 1000 FIT/Mb).

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_180nm_alpha_qcrit_profiling_report.pdf`
- [ ] `seu_cross_section_vs_voltage_data.csv`
- [ ] `alpha_exposure_dose_and_wipe_test_log.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Storage node critical charge (Qcrit) extracted from Weibull cross-section threshold under 5.48 MeV alpha irradiation at 1.8V VDD.** | `19.6 fC` | ± 1.5 fC | Automated voltage-stepped pattern upset analysis via FPGA DRAM test bench with Weibull cumulative distribution fitting. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Saturated single-event upset (SEU) cross-section per bit in the 8F² active array under normal-incidence alpha flux.** | `1.8e-8 cm²/bit` | +0.7e-8 / -0.5e-8 cm²/bit | Direct ratio of total single-bit flips to integrated alpha fluence measured with calibrated surface-barrier detector. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Pre-rad versus post-rad unselected cell junction leakage degradation across 1000-second cumulative irradiation.** | `0.45 fA/cell` | <= 0.85 fA/cell | Sub-femtoamp parameter measurement via Keithley 4200A-SCS SMU on isolated test array pass transistors at 85°C. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires verification that Qcrit exceeds 18.0 fC across all sampled test blocks, confirmed wipe-test clearance (< 0.2 Bq/cm²) by the Radiation Safety Officer, and automated delivery of the comprehensive Weibull SER model and signed test artifacts into the DRAM Foundation VN metrology repository.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Calibrated Americium-241 (Am-241) Alpha Particle Radiation Source & Fixture Sourcing

### Scope & Context
This SOP defines the procurement, specification verification, geometric mounting, and flux calibration of an open/thin-window Americium-241 ($^{241}\text{Am}$) alpha particle radiation source assembly. This calibrated source is deployed in soft-error rate (SER) and critical charge ($Q_{\text{crit}}$) profiling for 180nm 1T1C DRAM test vehicles ($8F^2$ crown-capacitor cell, $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$, leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Procure Am-241     │
│        Source         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Verify Activity &   │
│    Energy Spectrum    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Inspect Fixture    │
│      Geometry &       │
│      Collimation      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Calibrate Flux     │
│   Uniformity Across   │
│          Die          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Acceptance Sign-Off  │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Procurement Specification & Sourcing (`Action: Buy`)**
   - Source a NIST-traceable calibrated planar $^{241}\text{Am}$ alpha disc source electrodeposited or foil-mounted with a thin protective gold or polymer overlayer ($< 100\text{ nm}$) to minimize self-absorption and energy degradation.
   - Specify active emission diameter to match or exceed the test die array footprint ($5\text{ mm} \times 5\text{ mm}$ minimum active aperture).
   - Procure a matched radiation-safe positioning fixture with precision micrometer Z-stage adjustment and an interchangeable aperture collimator (delivering normal incidence $\pm 5^\circ$).

2. **Incoming Certificate of Calibration & Activity Verification**
   - Inspect vendor calibration documentation verifying nominal alpha particle emission energy of $5.486\text{ MeV}$ ($^{241}\text{Am}$ primary alpha decay).
   - Confirm source nominal activity rating within certified tolerance ($\pm 5\%$) using a surface-barrier silicon charged-particle detector in a standard low-vacuum counting chamber.

3. **Mechanical Fixture & Positioning Alignment**
   - Mount the source into the shielded lead/tungsten housing and mate with the automated test fixture positioning bracket.
   - Adjust working distance (source-to-die air gap / vacuum gap) via micrometric Z-axis stage to maintain a calibrated distance of $1.00\text{ mm} \pm 0.05\text{ mm}$ above the unencapsulated DRAM silicon die surface.
   - Align shutter mechanism ensuring beam exposure timing can be set deterministically from $100\text{ ms}$ to continuous exposure.

4. **Surface Flux Uniformity & SER Integration Check**
   - Calibrate spatial alpha particle flux across the full exposure area using a calibrated solid-state PIN diode dosimeter or imaging detector.
   - Verify that flux spatial deviation does not exceed $\pm 5\%$ across the active DRAM cell array field.
   - Document background count rates and assemble safety interlocks prior to transferring the unit to the high-temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$) retention & SER metrology station.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Peak Alpha Emission Energy** | $5.48\pm 0.05$ | $\text{MeV}$ | Alpha particle spectroscopy (Si surface barrier detector) |
| **Source Activity Calibration Tolerance** | $\le \pm 5.0$ | $\%$ | NIST-traceable vendor certificate & radiometric count check |
| **Source-to-Die Z-Travel Positioning Error** | $\le \pm 0.05$ | $\text{mm}$ | Dial indicator / capacitive displacement sensor |
| **Beam Flux Non-Uniformity Across Die** | $\le 5.0$ | $\%$ | Multi-point PIN detector spatial flux scan |

---

### Source Citations
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Referenced metrics*: Baseline cell retention capacitance minimum of $28\text{ fF}$ per cell required for soft-error rate (SER) immunity against alpha-particle strikes, and leakage current limit $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain retention requirements under irradiation.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Referenced metrics*: Minimum cell storage capacitance $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ per cell and retention evaluation requirement ($> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Alpha flux uniformity across the active 180nm DRAM array depends critically on vacuum standoff distance and collimator design. Because 5.486 MeV alpha particles lose energy rapidly in air (~3.5 to 4.0 cm range) via Bragg peak deceleration, any variation in air gap (>±0.25 mm) or tilt introduces severe spatial flux non-uniformity across the 8F² cell array. The fixture must integrate a micrometer-adjustable Z-stage and maintain either low-pressure N2 purging or a controlled proximity gap (<2.0 mm) with a thin Mylar window to ensure repeatable incident kinetic energy at the silicon surface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For a 28 fF crown capacitor operating at VDD/2 = 0.9 V, the critical charge Qcrit is approximately 25.2 fC (corresponding to ~1.57e5 electron-hole pairs). A single Am-241 alpha particle deposits ~80 keV/µm in Si, generating >1e6 pairs along its first 10-15 µm trajectory. Without a calibrated multi-leaf or precision mechanical shutter to control discrete fluence pulses, the fixture risks flooding the array into catastrophic multi-cell upset (MCU) saturation rather than resolving single-event upset (SEU) cross-sections and soft-error rate (SER) scaling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring exempt-quantity (≤0.1 µCi to 1.0 µCi / 3.7 to 37 kBq) or sealed calibrated planar disc Am-241 sources requires specialized NRC/IAEA/VARANS regulatory declaration and chain-of-custody compliance for semiconductor labs in Vietnam. Vendors of radioisotope standards (e.g., Eckert & Ziegler) have lead times of 8-14 weeks; import licensing and customs radiation clearance must be initiated in parallel with mechanical collimation fixture fabrication.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Sourcing lead times and radiological clearance risks slipping Milestone M2.3 retention validation. The mechanical fixture and manual shutter mechanism must be designed, machined, and calibrated with optical non-radioactive mock-ups (photodiode beam targets) 4 weeks prior to physical source delivery to avoid holding up the automated wafer probe station integration.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Collimator window degradation or particulate contamination generating alpha energy spectrum broadening, leading to incorrect Qcrit extraction.
1. Mechanical fixture drift or Z-axis vibration causing non-uniform flux distribution (>15% gradient) across the array under test.
1. Inadvertent surface contamination or source encapsulation breach during manual wafer alignment, triggering radiation containment shutdown.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-3-1-01` | **Calibrated Alpha Source Surface Flux and Energy Spectrum Verification** | Passivated Implanted Planar Silicon (PIPS) detector, Multi-Channel Analyzer (MCA), precision vacuum/air stage, calibrated digital micrometer. | 1. Position PIPS detector at Z = 2.00 mm distance from source collimator aperture. 2. Acquire pulse-height alpha spectrum over 1800 seconds in ambient STP conditions. 3. Extract total count rate (cps) and peak centroid energy (MeV). 4. Repeat at 5 lateral grid positions (center, ±2 mm X, ±2 mm Y) to assess geometric beam uniformity. | `Total incident flux must be within 3.70 kBq ± 5% equivalent emission rate; peak centroid energy at 2.0 mm air standoff must measure 4.85 ± 0.15 MeV with Full-Width at Half-Maximum (FWHM) < 250 keV; spatial flux uniformity across 4x4 mm² field must be > 92%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-2-3-3-3-1-02` | **Shutter Repeatability and Exposure Timing Metrology** | High-speed optical interrupt sensor, digital storage oscilloscope (Keysight Infiniium or equivalent), surface barrier detector. | 1. Set shutter controller for exposure durations: 1.0 s, 5.0 s, 10.0 s, and 60.0 s. 2. Execute 20 consecutive open/close cycles for each exposure setpoint. 3. Measure rising edge to falling edge open duration via detector count profile and optical sensor sync. 4. Measure dark count rate when shutter is in fully closed state. | `Shutter actuation timing jitter must be < ±15 ms for exposures ≥ 1.0 s; closed-state alpha attenuation must achieve 100% suppression (zero detected alpha events above background over 600 seconds).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Nitrile gloves (double-gloved, 6 mil outer), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Low-lint anti-static laboratory cleanroom coat, Personal thermoluminescent dosimeter (TLD) badge or electronic personal dosimeter (EPD)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: External exposure: Remove contaminated outer PPE immediately; wash exposed skin thoroughly with mild soap and lukewarm water without abrading skin. Inhalation or ingestion: Immediate medical evacuation to designated radiological treatment facility; initiate DTPA (diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid) chelation assessment under radiation medical officer supervision.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation within dedicated class 10,000 clean hood or negative-pressure laminar enclosure equipped with continuous air monitoring (CAM) and alpha particulate HEPA exhaust filter.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wipe test swabs and contaminated gloves must be collected in labeled radioactive waste bags, surveyed via Geiger-Müller/ZnS scintillation counter, stored in lead-lined radionuclide lockbox, and disposed of through licensed national radioactive waste management agency (VARANS).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Americium-241 (encapsulated alpha source)** | `14596-10-2` | Sealed Source Standard | `1.0 µCi (37 kBq) sealed foil/disc` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, for wiping non-radioactive stages)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pristine passivation layer (Si3N4 / SiO2 cap) post-metallization bond pad opening; moisture-free, organic-free (<0.5 nm airborne molecular contamination).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Radiation-tested wafer surface verified free of alpha emitter particulate contamination via dry swipe/wipe radiological survey (<0.04 Bq/cm²).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes ambient humidity absorption and native oxide/hydrocarbon buildup on bare bond pads, increasing contact resistance and causing alpha trajectory energy degradation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Procured and verified NIST/IAEA-traceable sealed Am-241 alpha radiation source (nominal 37 kBq) and custom high-precision micrometer fixture with integrated fast shutter, calibrated for 180nm DRAM crown capacitor soft-error rate (SER) and Qcrit profiling.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AM241_SOURCE_CALIBRATION_CERT_NIST_TRACEABLE.pdf`
- [ ] `ALPHA_FIXTURE_BEAM_PROFILE_AND_FWHM_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `RADIOLOGICAL_WIPE_TEST_CLEARANCE_LOG.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Calibrated source activity at delivery** | `37.0 kBq (1.0 µCi)` | ±5.0% | Manufacturer primary calibration certificate and PIPS 2pi geometry activity measurement. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Collimated beam spatial uniformity across 4 mm x 4 mm DRAM target area** | `95.0%` | ≥ 90.0% | 5-point PIPS detector raster scan at Z = 2.0 mm standoff distance. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Alpha particle peak kinetic energy at Si target plane (Z = 2.0 mm ambient air)** | `4.85 MeV` | ±0.15 MeV | Multi-Channel Analyzer (MCA) pulse-height spectral analysis calibrated with standard multi-nuclide reference. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Radiation safety officer (RSO) swipe test clearance (<0.04 Bq/cm² removable activity), successful acquisition of 4.85 ± 0.15 MeV peak centroid at 2.0 mm standoff with >90% spatial uniformity, and formal signoff by Systems Engineer and Metrology Lead.
