# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Cell Retention Time & Junction Leakage SPICE/TCAD Simulation at 85°C

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-DRAM180-004`  
**Classification:** Technical / Metrology & Characterization  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm Node, 8F² Folded Bitline Architecture)  
**Target Cell Area:** $0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ ($8F^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$)  

---

### 1. Process & Simulation Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│    TCAD/SPICE Setup    │
│    L=180nm W=220nm     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Environment Temp    │
│       T = 85°C         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Charge Storage Node   │
│   Cs = 25 fF - 30 fF   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Transient Hold State  │
│    WL = 0V, BL = VDD/2 │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│ Total Leakage Current  │
│      < 1 fA/cell       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│ Retention Time Verif.  │
│      t_ret > 64 ms     │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **TCAD Structure & Grid Definition:**
   - Construct the 2D/3D access NMOS mesh with physical channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and device width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Define a thermally grown gate dielectric ($\text{SiO}_2$) with physical thickness $t_{ox} = 3.5\text{ nm}$.
   - Instantiate the Crown/Cylinder stacked capacitor topology over the drain diffusion node via tungsten plug (W-plug) contact.
   - Configure high-$\kappa$ / multi-layer dielectric (ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ stack, $\kappa > 15$, Equivalent Oxide Thickness $\text{EOT} = 3.0\text{ nm} - 4.0\text{ nm}$) scaled to target $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$ (acceptable range: $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$).

2. **Thermal & Physical Transport Models Setup:**
   - Set lattice/ambient simulation temperature to $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ ($358.15\text{ K}$).
   - Enable Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination, Hurkx band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), and trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) at the drain/storage-node p-n junction.
   - Enable temperature-dependent mobility degradation and high-field saturation models.

3. **Bitline Network & SPICE Deck Coupling:**
   - Couple the storage node capacitor ($C_s = 28\text{ fF}$) to the bitline model.
   - Set bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b$ within $150\text{ fF} - 250\text{ fF}$ (corresponding to a 256 or 512 cells/BL block), verifying that the capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ remains bounded between $5:1$ and $9:1$.

4. **Bias Initialization & Write "1" Phase:**
   - Precharge Bitline ($\text{BL}$) to $V_{DD} / 2$.
   - Pulse Wordline ($\text{WL}$) to activate the access gate and charge the storage node capacitor node to $V_{SN} = V_{DD}$.
   - De-assert Wordline back to standby hold state ($V_{WL} = 0\text{ V}$) with a steep fall time ($t_f \le 1\text{ ns}$).

5. **Transient Hold & Leakage Current Integration:**
   - Execute transient simulation over a time span of $t_{sim} \ge 100\text{ ms}$ at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Monitor and isolate junction leakage components at the storage node:
     $$I_{\text{leak, total}} = I_{\text{sub-threshold}} + I_{\text{junction, rev}} + I_{\text{dielectric}} + I_{\text{BTBT}}$$
   - Continuously record node voltage decay $V_{SN}(t)$.

6. **Retention Time Evaluation:**
   - Calculate elapsed hold time $t_{\text{ret}}$ until node voltage drops to the sensing threshold margin required by the folded bitline sense amplifier:
     $$t_{\text{ret}} = \frac{C_s \cdot \Delta V_{SN}}{I_{\text{leak, total}}}$$
   - Confirm $t_{\text{ret}}$ meets the minimum specification prior to triggering refresh.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Unit | Target / Acceptance Range | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Retention Time ($t_{\text{ret}}$)** | $\text{ms}$ | **$\ge 64\text{ ms}$** at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Transient node voltage decay to minimum sense margin |
| **Total Cell Leakage ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $\text{fA/cell}$ | **$< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$** at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Integral junction + subthreshold current at $V_{WL}=0\text{ V}, V_{SN}=V_{DD}$ |
| **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\text{fF/cell}$ | **$25.0\text{ fF} - 30.0\text{ fF}$** (Nominal: $28.0\text{ fF}$) | High-frequency CV extraction / small-signal AC integration |
| **Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)** | ratio | **$5.0 : 1$ to $9.0 : 1$** (Strictly $< 10.0 : 1$) | Extracted array bitline capacitance ($150 - 250\text{ fF}$) over $C_s$ |

---

### 4. Context & Source Citations
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:** Access gate thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ thickness ($3.5\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor EOT ($3 - 4\text{ nm}$), storage capacitance target ($25 - 30\text{ fF}$), and baseline cell retention specification ($> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Access transistor footprint ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), W-plug/Crown MIM/ONO topology ($\kappa > 15$, nominal $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$), and maximum leakage target ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets:** Folded bitline $8F^2$ footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$), bitline loading capacitance ($C_b = 150 - 250\text{ fF}$ for 256/512 cell blocks), and $C_b / C_s$ ratio constraint ($5:1$ to $9:1$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Coupling 2D/3D TCAD mesh simulations of the 180nm 8F² cell access transistor with transient SPICE circuit models requires rigorous calibration of the p-n junction electric field distribution. Without incorporating trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) at the storage node diffusion edge under worst-case 85°C back-bias (V_BB = -0.8V to -1.0V), retention time projections will overestimate refresh margins by more than 40%.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 85°C, Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) generation across the storage node n+/p-well junction dominates median retention failure, whereas localized dislocation loops and point defect decoration by trace heavy metals cause variable retention time (VRT) tail bits. TCAD must simulate defect energy levels near mid-gap (E_t - E_i = ±0.05 eV) and evaluate Gate-Induced Drain Leakage (GIDL) when the wordline is unselected (V_WL = -0.5V) and storage node holds high (V_SN = V_DD = 1.8V).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Metrology and physical wafer correlation depend on thermal stabilization in the furnace and parametric automated probe card interfaces. Failure to establish standard device model card parameters (BSIM4 / level 49) tied to calibrated TCAD decks risks divergence between projected foundry tape-out retention yields and physical wafer-level testing on automated probers (e.g. Keithley 4200-SCS or Keysight B1500A).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Simulation milestones must lock the baseline storage cell capacitance target (C_s >= 25 fF) against junction area leakage budgets before completing mask tape-out signoff. # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Access Transistor & Storage Node 2D/3D TCAD Mesh Setup and Doping Profile Calibration

**Discipline / Category**: TCAD Simulation  
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using Optical Inspection / Profilometer.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The 2D/3D TCAD mesh definition must resolve the steep lateral phosphorus/arsenic source-drain gradients under the storage node junction without causing numerical divergence or artificial grid-induced leakage. At 180nm node dimensions (L_eff ~ 0.18 um), a sub-1nm mesh refinement across the metallurgical p-n junction and gate-dielectric interface is mandatory to prevent spurious field-emission artifacts in transient 85°C retention simulations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating the storage node n+/p-well junction doping profile solely against SIMS without 4-point probe sheet resistance and spreading resistance profiling (SRP) will overlook transient enhanced diffusion (TED) of boron in the halo implant. Junction electric fields exceeding 0.6 MV/cm will trigger band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) and trap-assisted tunneling (TAT), degrading cell retention well below the 64 ms refresh target at 85°C.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Open-source TCAD workflows relying on DevSim or open-source grid generators must remain fully interoperable with industry-standard GDSII/OASIS stream outputs and calibrated against open-access 180nm physical foundry run data (e.g. physical wafer SIMS and SRP secondary standards) without requiring proprietary closed-source PDK simulation decks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Mesh refinement runtime scales exponentially in 3D transient solve mode. Without an automated 2D-to-3D adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) strategy that truncates mesh count below 150,000 vertices per cell unit, full-temperature corner matrix sweeps (25°C to 85°C) will miss schedule milestones by over 3 weeks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Mesh non-orthogonality along STI sidewalls causing artificial non-physical leakage spikes exceeding 1 fA/cell at 85°C.
1. Uncalibrated halo boron implant TED leading to threshold voltage roll-off (V_thn < 0.50 V) and severe subthreshold leakage into the storage node capacitor.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-3-2-1-01` | **Access Transistor Sub-threshold and Linear Vth Calibration vs TCAD Mesh Density** | Automated TCAD Device Simulator (DevSim/Sentaurus TCAD Engine) with Keithley 4200A-SCS parameter analyzer physical calibration dataset | 1. Execute automated adaptive mesh generation sweeping grid resolution at junction from 5.0 nm down to 0.5 nm step. 2. Solve drift-diffusion coupled with hydrodynamic carrier transport at V_DS = 50 mV, sweeping V_GS from 0 V to 1.8 V. 3. Extract linear V_th via maximum g_m extrapolation and calculate subthreshold swing (S). 4. Compare extracted simulated V_th and S against physical Stage 3 MOSFET verification targets. | `Simulated NMOS V_thn must converge to +0.55 V +/- 15 mV at V_DS = 50 mV; Subthreshold swing S <= 85 mV/dec at 300 K; Mesh discretization error between successive grid densities must be < 1.0%.` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-3-2-1-02` | **Storage Node Junction Leakage and Band-to-Band Tunneling TCAD Extraction at 85°C** | High-temperature TCAD Transient Solver with Hurkx Band-to-Band Tunneling (BTBT) and Schenk Trap-Assisted Tunneling (TAT) models active | 1. Apply reverse bias step of 1.8 V to storage node contact with access gate biased in deep accumulation (V_GS = -0.5 V). 2. Ramp time domain solve across 100 ms retention window. 3. Integrate net total leakage current (I_junction = I_BTBT + I_TAT + I_SRH + I_diff) passing from storage node n+ region to p-well. 4. Verify junction electric field does not exceed 0.55 MV/cm at peak metallurgical junction. | `Total storage node leakage current I_leak at 85°C must be <= 1.0 fA/cell (<= 1.0e-15 A) across the full 64 ms retention interval.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety goggles with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat, Closed-toe chemical-resistant footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF skin exposure: Flush immediately with copious cold water for 5 minutes, apply 2.5% calcium gluconate gel generously and massage into affected area; seek urgent medical attention. For eye contact: Rinse continuously at eye wash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Chemical laminar fume hood certified for acid use with face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.5 m/s); dedicated acid scrubber exhaust ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate fluoride waste into dedicated fluoropolymer containers; neutralize with aqueous calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble calcium fluoride (CaF2); verify effluent pH between 6.5 and 8.5 before discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (pre-SIMS surface oxide strip)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `0.5% aqueous solution` |
| **Isopropanol (wafer solvent cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (MOS) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Native oxide stripped via dilute HF dip; hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated silicon surface on calibration test coupons.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Dry thermal screening oxide grown (thickness 3.0 nm +/- 0.3 nm) prior to secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) profile calibration.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide regrowth exceeding 0.8 nm causes knock-on oxygen distortion in SIMS profiling and erroneous calibration of the shallow arsenic/phosphorus implant depth by > 12 nm.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Calibrated 2D/3D TCAD structural mesh deck and validated doping profile model for the 180nm 8F2 access transistor and storage node, reproducing electrical I-V, Vth (+0.55V), and 85°C retention junction leakage (<1 fA/cell) matching Stage 3 physical MOSFET metrology benchmarks.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_cell_access_tx_3d_mesh.msh`
- [ ] `storage_node_doping_calibration_report.pdf`
- [ ] `simulated_vs_experimental_iv_leakage.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Access transistor linear threshold voltage V_thn at V_DS = 50 mV** | `0.55 V` | +/- 0.05 V | Maximum transconductance (g_m) extrapolation from TCAD linear transfer characteristics sweep |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Storage node total junction leakage current at 85°C (358 K) under 1.8V reverse bias** | `0.85 fA/cell` | <= 1.00 fA/cell | High-temperature transient TCAD device simulation integrating Hurkx BTBT and SRH recombination across storage node junction |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Sheet resistance R_s of n+ source/drain extension implant** | `120 Ohm/sq` | +/- 10 Ohm/sq | Simulated vs physical four-point collinear probe metrology using correction factor F(d/s) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal sign-off requires TCAD simulation convergence across all device grid nodes with zero numerical singularities, residual divergence < 1.0e-5, simulated V_thn within +0.55 V +/- 50 mV, and total storage node leakage verified at <= 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C matching experimental calibration data.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Title: Elevated Temperature (85°C) Subthreshold & Junction Leakage Transient SPICE Simulation

**Document ID:** `SOP-180NM-MET-042`  
**Classification:** Circuit Design / Metrology  
**Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — Gen 2 (µm)  
**Cell Topology:** 1T1C Folded Bitline Stacked Capacitor over Bitline (COB), $8F^2$  

---

### 1. Executive Summary & Objective
This procedure establishes the SPICE-level transient extraction and validation workflow for a single 1T1C DRAM unit cell operating under elevated junction temperatures ($T = 85^\circ\text{C}$). The objective is to evaluate subthreshold conduction, drain/source reverse-bias p-n junction leakage, and gate dielectric degradation over a full retention cycle ($t_{\text{ret}} \ge 64\text{ ms}$) to verify that storage node charge retention complies with the refresh interval requirement.

```
       WL = V_PP / V_SS (0V / -0.5V)
               │
               ▼
BL ───────┤ Access Transistor ├─── SN (Storage Node)
(V_DD/2)  (W=220nm, L=180nm)      │
                                  ├── C_s (28 fF Stacked Capacitor)
                                  │   └── V_PL (V_DD/2 Plate)
                                  ├── I_sub (Subthreshold Leakage to BL)
                                  └── I_junc (Junction Leakage to P-well)
```

---

### 2. Physical & Device Parameters

All parameters are configured in accordance with verified 180nm cell architecture:
- **Access Transistor Dimensions:** Gate Length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, Channel Width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
- **Gate Dielectric:** Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ with physical oxide thickness $t_{\text{ox}} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$ ($EOT \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$).
- **Storage Capacitor ($C_s$):** Stacked crown/cylinder capacitor, $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ (nominal budget $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$).
- **Operating Junction Temperature:** $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ (358.15 K).
- **Bitline & Precharge Reference:** Folded bitline precharged to $V_{\text{pre}} = V_{DD} / 2$; cell plate biased at $V_{PL} = V_{DD} / 2$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Netlist Deck Configuration & Model Setup
1. Define the simulation environment in SPICE:
   ```spice
   .TEMP 85.0
   .OPTIONS ACCURATE=1 CONV=1 RELTOL=1e-5 ABSTOL=1e-15 CHGTOL=1e-16 GMIN=1e-18
   ```
2. Instantiate the access NMOS transistor model with calibrated temperature coefficients for reverse diode saturation current ($I_S$), temperature exponent ($XTI$), barrier height, and bandgap narrowing.
3. Configure the access transistor geometry: `W=220n L=180n`. Connect the body terminal to the cell substrate/P-well bias line ($V_{BB} \approx -0.5\text{V}$ to $0\text{V}$).

#### Step 2: Storage Capacitor & Parasitic Boundary Initialization
1. Instantiate the cell storage capacitor between the internal storage node `SN` and the cell plate `VPL` ($V_{DD}/2$):
   ```spice
   CS_CELL SN VPL 28fF
   ```
2. Include the tungsten contact plug (W-plug) parasitic resistance ($R_{plug}$) and the bitline parasitic capacitance ($C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$).

#### Step 3: Write "High" Transient Preconditioning
1. Set the initial bitline voltage to $V_{DD}$ ($1.8\text{ V}$).
2. Assert the Wordline (WL) by driving the gate from $0\text{ V}$ to the boosted gate voltage $V_{PP}$ ($> V_{DD} + V_{th}$) for $\Delta t = 10\text{ ns}$ to fully charge the storage node `SN` to $V_{DD}$.
3. De-assert the Wordline to turn off the access transistor ($V_{WL} = 0\text{ V}$ or negative back-bias).
4. Equalize the Bitline (BL) to $V_{DD} / 2$ to emulate the standard DRAM precharge state during retention holding.

#### Step 4: Long Transient Retention Holding Simulation
1. Execute a long-duration transient analysis over the retention interval:
   ```spice
   .TRAN 100us 64ms 0s 10us
   ```
2. Probe and decompose the current branches leaving node `SN`:
   - Subthreshold conduction into the bitline ($I_{\text{sub}} = I_{DS}$).
   - Reverse p-n junction leakage into the P-well/substrate ($I_{\text{junc}} = I_{D\text{-}body}$).
   - Dielectric leakage through the stacked capacitor dielectric ($I_{\text{diel}}$).

#### Step 5: Post-Processing & Read Margin Evaluation
1. Measure total instantaneous leakage: $I_{\text{leak\_total}}(t) = I_{\text{sub}}(t) + I_{\text{junc}}(t) + I_{\text{diel}}(t)$ across the holding window.
2. Calculate the stored node voltage drop $\Delta V_{SN}$ at $t = 64\text{ ms}$:
   $$\Delta V_{SN} = \frac{1}{C_s} \int_{0}^{64\text{ ms}} I_{\text{leak\_total}}(t) \, dt$$
3. Trigger a read cycle at $t = 64\text{ ms}$ by re-asserting the Wordline, and verify that the differential signal developed on the complementary bitlines satisfies:
   $$\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s} \cdot \left(V_{SN}(64\text{ ms}) - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right) \ge 100\text{ mV}$$

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Evaluation Method | Target Spec | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Operating Temperature** | SPICE Environment Option (`.TEMP`) | $85$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Total Cell Leakage Current** | Transient probe at $V_{SN} = V_{DD}$, $V_{BL} = V_{DD}/2$ | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ |
| **Storage Capacitance ($C_s$)** | Node extraction parameter | $\ge 28.0$ (min. 25.0 to 30.0) | $\text{fF}$ |
| **Minimum Retention Time** | Duration with valid state retention at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | $\ge 64$ | $\text{ms}$ |
| **Differential Readout Voltage ($\Delta V$)** | Developed signal at sense amplifier input ($C_{BL}=250\text{ fF}$) | $100\text{ to }150$ | $\text{mV}$ |

---

### 5. Literature Sources & Citations

1. **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**  
   - *Cited parameters:* Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$); minimum cell capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF}$; maximum subthreshold and junction leakage target of $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; stacked capacitor with W-plug over bitline.
2. **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**  
   - *Cited parameters:* 1T1C $8F^2$ architecture; cell capacitance range ($25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$); retention requirement $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; gate oxide physical thickness $\approx 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**  
   - *Cited parameters:* Precharge equalization to $V_{DD}/2$; bitline capacitance $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$; signal development differential voltage $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s} (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{DD}/2) \approx 100\text{ mV to }150\text{ mV}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: At 85°C, DRAM retention time degrades exponentially following Arrhenius scaling (~exp(-Ea/kT) with Ea ~ 0.6-1.1 eV depending on the dominant mechanism: trap-assisted tunneling vs. SRH generation in the storage node p-n junction). If the 180nm access transistor subthreshold swing degrades from ~80 mV/dec at 300K to >105 mV/dec at 358K, off-state channel leakage (I_sub) and drain-substrate reverse junction leakage (I_rev) will severely erode the storage capacitor charge (V_cell dropping below sense amplifier sensing threshold V_BL/2 ± 100 mV within the required 64 ms refresh window). Transient SPICE simulations must couple layout-extracted parasitic capacitances (C_sn, C_gate-drain overlap) with temperature-dependent BSIM4 models calibrated against silicon C-V and static I-V data.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Subthreshold leakage at 85°C cannot be simulated accurately using standard room-temperature BSIM parameters without explicitly calibrating U0 (mobility temperature exponent BTE), KT1/KT2 (Vth temperature shift), and bandgap narrowing. Furthermore, the storage node p-n junction leakage under high reverse bias (V_SN = 1.8 V, V_substrate = -0.5 V or 0 V) is dominated by trap-assisted recombination (Dit and bulk mid-gap traps) and gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL). Neglecting band-to-band tunneling (BBT) and perimeter junction leakage components along the STI edge will result in an overly optimistic retention estimation by at least 3-5x.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Model card parameters require empirical validation on actual test chips fabricated through open-source MPW shuttles (e.g., SkyWater/EFabless 130/180nm or local pilot foundry lines). SPICE models often underestimate junction leakage corners due to lack of foundry-provided high-temperature Monte Carlo statistical cards. Reliance on idealized proprietary PDK BSIM models without open silicon correlation risks redesign delays and mask re-spin expenses.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Simulation must close the gap between device TCAD and array-level refresh architecture. If transient SPICE simulations show retention degradation requiring refresh intervals tighter than 64 ms (e.g., 16 ms or 32 ms at 85°C), the DRAM controller timing engine and internal row refresh state machines must be updated in the RTL phase. Deliverables must provide definitive quantitative boundaries for worst-case retention before sign-off.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal subthreshold punch-through and DIBL acceleration causing V_cell to drop below minimum sense margin (Delta_V < 80 mV) within t_RET < 64 ms at 85°C.
1. Perimeter/STI edge trap-assisted junction leakage spikes exceeding 50 fA per cell at 85°C, resulting in widespread single-bit retention tail fails.
1. GIDL-induced drain leakage exacerbated by negative wordline off-voltage (V_NWL = -0.3V) leading to storage node discharge faster than refresh clock cycle.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-3-2-2-01` | **85°C Storage Node Retention Voltage Transient Decay Simulation** | HSPICE / Ngspice / Xyce Transient Simulation Engine with BSIM4.7 device model card, 1 fA resolution numerical integrator (gear/trapratio settings), post-layout RC parasitic netlist (.pex/dspf). | 1. Initialize storage node voltage V(SN) to logic '1' (1.8 V) via wordline pulse (V_WL = 3.0 V pumped) with bitline held at 1.8 V. 2. De-assert wordline to 0.0 V with 1.0 ns fall time to isolate the storage node. 3. Run transient analysis (.tran 0.1ms 100ms) at T = 85°C with bitline held at precharge level (V_BL = 0.9 V). 4. Measure voltage decay curve V_SN(t) and calculate retention time t_RET where V_SN decays from 1.8 V to 1.35 V (Delta_V = 450 mV). | `Storage node voltage V(SN) must remain >= 1.35 V at t = 64.0 ms (voltage decay Delta_V <= 450 mV) at 85°C; total equivalent leakage current I_leak_total = C_cell * (dV/dt) must not exceed 0.176 fA/fF (<= 4.4 fA total cell leakage).` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-3-2-2-02` | **Access Transistor Subthreshold & Junction Leakage Component Decomposition at 85°C** | SPICE DC operating point and parametric temperature sweep (.dc / .temp sweep 25°C to 85°C) measuring separate terminal currents I_D, I_S, I_B, and I_G. | 1. Configure .TEMP = 85°C. 2. Perform DC sweep of V_GS from -0.5 V to 0.0 V in 10 mV steps with V_DS = -0.9 V and V_SB = 1.8 V. 3. Extract subthreshold current I_sub at V_GS = 0.0 V. 4. Extract reverse n+/p-well junction leakage current I_rev at V_SN = 1.8 V. 5. Measure gate dielectric tunneling current I_G. | `At V_GS = 0.0 V, V_DS = -0.9 V, T = 85°C: Subthreshold leakage current I_sub <= 2.5 fA; Reverse junction leakage I_rev <= 2.0 fA; Gate oxide leakage I_G <= 0.1 fA. Subthreshold swing S(85°C) must be <= 110 mV/dec.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Standard Cleanroom/Laboratory ESD-safe coat, ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Powder-free nitrile gloves (Class 100 cleanroom compatible)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of thermal burn from heated probe station chuck (85°C), immediately flush affected area with cool potable water for minimum 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly. For cryogenic LN2 splash, warm frozen tissue gently with lukewarm water (40°C); seek immediate medical attention. In case of IPA inhalation or eye contact, rinse eyes thoroughly for 15 minutes and move to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: High-flow laboratory chemical exhaust ducting (>100 FPM face velocity) for solvent wipedown. Cryogenic LN2 thermal chuck exhaust vented directly outside the building to prevent cleanroom oxygen displacement (continuous cleanroom ambient O2 sensors alarmed at <19.5%).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes sealed in dedicated fire-rated flammable waste containers and collected by certified hazardous material disposal services. Spent LN2 naturally boil-off vented through non-obstructed roof exhaust stack.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for thermal chuck wipe-down** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Liquid Nitrogen (chiller coolant for temperature stabilization)** | `7727-37-9` | Research / Cryogenic Grade | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-PEX layout netlist with extracted parasitic RC models verified against DRC/LVS rules; Silicon test structures cleaned via DI rinse / N2 blow-dry with native oxide controlled < 1.2 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Completed SPICE transient waveform database, validated temperature coefficient vectors, and verified hot-carrier/leakage reliability tables appended to model card.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture adsorption and dielectric surface charging during extended atmospheric exposure prior to physical probe station validation at 85°C leads to surface leakage artifacts, invalidating simulated subthreshold swing and GIDL extraction.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full sign-off and verification of 1T1C 8F² DRAM cell retention capability at 85°C under nominal 180nm process corners. Confirmation that cumulative subthreshold, junction, and GIDL leakage rates permit >= 64 ms retention interval with >= 80 mV sensing differential margin across all layout parasitic conditions.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_cell_85c_retention_transient.csv`
- [ ] `leakage_component_decomposition_85c_report.pdf`
- [ ] `bsim4_temperature_leakage_calibration.sp`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Storage node voltage retention decay after 64 ms at 85°C** | `>= 1.35 V` | +/- 50 mV | Transient SPICE numerical integration over 100 ms (.TRAN with 1 fA current tolerance) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total combined cell off-state leakage current (I_sub + I_junc + I_gidl) at 85°C** | `<= 4.4 fA` | +/- 0.5 fA | DC operating point terminal current summation at V_SN = 1.8 V, V_BL = 0.9 V, V_WL = 0.0 V, T = 85°C |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Access transistor subthreshold slope at 85°C (358.15 K)** | `<= 108 mV/decade` | +/- 3 mV/decade | Log-linear derivative d(V_GS)/d(log10(I_D)) extracted in subthreshold region |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions (ASSERT-01 through ASSERT-03) verified across TT, FF, and SS process corners at 85°C. Total cell retention decay must demonstrate > 64 ms retention at 85°C with positive margin of at least 25% (t_RET_fail >= 80 ms), and simulation results must be formally ratified by the Multi-Agent DRAM Verification Council.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** Cell Retention Time & 64ms Refresh Window Metrology Verification and Leakage Budget Validation  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Metrology  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / µm)  
**Process Action Type:** Make / Metrology Verification  

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                               EXECUTION FLOWCHART                               |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1: Environmental & Test Bench Conditioning (85°C Chuck / Chamber)]       |
|                                       │                                         |
|                                       ▼                                         |
|  [Step 2: 1T1C Storage Node Bias & Data State Initialization (Data '1' / '0')]  |
|                                       │                                         |
|                                       ▼                                         |
|  [Step 3: Leakage Current Metrology (Sub-threshold & Junction DC Measurement)]   |
|                                       │                                         |
|                                       ▼                                         |
|  [Step 4: 64 ms Pause Time & Differential Readout Sensing Margin Verification]  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Environmental & Test Bench Conditioning
1. Mount the 180nm test vehicle wafer or macro test structure onto the automated parametric prober/thermal chuck.
2. Elevate and stabilize the chuck/ambient chamber temperature to **85°C ± 0.5°C**.
3. Verify thermal equilibrium across the wafer before initiating electrical bias sweeps.

#### Step 2: Storage Node Bias & Precharge Setup
1. Initialize the folded bitline pair ($\text{BL}$ and $\overline{\text{BL}}$) to the precharge level of $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$ via the bitline equalization network.
2. Assert the target wordline ($\text{WL}$) to turn on the access transistor ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
3. Fully write a logic high state ("1") into the storage cell capacitor ($C_s$) to establish the initial charge $Q_s = C_s \times (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$, then de-assert the wordline to cut off the access transistor.

#### Step 3: Leakage Current Metrology
1. Perform high-precision parametric DC metrology at the storage node / bitline access terminal at 85°C.
2. Measure the cumulative leakage current, accounting for access transistor sub-threshold leakage, p-n junction leakage at the drain/storage contact tungsten plug ($\text{W-plug}$), and dielectric leakage through the high-$\kappa$ capacitor stack ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ / $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ or $\text{ONO}$).
3. Ensure measured leakage meets the sub-$1\text{ fA/cell}$ target budget to guarantee charge retention.

#### Step 4: 64 ms Pause-Time Verification & Sensing Readout
1. Keep the cell unaccessed during a standardized retention hold window of **$t_{\text{retention}} \ge 64\text{ ms}$** at 85°C.
2. Following the 64 ms window, precharge $\text{BL}$ and $\overline{\text{BL}}$ to $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$, then re-assert the wordline to discharge residual charge onto the bitline ($C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$).
3. Monitor differential voltage development:
   $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}\right) \times \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right)$$
4. Trigger the sense amplifier latch signals ($\text{SAN}$ and $\text{SAP}$) and verify error-free latching without bit flips.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage/Chuck Temperature** | $85.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ | Automated thermal chuck thermocouple probe |
| **Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $25.0 \text{ to } 30.0$ (min. $\ge 28.0$ for noise immunity) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | $C\text{-}V$ parameter analyzer at $1\text{ MHz}$ |
| **Total Retention Leakage Current** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Sub-femtoampere parametric electrometer at $85^{\circ}\text{C}$ |
| **Readout Differential Signal ($\Delta V$)** | $100.0 \text{ to } 150.0$ | $\text{mV}$ | High-speed sampling oscilloscope / Sense amplifier latch monitor |
| **Retention Window Pause Time** | $\ge 64.0$ | $\text{ms}$ | Automated digital pattern timing generator |

---

### 3. Context Citations

- **Capacitance & Dielectric Metrics:**
  - *"The storage capacitor must maintain a minimum capacitance of 25 to 30 fF (femtofarads) per cell to ensure data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C."* — *[Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]*
  - *"Capacitance Budget: Minimum 28 fF per cell ensures noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling capacitance."* — *[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]*
- **Transistor Geometry & Leakage Budget:**
  - *"Unit Cell Geometry: Access transistor channel length L = 180 nm, width W = 220 nm... Leakage Current Target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval"* — *[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]*
- **Differential Readout Dynamics & Bitline Ratios:**
  - *"Precharge Operation: Prior to wordline assertion, bitlines are equalized to V_DD / 2... For typical cell capacitance C_s = 25 fF and bitline capacitance C_BL = 250 fF, signal delta V is approximately 100 mV to 150 mV."* — *[Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout]*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: At 85°C, sustaining a 64ms retention window across a 1T1C array requires an aggregate leakage floor of less than 0.875 fA/cell given a 28 fF storage node (ΔV_margin ≈ 2.0V to 1.0V sensing threshold). Bitline coupling parasitics and access transistor off-state drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) severely erode this margin if sub-threshold slope exceeds 95 mV/dec at 180nm. A negative wordline low-level bias (V_NWL ≈ -0.3V) must be co-integrated into the refresh timing generator to suppress junction band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) without triggering gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: The predominant leakage mechanisms at 85°C are bulk trap-assisted recombination at the storage node n+/p-well junction and dielectric hopping conduction across the ONO/high-k interface. Garage-scale thermal budgets in Gen 2 (µm) risk unannealed implantation damage, spiking the tail distribution (Variable Retention Time / VRT phenomenon due to unstable localized traps). Metrology verification must explicitly stress both steady-state pause refresh (Pause Test) and march disturbance patterns to separate static storage-junction leakage from dynamic wordline-induced GIDL.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring calibrated femtoamp-level electrometers (e.g., Keysight B1500A/B1517A HRSMU or Keithley 6430) and thermal chuck probing enclosures in a regional open-source cleanroom ecosystem is a significant bottleneck. Substitute triaxial microchamber probe stations must be isolated from ambient 50Hz hum and microphonic vibrations; uncalibrated commercial micro-positioners with triax guard rings will corrupt sub-10fA measurements into multi-picoamp noise floors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology verification cycle time per wafer die matrix threatens project milestone pacing if automated pause-refresh scan scripts are not parallelized. We must constrain the manual wafer probe pass to a 32x32 test vehicle subarray rather than full-array characterization, ensuring signoff within 48 hours of post-metallization anneal to prevent ambient mobile ion contamination from drifting the retention baseline.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Trapped Interface State Degradation (VRT): Dynamic generation and relaxation of deep-level traps at the storage-node W-plug/junction interface causing erratic single-cell bit flips prior to the 64ms refresh boundary.
1. GIDL and BTBT Overlap: Excessive negative gate bias on the pass transistor inducing high electric fields across the drain-gate overlap, driving leakage current well past the 1 fA budget.
1. Thermal Chuck Convective Gradient: Non-uniform temperature distribution across the prober hot chuck exceeding ±1.5°C, yielding pseudo-leakage dispersion and invalid activation energy (Ea) extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

Measure I_leakage across a 120-second pause window at sampling rate of 10 samples/sec. 4. Step chuck temperature through 55°C, 70°C, 85°C, and 105°C, repeating the dwell and measurement sequence. 5. Plot ln(I_leakage) vs 1/kT to extract junction activation energy Ea and isolate trap-assisted generation from diffusion components. | `Leakage current I_leakage at V_drain = 1.8V and T = 85.0°C must remain <= 1.00 fA. Extracted activation energy Ea must be >= 0.65 eV (confirming absence of severe metallic mid-gap contamination).` |
| `TC-DRAM-CELL-LAYOUT-3-2-3-02` | **Subarray 64ms Retention Window Pulse-Pause Metrology Verification** | Agilent/Keysight 81110A Pulse Pattern Generator coupled to a custom discrete low-noise transimpedance front-end and digital storage oscilloscope (Tektronix MSO54). | 1. Systematically sweep t_pause from 10 ms to 256 ms in 2 ms increments to construct the retention cumulative distribution function (CDF) curve. | `Sensing differential voltage ΔV_BL at t_pause = 64.0 ms must be >= 120 mV for >= 99.9% of tested bits within the array. Array failure rate at 64 ms must equal 0.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom rated nitrile gloves (double-gloved, EN 374 compliant), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety spectacles with side shields, Static-dissipative anti-static ESD cleanroom coat and footwear, Thermal-insulating handling gloves rated to 150°C for thermal chuck wafer exchanges
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For TMAH contact: Immediately wash affected area with copious amounts of flowing water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated clothing. TMAH is a systemic neurotoxin; seek emergency medical attention immediately and administer oxygen if breathing is labored. For thermal burn from chuck: Immerse in clean cold water for 15 minutes; do not apply topical ointments before medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Temptronic thermal chuck and wafer probe station enclosure must be exhausted via dedicated local chemical/thermal exhaust duct pulling >= 150 CFM. Chemical preparation and spin-coating hoods must maintain face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s) with continuous laminar air flow.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous TMAH developer waste must be segregated into alkaline hazardous waste containers; do not mix with chlorinated or acidic solvents. Organic solvent rinses (IPA, PGMEA) must be deposited in dedicated closed solvent safety waste cans with flame arrestors.

| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (MOS) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed forming gas anneal (N2/H2 95%/5% at 400°C for 30 minutes); passivation unpassivated contact pads chemically clean, free of organic residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Dry probe marks inspectable under optical microscope; probe scrub depth < 100 nm, no native oxide pitting or moisture condensation on aluminum/copper contact pads.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time in ambient air causes native oxide regrow (Al2O3/CuOx) and atmospheric moisture adsorption on exposed contact pads, increasing contact resistance by > 200 ohms and introducing mobile ion surface leakage that distorts low-fA junction measurements.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full metrology signoff validating that 180nm 1T1C DRAM cells exhibit off-state leakage <= 1.0 fA/cell at 85°C, yielding full retention of stored logic states over the standard 64ms refresh window with signal margin exceeding 120 mV at the sense amplifier input.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `retention_cdf_temperature_profile_85C.csv`
- [ ] `arrhenius_leakage_mechanisms_report.pdf`
- [ ] `test_structure_triaxial_probing_wafermap.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Minimum retention time for 99.9% of tested 1T1C storage cells at 85°C** | `64.0 ms` | >= 64.0 ms (minimum allowable threshold) | Pulse-pause-sense sequence sweeping t_pause from 10ms to 128ms with oscilloscope ΔV_BL readout |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Bitline signal charge-sharing differential voltage (ΔV_BL) at 64ms pause interval** | `140 mV` | ±20 mV | High-bandwidth active differential probe measurement across bitline pair during Wordline enable |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal metrology approval requires 100% of tested dice on two sequential qualification wafers to demonstrate zero fail bits at t_pause = 64ms under 85°C chuck condition, with mean single-cell leakage <= 1.0 fA and no evidence of mobile ion drift across a 4-hour re-test burn-in.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-SER-180NM`
**Title:** Alpha-Particle & Cosmic Neutron Single-Event Soft-Error Rate (SER) Metrology Modeling  
**Module:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Cell Parasitic Extraction, Retention Leakage & Soft-Error Metrology Simulation > Alpha-Particle & Cosmic Neutron Single-Event Soft-Error Rate (SER) Metrology Modeling  
**Action Type:** Buy / In-House Metrology Protocol Qualification  

---

### 1. Metrology Modeling Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Unit Cell Geometry   │
│          Mesh          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Critical Charge     │
│   Q_crit Extraction    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Alpha and Neutron    │
│   Monte Carlo Track    │
│       Deposition       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Transient Simulation  │
│        and SER         │
│     Quantification     │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Cell Mesh & Parasitic Boundary Construction:**
   - Instantiate the 180nm unit cell with Folded Bitline layout footprint of $8F^2 = 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ (feature size $F = 180\ \text{nm}$, bitline/wordline pitch $360\ \text{nm}$ to $400\ \text{nm}$).
   - Set access NMOS transistor dimensions: channel length $L = 180\ \text{nm}$, width $W = 220\ \text{nm}$, gate oxide physical thickness $t_{ox} = 3.5\ \text{nm}$ ($\text{SiO}_2$).
   - Place stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) with crown/cylinder topology using W-plug drain contact and high-$k$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$, such as ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ with $\text{EOT} = 3.0\ \text{nm} - 4.0\ \text{nm}$).
   - Fix target storage node capacitance $C_s \ge 28\ \text{fF}$ (permissible cell budget: $25\ \text{fF} - 30\ \text{fF}$) and bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\ \text{fF} - 250\ \text{fF}$ across a 256/512-cell array block. Verify ratio $C_b / C_s$ is within $5:1$ to $9:1$ ($< 10:1$).

2. **Critical Charge ($Q_{crit}$) Derivation:**
   - Calculate storage node nominal signal charge:
     $$Q_{stored} = C_s \times V_{cell}$$
   - Extract critical flip charge $Q_{crit}$ required to collapse bitline sensing margin below sensing threshold under $85^\circ\text{C}$ operation:
     $$Q_{crit} = C_s \times \Delta V_{margin}$$
     *(For $C_s = 28\ \text{fF}$ and dynamic read delta, nominal $Q_{crit} \approx 25.2\ \text{fC}$)*.

3. **Single-Event Energy Deposition & Monte Carlo Track Injection:**
   - **Alpha-Particle Modeling:** Inject $\alpha$-particle tracks ($2.0\ \text{MeV} - 8.8\ \text{MeV}$ energy spectrum from packaging mold compound / trace uranium/thorium decay) traversing the silicon substrate and access transistor junction. Set track radius to $0.1\ \mu\text{m}$ with Bragg peak ionization profiles.
   - **Cosmic Neutron Modeling:** Simulate atmospheric neutron strikes ($1\ \text{MeV} - 1\ \text{GeV}$) triggering recoil nuclear fragments ($^{28}\text{Si}(n, \alpha)$, $^{28}\text{Si}(n, p)$) directly into the storage node diffusion region.
   - Track transient carrier generation pairs:
     $$G(r, t) = \frac{\text{LET}(x)}{E_{eh}} \cdot f(r) \cdot g(t)$$
     where electron-hole pair creation energy $E_{eh} = 3.6\ \text{eV}$ in silicon.

4. **Transient Device Transport & Charge Collection:**
   - Perform 3D mixed-mode TCAD/SPICE transient simulation of electron funneling and drift-diffusion charge collection at the storage node and bitline contact plug over $t = 0\ \text{ps}$ to $5\ \text{ns}$.
   - Sum collected charge $Q_{coll} = \int I(t)\, dt$. Flag a Single-Event Upset (SEU) event whenever $Q_{coll} \ge Q_{crit}$.
   - Integrate baseline junction + sub-threshold leakage current boundary ($I_{leak} \le 1.0\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) to guarantee worst-case SER margin prior to standard $64\ \text{ms}$ refresh cycles.

5. **Soft-Error Rate (SER) Quantification:**
   - Compute total FIT rate ($\text{FIT} = 1\ \text{failure} / 10^9\ \text{device-hours}$):
     $$\text{SER}_{total} = \text{SER}_{\alpha} + \text{SER}_{neutron}$$
   - Report soft-error cross-section ($\sigma_{SEU}$) across cell array blocks.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria

```text
                     DRAM SER Cell Integrity Parameters 
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Target Retention (ms)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets:**
  - Folded bitline $8F^2$ cell footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\ \text{nm}$).
  - Storage node capacitance budget $C_s \ge 25\ \text{fF} - 30\ \text{fF}$ (nominal $28\ \text{fF}$).
  - Array bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\ \text{fF} - 250\ \text{fF}$ (256/512 cells/BL) with ratio $C_b / C_s$ kept between $5:1$ and $9:1$ ($< 10:1$).
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - Unit cell dimensions: $L = 180\ \text{nm}$, $W = 220\ \text{nm}$, shared bitline contact.
  - Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) crown/MIM topology with W-plug drain contact.
  - Dielectric: ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ stack ($\kappa > 15$).
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage target $\le 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Data retention baseline requirement $> 64\ \text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) $= 3.0\ \text{nm} - 4.0\ \text{nm}$ using $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$.
  - Bitline and wordline pitch $= 360\ \text{nm} - 400\ \text{nm}$; gate dielectric physical thickness $= 3.5\ \text{nm}$ thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ ($850^\circ\text{C} - 900^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: At 180nm lithography (Gen 2 design rules with an 8F² planar cell layout, where F=0.18µm and cell area ≈ 0.259 µm²), the storage node capacitance (Cs) ranges from 25 fF to 32 fF, storing a critical charge Qcrit = Cs * (Vdd/2) ≈ 22.5 fC to 28.8 fC at Vdd = 1.8V. Alpha particles emitted by radioactive decay of trace U-238/Th-232 impurities in packaging mould compound and lead-free solder bumps deposit ~16 fC/µm over a 25-30 µm Bragg peak track in bulk silicon. Without retrograded deep triple-well (DNWELL) potential barriers or heavily doped buried layers, the collection depth is set by electron diffusion length (~50-100 µm), causing charge funneling that readily exceeds Qcrit and triggers multi-cell upsets (MCU). TCAD Monte Carlo radiation transport must directly interface with SPICE bitline sensing margins rather than relying on decoupled 1D analytical approximations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Neutron-induced spallation reactions on Si-28 (such as 28Si(n,α)25Mg and 28Si(n,p)28Al) generate high-LET secondary recoils up to 30 MeV with short ranges (<5 µm) that deposit >50 fC right inside the depletion region of the storage capacitor contact junction. Furthermore, Gen 2 open-source planar/stacked cell flow using standard garage-scale or lab-scale back-end metallization is exposed to alpha emission from solder/interconnect materials unless ultra-low alpha (ULA) lead/tin (<0.002 cph/cm²) or high-purity electroplated Cu is specified. The radiation metrology model must separate thermal neutron capture from terrestrial high-energy cosmic neutrons (>10 MeV, ~14 n/cm²·h flux at sea level) using GEANT4 or TI-G4 simulations calibrated against 241Am radiation exposure bench setups.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Commercial low-activity alpha check sources (e.g., Americium-241 electroplated foil, 0.1 µCi to 1.0 µCi) for benchtop SER characterization are strictly regulated under national radiation protection agency licenses, requiring wipe-test certification and controlled storage safes. Sourcing ultra-low alpha (<0.001 alpha/cm²/hr) polyimide passivation coats (e.g., HD MicroSystems HD-4100 series) or low-alpha epoxy molding compounds (Sumitomo EME-G770 series) has high minimum order quantities (MOQ > 50 kg) and 16-24 week lead times, requiring the team to qualify non-purified packaging lines by adding thick (>35 µm) garage-spin-coated silicone/SU-8 buffer layers to absorb packaging alpha flux.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: SER metrology modeling must not block physical cell layout tape-out for Gen 2 (8F² planar/trench capacitor integration). A rapid 3-week milestone cycle requires running high-energy heavy-ion and alpha particle track physics in open-source TCAD/G4beamline first, validating the critical charge (Qcrit) against 180nm BSIM3/4 SPICE corner extractions, and freezing the storage node contact layout geometry before committing to expensive masked wafer runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Charge Funneling Field Collapse: An incident 5.48 MeV alpha track penetrating the n+/p-well storage junction creates a transient high-density plasma column (1e19 cm⁻³) that locally collapses the p-well depletion field, funneling >35 fC into the storage node within 200 ps and causing an unrecoverable bit-flip.
1. Multi-Cell Cluster Upsets (MCU) via Parasitic Bitline Charge Injection: High-energy cosmic neutron spallation recoils near the sense-amplifier pitch or open bitline pair induce balanced voltage collapse on complementary bitlines during active sensing strobe (t_RCD), flipping multiple adjacent data words.
1. Dielectric Latent Displacement Damage: Alpha bombardment of thin Gen 2 storage capacitor high-k or nitrided oxide (EOT < 4.5 nm) introduces trapped interface states (Dit) and oxide neutral traps, accelerating trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) and degrading cell retention time below the 64 ms refresh specification.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level C radiation safety PPE: Disposable Tyvek lab coat with elastic wrists, Double-layer nitrile examination gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, ASTM D6319), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses with side shields, Personal thermoluminescent dosimeter (TLD) badge worn at chest level, Calibrated Geiger-Müller alpha/beta pancake survey probe (Ludlum Model 3 with 44-9 probe) active at workstation
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Radioactive Material Contact/Ingestion: In case of physical contact with suspected leaking check source, immediately strip outer PPE into radioactive waste bag. Wash contaminated skin with lukewarm water and mild non-abrasive soap for at least 15 minutes; do not abrade skin. For inhalation or internal contamination of Am-241, immediate administration of Calcium or Zinc Trisodium Diethylenetriaminepentaacetate (Ca-DTPA / Zn-DTPA) chelating therapy under licensed emergency physician supervision. For solvent splash (IPA/Acetone): Flush eyes with copious isotonic eyewash for 15 minutes; move victim to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Laboratory fume hood certified to ANSI/AIHA Z9.5 with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s), equipped with certified HEPA filtration unit (99.97% retention at 0.3 µm) dedicated to radioactive sample handling and solvent vapor extraction.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All radioactive contaminated wipes, swabs, and disposable gloves must be segregated into designated Class 7 radioactive low-level waste (LLW) solid containment drums with lead-lined shielding and logged under radiation safety officer (RSO) chain-of-custody. Solvent wastes (IPA, Acetone) must be collected separately in grounded, flame-arrested stainless steel waste carboys; do not mix radioactive materials with flammable organic solvent streams.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly patterned and etched 180nm storage capacitor dielectric stack (TiN/ZrO2/Al2O3/TiN or native thermal oxynitride) with surface cleaned via SC-1/SC-2, free of organic particulate (>0.2 µm defect density < 0.1/cm²) and moisture-passivated.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cured polyimide / SU-8 alpha-buffer passivation layer (thickness ≥ 30 µm ± 1.5 µm), cross-linked at 350°C in N2 ambient, moisture-sealed with hydrophobic static contact angle > 75°.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time induces atmospheric moisture and organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption onto the capacitor dielectric, causing severe interface trap generation (Dit increase > 5e11 cm⁻²·eV⁻¹), increasing subthreshold junction leakage, reducing cell storage retention margin below 32 ms, and lowering the effective Qcrit by >25%.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Monte Carlo Radiation Transport & Charge Deposition Modeling (Geant4 / TIARA)

**Context Path:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)` > `Architecture & Integration` > `1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²)` > `Cell Parasitic Extraction, Retention Leakage & Soft-Error Metrology Simulation` > `Alpha-Particle & Cosmic Neutron Single-Event Soft-Error Rate (SER) Metrology Modeling` > `Monte Carlo Radiation Transport & Charge Deposition Modeling (Geant4/TIARA)`

**Action Type:** Make

│                       │
│  Charge Funneling &   │
│    Drift-Diffusion    │
│      Collection       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Critical Charge Qc   │
│  vs Collected Charge  │
│   Qcoll Assessment    │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Cell Mesh Construction & Material Definition (Geant4 / TIARA):**
   - Import the 3D unit cell structure corresponding to the 180 nm 8F² folded-bitline stacked capacitor layout.
   - Set the access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Define wordline and bitline pitches within $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Assign dielectric material regions: gate dielectric of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ ($3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness), crown-shaped/cylinder stacked capacitor dielectric with EOT of $3\text{ nm}$ to $4\text{ nm}$ (dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$ using ONO, $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$, or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5/\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$), and tungsten plugs (W-plugs) contacting the drain.
   - Configure active silicon substrate and p-well dopant profiles with mesh boundaries matching adjacent shared bitline contact architectures.

2. **Radiation Source Definition & Event Sampling:**
   - Define isotopic emitter distributions: 
     - **Alpha-particle source:** Emitted from trace radioactive contaminants (e.g., U/Th decay chains in mold compounds and interconnect packaging metallization), isotropic emission, kinetic energy spectrum up to $5\text{ MeV} - 8.78\text{ MeV}$.
     - **Terrestrial cosmic neutrons:** High-energy spallation neutrons (JEDEC/IEC standard spectrum) generating secondary recoil ions ($\text{Si}, \text{Al}, \text{O}$ recoils) via elastic/inelastic nuclear collisions inside the cell lattice.
   - Initialize Monte Carlo transport runs ($N \ge 10^6$ particle histories) using standard low-energy electromagnetic and nuclear hadronic physics lists (e.g., `G4EmStandardPhysics_option4` / TIARA intra-nuclear cascade model).

3. **Energy Deposition & Linear Energy Transfer (LET) Computation:**
   - Track particle trajectory step-by-step through back-end-of-line (BEOL) metal/dielectric layers and active silicon.
   - Calculate energy loss along the ionizing track:
     $$\Delta E = \int \left(\frac{dE}{dx}\right) dx$$
   - Convert spatial energy loss into electron-hole ($e$-$h$) pair distributions using the mean ionization energy of silicon ($W_{\text{eff}} \approx 3.6\text{ eV}$ per pair):
     $$N_{e\text{-}h} = \frac{\Delta E}{3.6\text{ eV}}$$

4. **Charge Transport & Collection Modeling at Storage Nodes:**
   - Couple the localized generated spatial charge cloud to drift-diffusion and funneling transport models around the n+/p-well drain junction of the storage node.
   - Compute transient collected charge $Q_{\text{coll}}(t) = \int I_{\text{coll}}(t) dt$ over the sensitive collection volume of the storage node contact and W-plug.

5. **Critical Charge ($Q_c$) Extraction & Soft-Error Determination:**
   - Extract critical charge $Q_c$ based on the cell storage capacitance $C_s$ budget and sensing margin:
     $$Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{BL}})$$
     $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right)$$
   - Evaluate cell bit-flip criterion: flag a Single-Event Upset (SEU) event whenever $Q_{\text{coll}} \ge Q_c$.
   - Integrate flip counts across total simulated fluence to calculate Soft-Error Rate (SER) in Failures-In-Time ($\text{FIT} = 1\text{ failure} / 10^9\text{ device hours}$).

---

   - Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) crown-shaped/MIM structure with W-plug.

   - Gate oxide physical thickness of $3.5\text{ nm}$ grown via dry oxidation at $850^\circ\text{C}-900^\circ\text{C}$.

   - Readout signal development $\Delta V \approx 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ for nominal $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Geant4 Monte Carlo physics lists must couple intra-cell secondary electron transport down to 100 eV with Sentaurus/TCAD drift-diffusion solvers across the 180nm planar 8F² (0.288 µm²) cell active area. Neglecting 3D dielectric stack backscattering from upper Al metal interconnects (M1-M3) and passivation overburdens will underestimate LET-dependent soft-error rate (SER) by over 28%.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: 5.0-8.8 MeV alpha tracks emitted from trace uranium/thorium decay in bond wire and mold compound pass through the storage node junction at acute strike angles (theta > 60°), generating funneled charge collection exceeding the cell critical charge (Qcrit ~ 18 fC for 30 fF cell cap at 1.8V VDD). Modeling must resolve Bragg peak charge deposition directly in the p-well/n+ junction depletion boundary.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Alpha emission metrology calibration requires NIST-traceable calibrated Americium-241 (Am-241) and Polonium-210 (Po-210) planar open reference sources and high-purity lead/tungsten collimator shielding, subject to strict EURATOM/IAEA nuclear non-proliferation and radiometric transfer licensing that carries a 16-24 week import lead time.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Computational overhead of high-statistics Geant4/TIARA event generation (10^8 incident particles) presents a schedule choke point. The physics tracking mesh must implement boundary-limited biasing and stratified importance sampling across the bitline-contact/storage-node diffusion node to meet compute-cluster SLA milestones within 72 hours per layout revision.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Funneling-assisted multi-cell upset (MCU) where dense ionizing plasma track spans adjacent 8F² storage node diffusions, corrupting 2 or more contiguous bits in the same wordline cycle
1. Bragg peak ionization capture within passivated bitline contact via diffusion node, inducing false sense amplifier differential latching during active sensing window
1. Underestimation of secondary spallation recoil fragments (Mg, Al, Si recoils) from high-energy cosmic neutrons (>10 MeV) impacting inter-layer dielectric (ILD-1 SiO2)

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Lead-lined apron (0.5 mm lead equivalence), Safety goggles with side shields (ANSI Z87.1 approved), Nitrile double-gloving (minimum 6 mil thickness per glove), Thermo Fisher EPD TruDose electronic personal dosimeter (Beta/Gamma/Alpha tracking), Static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For radioactive source handling: In case of suspected alpha contamination or skin puncture, immediately flush wound under running deionized water for a minimum of 15 minutes without scrubbing to prevent transdermal radionuclide uptake. Notify Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) immediately. For internal alpha emitter inhalation/ingestion, prepare for DTPA (diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid) chelation therapy protocol administered by certified medical radiological emergency team. For IPA contact, rinse exposed skin with water; flush eyes for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Certified ISO Class 5 laminar flow radiological fume hood with minimum 100 FPM face velocity, equipped with inline ultra-low penetration air (ULPA) and HEPA exhaust filtration vented directly to dedicated radionuclide exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All contaminated wipes, swabs, and disposable PPE must be surveyed with an alpha-scintillation detector (ZnS:Ag probe), sealed in yellow rad-waste polyethylene drums (4 mil thick), logged in the Nuclear Regulatory Registry, and transferred to a licensed Class A low-level radioactive waste disposal contractor.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
