# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): SPICE Timing Critical-Path Metrology & Post-Layout Parasitic Delay Verification

**Discipline / Category**: Metrology  
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using Optical Inspection / Profilometer.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-layout parasitic extraction (PEX) for the hierarchical row/column predecoder tree must include 3D distributed interconnect parasitics (RC extraction using standard Calibre xRC or Magic/Netgen flow adapted for 180nm) across Metal 1 through Metal 3 routing channels. Omitting inter-wire fringing capacitance and VPP pump supply rail inductive/resistive drops across the decoder array will yield over-optimistic critical-path propagation delays, risking wordline access latency budget blowouts beyond the DRAM specification (t_RCD/t_RP).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Wordline driver stages in a 180nm DRAM node face extreme dV/dt slew rates when switching to boosted wordline voltage (VPP ~ 2.8V-3.3V against 1.8V core VDD). The SPICE timing metrology must explicitly account for Miller capacitance (C_gd) amplification, substrate noise coupling into adjacent inactive row select lines, and hot-carrier degradation/gate dielectric stress under VPP overdrive, verifying that intermediate predecoder NAND/NOR stages do not trigger false activate pulses during address bit transitions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Model characterization relies on open-source SkyWater 180nm (SKY130) or equivalent legacy foundry PDK devices. Accurate corner extraction (TT, FF, SS, FS, SF at -40°C to +125°C) requires verified SPICE BSIM4 model cards with complete binning parameters. Sourcing calibrated micro-probing tips (DC to 5 GHz bandwidth) and high-speed mixed-signal oscilloscope channels for physical validation of test-bench silicon requires securing precision beryllium-copper RF probe cards well in advance.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Simulation coverage must close before tape-out signoff without stalling the physical verification schedule. Parasitic-extracted netlists must be partitioned into modular hierarchical trees (predecoder stage 1, predecoder stage 2, and wordline driver buffer) to avoid intractable transient runtimes in open-source SPICE engines (e.g., ngspice or Xyce), with automated pass/fail verification pipelines tied directly to Git commit hashes.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dynamic address race conditions leading to simultaneous multiple-wordline activation (multi-WL selection) and irreversible destructive memory cell read/write corruption.
1. Underestimated Metal-2/Metal-3 RC delay on distributed predecoder select buses exceeding the allocated 3.5 ns address-setup window, causing timing violations under worst-case slow-slow (SS, 1.62V VDD, 125°C) conditions.
1. VPP boost rail collapse due to unmodeled parasitic line resistance and peak switching surge currents (dI/dt) during simultaneous predecoder tree transition, starving driver pull-up PMOS/NMOS devices.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ROW-COLUMN-DECODER-2-1-3-01` | **Post-Layout Extracted Critical Path Propagation Delay & Slew Metrology** | Synopsys PrimeSim / ngspice 42+ parallel transient solver, Keysight Infiniium UXR 33 GHz Oscilloscope with |Z| probe station (for post-fab correlation) | 1. Instantiate extracted netlist with 50 fF lumped equivalent gate load per wordline driver branch. 2. Initialize address bus inputs to 0x00 and toggle address MSB to 0xFF with 100 ps input slew rate. 3. Execute transient simulation from 0.0 ns to 20.0 ns using 1 ps maximum integration timestep. 4. Measure t_pd (50% input address transition to 50% wordline driver output activation) and 10%-90% rise/fall slew times. | `Total critical-path propagation delay t_pd <= 3.20 ns under SS corner (1.62V, 125°C); wordline output 10%-90% rise time t_r <= 850 ps; signal overshoot/undershoot on unselected adjacent lines <= 150 mV.` |
| `TC-ROW-COLUMN-DECODER-2-1-3-02` | **VPP Rail Dynamic IR-Drop and Multi-Line Glitch Metrology** | SPICE transient solver with distributed RLC supply grid model, differential high-bandwidth active probe station | 1. Apply multi-cycle address switching sequence cycling through alternating row addresses at 100 MHz operating frequency. 2. Monitor dynamic voltage droop on the local VPP driver rail at the furthest physical driver node. 3. Evaluate peak glitch amplitude on unselected wordlines (WL_unsel) across all 255 unselected lines during transition edges. | `Peak instantaneous dynamic VPP voltage drop Delta_VPP <= 180 mV; maximum transient glitch voltage on any unselected wordline <= 250 mV (must remain strictly below pass-gate NMOS threshold V_th = 450 mV).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/ISO 5 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat, ESD-grounded heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with solvent splashes, flush immediately at eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For inhalation exposure to solvent vapors, move individual to fresh laminar flow air. For skin contact, remove contaminated apparel and wash thoroughly with non-ionic cleanroom soap and deionized water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Local chemical exhaust hood with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); continuous airflow monitoring with interlocked audio-visual alarm; probing cleanroom ambient ventilation at 45 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solvent wipes and washings in dedicated, grounded, flame-proof stainless steel hazardous waste carboys; seal and label as Non-Halogenated Flammable Organic Waste for professional treatment via high-temperature incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Acetone** | `67-64-1` | Electronic Grade MOS | `99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-passivation silicon test die with exposed Al/Cu probe pads; surface deoxidized and free of organic residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and validated wafer/die dried via ultra-high purity N2 blowoff, vacuum packaged in antistatic moisture-barrier bags.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide formation and moisture condensation on aluminum/copper probe pads causing high contact resistance (> 10 Ohm per pad), spurious electrical opens, and probe skate damage during critical-path RF characterization.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full electrical signoff of hierarchical row/column address predecoder and wordline driver critical path via post-layout parasitic extraction and SPICE transient timing metrology, guaranteeing robust access timing and noise immunity across all PVT corners.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `decoder_timing_critical_path_pex.csv`
- [ ] `decoder_pex_timing_metrology_report.pdf`
- [ ] `dynamic_vpp_droop_waveform.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum address-to-wordline propagation delay under worst-case slow corner (SS, 1.62V VDD, 125°C)** | `3.20 ns` | +/- 0.15 ns | Post-layout DSPF transient SPICE simulation with 50 fF load |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Unselected wordline maximum transient coupling glitch voltage** | `200 mV` | <= 250 mV upper bound | Transient node voltage extraction during 100 MHz full-bus address switching |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Peak dynamic VPP supply mesh droop across decoder tree during concurrent activation** | `150 mV` | <= 180 mV upper bound | Dynamic RLC rail extraction and transient current surge analysis |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All predecoder stage logic paths and wordline drivers demonstrate zero DRC/LVS mismatches, worst-case propagation delay <= 3.35 ns across all 5 PVT corners (-40°C to +125°C), maximum unselected wordline glitch strictly below 250 mV, and formal signoff approved by the Lead DRAM Metrology & Integration Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Voltage $V_{PP}$ Wordline Driver Transistor Sizing & Taper Optimization

- **Scope / Module:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — Gen 2 (µm)
- **Classification:** Address Decoders & Wordline $V_{PP}$ Voltage Pump / Circuit Design
- **Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Architectural Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Address Predecoder /  │
│     Level Shifter      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │ (0V to 1.8V -> 0V to V_PP)
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Intermediate Taper   │
│         Buffer         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │ (Optimized Fanout Taper Factor e ~ 3-4)
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Final High-Voltage   │
│       VPP Driver       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │ (V_PP = 2.5V - 2.8V Drive)
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wordline Array Load   │
│    L=180nm, W=220nm    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Array Wordline Capacitive & Resistive Load Extraction**:
   - Model the target distributed wordline line load based on unit cell access transistor geometry: gate length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and gate width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ with gate oxide $t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$ ($EOT \approx 3\text{ nm to } 4\text{ nm}$).
   - Calculate total parasitic gate-to-channel capacitance across the wordline pitch ($360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$) accounting for cell storage capacitance $C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\text{ fF}$ (25 fF to 30 fF range) to establish the total lumped/distributed array line capacitance $C_{WL\_total}$.

2. **Supply & Overdrive Voltage Boundary Establishment**:
   - Couple the final driver rail to the regulated on-chip Dickson charge pump delivery network.
   - Set driver high rail $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\text{ V to } 2.8\text{ V}$ (nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$, NMOS access gate $V_{th} \approx 0.5\text{ V to } 0.7\text{ V}$, eliminating the $33\%$ threshold voltage loss to ensure a full $1.8\text{ V}$ level is stored onto the cell capacitor).

3. **Level Shifter Stage Integration**:
   - Insert cross-coupled high-voltage level shifters between the standard core logic predecoder ($1.8\text{ V}$ logic swing) and the wordline driver buffer stages to transition the swing to $0\text{ V} \leftrightarrow V_{PP}$ without gate oxide breakdown.

4. **Multi-Stage Inverter Taper Optimization**:
   - Determine the required tapering factor $u$ ($u \approx 3\text{ to } 4$) across $N$ stages:
     $$N = \ln\left(\frac{C_{WL\_total}}{C_{in}}\right)$$
   - Size stage-by-stage PMOS and NMOS high-voltage thick-oxide devices proportionally. Ensure pull-up PMOS width to pull-down NMOS width ratio accounts for hole-to-electron mobility difference ($\approx 2:1$ to $2.5:1$).

5. **Physical Layout Pitch-Matching & Verification**:
   - Pitch-match the final driver output fingers to the physical DRAM wordline array pitch ($360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$).
   - Perform transient spice simulations under worst-case corner ($85^\circ\text{C}$) to guarantee wordline rise/fall slew times while maintaining junction and sub-threshold leakage targets $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                    Target Acceptance Criteria Metrics  
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░                                │
   Max T_rise (ns)┤░░░░                                │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                    │
   Min C_cell (fF)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                    │
Min Retention (ms)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                  │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
   V_PP Supply (V)┤███                                 │
                  │███                                 │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0       16       32      48       64 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$V_{PP}$ Wordline Boosted Level** | $\ge 2.5\text{ to } 2.8$ | $\text{V}$ | Regulated output under active wordline switching |
| **Storage Node Stored Voltage ($V_{SN}$)** | $1.8$ (full $V_{DD}$, no $V_{th}$ loss) | $\text{V}$ | Write '1' into cell node with $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{--}0.7\text{ V}$ |
| **Cell Retention Time** | $> 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | Measured at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$, $I_{leak} < 1\text{ fA/cell}$ |
| **Unit Cell Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | $\ge 28$ ($25\text{ to } 30$) | $\text{fF}$ | Stacked capacitor at $3\text{--}4\text{ nm}$ EOT |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump ($V_{PP}$) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:
  - $V_{th} \sim 0.5\text{ V to } 0.7\text{ V}$; $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$; threshold loss mitigation via $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\text{ V to } 2.8\text{ V}$.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Unit cell access transistor dimensions $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; minimum storage capacitance budget $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$; leakage current $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Wordline and bitline pitch $\approx 360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$; physical gate oxide $t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$ (dry oxidation at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$); EOT $\approx 3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$; minimum data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Driving distributed wordline capacitance (~1.8 pF over 512 cells per sub-array plus routing) requires a multi-stage inverter taper from the core logic level (1.8V VDD) up to the boosted VPP domain (2.8V). A suboptimal taper factor (exceeding e ~ 2.7 to 3.0) will cause excessive propagation delay exceeding the row cycle budget (t_RCD penalty > 2.5 ns). Furthermore, dynamic current spikes from simultaneous firing of multiple WL drivers can collapse the unbuffered VPP rail without localized decoupling capacitance.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Standard 180nm thin-oxide transistors have a gate dielectric breakdown (TDDB) limit around 2.0V to 2.2V. Operating at VPP = 2.8V mandates thick-oxide dual-gate I/O MOSFETs (tox ~ 6.5 nm to 7.0 nm) for both the high-voltage level shifter and driver pull-up/pull-down stages to eliminate Fowler-Nordheim stress and hot-carrier injection (HCI). Proper channel length rounding (L >= 0.35 µm to 0.40 µm) is required to suppress drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) under 2.8V drain-to-source bias.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-gate thick-oxide process options in open-source/pure-play 180nm foundry PDKs (such as SCL 180nm or open PDK variants) require an additional dual-gate lithography and oxide wet etch/regrowth mask layer. Sizing excessively wide PMOS pull-up transistors expands the pitch-matched wordline driver pitch beyond the DRAM sub-array cell height, forcing multi-level layout folding and driving die area overhead up by ~12%.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Wordline driver layout pitch is tightly bounded by the cell pitch (unit cell width ~ 0.44 µm across paired cells, matching metal pitch). Layout engineers must ensure that layout parasitic capacitance (C_gdo, C_gso, perimeter junction capacitance) is accurately extracted in post-layout netlists. Taper optimization must be finalized prior to tape-out milestone M3 to prevent redesign of the primary row predecoder routing channel.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) or catastrophic gate oxide rupture on final-stage PMOS/NMOS pull-up devices under sustained VPP = 2.8V stress when standard thin-oxide core devices are accidentally inserted.
1. Crowbar cross-conduction current during level-shifting from VDD (1.8V) to VPP (2.8V), starving the Dickson charge pump and dropping VPP below 2.4V, causing unwritten high levels into the 28 fF storage cell node.
1. Driver slew-rate degradation (t_rise > 4.5 ns) induced by excessive layout parasitic drain junction capacitance and uncompensated interconnect RC delay across the poly/metal wordline strap.

Apply active row address decode vector with step input t_rise = 100 ps at node PREDEC_OUT. 2. Measure propagation delay from 50% PREDEC_OUT to 50% WL_OUT at the far end of the wordline stripe. 3. Measure 10%-to-90% rise time (t_r) and 90%-to-10% fall time (t_f) at near and far nodes. 4. Integrate dynamic supply current drawn from VPP rail during the 10 ns switching window to compute total charge transfer Q_switch. 5. Repeat transient analysis across Monte Carlo 500-run statistical mismatch and process variations. | `Wordline far-end t_rise <= 2.20 ns; wordline far-end t_fall <= 1.80 ns; maximum instantaneous VPP drop <= 120 mV; net charge per access Q_switch <= 6.8 pC; steady-state crowbar leakage I_leak < 100 nA at 85°C.` |

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Wordline RC Load Extraction and Breakdown-Reliability Transistor Sizing

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Scope
This SOP defines the circuit-design and parasitic-extraction flow for calculating distributed wordline (WL) RC transmission line parameters and sizing the boosted high-voltage wordline driver ($V_{PP}$) in 180nm open-source DRAM architectures.

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Extract Unit Cell WL  │
│        C and R         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Assemble Distributed  │
│       RC Ladder        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Size VPP Driver     │
│      Transistors       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Transient Rise Time   │
│        Sign-Off        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Extract Unit Cell Geometric Capacitance & Parasitic Overlap:**
   - Parameterize the access transistor gate with channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and active width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ across the wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Compute gate capacitance components:
     $$C_{\text{ox}} = \frac{\epsilon_{\text{ox}}}{t_{\text{ox}}}$$
     where gate dielectric is dry thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ with physical thickness $t_{\text{ox}} = 3.5\text{ nm}$ (EOT $\approx 3.5\text{ nm}$).
   - Include cell-level coupling capacitances to adjacent bitline lines (pitch $360\text{ nm}\text{--}400\text{ nm}$) and tungsten contact plug (W-plug) vertical sidewalls.

2. **Assemble Wordline Distributed RC Ladder:**
   - For an array block of $N$ access transistors per wordline, compute total wordline capacitance $C_{\text{WL\_total}} = \sum (C_{\text{gate}} + C_{\text{fringe}} + C_{\text{interconnect}})$.
   - Extract polycide/refractory metal wordline sheet resistance $R_{\square}$ and interconnect line length per unit cell ($360\text{ nm}\text{--}400\text{ nm}$).
   - Model the wordline as a multi-stage distributed $\Pi$ or T-ladder network. Calculate the far-end Elmore delay:
     $$\tau_{\text{Elmore}} = R_{\text{driver}} C_{\text{WL\_total}} + \sum_{k=1}^N R_k \left(\sum_{j=k}^N C_j\right)$$

3. **Breakdown-Reliability Transistor Sizing ($V_{PP}$ Driver):**
   - Size the final stage $V_{PP}$ pull-up PMOS and pull-down NMOS drivers against gate-oxide breakdown limits. Because the wordline carries boosted $V_{PP}$ to fully transfer high levels into the cell capacitor ($25\text{ fF}\text{--}30\text{ fF}$ minimum budget), the gate oxide electric field under $V_{PP}$ stress must not exceed time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) limits for $3.5\text{ nm}$ oxide thickness ($E_{\text{ox}} = V_{PP} / t_{\text{ox}}$).
   - Increase driver transistor channel length $L > 180\text{ nm}$ or implement a thick-oxide cascode topology if $V_{PP} / t_{\text{ox}}$ exceeds peak reliability limits.
   - Adjust channel width $W_{\text{driver}}$ to match driving impedance $R_{\text{driver}}$ such that total wordline rise time to 90% $V_{PP}$ meets the subarray row cycle target.

4. **SPICE Extraction & Dynamic Transient Sign-Off:**
   - Simulate corner cases (Fast-Fast, Typical-Typical, Slow-Slow) at elevated junction temperature $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Verify that far-end wordline activation does not inject noise exceeding the margin on unselected bitlines, and confirm bitline differential sensing window ($\Delta V \approx 100\text{ mV}\text{--}150\text{ mV}$ developed from access to $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$) is preserved.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
Baseline 180nm Reliability Parameters
                         ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                         │█████████████████████████████│
   Retention Temp (deg C)┤█████████████████████████████│
                         │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                   │
      Min Cap Budget (fF)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                   │
Dielectric Thickness (nm)┤▒▒                           │
                         │▒▒                           │
                 EOT (nm)┤░░                           │
                         │░░                           │
                         └┬──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                         0.0   21.2   42.5   63.8  85.0 
```

| Metric ID | Parameter | Target / Tolerance Value | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-WL-01** | Access Transistor Dimensions | $L = 180 \pm 10$, $W = 220 \pm 15$ | $\text{nm}$ | GDS/OASIS DRC & LVS extraction |
| **AC-WL-02** | Gate Dielectric Physical Thickness | $3.5 \pm 0.2$ (grown at $850\text{--}900$) | $\text{nm}$ (at $^\circ\text{C}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / TEM |
| **AC-WL-03** | Wordline Layout Pitch | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\text{nm}$ | CD-SEM metrology / Layout DRC |
| **AC-WL-04** | Cell Capacitor Load Budget | $25.0\text{ to }30.0$ (minimum $28.0$) | $\text{fF}$ | Dynamic charge extraction at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Unit Cell Geometry: Access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Capacitance Budget: Minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ for soft-error immunity and bitline coupling mitigation.
  - Leakage constraint: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - Storage capacitance baseline: $25\text{ fF}\text{--}30\text{ fF}$ per cell (data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
  - Dielectric stack: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ gate dielectric at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness; high-k capacitor stack EOT $3\text{--}4\text{ nm}$.
  - Wordline and bitline pitch: $360\text{ nm}\text{ to }400\text{ nm}$.
- **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**
  - Readout development: $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s} (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{DD}/2) \approx 100\text{ mV}\text{--}150\text{ mV}$ with $C_s \approx 25\text{ fF}$ and $C_{\text{BL}} \approx 250\text{ fF}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Driving distributed wordline RC networks from a 2.8V VPP rail requires tight integration between Dickson pump output impedance and the local wordline driver stage. A 512-cell wordline line with aggregated poly/silicide sheet resistance (~8-12 ohm/sq) and gate oxide capacitive loading (~1.8-2.2 pF total load) induces significant IR drop and rise-time dispersion across the array. The driver stage PMOS pull-up and NMOS pull-down must maintain symmetric propagation delay (<3.2 ns to 90% VPP) without inducing dynamic droop >150 mV on the shared VPP distribution spine during simultaneous sub-bank row activation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node with nominal core oxide thickness tox ~4.0 nm (designed for 1.8V VDD), sustaining a boosted VPP of 2.8V accelerates Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB), Hot-Carrier Injection (HCI), and junction band-to-band tunneling (BTBT). Thick-oxide I/O devices (dual gate oxide process, tox ~6.5 nm to 7.0 nm rated for 3.3V) must be utilized for all drivers exposed to VPP. Transistor channel lengths must be sized with an overdrive safety margin (L >= 0.35 µm for VPP pull-ups) to prevent drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) and punch-through breakdown under 3.1V burn-in stress.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing dual-gate-oxide (dual-tox) masks for high-voltage VPP driver transistors adds 2 dedicated lithography and clean/oxidation steps, increasing wafer raw manufacturing cost by 3.8% and lengthening fab cycle time by 4-6 days. Mask tape-out must verify that open-source PDK DRC rules for thick-to-thin gate oxide boundary enclosures (OD2/DG enclosure >= 0.6 µm) are compatible with target 180nm foundry DRC/LVS decks to prevent yield-limiting pinhole defects and gate oxide notch formation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Wordline driver layout pitch is strictly bounded by memory array unit cell dimensions. Across a 512-cell mat, hierarchical row address predecoders (X-decoders) and sub-wordline drivers (SWD) must fit within a tight vertical cell pitch (pitch-matched to 4F or 8F cell boundaries, typically <= 1.44 µm per wordline track). Aggressive tapering of the PMOS driver width must balance driver area overhead against wordline rise delay (<3.5 ns) to ensure the 64ms refresh budget across 4096 rows is not throttled by driver footprint bloat.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. TDDB gate dielectric rupture in thin-oxide access or driver transistors subjected to steady-state or transient VPP ringing exceeding 3.3V during rapid clock-boosted wordline de-assertion.
1. Severe wordline RC propagation delay skew across far-end memory cells resulting in incomplete full-rail (1.8V VDD) charge restoration into the 28 fF MIM stacked capacitor prior to sense amplifier latching.
1. Hot carrier degradation of NMOS pull-down transistors in the final driver inverter leading to cumulative threshold voltage shift (Delta Vth > 80 mV over 10-year operating life) and wordline deactivation undershoot.

### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** VPP High-Voltage Multi-Stage Tapered Inverter Buffer Sizing & Layout Implementation  
**Discipline:** Circuit Design & Layout Engineering  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Address Decoders & Wordline VPP Voltage Pump > Hierarchical Row/Column Address Predecoder & Wordline Driver Sizing > High-Voltage VPP Wordline Driver Transistor Sizing & Taper Optimization  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

#### 1. Workflow Architecture & Sizing Budget

│   1. Taper Factor    │
│        Sizing        │

            │
            ▼

│       Matching       │
│                      │

            │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Calculate Wordline Equivalent Load & Multi-Stage Taper Ratio**:
   - Determine the total wordline capacitive loading presented by array unit cells (each cell access gate having nominal channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$) plus interconnect capacitance across the row.
   - Establish a geometric staging taper factor $f \approx 2.7\text{ -- }3.2$ to drive the large wordline capacitive load from the internal predecoder logic levels up to the boosted $V_{PP}$ domain while minimizing total propagation delay $\sum t_{pd}$.

2. **Size High-Voltage Pull-Up and Pull-Down Transistors**:
   - For all high-voltage $V_{PP}$ inverter stages, specify driver transistor gate channels respecting the core/access baseline channel length ($L \ge 180\text{ nm}$) and channel width ($W \ge 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Verify that gate oxide thickness adheres to the thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ dielectric physical thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ (grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation) or utilizes thick-oxide dual-gate/I-O high-voltage transistor variants to prevent time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) under elevated $V_{PP}$ bias.
   - Scale final-stage PMOS pull-up and NMOS pull-down finger widths to guarantee sharp rise/fall transition edges into the multi-cell row array.

3. **Pitch-Matched Multi-Finger Layout Implementation**:
   - Route and arrange the final driver stage layout into folded, interdigitated multi-finger geometries to fit within the memory array boundary.
   - Constrain driver output routing and cell pitch to match the standard array wordline pitch specification of **$360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$**.
   - Share adjacent drain contacts where appropriate to lower extrinsic diffusion junction capacitance and minimize silicon area consumption.

4. **High-Voltage Well Isolation, Guard Rings & Sign-off**:
   - Enclose PMOS drivers within an isolated deep N-well biased strictly at $V_{PP}$, bounded by continuous $N^+$ and $P^+$ guard rings to suppress minority-carrier injection and eliminate latch-up risks during rapid $V_{PP}$ switching.
   - Perform full-chip physical verification (DRC and LVS) on the driver block, extract parasitic RC interconnects, and verify that wordline driver assertion meets array activation timing specs without exceeding junction leakage constraints ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

#### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Acceptance Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wordline Pitch Layout Envelope** | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Automated DRC pitch spacing check / GDSII measurement |
| **Transistor Physical Gate Oxide Thickness ($t_{ox}$)** | $\sim 3.5$ | $\text{nm}$ | Ellipsometry / TEM / Process Tech File Rule |
| **Driver Transistor Minimum Channel Length ($L$)** | $\ge 180$ | $\text{nm}$ | Calibre / Pegasus DRC minimum channel length check |
| **Unit Cell Access Transistor Channel Width ($W$)** | $220$ | $\text{nm}$ | Layout vs. Schematic (LVS) parameter extraction |
| **Cell Retention Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage** | $< 1$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Post-layout corner SPICE simulation & wafer test |

---

#### 4. Literature & Context Citations

- **[1] 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Unit cell geometry defines access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, shared contact topology, and junction leakage limits $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ for retention integrity.
- **[2] Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: Defines wordline and bitline pitch at $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$, gate dielectric thermal oxidation conditions at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$, and physical $\text{SiO}_2$ thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$.
- **[3] Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Defines array parasitic balancing, precharge levels ($V_{DD}/2$), and differential activation sensitivities under cell capacitance loading ($C_s = 25\text{--}28\text{ fF}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Driving a capacitive distributed wordline load (approx. 2.5 pF - 5.0 pF per sub-array bank) from a nominal 2.7V VPP rail demands strict multi-stage tapering to minimize propagation delay below 1.8 ns while strictly confining peak instantaneous dynamic current to < 12 mA per active driver. Without an optimal stage taper factor (typically e ≈ 2.7 to 3.2 for 3-4 stages), excessive switching di/dt on the shared VPP line will generate transient voltage dips exceeding the 30 mV peak-to-peak ripple budget, collapsing internal row activation margins across neighboring blocks.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm mixed-voltage CMOS, regular core 1.8V thin-oxide transistors suffer severe time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) and hot-carrier injection (HCI) when operated continuously or repetitively at VPP = 2.7V - 2.8V (V_gs / V_gd / V_ds stress > 2.0V). The layout must employ dedicated thick gate oxide (dual-gate oxide 3.3V I/O devices with Tox ~ 6.5 nm - 7.0 nm) for the output pull-up PMOS and final inverter stages, combined with cascode topology or level-shifting pre-driver circuits to prevent gate-oxide punch-through during standby-to-active wordline assertions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dual-gate oxide (thick oxide 3.3V module) and high-voltage deep N-well (DNW) masking layers require specialized PDK reticles and additional implant masks, adding roughly 12% to the baseline 180nm CMOS wafer processing cost and 2-3 weeks to fab turnaround time. If layout density for the tapered inverter array exceeds pitch-matching requirements of the 180nm open-source cell pitch (0.56 µm cell height), the silicon area penalty will force metal routing overhead into 5-metal-layer configurations instead of standard 4-metal open PDKs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The physical layout pitch of the final stage tapered inverter must precisely pitch-match or multi-pitch interleave with the wordline stitch rows to avoid routing congestion and parasitic line resistance penalties (Rw > 250 ohms). Tapered buffer finger configurations must be fully DRC/LVS validated in KLayout against density, antenna ratio limits (< 200:1 on poly gates connected to long wordlines), and latchup guard-ring design rules before tapeout sign-off.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Gate dielectric puncture (TDDB failure) on the final VPP driver pull-up PMOS caused by transient overshoots exceeding 3.1V during charge pump regulator clock disable cycles.
1. Excessive VPP IR-drop and dV/dt sag (> 85 mV) causing unselected or partially addressed row pass-transistor threshold loss (V_storage < 1.4V), inducing immediate retention bit failures in DRAM test arrays.
1. Latchup in dense inverter arrays due to parasitic p-n-p-n SCR firing triggered by VPP substrate minority carrier injection during rapid high-to-low wordline discharge transitions.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Post-Layout Wordline Rise-Time Transient Simulation & Slew/Overshoot Verification
**Module Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Address Decoders & Wordline VPP Voltage Pump > Hierarchical Row/Column Address Predecoder & Wordline Driver Sizing > High-Voltage VPP Wordline Driver Transistor Sizing & Taper Optimization > Post-Layout Wordline Rise-Time Transient Simulation & Slew/Overshoot Verification  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Action Type:** Make

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Extract Parasitics   │
│          RLC          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Configure SPICE    │
│    Transient Setup    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Simulate Wordline   │
│   Rise-Time & Slew    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│      Measure VPP      │
│  Overshoot & Ringing  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────◇───────────┐
│                       │
│   Acceptance Check    │
│                       │
└───────────◇───────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Parasitic Extraction (PEX / RLC Extraction):**
   - Extract distributed 3D parasitic RC netlists from the finalized wordline decoder layout, driver taper chain, and array wordline stitch strap geometry (pitch $\sim 360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$).
   - Model the distributed line loading consisting of access transistor gates ($W = 220\text{ nm}, L = 180\text{ nm}$) and stacked capacitor nodes ($C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $28\text{ fF}$).

2. **Transient Testbench & Corner Initialization:**
   - Instantiate post-layout netlists into SPICE/Spectre netlist under Fast-Fast (FF), Typical-Typical (TT), and Slow-Slow (SS) process corners at operating junction temperature $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Connect the high-voltage $V_{PP}$ boosted supply rail driving the tapered CMOS stage.

3. **Transient Execution & Waveform Measurement:**
   - Apply address predecode switching pulses and trigger the high-voltage wordline driver.
   - Measure transient rise-time ($t_r$, 10% to 90% of $V_{PP}$) at both near-end (adjacent to the driver output) and far-end (furthest cell gate in the memory mat) nodes.
   - Capture dynamic transition slew rate ($dV/dt$) across the $V_{DD}/2$ bitline equalization baseline to prevent sense amplifier disturbed latching.

4. **Overshoot, Ringing & Oxide Reliability Check:**
   - Measure peak positive voltage spike ($V_{\text{peak}} - V_{PP}$) and ringing settling time on the access transistor gate.
   - Verify electrical stress against the thermal dry $\text{SiO}_2$ gate oxide layer ($t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$) to prevent dielectric wearout or subthreshold leakage degradation ($I_{\text{leak}} \le 1\text{ fA/cell}$).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Metric Target / Tolerance | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wordline Far-End Rise Time ($10\% \to 90\%$)** | $\le 3.5 \pm 0.2$ | $\text{ns}$ | SPICE transient simulation (`.measure tran`) at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (SS Corner) |
| **Wordline Driver Peak Voltage Overshoot** | $\le 5\%$ above nominal $V_{PP}$ (Peak margin $< 150$) | $\text{mV}$ | Automated peak detector (`.measure tran MAX v(wl_far)`) |
| **Access Transistor Slew Rate ($dV/dt$)** | $\ge 0.80$ | $\text{V/ns}$ | Transient derivative measurement at $V_{PP}/2$ trip point |
| **Gate Oxide Dielectric Field Stress ($E_{ox}$)** | $\le 7.5$ (on $3.5\text{ nm}$ $\text{SiO}_2$) | $\text{MV/cm}$ | Peak electrical field calculation across $t_{ox} = 3.5\text{ nm}$ |

---

### Citations & Literature Context
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Unit cell geometry parameters (access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor structure, minimum capacitance target ($28\text{ fF/cell}$), and leakage constraint ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Bitline equalization ($V_{DD}/2$), cell signal development $\Delta V = (C_s / (C_{BL} + C_s)) \cdot (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$ with $C_s = 25\text{ fF}, C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$, and timing coordination with wordline assertion.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: 1T1C array layout ($8F^2 / 6F^2$), wordline/bitline pitch ($360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$), data retention target ($> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$), and gate dielectric parameters ($\text{SiO}_2$ thermally grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$, physical thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$).

---

*Extracted micro-knowledge documentation persisted in [docs/knowledge/post_layout_wordline_transient_verification.md](docs/knowledge/post_layout_wordline_transient_verification.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-layout transient verification must couple the high-voltage VPP charge pump source impedance (R_out ~ 150-350 ohms) with distributed RC interconnect models (pi-segments) along the entire polysilicon/metal wordline. Omitting pump loading dynamics risks masking severe local VPP voltage sag (>250 mV) during simultaneous row activations across 512 WL segments, causing false-positive timing closure.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm high-voltage thick-oxide (5V/3.3V dual gate oxide) driver stages, excessive wordline overshoot beyond VPP + 10% (nominally VPP = 2.8V to 3.3V) induces accelerated Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) and Hot-Carrier Injection (HCI) on the access NMOS transistors. Conversely, slow slew (<0.4 V/ns) degrades the tRCD access latency and increases sub-threshold leakage during wordline transitions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Cadence Spectre / Synopsys FineSim PDK models for open-source high-voltage 180nm rules (e.g., SkyWater 180nm / TSMC 0.18um BCD variants) require exact extraction rule decks (PEX/QRC) compatible with open-source toolchains (Magic/KLayout/Ngspice/Xyce). Inaccurate extraction of parasitic fringing capacitance between adjacent wordlines leads to unmodeled dynamic cross-coupling noise.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Transient metrology runs must complete automated monte-carlo corner sweeps (SS, TT, FF across -40C to 125C) and deliver clean transient waveform artifacts before taped-out mask generation signoff, maintaining strict project schedule alignment for Gen 2 silicon delivery.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. VPP gate-oxide dielectric punch-through caused by un-clamped inductive/capacitive overshoot exceeding VDD_max breakdown thresholds (>3.6V on 3.3V I/O devices).
1. Dynamic cross-coupling crosstalk glitch exceeding access transistor V_th (0.65V) on adjacent unselected wordlines, causing destructive multi-cell soft bit flips.
1. Severe wordline far-end rise-time degradation (>6.5 ns) due to underestimated distributed wire resistance (R_poly + R_metal1 strapping), violating cell activation timing tRCD.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ROW-COLUMN-DECODER-2-2-3-01` | **Post-Layout Distributed Wordline Rise-Time (10%-90%) and Slew Rate Characterization** | HSPICE/Ngspice transient engine with Calibre xRC/Magic PEX extracted netlist, precision automated measurement scripts (.measure tran rise_time TRIG v(WL_far) VAL=0.33 RISE=1 TARG v(WL_far) VAL=2.97 RISE=1), and 12-bit virtual oscilloscope sampling at 10 ps steps. | 1. Instantiate the predecoded wordline driver chain loaded with a 512-cell distributed access transistor gate line. 2. Assert the predecoded row address input vector from 0V to 1.8V with an ideal 100 ps transition edge. 3. Record transient voltage waveforms at near-end (driver output pad) and far-end (terminal cell 512) nodes over a 50 ns window. 4. Calculate 10%-90% rise-time and instantaneous slew rate (dV/dt) across the 20%-80% voltage swing. | `Wordline far-end 10%-90% rise-time must be <= 3.20 ns; instantaneous slew rate between 20% and 80% must remain >= 0.85 V/ns and <= 2.20 V/ns across all process corners.` |
| `TC-ROW-COLUMN-DECODER-2-2-3-02` | **Post-Layout VPP Wordline Peak Overshoot and Ringing Damping Verification** | Transient SPICE solver (GEAR integration method, reltol=1e-4) linked with automated Python waveform analyzer tracking peak voltage extremum and settle-time envelope. | 1. Initialize the circuit in row-standby state (all wordlines held at VSS = 0V). 2. Step the row enable pulse to trigger maximum taper driver conduction. 3. Sample the peak voltage spike on the driver internal node and the far-end wordline node. 4. Measure the ringing oscillation decay envelope until oscillation stays within ±2% of steady-state VPP. | `Peak overshoot voltage must not exceed 3.63 V (<= 110% of nominal VPP); ringing oscillations must settle within ±2% of steady-state VPP in <= 1.80 ns.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD wrist strap (ANSI/ESD S20.20 compliant), Standard laboratory safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1), Nitrile gloves for high-performance computing hardware maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with cleaning solvents (IPA), flush immediately with copious clean water or eyewash station for 15 minutes. For server electrical shock emergencies, de-energize primary breaker immediately and initiate CPR if unresponsive.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard clean server room HVAC with positive pressure, HEPA filtration (Class 10,000 / ISO 7 airflow), and 15 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA solvent wipes and residue must be collected in dedicated airtight flammables disposal containers and processed according to local hazardous organic solvent waste regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for workstation and server rack optical connector cleaning** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Completed and DRC/LVS-clean GDSII/OASIS layout with extracted parasitic SPEF/DSPF database verified against high-voltage design rules.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Validated electrical transient signoff state with annotated timing models ready for full-chip DRAM array timing integration.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Data drift between layout modifications and parasitic databases; running transient metrology on stale netlists risks taping out an unverified high-voltage driver causing permanent dielectric failure.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WL_transient_corner_analysis_report.pdf`
- [ ] `WL_rise_slew_overshoot_raw_metrics.csv`
- [ ] `WL_far_end_transient_waveform_plots.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wordline far-end transient rise-time (10% to 90% of VPP)** | `2.75 ns` | +/- 0.45 ns | Automated SPICE .measure transient statement on Calibre xRC RC-extracted netlist at SS/125C corner. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Wordline maximum transient overshoot above VPP rail** | `120 mV` | <= 180 mV peak | Python automated waveform extremum analysis tracking maximum positive excursion during fast-fast corner. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Wordline driver slew rate in active transition region (20% to 80%)** | `1.25 V/ns` | +/- 0.35 V/ns | Derivative dV/dt extraction of voltage curve between 0.66V and 2.64V on near-end driver output. |

> All quantitative assertions pass across all 9 PVT corners (FF, TT, SS across -40°C, 27°C, 125°C) with zero DRC/ERC violations and formal multi-agent council signoff recorded in deliverable artifacts.

critics.systems_engineer: Post-layout transient verification must couple the high-voltage VPP charge pump source impedance (R_out ~ 150-350 ohms) with distributed RC interconnect models (pi-segments) along the entire polysilicon/metal wordline. Omitting pump loading dynamics risks masking severe local VPP voltage sag (>250 mV) during simultaneous row activations across 512 WL segments, causing false-positive timing closure.
critics.domain_expert: In 180nm high-voltage thick-oxide (5V/3.3V dual gate oxide) driver stages, excessive wordline overshoot beyond VPP + 10% (nominally VPP = 2.8V to 3.3V) induces accelerated Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) and Hot-Carrier Injection (HCI) on the access NMOS transistors. Conversely, slow slew (<0.4 V/ns) degrades the tRCD access latency and increases sub-threshold leakage during wordline transitions.
critics.supply_chain: Cadence Spectre / Synopsys FineSim PDK models for open-source high-voltage 180nm rules (e.g., SkyWater 180nm / TSMC 0.18um BCD variants) require exact extraction rule decks (PEX/QRC) compatible with open-source toolchains (Magic/KLayout/Ngspice/Xyce). Inaccurate extraction of parasitic fringing capacitance between adjacent wordlines leads to unmodeled dynamic cross-coupling noise.
critics.laya_pm: Transient metrology runs must complete automated monte-carlo corner sweeps (SS, TT, FF across -40C to 125C) and deliver clean transient waveform artifacts before taped-out mask generation signoff, maintaining strict project schedule alignment for Gen 2 silicon delivery.
critical_failure_modes: VPP gate-oxide dielectric punch-through caused by un-clamped inductive/capacitive overshoot exceeding VDD_max breakdown thresholds (>3.6V on 3.3V I/O devices).
Dynamic cross-coupling crosstalk glitch exceeding access transistor V_th (0.65V) on adjacent unselected wordlines, causing destructive multi-cell soft bit flips.
Severe wordline far-end rise-time degradation (>6.5 ns) due to underestimated distributed wire resistance (R_poly + R_metal1 strapping), violating cell activation timing tRCD.

testcases.title: Post-Layout Distributed Wordline Rise-Time (10%-90%) and Slew Rate Characterization
testcases.instrumentation: HSPICE/Ngspice transient engine with Calibre xRC/Magic PEX extracted netlist, precision automated measurement scripts (.measure tran rise_time TRIG v(WL_far) VAL=0.33 RISE=1 TARG v(WL_far) VAL=2.97 RISE=1), and 12-bit virtual oscilloscope sampling at 10 ps steps.
testcases.pre_conditions: Extracted parasitic netlist with full 3D field solver parasitic capacitors (C_couple, C_ground) and distributed resistors; nominal VPP regulated at 3.30 V; VSS = 0.00 V; simulation temperature set to worst-case slow corner (SS, 125°C, VPP = 3.00 V).
testcases.procedure:
1. Instantiate the predecoded wordline driver chain loaded with a 512-cell distributed access transistor gate line.
2. Assert the predecoded row address input vector from 0V to 1.8V with an ideal 100 ps transition edge.
3. Record transient voltage waveforms at near-end (driver output pad) and far-end (terminal cell 512) nodes over a 50 ns window.
4. Calculate 10%-90% rise-time and instantaneous slew rate (dV/dt) across the 20%-80% voltage swing.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Wordline far-end 10%-90% rise-time must be <= 3.20 ns; instantaneous slew rate between 20% and 80% must remain >= 0.85 V/ns and <= 2.20 V/ns across all process corners.

testcases.title: Post-Layout VPP Wordline Peak Overshoot and Ringing Damping Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Transient SPICE solver (GEAR integration method, reltol=1e-4) linked with automated Python waveform analyzer tracking peak voltage extremum and settle-time envelope.
testcases.pre_conditions: Worst-case fast corner (FF, -40°C, VPP = 3.60 V); include bondwire and power-grid parasitic inductances (L_vpp = 1.2 nH, R_vpp = 0.45 ohm).
testcases.procedure:
1. Initialize the circuit in row-standby state (all wordlines held at VSS = 0V).
2. Step the row enable pulse to trigger maximum taper driver conduction.
3. Sample the peak voltage spike on the driver internal node and the far-end wordline node.
4. Measure the ringing oscillation decay envelope until oscillation stays within ±2% of steady-state VPP.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Peak overshoot voltage must not exceed 3.63 V (<= 110% of nominal VPP); ringing oscillations must settle within ±2% of steady-state VPP in <= 1.80 ns.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Distributed RC Wordline Slew Rate & Activation Delay Transient Metrology

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > Address Decoders & Wordline VPP Voltage Pump [DRAM Circuit Design] > Hierarchical Row/Column Address Predecoder & Wordline Driver Sizing [Circuit Design] > Distributed RC Wordline Slew Rate & Activation Delay Transient Metrology [Metrology]
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Cell Capacitance Cs >= 28 fF, Read Margin Delta V >= 150 mV.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer / SPICE Verification.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Distributed RC line modeling for the polysilicon/silicide wordline must account for lumped parasitic capacitance from passing bitlines and cell gate dielectrics across the full 512-wordline array segment. Using an off-chip high-impedance active probe introduces a >0.8 pF capacitive loading artifact that skews transient slew rate measurements beyond the intrinsic sub-nanosecond rise time; on-chip source-follower test taps or picoprobe micro-contacting tips with <0.04 pF input capacitance are mandatory to isolate intrinsic Elmore delay from measurement loading.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Activation delay transient is governed by non-linear sheet resistance of the polycide stack and gate-to-channel capacitance inversion during VPP boosting (overdriven to 2.8V-3.3V on 1.8V nominal core oxide). If wordline slew rate drops below 0.6 V/ns at the far-end cell node, the transfer FET exhibits partial conduction during sense-amplifier latch strobing, directly inducing tRCD timing collapse and single-bit retention degradation due to incomplete storage cell charge transfer.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Sub-picofarad active micro-probing tips (e.g., GGB Picoprobe Model 18C or Model 34A) and high-bandwidth RF micropositioners (0.1 µm resolution) face stringent procurement lead times and single-source distributor constraints in VN cleanrooms. Mitigate this by standardizing pads for ground-signal-ground (GSG) 50-ohm micro-coaxial probes with integrated 20:1 resistive divider networks fabricable on standard Gen 2 test coupons.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Transient metrology validation must strictly gate tapeout milestone M2.3 prior to mask generation for the wordline booster stage. Unmitigated parasitic skew will force an expensive silicon re-spin. The schedule mandates parallel execution of SPICE distributed RC extraction against physical micro-bench probing data within a 5-day metrology sprint.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Far-end wordline slew rate attenuation (>4.8 ns 10%-90% rise time) causing sense-amplifier timing skew and cell data corruption during access cycles.
1. VPP transient undershoot (>250 mV droop) under high-speed row-address predecode switching due to inadequate decoupled driver capacitance.
1. Excessive capacitive loading (>0.5 pF) from active probing tip falsifying measured Elmore delay and inducing false pass/fail classifications.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-ROW-COLUMN-DECODER-2-3-01` | **Near-End vs. Far-End Wordline Slew Rate & Transient Propagation Delay** | Tektronix DPO72004C 20GHz Oscilloscope, Dual GGB Industries Model 34A Active Picoprobes (0.1 pF input C, 10 MΩ input R), Semi-automatic RF Analytical Probe Station with vibration isolation table. | 1. Land Probe A on the wordline driver output node (near-end tap) and Probe B on the terminal cell pass-transistor gate (far-end tap, 512 cells downstream). 2. Assert Row Address Strobe (RAS#) with a 200 ps edge-rate pulse generator to trigger row predecoder and wordline activation. 3. Capture transient waveforms at 50 GSa/s across 100 consecutive activation cycles. 4. Measure 10%-90% slew time on near-end and far-end nodes. 5. Compute distributed RC propagation delay t_delay = t(50% far-end) - t(50% near-end). | `Near-end 10%-90% rise time <= 1.20 ns; Far-end 10%-90% rise time <= 3.80 ns; Total distributed propagation delay (t_delay) <= 2.40 ns across all tested array sectors.` |
| `TC-ROW-COLUMN-DECODER-2-3-02` | **Wordline VPP Voltage Droop & Ground Bounce Transient Metrology** | Keysight Infiniium UXR0254A 25GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope, differential high-bandwidth active probe (Keysight N7000A / InfiniiMax III+ 13GHz), Keithley 2450 SourceMeter. | 1. Position differential active probe across VPP supply tap and local driver VSS return rail directly adjacent to the hierarchical row predecoder block. 2. Execute a continuous row address toggling sequence across alternating wordline banks. 3. Monitor transient voltage waveform for maximum dynamic sag (V_droop) and recovery time back to 95% of nominal VPP. 4. Record peak-to-peak ground bounce on local VSS rail during wordline turn-off. | `Peak transient VPP droop <= 180 mV from nominal 3.00V rail; VPP recovery time to 95% nominal <= 4.5 ns; Driver ground bounce peak <= 120 mV.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/ISO 5 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (double-gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat with continuous grounding wrist strap, Chemical splash apron and face shield during solvent wipe operations
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with solvent: Flush with copious amounts of running water for at least 15 minutes. In case of eye exposure: Immediately rinse at the emergency eyewash station for 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. For inhalation of solvent vapors: Move exposed person to fresh cleanroom air supply immediately; seek medical attention if irritation persists. No specific antidote; provide supportive care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation within laminar flow cleanroom hood (ISO Class 5) with dedicated point-of-use VOC local exhaust ventilation maintaining continuous face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solvent wipes and cleaning effluents in dedicated grounded flammables containment drums labeled 'Hazardous Waste - Flammable Solvents (IPA)'; dispose via licensed semiconductor hazardous waste management contractor.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI / Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (>18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched contact pads with intact aluminum/copper metallization free of organic residues and native oxide thickness < 1.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probed test structures with micro-scrub scrub marks < 15 µm in diameter, clean of particulate debris, ready for top passivation or secondary dicing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure forms thick non-conductive native alumina (Al2O3) or oxide layers on probe test pads, inducing erratic high-resistance contact (>50 Ω probe contact resistance) which distorts transient edge-rate captures and damages active probe tips.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full empirical validation of the distributed RC wordline slew rates and row-activation delay profiles on 180nm Gen 2 test vehicles, confirming that far-end wordline activation meets timing closures for sense-amplifier access without exceeding VPP rail droop tolerances.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WP23_Wordline_Transient_Slew_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `WP23_RC_FarEnd_Delay_RawData.csv`
- [ ] `WP23_Microprobe_Contact_Scrub_Verification.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Far-end wordline 10% to 90% activation rise time across 512 cells** | `3.50 ns` | ±0.30 ns | High-bandwidth active microprobe (0.1 pF load) transient capture averaged over 100 cycles at 50 GSa/s on Tektronix DPO72004C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Distributed RC propagation delay from driver output to far-end cell node** | `2.10 ns` | +0.30 ns / -0.20 ns | Dual-channel 50% VPP cross-point delay measurement between near-end tap and far-end tap using synchronized active differential probes |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Peak VPP supply bounce/droop during concurrent bank predecoder switching** | `150 mV` | Max <= 180 mV | AC-coupled differential probe capture across local VPP decoupling pad during 100 MHz row-cycle burst |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% of tested die across 3 sample wafers to demonstrate far-end rise times <= 3.80 ns and total delay <= 2.40 ns, with contact pad scrub inspection verifying probe impact integrity, accompanied by engineering signoff from Systems Engineer and Lead Metrology Researcher.
